set_blend_shape_name.description: Sets the name of the blend shape at this index.

clear_blend_shapes.description: Removes all blend shapes from this .

add_surface_from_arrays.description:
Creates a new surface. Mesh.get_surface_count will become the surf_idx for this new surface.
				Surfaces are created to be rendered using a primitive, which may be any of the values defined in .
				The arrays argument is an array of arrays. Each of the  elements contains an array with some of the mesh data for this surface as described by the corresponding member of  or null if it is not used by the surface. For example, arrays is the array of vertices. That first vertex sub-array is always required; the others are optional. Adding an index array puts this surface into "index mode" where the vertex and other arrays become the sources of data and the index array defines the vertex order. All sub-arrays must have the same length as the vertex array (or be an exact multiple of the vertex array's length, when multiple elements of a sub-array correspond to a single vertex) or be empty, except for  if it is used.
				The blend_shapes argument is an array of vertex data for each blend shape. Each element is an array of the same structure as arrays, but , , and  are set if and only if they are set in arrays and all other entries are null.
				The lods argument is a dictionary with  keys and  values. Each entry in the dictionary represents an LOD level of the surface, where the value is the  array to use for the LOD level and the key is roughly proportional to the distance at which the LOD stats being used. I.e., increasing the key of an LOD also increases the distance that the objects has to be from the camera before the LOD is used.
				The flags argument is the bitwise OR of, as required: One value of  left shifted by ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOMn_SHIFT for each custom channel in use, , , or .
				Note: When using indices, it is recommended to only use points, lines, or triangles.

surface_remove.description: Removes the surface at the given index from the Mesh, shifting surfaces with higher index down by one.

surface_get_array_len.description: Returns the length in vertices of the vertex array in the requested surface (see add_surface_from_arrays).

surface_get_array_index_len.description: Returns the length in indices of the index array in the requested surface (see add_surface_from_arrays).

surface_get_format.description: Returns the format mask of the requested surface (see add_surface_from_arrays).

surface_get_primitive_type.description: Returns the primitive type of the requested surface (see add_surface_from_arrays).

surface_find_by_name.description: Returns the index of the first surface with this name held within this . If none are found, -1 is returned.

surface_set_name.description: Sets a name for a given surface.

surface_get_name.description: Gets the name assigned to this surface.

regen_normal_maps.description: Regenerates tangents for each of the 's surfaces.

lightmap_unwrap.description: Performs a UV unwrap on the  to prepare the mesh for lightmapping.

custom_aabb.description: Overrides the  with one defined by user for use with frustum culling. Especially useful to avoid unexpected culling when using a shader to offset vertices.

shadow_mesh.description:
An optional mesh which can be used for rendering shadows and the depth prepass. Can be used to increase performance by supplying a mesh with fused vertices and only vertex position data (without normals, UVs, colors, etc.).
			Note: This mesh must have exactly the same vertex positions as the source mesh (including the source mesh's LODs, if present). If vertex positions differ, then the mesh will not draw correctly.

ArrayOccluder3D.brief_description: 3D polygon shape for use with occlusion culling in .
ArrayOccluder3D.description:
stores an arbitrary 3D polygon shape that can be used by the engine's occlusion culling system. This is analogous to , but for occluders.
		See 's documentation for instructions on setting up occlusion culling.

set_arrays.description: Sets indices and vertices, while updating the final occluder only once after both values are set.

vertices.description:
The occluder's vertex positions in local 3D coordinates.
			Note: The occluder is always updated after setting this value. If creating occluders procedurally, consider using set_arrays instead to avoid updating the occluder twice when it's created.

indices.description:
The occluder's index position. Indices determine which points from the vertices array should be drawn, and in which order.
			Note: The occluder is always updated after setting this value. If creating occluders procedurally, consider using set_arrays instead to avoid updating the occluder twice when it's created.

AspectRatioContainer.brief_description: A container that preserves the proportions of its child controls.
AspectRatioContainer.description: A container type that arranges its child controls in a way that preserves their proportions automatically when the container is resized. Useful when a container has a dynamic size and the child nodes must adjust their sizes accordingly without losing their aspect ratios.

ratio.description: The aspect ratio to enforce on child controls. This is the width divided by the height. The ratio depends on the stretch_mode.

stretch_mode.description: The stretch mode used to align child controls.

alignment_horizontal.description: Specifies the horizontal relative position of child controls.

alignment_vertical.description: Specifies the vertical relative position of child controls.

AtlasTexture.brief_description: A texture that crops out part of another Texture2D.
AtlasTexture.description:
resource that draws only part of its atlas texture, as defined by the region. An additional margin can also be set, which is useful for small adjustments.
		Multiple  resources can be cropped from the same atlas. Packing many smaller textures into a singular large texture helps to optimize video memory costs and render calls.
		Note:  cannot be used in an , and will not tile properly in nodes such as  or . To tile an , modify its region instead.

atlas.description: The texture that contains the atlas. Can be any type inheriting from , including another .

region.description:
The region used to draw the atlas. If either dimension of the region's size is 0, the value from atlas size will be used for that axis instead.
			Note: The image size is always an integer, so the actual region size is rounded down.

margin.description: The margin around the region. Useful for small adjustments. If the Rect2.size of this property ("w" and "h" in the editor) is set, the drawn texture is resized to fit within the margin.

filter_clip.description: If true, the area outside of the region is clipped to avoid bleeding of the surrounding texture pixels.

AudioBusLayout.brief_description: Stores information about the audio buses.
AudioBusLayout.description: Stores position, muting, solo, bypass, effects, effect position, volume, and the connections between buses. See  for usage.

AudioEffect.brief_description: Base class for audio effect resources.
AudioEffect.description:
The base  for every audio effect. In the editor, an audio effect can be added to the current bus layout through the Audio panel. At run-time, it is also possible to manipulate audio effects through AudioServer.add_bus_effect, AudioServer.remove_bus_effect, and AudioServer.get_bus_effect.
		When applied on a bus, an audio effect creates a corresponding . The instance is directly responsible for manipulating the sound, based on the original audio effect's properties.

AudioEffectAmplify.brief_description: Adds an amplifying audio effect to an audio bus.
AudioEffectAmplify.description: Increases or decreases the volume being routed through the audio bus.

volume_db.description: Amount of amplification in decibels. Positive values make the sound louder, negative values make it quieter. Value can range from -80 to 24.

volume_linear.description:
Amount of amplification as a linear value.
			Note: This member modifies volume_db for convenience. The returned value is equivalent to the result of @GlobalScope.db_to_linear on volume_db. Setting this member is equivalent to setting volume_db to the result of @GlobalScope.linear_to_db on a value.

AudioEffectBandLimitFilter.brief_description: Adds a band limit filter to the audio bus.
AudioEffectBandLimitFilter.description: Limits the frequencies in a range around the AudioEffectFilter.cutoff_hz and allows frequencies outside of this range to pass.

AudioEffectBandPassFilter.brief_description: Adds a band pass filter to the audio bus.
AudioEffectBandPassFilter.description: Attenuates the frequencies inside of a range around the AudioEffectFilter.cutoff_hz and cuts frequencies outside of this band.

AudioEffectCapture.brief_description: Captures audio from an audio bus in real-time.
AudioEffectCapture.description:
AudioEffectCapture is an AudioEffect which copies all audio frames from the attached audio effect bus into its internal ring buffer.
		Application code should consume these audio frames from this ring buffer using get_buffer and process it as needed, for example to capture data from an , implement application-defined effects, or to transmit audio over the network. When capturing audio data from a microphone, the format of the samples will be stereo 32-bit floating-point PCM.
		Unlike , this effect only returns the raw audio samples instead of encoding them into an .

can_get_buffer.description: Returns true if at least frames audio frames are available to read in the internal ring buffer.

get_buffer.description:
Gets the next frames audio samples from the internal ring buffer.
				Returns a  containing exactly frames audio samples if available, or an empty  if insufficient data was available.
				The samples are signed floating-point PCM between -1 and 1. You will have to scale them if you want to use them as 8 or 16-bit integer samples. (v = 0x7fff * samples.x)

clear_buffer.description:
Clears the internal ring buffer.
				Note: Calling this during a capture can cause the loss of samples which causes popping in the playback.

get_frames_available.description: Returns the number of frames available to read using get_buffer.

get_discarded_frames.description: Returns the number of audio frames discarded from the audio bus due to full buffer.

get_buffer_length_frames.description: Returns the total size of the internal ring buffer in frames.

get_pushed_frames.description: Returns the number of audio frames inserted from the audio bus.

buffer_length.description: Length of the internal ring buffer, in seconds. Setting the buffer length will have no effect if already initialized.

AudioEffectChorus.description: Adds a chorus audio effect. The effect applies a filter with voices to duplicate the audio source and manipulate it through the filter.

voice_count.description: The number of voices in the effect.

AudioEffectCompressor.brief_description:
Adds a compressor audio effect to an audio bus.
		Reduces sounds that exceed a certain threshold level, smooths out the dynamics and increases the overall volume.
AudioEffectCompressor.description:
Dynamic range compressor reduces the level of the sound when the amplitude goes over a certain threshold in Decibels. One of the main uses of a compressor is to increase the dynamic range by clipping as little as possible (when sound goes over 0dB).
		Compressor has many uses in the mix:
		- In the Master bus to compress the whole output (although an  is probably better).
		- In voice channels to ensure they sound as balanced as possible.
		- Sidechained. This can reduce the sound level sidechained with another audio bus for threshold detection. This technique is common in video game mixing to the level of music and SFX while voices are being heard.
		- Accentuates transients by using a wider attack, making effects sound more punchy.

threshold.description: The level above which compression is applied to the audio. Value can range from -60 to 0.

ratio.description: Amount of compression applied to the audio once it passes the threshold level. The higher the ratio, the more the loud parts of the audio will be compressed. Value can range from 1 to 48.

gain.description: Gain applied to the output signal.

attack_us.description: Compressor's reaction time when the signal exceeds the threshold, in microseconds. Value can range from 20 to 2000.

release_ms.description: Compressor's delay time to stop reducing the signal after the signal level falls below the threshold, in milliseconds. Value can range from 20 to 2000.

mix.description: Balance between original signal and effect signal. Value can range from 0 (totally dry) to 1 (totally wet).

sidechain.description: Reduce the sound level using another audio bus for threshold detection.

AudioEffectDelay.brief_description:
Adds a delay audio effect to an audio bus. Plays input signal back after a period of time.
		Two tap delay and feedback options.
AudioEffectDelay.description: Plays input signal back after a period of time. The delayed signal may be played back multiple times to create the sound of a repeating, decaying echo. Delay effects range from a subtle echo effect to a pronounced blending of previous sounds with new sounds.

dry.description: Output percent of original sound. At 0, only delayed sounds are output. Value can range from 0 to 1.

tap1_active.description: If true, the first tap will be enabled.

tap1_delay_ms.description: First tap delay time in milliseconds.

tap1_level_db.description: Sound level for the first tap.

tap1_pan.description: Pan position for the first tap. Value can range from -1 (fully left) to 1 (fully right).

tap2_active.description: If true, the second tap will be enabled.

tap2_delay_ms.description: Second tap delay time in milliseconds.

tap2_level_db.description: Sound level for the second tap.

tap2_pan.description: Pan position for the second tap. Value can range from -1 (fully left) to 1 (fully right).

feedback_lowpass.description: Low-pass filter for feedback, in Hz. Frequencies below this value are filtered out of the source signal.

AudioEffectDistortion.brief_description:
Adds a distortion audio effect to an Audio bus.
		Modifies the sound to make it distorted.
AudioEffectDistortion.description:
Different types are available: clip, tan, lo-fi (bit crushing), overdrive, or waveshape.
		By distorting the waveform the frequency content changes, which will often make the sound "crunchy" or "abrasive". For games, it can simulate sound coming from some saturated device or speaker very efficiently.

pre_gain.description: Increases or decreases the volume before the effect, in decibels. Value can range from -60 to 60.

keep_hf_hz.description: High-pass filter, in Hz. Frequencies higher than this value will not be affected by the distortion. Value can range from 1 to 20000.

drive.description: Distortion power. Value can range from 0 to 1.

post_gain.description: Increases or decreases the volume after the effect, in decibels. Value can range from -80 to 24.

AudioEffectEQ.brief_description:
Base class for audio equalizers. Gives you control over frequencies.
		Use it to create a custom equalizer if ,  or  don't fit your needs.
AudioEffectEQ.description: AudioEffectEQ gives you control over frequencies. Use it to compensate for existing deficiencies in audio. AudioEffectEQs are useful on the Master bus to completely master a mix and give it more character. They are also useful when a game is run on a mobile device, to adjust the mix to that kind of speakers (it can be added but disabled when headphones are plugged).

set_band_gain_db.description: Sets band's gain at the specified index, in dB.

get_band_gain_db.description: Returns the band's gain at the specified index, in dB.

get_band_count.description: Returns the number of bands of the equalizer.

AudioEffectEQ10.brief_description:
Adds a 10-band equalizer audio effect to an Audio bus. Gives you control over frequencies from 31 Hz to 16000 Hz.
		Each frequency can be modulated between -60/+24 dB.
AudioEffectEQ10.description:
Frequency bands:
		Band 1: 31 Hz
		Band 2: 62 Hz
		Band 3: 125 Hz
		Band 4: 250 Hz
		Band 5: 500 Hz
		Band 6: 1000 Hz
		Band 7: 2000 Hz
		Band 8: 4000 Hz
		Band 9: 8000 Hz
		Band 10: 16000 Hz
		See also , , .

AudioEffectEQ21.brief_description:
Adds a 21-band equalizer audio effect to an Audio bus. Gives you control over frequencies from 22 Hz to 22000 Hz.
		Each frequency can be modulated between -60/+24 dB.
AudioEffectEQ21.description:
Frequency bands:
		Band 1: 22 Hz
		Band 2: 32 Hz
		Band 3: 44 Hz
		Band 4: 63 Hz
		Band 5: 90 Hz
		Band 6: 125 Hz
		Band 7: 175 Hz
		Band 8: 250 Hz
		Band 9: 350 Hz
		Band 10: 500 Hz
		Band 11: 700 Hz
		Band 12: 1000 Hz
		Band 13: 1400 Hz
		Band 14: 2000 Hz
		Band 15: 2800 Hz
		Band 16: 4000 Hz
		Band 17: 5600 Hz
		Band 18: 8000 Hz
		Band 19: 11000 Hz
		Band 20: 16000 Hz
		Band 21: 22000 Hz
		See also , , .

AudioEffectEQ6.brief_description:
Adds a 6-band equalizer audio effect to an audio bus. Gives you control over frequencies from 32 Hz to 10000 Hz.
		Each frequency can be modulated between -60/+24 dB.
AudioEffectEQ6.description:
Frequency bands:
		Band 1: 32 Hz
		Band 2: 100 Hz
		Band 3: 320 Hz
		Band 4: 1000 Hz
		Band 5: 3200 Hz
		Band 6: 10000 Hz
		See also , , .

AudioEffectFilter.brief_description: Adds a filter to the audio bus.
AudioEffectFilter.description: Allows frequencies other than the cutoff_hz to pass.

cutoff_hz.description: Threshold frequency for the filter, in Hz.

resonance.description: Amount of boost in the frequency range near the cutoff frequency.

gain.description: Gain amount of the frequencies after the filter.

db.description: Steepness of the cutoff curve in dB per octave, also known as the order of the filter. Higher orders have a more aggressive cutoff.

AudioEffectHardLimiter.brief_description: Adds a hard limiter audio effect to an Audio bus.
AudioEffectHardLimiter.description: A limiter is an effect designed to disallow sound from going over a given dB threshold. Hard limiters predict volume peaks, and will smoothly apply gain reduction when a peak crosses the ceiling threshold to prevent clipping and distortion. It preserves the waveform and prevents it from crossing the ceiling threshold. Adding one in the Master bus is recommended as a safety measure to prevent sudden volume peaks from occurring, and to prevent distortion caused by clipping.

pre_gain_db.description: Gain to apply before limiting, in decibels.

ceiling_db.description:
The waveform's maximum allowed value, in decibels. This value can range from -24.0 to 0.0.
			The default value of -0.3 prevents potential inter-sample peaks (ISP) from crossing over 0 dB, which can cause slight distortion on some older hardware.

release.description: Time it takes in seconds for the gain reduction to fully release.

AudioEffectHighPassFilter.brief_description: Adds a high-pass filter to the audio bus.
AudioEffectHighPassFilter.description: Cuts frequencies lower than the AudioEffectFilter.cutoff_hz and allows higher frequencies to pass.

AudioEffectHighShelfFilter.brief_description: Adds a high-shelf filter to the audio bus.
AudioEffectHighShelfFilter.description: Reduces all frequencies above the AudioEffectFilter.cutoff_hz.

AudioEffectInstance.brief_description: Manipulates the audio it receives for a given effect.
AudioEffectInstance.description: An audio effect instance manipulates the audio it receives for a given effect. This instance is automatically created by an  when it is added to a bus, and should usually not be created directly. If necessary, it can be fetched at run-time with AudioServer.get_bus_effect_instance.

_process.description:
Called by the  to process this effect. When _process_silence is not overridden or it returns false, this method is called only when the bus is active.
				Note: It is not useful to override this method in GDScript or C#. Only GDExtension can take advantage of it.

_process_silence.description:
Override this method to customize the processing behavior of this effect instance.
				Should return true to force the  to always call _process, even if the bus has been muted or cannot otherwise be heard.

AudioEffectLimiter.brief_description: Adds a soft-clip limiter audio effect to an Audio bus.
AudioEffectLimiter.description:
A limiter is similar to a compressor, but it's less flexible and designed to disallow sound going over a given dB threshold. Adding one in the Master bus is always recommended to reduce the effects of clipping.
		Soft clipping starts to reduce the peaks a little below the threshold level and progressively increases its effect as the input level increases such that the threshold is never exceeded.

ceiling_db.description: The waveform's maximum allowed value, in decibels. Value can range from -20 to -0.1.

threshold_db.description: Threshold from which the limiter begins to be active, in decibels. Value can range from -30 to 0.

soft_clip_db.description: Applies a gain to the limited waves, in decibels. Value can range from 0 to 6.

AudioEffectLowPassFilter.brief_description: Adds a low-pass filter to the audio bus.
AudioEffectLowPassFilter.description: Cuts frequencies higher than the AudioEffectFilter.cutoff_hz and allows lower frequencies to pass.

AudioEffectLowShelfFilter.brief_description: Adds a low-shelf filter to the audio bus.
AudioEffectLowShelfFilter.description: Reduces all frequencies below the AudioEffectFilter.cutoff_hz.

AudioEffectNotchFilter.brief_description: Adds a notch filter to the Audio bus.
AudioEffectNotchFilter.description: Attenuates frequencies in a narrow band around the AudioEffectFilter.cutoff_hz and cuts frequencies outside of this range.

AudioEffectPanner.brief_description: Adds a panner audio effect to an audio bus. Pans sound left or right.
AudioEffectPanner.description: Determines how much of an audio signal is sent to the left and right buses.

pan.description: Pan position. Value can range from -1 (fully left) to 1 (fully right).

AudioEffectPhaser.brief_description:
Adds a phaser audio effect to an audio bus.
		Combines the original signal with a copy that is slightly out of phase with the original.
AudioEffectPhaser.description: Combines phase-shifted signals with the original signal. The movement of the phase-shifted signals is controlled using a low-frequency oscillator.

range_min_hz.description: Determines the minimum frequency affected by the LFO modulations, in Hz. Value can range from 10 to 10000.

range_max_hz.description: Determines the maximum frequency affected by the LFO modulations, in Hz. Value can range from 10 to 10000.

rate_hz.description: Adjusts the rate in Hz at which the effect sweeps up and down across the frequency range.

feedback.description: Output percent of modified sound. Value can range from 0.1 to 0.9.

depth.description: Determines how high the filter frequencies sweep. Low value will primarily affect bass frequencies. High value can sweep high into the treble. Value can range from 0.1 to 4.0.

AudioEffectPitchShift.brief_description:
Adds a pitch-shifting audio effect to an audio bus.
		Raises or lowers the pitch of original sound.
AudioEffectPitchShift.description: Allows modulation of pitch independently of tempo. All frequencies can be increased/decreased with minimal effect on transients.

pitch_scale.description: The pitch scale to use. 1.0 is the default pitch and plays sounds unaffected. pitch_scale can range from 0.0 (infinitely low pitch, inaudible) to 16 (16 times higher than the initial pitch).

oversampling.description: The oversampling factor to use. Higher values result in better quality, but are more demanding on the CPU and may cause audio cracking if the CPU can't keep up.

fft_size.description: The size of the Fast Fourier transform buffer. Higher values smooth out the effect over time, but have greater latency. The effects of this higher latency are especially noticeable on sounds that have sudden amplitude changes.

AudioEffectRecord.brief_description: Audio effect used for recording the sound from an audio bus.
AudioEffectRecord.description:
Allows the user to record the sound from an audio bus into an . When used on the "Master" audio bus, this includes all audio output by Godot.
		Unlike , this effect encodes the recording with the given format (8-bit, 16-bit, or compressed) instead of giving access to the raw audio samples.
		Can be used (with an ) to record from a microphone.
		Note: ProjectSettings.audio/driver/enable_input must be true for audio input to work. See also that setting's description for caveats related to permissions and operating system privacy settings.

set_recording_active.description: If true, the sound will be recorded. Note that restarting the recording will remove the previously recorded sample.

is_recording_active.description: Returns whether the recording is active or not.

format.description: Specifies the format in which the sample will be recorded.

AudioEffectReverb.brief_description: Adds a reverberation audio effect to an Audio bus.
AudioEffectReverb.description: Simulates the sound of acoustic environments such as rooms, concert halls, caverns, or an open spaces.

predelay_msec.description: Time between the original signal and the early reflections of the reverb signal, in milliseconds.

predelay_feedback.description: Output percent of predelay. Value can range from 0 to 1.

room_size.description: Dimensions of simulated room. Bigger means more echoes. Value can range from 0 to 1.

damping.description: Defines how reflective the imaginary room's walls are. Value can range from 0 to 1.

spread.description: Widens or narrows the stereo image of the reverb tail. 1 means fully widens. Value can range from 0 to 1.

hipass.description: High-pass filter passes signals with a frequency higher than a certain cutoff frequency and attenuates signals with frequencies lower than the cutoff frequency. Value can range from 0 to 1.

dry.description: Output percent of original sound. At 0, only modified sound is outputted. Value can range from 0 to 1.

wet.description: Output percent of modified sound. At 0, only original sound is outputted. Value can range from 0 to 1.

AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.brief_description: Audio effect that can be used for real-time audio visualizations.
AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.description:
This audio effect does not affect sound output, but can be used for real-time audio visualizations.
		This resource configures an , which performs the actual analysis at runtime. An instance can be obtained with AudioServer.get_bus_effect_instance.
		See also  for procedurally generating sounds.

buffer_length.description: The length of the buffer to keep (in seconds). Higher values keep data around for longer, but require more memory.

fft_size.description: The size of the Fast Fourier transform buffer. Higher values smooth out the spectrum analysis over time, but have greater latency. The effects of this higher latency are especially noticeable with sudden amplitude changes.

AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzerInstance.description:
The runtime part of an , which can be used to query the magnitude of a frequency range on its host bus.
		An instance of this class can be obtained with AudioServer.get_bus_effect_instance.

get_magnitude_for_frequency_range.description:
Returns the magnitude of the frequencies from from_hz to to_hz in linear energy as a Vector2. The x component of the return value represents the left stereo channel, and y represents the right channel.
				mode determines how the frequency range will be processed.

AudioEffectStereoEnhance.brief_description: An audio effect that can be used to adjust the intensity of stereo panning.
AudioEffectStereoEnhance.description: An audio effect that can be used to adjust the intensity of stereo panning.

pan_pullout.description: Amplifies the difference between stereo channels, increasing or decreasing existing panning. A value of 0.0 will downmix stereo to mono. Does not affect a mono signal.

time_pullout_ms.description: Widens sound stage through phase shifting in conjunction with surround. Just delays the right channel if surround is 0.

surround.description: Widens sound stage through phase shifting in conjunction with time_pullout_ms. Just pans sound to the left channel if time_pullout_ms is 0.

AudioListener2D.brief_description: Overrides the location sounds are heard from.
AudioListener2D.description:
Once added to the scene tree and enabled using make_current, this node will override the location sounds are heard from. Only one  can be current. Using make_current will disable the previous .
		If there is no active  in the current , center of the screen will be used as a hearing point for the audio.  needs to be inside  to function.

make_current.description:
Makes the  active, setting it as the hearing point for the sounds. If there is already another active , it will be disabled.
				This method will have no effect if the  is not added to .

clear_current.description: Disables the . If it's not set as current, this method will have no effect.

is_current.description: Returns true if this  is currently active.

AudioListener3D.brief_description: Overrides the location sounds are heard from.
AudioListener3D.description: Once added to the scene tree and enabled using make_current, this node will override the location sounds are heard from. This can be used to listen from a location different from the .

make_current.description: Enables the listener. This will override the current camera's listener.

clear_current.description: Disables the listener to use the current camera's listener instead.

is_current.description:
Returns true if the listener was made current using make_current, false otherwise.
				Note: There may be more than one AudioListener3D marked as "current" in the scene tree, but only the one that was made current last will be used.

doppler_tracking.description:
If not , this listener will simulate the Doppler effect for objects changed in particular _process methods.
			Note: The Doppler effect will only be heard on s if AudioStreamPlayer3D.doppler_tracking is not set to .

AudioSamplePlayback.brief_description: Meta class for playing back audio samples.
AudioSamplePlayback.description: Meta class for playing back audio samples.

AudioServer.brief_description: Server interface for low-level audio access.
AudioServer.description: is a low-level server interface for audio access. It is in charge of creating sample data (playable audio) as well as its playback via a voice interface.

remove_bus.description: Removes the bus at index index.

move_bus.description: Moves the bus from index index to index to_index.

set_bus_name.description: Sets the name of the bus at index bus_idx to name.

get_bus_name.description: Returns the name of the bus with the index bus_idx.

get_bus_index.description: Returns the index of the bus with the name bus_name. Returns -1 if no bus with the specified name exist.

get_bus_channels.description: Returns the number of channels of the bus at index bus_idx.

set_bus_volume_db.description: Sets the volume in decibels of the bus at index bus_idx to volume_db.

get_bus_volume_db.description: Returns the volume of the bus at index bus_idx in dB.

set_bus_volume_linear.description:
Sets the volume as a linear value of the bus at index bus_idx to volume_linear.
				Note: Using this method is equivalent to calling set_bus_volume_db with the result of @GlobalScope.linear_to_db on a value.

get_bus_volume_linear.description:
Returns the volume of the bus at index bus_idx as a linear value.
				Note: The returned value is equivalent to the result of @GlobalScope.db_to_linear on the result of get_bus_volume_db.

set_bus_send.description: Connects the output of the bus at bus_idx to the bus named send.

get_bus_send.description: Returns the name of the bus that the bus at index bus_idx sends to.

set_bus_solo.description: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is in solo mode.

is_bus_solo.description: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is in solo mode.

set_bus_mute.description: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is muted.

is_bus_mute.description: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is muted.

set_bus_bypass_effects.description: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is bypassing effects.

is_bus_bypassing_effects.description: If true, the bus at index bus_idx is bypassing effects.

add_bus_effect.description: Adds an  effect to the bus bus_idx at at_position.

remove_bus_effect.description: Removes the effect at index effect_idx from the bus at index bus_idx.

get_bus_effect_count.description: Returns the number of effects on the bus at bus_idx.

get_bus_effect.description: Returns the  at position effect_idx in bus bus_idx.

get_bus_effect_instance.description: Returns the  assigned to the given bus and effect indices (and optionally channel).

swap_bus_effects.description: Swaps the position of two effects in bus bus_idx.

set_bus_effect_enabled.description: If true, the effect at index effect_idx on the bus at index bus_idx is enabled.

is_bus_effect_enabled.description: If true, the effect at index effect_idx on the bus at index bus_idx is enabled.

get_bus_peak_volume_left_db.description: Returns the peak volume of the left speaker at bus index bus_idx and channel index channel.

get_bus_peak_volume_right_db.description: Returns the peak volume of the right speaker at bus index bus_idx and channel index channel.

lock.description:
Locks the audio driver's main loop.
				Note: Remember to unlock it afterwards.

unlock.description: Unlocks the audio driver's main loop. (After locking it, you should always unlock it.)

get_mix_rate.description: Returns the sample rate at the output of the .

get_input_mix_rate.description: Returns the sample rate at the input of the .

get_driver_name.description: Returns the name of the current audio driver. The default usually depends on the operating system, but may be overridden via the --audio-driver command line argument. --headless also automatically sets the audio driver to Dummy. See also ProjectSettings.audio/driver/driver.

get_output_device_list.description: Returns the names of all audio output devices detected on the system.

get_time_to_next_mix.description: Returns the relative time until the next mix occurs.

get_time_since_last_mix.description: Returns the relative time since the last mix occurred.

get_output_latency.description:
Returns the audio driver's effective output latency. This is based on ProjectSettings.audio/driver/output_latency, but the exact returned value will differ depending on the operating system and audio driver.
				Note: This can be expensive; it is not recommended to call get_output_latency every frame.

get_input_device_list.description:
Returns the names of all audio input devices detected on the system.
				Note: ProjectSettings.audio/driver/enable_input must be true for audio input to work. See also that setting's description for caveats related to permissions and operating system privacy settings.

set_input_device_active.description:
If active is true, starts the microphone input stream specified by input_device or returns an error if it failed.
				If active is false, stops the input stream if it is running.

get_input_frames_available.description: Returns the number of frames available to read using get_input_frames.

get_input_buffer_length_frames.description: Returns the absolute size of the microphone input buffer. This is set to a multiple of the audio latency and can be used to estimate the minimum rate at which the frames need to be fetched.

get_input_frames.description:
Returns a  containing exactly frames audio samples from the internal microphone buffer if available, otherwise returns an empty .
				The buffer is filled at the rate of get_input_mix_rate frames per second when set_input_device_active has successfully been set to true.
				The samples are signed floating-point PCM values between -1 and 1.

generate_bus_layout.description: Generates an  using the available buses and effects.

set_enable_tagging_used_audio_streams.description:
If set to true, all instances of  will call AudioStreamPlayback._tag_used_streams every mix step.
				Note: This is enabled by default in the editor, as it is used by editor plugins for the audio stream previews.

is_stream_registered_as_sample.description:
If true, the stream is registered as a sample. The engine will not have to register it before playing the sample.
				If false, the stream will have to be registered before playing it. To prevent lag spikes, register the stream as sample with register_stream_as_sample.

register_stream_as_sample.description:
Forces the registration of a stream as a sample.
				Note: Lag spikes may occur when calling this method, especially on single-threaded builds. It is suggested to call this method while loading assets, where the lag spike could be masked, instead of registering the sample right before it needs to be played.

output_device.description: Name of the current device for audio output (see get_output_device_list). On systems with multiple audio outputs (such as analog, USB and HDMI audio), this can be used to select the audio output device. The value "Default" will play audio on the system-wide default audio output. If an invalid device name is set, the value will be reverted back to "Default".

input_device.description:
Name of the current device for audio input (see get_input_device_list). On systems with multiple audio inputs (such as analog, USB and HDMI audio), this can be used to select the audio input device. The value "Default" will record audio on the system-wide default audio input. If an invalid device name is set, the value will be reverted back to "Default".
			Note: ProjectSettings.audio/driver/enable_input must be true for audio input to work. See also that setting's description for caveats related to permissions and operating system privacy settings.

playback_speed_scale.description: Scales the rate at which audio is played (i.e. setting it to 0.5 will make the audio be played at half its speed). See also Engine.time_scale to affect the general simulation speed, which is independent from AudioServer.playback_speed_scale.

AudioStream.description: Base class for audio streams. Audio streams are used for sound effects and music playback, and support WAV (via ) and Ogg (via ) file formats.

_instantiate_playback.description: Override this method to customize the returned value of instantiate_playback. Should return a new  created when the stream is played (such as by an ).

_get_stream_name.description: Override this method to customize the name assigned to this audio stream. Unused by the engine.

_get_length.description: Override this method to customize the returned value of get_length. Should return the length of this audio stream, in seconds.

_is_monophonic.description: Override this method to customize the returned value of is_monophonic. Should return true if this audio stream only supports one channel.

_get_bpm.description:
Overridable method. Should return the tempo of this audio stream, in beats per minute (BPM). Used by the engine to determine the position of every beat.
				Ideally, the returned value should be based off the stream's sample rate (AudioStreamWAV.mix_rate, for example).

_get_beat_count.description:
Overridable method. Should return the total number of beats of this audio stream. Used by the engine to determine the position of every beat.
				Ideally, the returned value should be based off the stream's sample rate (AudioStreamWAV.mix_rate, for example).

_get_tags.description:
Override this method to customize the tags for this audio stream. Should return a  of strings with the tag as the key and its content as the value.
				Commonly used tags include title, artist, album, tracknumber, and date.

_get_parameter_list.description: Return the controllable parameters of this stream. This array contains dictionaries with a property info description format (see Object.get_property_list). Additionally, the default value for this parameter must be added tho each dictionary in "default_value" field.

_has_loop.description: Override this method to return true if this stream has a loop.

_get_bar_beats.description: Override this method to return the bar beats of this stream.

get_length.description: Returns the length of the audio stream in seconds. If this stream is an , returns the length of the last played stream. If this stream has an indefinite length (such as for  and ), returns 0.0.

is_monophonic.description: Returns true if this audio stream only supports one channel (monophony), or false if the audio stream supports two or more channels (polyphony).

instantiate_playback.description: Returns a newly created  intended to play this audio stream. Useful for when you want to extend _instantiate_playback but call instantiate_playback from an internally held AudioStream subresource. An example of this can be found in the source code for AudioStreamRandomPitch::instantiate_playback.

can_be_sampled.description: Returns if the current  can be used as a sample. Only static streams can be sampled.

generate_sample.description: Generates an  based on the current stream.

is_meta_stream.description: Returns true if the stream is a collection of other streams, false otherwise.

AudioStreamGenerator.brief_description: An audio stream with utilities for procedural sound generation.

mix_rate_mode.description: Mixing rate mode. If set to , mix_rate is used, otherwise current  mixing rate is used.

mix_rate.description:
The sample rate to use (in Hz). Higher values are more demanding for the CPU to generate, but result in better quality.
			In games, common sample rates in use are 11025, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, and 48000.
			According to the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem, there is no quality difference to human hearing when going past 40,000 Hz (since most humans can only hear up to ~20,000 Hz, often less). If you are generating lower-pitched sounds such as voices, lower sample rates such as 32000 or 22050 may be usable with no loss in quality.
			Note:  is not automatically resampling input data, to produce expected result mix_rate_mode should match the sampling rate of input data.
			Note: If you are using  as the source of your data, set mix_rate_mode to  or  to automatically match current  mixing rate.

buffer_length.description: The length of the buffer to generate (in seconds). Lower values result in less latency, but require the script to generate audio data faster, resulting in increased CPU usage and more risk for audio cracking if the CPU can't keep up.

AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback.description: This class is meant to be used with  to play back the generated audio in real-time.

push_frame.description: Pushes a single audio data frame to the buffer. This is usually less efficient than push_buffer in C# and compiled languages via GDExtension, but push_frame may be more efficient in GDScript.

can_push_buffer.description: Returns true if a buffer of the size amount can be pushed to the audio sample data buffer without overflowing it, false otherwise.

push_buffer.description: Pushes several audio data frames to the buffer. This is usually more efficient than push_frame in C# and compiled languages via GDExtension, but push_buffer may be less efficient in GDScript.

get_frames_available.description: Returns the number of frames that can be pushed to the audio sample data buffer without overflowing it. If the result is 0, the buffer is full.

get_skips.description: Returns the number of times the playback skipped due to a buffer underrun in the audio sample data. This value is reset at the start of the playback.

clear_buffer.description: Clears the audio sample data buffer.

AudioStreamMicrophone.description:
When used directly in an  node,  plays back microphone input in real-time. This can be used in conjunction with  to process the data or save it.
		Note: ProjectSettings.audio/driver/enable_input must be true for audio input to work. See also that setting's description for caveats related to permissions and operating system privacy settings.

AudioStreamPlayback.brief_description: Meta class for playing back audio.
AudioStreamPlayback.description: Can play, loop, pause a scroll through audio. See  and  for usage.

_start.description: Override this method to customize what happens when the playback starts at the given position, such as by calling AudioStreamPlayer.play.

_stop.description: Override this method to customize what happens when the playback is stopped, such as by calling AudioStreamPlayer.stop.

_is_playing.description: Overridable method. Should return true if this playback is active and playing its audio stream.

_get_loop_count.description: Overridable method. Should return how many times this audio stream has looped. Most built-in playbacks always return 0.

_get_playback_position.description: Overridable method. Should return the current progress along the audio stream, in seconds.

_seek.description: Override this method to customize what happens when seeking this audio stream at the given position, such as by calling AudioStreamPlayer.seek.

_mix.description:
Override this method to customize how the audio stream is mixed. This method is called even if the playback is not active.
				Note: It is not useful to override this method in GDScript or C#. Only GDExtension can take advantage of it.

_tag_used_streams.description: Overridable method. Called whenever the audio stream is mixed if the playback is active and AudioServer.set_enable_tagging_used_audio_streams has been set to true. Editor plugins may use this method to "tag" the current position along the audio stream and display it in a preview.

_set_parameter.description: Set the current value of a playback parameter by name (see AudioStream._get_parameter_list).

_get_parameter.description: Return the current value of a playback parameter by name (see AudioStream._get_parameter_list).

set_sample_playback.description: Associates  to this  for playing back the audio sample of this stream.

get_sample_playback.description: Returns the  associated with this  for playing back the audio sample of this stream.

mix_audio.description:
Mixes up to frames of audio from the stream from the current position, at a rate of rate_scale, advancing the stream.
				Returns a  where each element holds the left and right channel volume levels of each frame.
				Note: Can return fewer frames than requested, make sure to use the size of the return value.

start.description: Starts the stream from the given from_pos, in seconds.

seek.description: Seeks the stream at the given time, in seconds.

get_loop_count.description: Returns the number of times the stream has looped.

get_playback_position.description: Returns the current position in the stream, in seconds.

is_playing.description: Returns true if the stream is playing.

AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic.description: Playback instance for . After setting the stream property of , , or , the playback instance can be obtained by calling AudioStreamPlayer.get_stream_playback, AudioStreamPlayer2D.get_stream_playback or AudioStreamPlayer3D.get_stream_playback methods.

play_stream.description:
Play an  at a given offset, volume, pitch scale, playback type, and bus. Playback starts immediately.
				The return value is a unique integer ID that is associated to this playback stream and which can be used to control it.
				This ID becomes invalid when the stream ends (if it does not loop), when the  is stopped, or when stop_stream is called.
				This function returns  if the amount of streams currently playing equals AudioStreamPolyphonic.polyphony. If you need a higher amount of maximum polyphony, raise this value.

set_stream_volume.description: Change the stream volume (in db). The stream argument is an integer ID returned by play_stream.

set_stream_pitch_scale.description: Change the stream pitch scale. The stream argument is an integer ID returned by play_stream.

is_stream_playing.description: Returns true if the stream associated with the given integer ID is still playing. Check play_stream for information on when this ID becomes invalid.

stop_stream.description: Stop a stream. The stream argument is an integer ID returned by play_stream, which becomes invalid after calling this function.

AudioStreamPlayer.description:
The  node plays an audio stream non-positionally. It is ideal for user interfaces, menus, or background music.
		To use this node, stream needs to be set to a valid  resource. Playing more than one sound at the same time is also supported, see max_polyphony.
		If you need to play audio at a specific position, use  or  instead.

play.description: Plays a sound from the beginning, or the given from_position in seconds.

seek.description: Restarts all sounds to be played from the given to_position, in seconds. Does nothing if no sounds are playing.

stop.description: Stops all sounds from this node.

get_playback_position.description:
Returns the position in the  of the latest sound, in seconds. Returns 0.0 if no sounds are playing.
				Note: The position is not always accurate, as the  does not mix audio every processed frame. To get more accurate results, add AudioServer.get_time_since_last_mix to the returned position.
				Note: This method always returns 0.0 if the stream is an , since it can have multiple clips playing at once.

has_stream_playback.description: Returns true if any sound is active, even if stream_paused is set to true. See also playing and get_stream_playback.

get_stream_playback.description: Returns the latest  of this node, usually the most recently created by play. If no sounds are playing, this method fails and returns an empty playback.

stream.description: The  resource to be played. Setting this property stops all currently playing sounds. If left empty, the  does not work.

volume_db.description:
Volume of sound, in decibels. This is an offset of the stream's volume.
			Note: To convert between decibel and linear energy (like most volume sliders do), use volume_linear, or @GlobalScope.db_to_linear and @GlobalScope.linear_to_db.

volume_linear.description:
Volume of sound, as a linear value.
			Note: This member modifies volume_db for convenience. The returned value is equivalent to the result of @GlobalScope.db_to_linear on volume_db. Setting this member is equivalent to setting volume_db to the result of @GlobalScope.linear_to_db on a value.

pitch_scale.description: The audio's pitch and tempo, as a multiplier of the stream's sample rate. A value of 2.0 doubles the audio's pitch, while a value of 0.5 halves the pitch.

playing.description: If true, this node is playing sounds. Setting this property has the same effect as play and stop.

autoplay.description: If true, this node calls play when entering the tree.

stream_paused.description:
If true, the sounds are paused. Setting stream_paused to false resumes all sounds.
			Note: This property is automatically changed when exiting or entering the tree, or this node is paused (see Node.process_mode).

mix_target.description: The mix target channels. Has no effect when two speakers or less are detected (see ).

max_polyphony.description: The maximum number of sounds this node can play at the same time. Calling play after this value is reached will cut off the oldest sounds.

bus.description:
The target bus name. All sounds from this node will be playing on this bus.
			Note: At runtime, if no bus with the given name exists, all sounds will fall back on "Master". See also AudioServer.get_bus_name.

playback_type.description: The playback type of the stream player. If set other than to the default value, it will force that playback type.

AudioStreamPlayer2D.description:
Plays audio that is attenuated with distance to the listener.
		By default, audio is heard from the screen center. This can be changed by adding an  node to the scene and enabling it by calling AudioListener2D.make_current on it.
		See also  to play a sound non-positionally.
		Note: Hiding an  node does not disable its audio output. To temporarily disable an 's audio output, set volume_db to a very low value like -100 (which isn't audible to human hearing).

play.description: Queues the audio to play on the next physics frame, from the given position from_position, in seconds.

seek.description: Sets the position from which audio will be played, in seconds.

has_stream_playback.description: Returns whether the  can return the  object or not.

get_stream_playback.description: Returns the  object associated with this .

volume_db.description: Base volume before attenuation, in decibels.

volume_linear.description:
Base volume before attenuation, as a linear value.
			Note: This member modifies volume_db for convenience. The returned value is equivalent to the result of @GlobalScope.db_to_linear on volume_db. Setting this member is equivalent to setting volume_db to the result of @GlobalScope.linear_to_db on a value.

pitch_scale.description: The pitch and the tempo of the audio, as a multiplier of the audio sample's sample rate.

playing.description: If true, audio is playing or is queued to be played (see play).

autoplay.description: If true, audio plays when added to scene tree.

stream_paused.description: If true, the playback is paused. You can resume it by setting stream_paused to false.

max_distance.description: Maximum distance from which audio is still hearable.

attenuation.description: The volume is attenuated over distance with this as an exponent.

max_polyphony.description: The maximum number of sounds this node can play at the same time. Playing additional sounds after this value is reached will cut off the oldest sounds.

panning_strength.description: Scales the panning strength for this node by multiplying the base ProjectSettings.audio/general/2d_panning_strength with this factor. Higher values will pan audio from left to right more dramatically than lower values.

bus.description:
Bus on which this audio is playing.
			Note: When setting this property, keep in mind that no validation is performed to see if the given name matches an existing bus. This is because audio bus layouts might be loaded after this property is set. If this given name can't be resolved at runtime, it will fall back to "Master".

area_mask.description: Determines which  layers affect the sound for reverb and audio bus effects. Areas can be used to redirect s so that they play in a certain audio bus. An example of how you might use this is making a "water" area so that sounds played in the water are redirected through an audio bus to make them sound like they are being played underwater.

playback_type.description: The playback type of the stream player. If set other than to the default value, it will force that playback type.

AudioStreamPlayer3D.description:
Plays audio with positional sound effects, based on the relative position of the audio listener. Positional effects include distance attenuation, directionality, and the Doppler effect. For greater realism, a low-pass filter is applied to distant sounds. This can be disabled by setting attenuation_filter_cutoff_hz to 20500.
		By default, audio is heard from the camera position. This can be changed by adding an  node to the scene and enabling it by calling AudioListener3D.make_current on it.
		See also  to play a sound non-positionally.
		Note: Hiding an  node does not disable its audio output. To temporarily disable an 's audio output, set volume_db to a very low value like -100 (which isn't audible to human hearing).

play.description: Queues the audio to play on the next physics frame, from the given position from_position, in seconds.

seek.description: Sets the position from which audio will be played, in seconds.

has_stream_playback.description: Returns whether the  can return the  object or not.

get_stream_playback.description: Returns the  object associated with this .

attenuation_model.description: Decides if audio should get quieter with distance linearly, quadratically, logarithmically, or not be affected by distance, effectively disabling attenuation.

volume_db.description: The base sound level before attenuation, in decibels.

volume_linear.description:
The base sound level before attenuation, as a linear value.
			Note: This member modifies volume_db for convenience. The returned value is equivalent to the result of @GlobalScope.db_to_linear on volume_db. Setting this member is equivalent to setting volume_db to the result of @GlobalScope.linear_to_db on a value.

unit_size.description: The factor for the attenuation effect. Higher values make the sound audible over a larger distance.

max_db.description: Sets the absolute maximum of the sound level, in decibels.

pitch_scale.description: The pitch and the tempo of the audio, as a multiplier of the audio sample's sample rate.

playing.description: If true, audio is playing or is queued to be played (see play).

autoplay.description: If true, audio plays when the AudioStreamPlayer3D node is added to scene tree.

stream_paused.description: If true, the playback is paused. You can resume it by setting stream_paused to false.

max_distance.description: The distance past which the sound can no longer be heard at all. Only has an effect if set to a value greater than 0.0. max_distance works in tandem with unit_size. However, unlike unit_size whose behavior depends on the attenuation_model, max_distance always works in a linear fashion. This can be used to prevent the  from requiring audio mixing when the listener is far away, which saves CPU resources.

max_polyphony.description: The maximum number of sounds this node can play at the same time. Playing additional sounds after this value is reached will cut off the oldest sounds.

panning_strength.description:
Scales the panning strength for this node by multiplying the base ProjectSettings.audio/general/3d_panning_strength by this factor. If the product is 0.0 then stereo panning is disabled and the volume is the same for all channels. If the product is 1.0 then one of the channels will be muted when the sound is located exactly to the left (or right) of the listener.
			Two speaker stereo arrangements implement the WebAudio standard for StereoPannerNode Panning where the volume is cosine of half the azimuth angle to the ear.
			For other speaker arrangements such as the 5.1 and 7.1 the SPCAP (Speaker-Placement Correction Amplitude) algorithm is implemented.

bus.description:
The bus on which this audio is playing.
			Note: When setting this property, keep in mind that no validation is performed to see if the given name matches an existing bus. This is because audio bus layouts might be loaded after this property is set. If this given name can't be resolved at runtime, it will fall back to "Master".

area_mask.description: Determines which  layers affect the sound for reverb and audio bus effects. Areas can be used to redirect s so that they play in a certain audio bus. An example of how you might use this is making a "water" area so that sounds played in the water are redirected through an audio bus to make them sound like they are being played underwater.

playback_type.description: The playback type of the stream player. If set other than to the default value, it will force that playback type.

emission_angle_enabled.description: If true, the audio should be attenuated according to the direction of the sound.

emission_angle_degrees.description: The angle in which the audio reaches a listener unattenuated.

emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db.description: Attenuation factor used if listener is outside of emission_angle_degrees and emission_angle_enabled is set, in decibels.

attenuation_filter_cutoff_hz.description: The cutoff frequency of the attenuation low-pass filter, in Hz. A sound above this frequency is attenuated more than a sound below this frequency. To disable this effect, set this to 20500 as this frequency is above the human hearing limit.

attenuation_filter_db.description: Amount how much the filter affects the loudness, in decibels.

doppler_tracking.description:
Decides in which step the Doppler effect should be calculated.
			Note: If doppler_tracking is not  but the current / has doppler tracking disabled, the Doppler effect will be heard but will not take the movement of the current listener into account. If accurate Doppler effect is desired, doppler tracking should be enabled on both the  and the current /.

AudioStreamPolyphonic.brief_description: AudioStream that lets the user play custom streams at any time from code, simultaneously using a single player.
AudioStreamPolyphonic.description:
AudioStream that lets the user play custom streams at any time from code, simultaneously using a single player.
		Playback control is done via the  instance set inside the player, which can be obtained via AudioStreamPlayer.get_stream_playback, AudioStreamPlayer2D.get_stream_playback or AudioStreamPlayer3D.get_stream_playback methods. Obtaining the playback instance is only valid after the stream property is set as an  in those players.

polyphony.description: Maximum amount of simultaneous streams that can be played.

AudioStreamRandomizer.brief_description: Wraps a pool of audio streams with pitch and volume shifting.
AudioStreamRandomizer.description: Picks a random AudioStream from the pool, depending on the playback mode, and applies random pitch shifting and volume shifting during playback.

add_stream.description: Insert a stream at the specified index. If the index is less than zero, the insertion occurs at the end of the underlying pool.

move_stream.description: Move a stream from one index to another.

remove_stream.description: Remove the stream at the specified index.

set_stream.description: Set the AudioStream at the specified index.

get_stream.description: Returns the stream at the specified index.

set_stream_probability_weight.description: Set the probability weight of the stream at the specified index. The higher this value, the more likely that the randomizer will choose this stream during random playback modes.

get_stream_probability_weight.description: Returns the probability weight associated with the stream at the given index.

playback_mode.description: Controls how this AudioStreamRandomizer picks which AudioStream to play next.

random_pitch.description:
The largest possible frequency multiplier of the random pitch variation. Pitch will be randomly chosen within a range of 1.0 / random_pitch and random_pitch. A value of 1.0 means no variation. A value of 2.0 means pitch will be randomized between double and half.
			Note: Setting this property also sets random_pitch_semitones.

random_pitch_semitones.description:
The largest possible distance, in semitones, of the random pitch variation. A value of 0.0 means no variation.
			Note: Setting this property also sets random_pitch.

random_volume_offset_db.description: The intensity of random volume variation. Volume will be increased or decreased by a random value up to random_volume_offset_db. A value of 0.0 means no variation. A value of 3.0 means volume will be randomized between -3.0 dB and +3.0 dB.

streams_count.description: The number of streams in the stream pool.

AudioStreamWAV.brief_description: Stores audio data loaded from WAV files.
AudioStreamWAV.description:
AudioStreamWAV stores sound samples loaded from WAV files. To play the stored sound, use an  (for non-positional audio) or / (for positional audio). The sound can be looped.
		This class can also be used to store dynamically-generated PCM audio data. See also  for procedural audio generation.

load_from_buffer.description:
Creates a new  instance from the given buffer. The buffer must contain WAV data.
				The keys and values of options match the properties of . The usage of options is identical to AudioStreamWAV.load_from_file.

save_to_wav.description:
Saves the AudioStreamWAV as a WAV file to path. Samples with IMA ADPCM or Quite OK Audio formats can't be saved.
				Note: A .wav extension is automatically appended to path if it is missing.

data.description:
Contains the audio data in bytes.
			Note: If format is set to , this property expects signed 8-bit PCM data. To convert from unsigned 8-bit PCM, subtract 128 from each byte.
			Note: If format is set to , this property expects data from a full QOA file.

loop_begin.description: The loop start point (in number of samples, relative to the beginning of the stream).

loop_end.description: The loop end point (in number of samples, relative to the beginning of the stream).

mix_rate.description:
The sample rate for mixing this audio. Higher values require more storage space, but result in better quality.
			In games, common sample rates in use are 11025, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, and 48000.
			According to the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem, there is no quality difference to human hearing when going past 40,000 Hz (since most humans can only hear up to ~20,000 Hz, often less). If you are using lower-pitched sounds such as voices, lower sample rates such as 32000 or 22050 may be usable with no loss in quality.

tags.description:
Contains user-defined tags if found in the WAV data.
			Commonly used tags include title, artist, album, tracknumber, and date (date does not have a standard date format).
			Note: No tag is guaranteed to be present in every file, so make sure to account for the keys not always existing.
			Note: Only WAV files using a LIST chunk with an identifier of INFO to encode the tags are currently supported.

BackBufferCopy.brief_description: A node that copies a region of the screen to a buffer for access in shader code.
BackBufferCopy.description:
Node for back-buffering the currently-displayed screen. The region defined in the  node is buffered with the content of the screen it covers, or the entire screen according to the copy_mode. It can be accessed in shader scripts using the screen texture (i.e. a uniform sampler with hint_screen_texture).
		Note: Since this node inherits from  (and not ), anchors and margins won't apply to child -derived nodes. This can be problematic when resizing the window. To avoid this, add -derived nodes as siblings to the  node instead of adding them as children.

rect.description: The area covered by the . Only used if copy_mode is .

BaseButton.brief_description: Abstract base class for GUI buttons.
BaseButton.description: is an abstract base class for GUI buttons. It doesn't display anything by itself.

_pressed.description: Called when the button is pressed. If you need to know the button's pressed state (and toggle_mode is active), use _toggled instead.

_toggled.description: Called when the button is toggled (only if toggle_mode is active).

set_pressed_no_signal.description:
Changes the button_pressed state of the button, without emitting . Use when you just want to change the state of the button without sending the pressed event (e.g. when initializing scene). Only works if toggle_mode is true.
				Note: This method doesn't unpress other buttons in button_group.

is_hovered.description: Returns true if the mouse has entered the button and has not left it yet.

get_draw_mode.description: Returns the visual state used to draw the button. This is useful mainly when implementing your own draw code by either overriding _draw() or connecting to "draw" signal. The visual state of the button is defined by the  enum.

disabled.description:
If true, the button is in disabled state and can't be clicked or toggled.
			Note: If the button is disabled while held down,  will be emitted.

toggle_mode.description: If true, the button is in toggle mode. Makes the button flip state between pressed and unpressed each time its area is clicked.

button_pressed.description:
If true, the button's state is pressed. Means the button is pressed down or toggled (if toggle_mode is active). Only works if toggle_mode is true.
			Note: Changing the value of button_pressed will result in  to be emitted. If you want to change the pressed state without emitting that signal, use set_pressed_no_signal.

action_mode.description: Determines when the button is considered clicked.

button_mask.description:
Binary mask to choose which mouse buttons this button will respond to.
			To allow both left-click and right-click, use MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_LEFT | MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_RIGHT.

keep_pressed_outside.description:
If true, the button stays pressed when moving the cursor outside the button while pressing it.
			Note: This property only affects the button's visual appearance. Signals will be emitted at the same moment regardless of this property's value.

button_group.description:
The  associated with the button. Not to be confused with node groups.
			Note: The button will be configured as a radio button if a  is assigned to it.

shortcut_feedback.description: If true, the button will highlight for a short amount of time when its shortcut is activated. If false and toggle_mode is false, the shortcut will activate without any visual feedback.

shortcut_in_tooltip.description:
If true, the button will add information about its shortcut in the tooltip.
			Note: This property does nothing when the tooltip control is customized using Control._make_custom_tooltip.

BaseMaterial3D.brief_description: Abstract base class for defining the 3D rendering properties of meshes.
BaseMaterial3D.description: This class serves as a default material with a wide variety of rendering features and properties without the need to write shader code. See the tutorial below for details.

set_flag.description: If enable is true, enables the specified flag. Flags are optional behavior that can be turned on and off. Only one flag can be enabled at a time with this function, the flag enumerators cannot be bit-masked together to enable or disable multiple flags at once. Flags can also be enabled by setting their corresponding property to true.

get_flag.description: Returns true if the specified flag is enabled.

set_feature.description: If enable is true, enables the specified feature. Many features that are available in  need to be enabled before use. This way, the cost for using the feature is only incurred when specified. Features can also be enabled by setting their corresponding property to true.

get_feature.description: Returns true if the specified feature is enabled.

set_texture.description: Sets the texture for the slot specified by param.

get_texture.description: Returns the  associated with the specified texture param.

transparency.description: The material's transparency mode. Some transparency modes will disable shadow casting. Any transparency mode other than  has a greater performance impact compared to opaque rendering. See also blend_mode.

alpha_scissor_threshold.description: Threshold at which the alpha scissor will discard values. Higher values will result in more pixels being discarded. If the material becomes too opaque at a distance, try increasing alpha_scissor_threshold. If the material disappears at a distance, try decreasing alpha_scissor_threshold.

alpha_hash_scale.description: The hashing scale for Alpha Hash. Recommended values between 0 and 2.

alpha_antialiasing_mode.description: The type of alpha antialiasing to apply.

alpha_antialiasing_edge.description: Threshold at which antialiasing will be applied on the alpha channel.

blend_mode.description:
The material's blend mode.
			Note: Values other than Mix force the object into the transparent pipeline.

cull_mode.description: Determines which side of the triangle to cull depending on whether the triangle faces towards or away from the camera.

depth_draw_mode.description: Determines when depth rendering takes place. See also transparency.

no_depth_test.description: If true, depth testing is disabled and the object will be drawn in render order.

depth_test.description:
Determines which comparison operator is used when testing depth.
			Note: Changing depth_test to a non-default value only has a visible effect when used on a transparent material, or a material that has depth_draw_mode set to .

shading_mode.description: Sets whether the shading takes place, per-pixel, per-vertex or unshaded. Per-vertex lighting is faster, making it the best choice for mobile applications, however it looks considerably worse than per-pixel. Unshaded rendering is the fastest, but disables all interactions with lights.

diffuse_mode.description: The algorithm used for diffuse light scattering.

specular_mode.description:
The method for rendering the specular blob.
			Note: specular_mode only applies to the specular blob. It does not affect specular reflections from the sky, screen-space reflections, , SDFGI or s. To disable reflections from these sources as well, set metallic_specular to 0.0 instead.

disable_ambient_light.description: If true, the object receives no ambient light.

disable_fog.description: If true, the object will not be affected by fog (neither volumetric nor depth fog). This is useful for unshaded or transparent materials (e.g. particles), which without this setting will be affected even if fully transparent.

disable_specular_occlusion.description: If true, disables specular occlusion even if ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/specular_occlusion/enabled is false.

vertex_color_use_as_albedo.description: If true, the vertex color is used as albedo color.

vertex_color_is_srgb.description:
If true, vertex colors are considered to be stored in nonlinear sRGB encoding and are converted to linear encoding during rendering. If false, vertex colors are considered to be stored in linear encoding and are rendered as-is. See also albedo_texture_force_srgb.
			Note: Only effective when using the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility.

albedo_color.description:
The material's base color.
			Note: If detail_enabled is true and a detail_albedo texture is specified, albedo_color will not modulate the detail texture. This can be used to color partial areas of a material by not specifying an albedo texture and using a transparent detail_albedo texture instead.

albedo_texture.description:
Texture to multiply by albedo_color. Used for basic texturing of objects.
			If the texture appears unexpectedly too dark or too bright, check albedo_texture_force_srgb.

albedo_texture_force_srgb.description:
If true, forces a conversion of the albedo_texture from nonlinear sRGB encoding to linear encoding. See also vertex_color_is_srgb.
			This should only be enabled when needed (typically when using a  as albedo_texture). If albedo_texture_force_srgb is true when it shouldn't be, the texture will appear to be too dark. If albedo_texture_force_srgb is false when it shouldn't be, the texture will appear to be too bright.

albedo_texture_msdf.description: Enables multichannel signed distance field rendering shader. Use msdf_pixel_range and msdf_outline_size to configure MSDF parameters.

orm_texture.description: The Occlusion/Roughness/Metallic texture to use. This is a more efficient replacement of ao_texture, roughness_texture and metallic_texture in . Ambient occlusion is stored in the red channel. Roughness map is stored in the green channel. Metallic map is stored in the blue channel. The alpha channel is ignored.

metallic.description: A high value makes the material appear more like a metal. Non-metals use their albedo as the diffuse color and add diffuse to the specular reflection. With non-metals, the reflection appears on top of the albedo color. Metals use their albedo as a multiplier to the specular reflection and set the diffuse color to black resulting in a tinted reflection. Materials work better when fully metal or fully non-metal, values between 0 and 1 should only be used for blending between metal and non-metal sections. To alter the amount of reflection use roughness.

metallic_specular.description:
Adjusts the strength of specular reflections. Specular reflections are composed of scene reflections and the specular lobe which is the bright spot that is reflected from light sources. When set to 0.0, no specular reflections will be visible. This differs from the   as  only applies to the specular lobe from the light source.
			Note: Unlike metallic, this is not energy-conserving, so it should be left at 0.5 in most cases. See also roughness.

metallic_texture.description: Texture used to specify metallic for an object. This is multiplied by metallic.

metallic_texture_channel.description: Specifies the channel of the metallic_texture in which the metallic information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored metallic in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.

roughness.description: Surface reflection. A value of 0 represents a perfect mirror while a value of 1 completely blurs the reflection. See also metallic.

roughness_texture.description: Texture used to control the roughness per-pixel. Multiplied by roughness.

roughness_texture_channel.description: Specifies the channel of the roughness_texture in which the roughness information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored metallic in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.

emission_enabled.description: If true, the body emits light. Emitting light makes the object appear brighter. The object can also cast light on other objects if a , SDFGI, or  is used and this object is used in baked lighting.

emission.description: The emitted light's color. See emission_enabled.

emission_energy_multiplier.description: Multiplier for emitted light. See emission_enabled.

emission_intensity.description: Luminance of emitted light, measured in nits (candela per square meter). Only available when ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units is enabled. The default is roughly equivalent to an indoor lightbulb.

emission_operator.description: Sets how emission interacts with emission_texture. Can either add or multiply.

emission_on_uv2.description: Use UV2 to read from the emission_texture.

emission_texture.description: Texture that specifies how much surface emits light at a given point.

normal_enabled.description: If true, normal mapping is enabled. This has a slight performance cost, especially on mobile GPUs.

normal_scale.description: The strength of the normal map's effect.

normal_texture.description:
Texture used to specify the normal at a given pixel. The normal_texture only uses the red and green channels; the blue and alpha channels are ignored. The normal read from normal_texture is oriented around the surface normal provided by the .
			Note: The mesh must have both normals and tangents defined in its vertex data. Otherwise, the normal map won't render correctly and will only appear to darken the whole surface. If creating geometry with , you can use SurfaceTool.generate_normals and SurfaceTool.generate_tangents to automatically generate normals and tangents respectively.
			Note: Godot expects the normal map to use X+, Y+, and Z+ coordinates. See this page for a comparison of normal map coordinates expected by popular engines.
			Note: If detail_enabled is true, the detail_albedo texture is drawn below the normal_texture. To display a normal map above the detail_albedo texture, use detail_normal instead.
