bent_normal_enabled.description: If true, the bent normal map is enabled. This allows for more accurate indirect lighting and specular occlusion.

bent_normal_texture.description:
Texture that specifies the average direction of incoming ambient light at a given pixel. The bent_normal_texture only uses the red and green channels; the blue and alpha channels are ignored. The normal read from bent_normal_texture is oriented around the surface normal provided by the .
			Note: A bent normal map is different from a regular normal map. When baking a bent normal map make sure to use a cosine distribution for the bent normal map to work correctly.
			Note: The mesh must have both normals and tangents defined in its vertex data. Otherwise, the shading produced by the bent normal map will not look correct. If creating geometry with , you can use SurfaceTool.generate_normals and SurfaceTool.generate_tangents to automatically generate normals and tangents respectively.
			Note: Godot expects the bent normal map to use X+, Y+, and Z+ coordinates. See this page for a comparison of normal map coordinates expected by popular engines.

rim_enabled.description:
If true, rim effect is enabled. Rim lighting increases the brightness at glancing angles on an object.
			Note: Rim lighting is not visible if the material's shading_mode is .

rim.description: Sets the strength of the rim lighting effect.

rim_tint.description: The amount of to blend light and albedo color when rendering rim effect. If 0 the light color is used, while 1 means albedo color is used. An intermediate value generally works best.

rim_texture.description: Texture used to set the strength of the rim lighting effect per-pixel. Multiplied by rim.

clearcoat_enabled.description:
If true, clearcoat rendering is enabled. Adds a secondary transparent pass to the lighting calculation resulting in an added specular blob. This makes materials appear as if they have a clear layer on them that can be either glossy or rough.
			Note: Clearcoat rendering is not visible if the material's shading_mode is .

clearcoat.description: Sets the strength of the clearcoat effect. Setting to 0 looks the same as disabling the clearcoat effect.

clearcoat_roughness.description: Sets the roughness of the clearcoat pass. A higher value results in a rougher clearcoat while a lower value results in a smoother clearcoat.

clearcoat_texture.description: Texture that defines the strength of the clearcoat effect and the glossiness of the clearcoat. Strength is specified in the red channel while glossiness is specified in the green channel.

anisotropy_enabled.description:
If true, anisotropy is enabled. Anisotropy changes the shape of the specular blob and aligns it to tangent space. This is useful for brushed aluminum and hair reflections.
			Note: Mesh tangents are needed for anisotropy to work. If the mesh does not contain tangents, the anisotropy effect will appear broken.
			Note: Material anisotropy should not to be confused with anisotropic texture filtering, which can be enabled by setting texture_filter to .

anisotropy.description: The strength of the anisotropy effect. This is multiplied by anisotropy_flowmap's alpha channel if a texture is defined there and the texture contains an alpha channel.

anisotropy_flowmap.description:
Texture that offsets the tangent map for anisotropy calculations and optionally controls the anisotropy effect (if an alpha channel is present). The flowmap texture is expected to be a derivative map, with the red channel representing distortion on the X axis and green channel representing distortion on the Y axis. Values below 0.5 will result in negative distortion, whereas values above 0.5 will result in positive distortion.
			If present, the texture's alpha channel will be used to multiply the strength of the anisotropy effect. Fully opaque pixels will keep the anisotropy effect's original strength while fully transparent pixels will disable the anisotropy effect entirely. The flowmap texture's blue channel is ignored.

ao_enabled.description: If true, ambient occlusion is enabled. Ambient occlusion darkens areas based on the ao_texture.

ao_light_affect.description: Amount that ambient occlusion affects lighting from lights. If 0, ambient occlusion only affects ambient light. If 1, ambient occlusion affects lights just as much as it affects ambient light. This can be used to impact the strength of the ambient occlusion effect, but typically looks unrealistic.

ao_texture.description: Texture that defines the amount of ambient occlusion for a given point on the object.

ao_on_uv2.description: If true, use UV2 coordinates to look up from the ao_texture.

ao_texture_channel.description: Specifies the channel of the ao_texture in which the ambient occlusion information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored metallic in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.

heightmap_enabled.description:
If true, height mapping is enabled (also called "parallax mapping" or "depth mapping"). See also normal_enabled. Height mapping is a demanding feature on the GPU, so it should only be used on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.
			Note: Height mapping is not supported if triplanar mapping is used on the same material. The value of heightmap_enabled will be ignored if uv1_triplanar is enabled.

heightmap_scale.description:
The heightmap scale to use for the parallax effect (see heightmap_enabled). The default value is tuned so that the highest point (value = 255) appears to be 5 cm higher than the lowest point (value = 0). Higher values result in a deeper appearance, but may result in artifacts appearing when looking at the material from oblique angles, especially when the camera moves. Negative values can be used to invert the parallax effect, but this is different from inverting the texture using heightmap_flip_texture as the material will also appear to be "closer" to the camera. In most cases, heightmap_scale should be kept to a positive value.
			Note: If the height map effect looks strange regardless of this value, try adjusting heightmap_flip_binormal and heightmap_flip_tangent. See also heightmap_texture for recommendations on authoring heightmap textures, as the way the heightmap texture is authored affects how heightmap_scale behaves.

heightmap_deep_parallax.description: If true, uses parallax occlusion mapping to represent depth in the material instead of simple offset mapping (see heightmap_enabled). This results in a more convincing depth effect, but is much more expensive on the GPU. Only enable this on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.

heightmap_min_layers.description:
The number of layers to use for parallax occlusion mapping when the camera is far away from the material. Higher values result in a more convincing depth effect, especially in materials that have steep height changes. Higher values have a significant cost on the GPU, so it should only be increased on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.
			Note: Only effective if heightmap_deep_parallax is true.

heightmap_max_layers.description:
The number of layers to use for parallax occlusion mapping when the camera is up close to the material. Higher values result in a more convincing depth effect, especially in materials that have steep height changes. Higher values have a significant cost on the GPU, so it should only be increased on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.
			Note: Only effective if heightmap_deep_parallax is true.

heightmap_flip_tangent.description: If true, flips the mesh's tangent vectors when interpreting the height map. If the heightmap effect looks strange when the camera moves (even with a reasonable heightmap_scale), try setting this to true.

heightmap_flip_binormal.description: If true, flips the mesh's binormal vectors when interpreting the height map. If the heightmap effect looks strange when the camera moves (even with a reasonable heightmap_scale), try setting this to true.

heightmap_texture.description:
The texture to use as a height map. See also heightmap_enabled.
			For best results, the texture should be normalized (with heightmap_scale reduced to compensate). In GIMP, this can be done using Colors > Auto > Equalize. If the texture only uses a small part of its available range, the parallax effect may look strange, especially when the camera moves.
			Note: To reduce memory usage and improve loading times, you may be able to use a lower-resolution heightmap texture as most heightmaps are only comprised of low-frequency data.

heightmap_flip_texture.description:
If true, interprets the height map texture as a depth map, with brighter values appearing to be "lower" in altitude compared to darker values.
			This can be enabled for compatibility with some materials authored for Godot 3.x. This is not necessary if the Invert import option was used to invert the depth map in Godot 3.x, in which case heightmap_flip_texture should remain false.

subsurf_scatter_enabled.description:
If true, subsurface scattering is enabled. Emulates light that penetrates an object's surface, is scattered, and then emerges. Subsurface scattering quality is controlled by ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/subsurface_scattering/subsurface_scattering_quality.
			Note: Subsurface scattering is not supported on viewports that have a transparent background (where Viewport.transparent_bg is true).

subsurf_scatter_strength.description: The strength of the subsurface scattering effect. The depth of the effect is also controlled by ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/subsurface_scattering/subsurface_scattering_scale, which is set globally.

subsurf_scatter_skin_mode.description: If true, subsurface scattering will use a special mode optimized for the color and density of human skin, such as boosting the intensity of the red channel in subsurface scattering.

subsurf_scatter_texture.description: Texture used to control the subsurface scattering strength. Stored in the red texture channel. Multiplied by subsurf_scatter_strength.

subsurf_scatter_transmittance_enabled.description: If true, enables subsurface scattering transmittance. Only effective if subsurf_scatter_enabled is true. See also backlight_enabled.

subsurf_scatter_transmittance_color.description: The color to multiply the subsurface scattering transmittance effect with. Ignored if subsurf_scatter_skin_mode is true.

subsurf_scatter_transmittance_texture.description: The texture to use for multiplying the intensity of the subsurface scattering transmittance intensity. See also subsurf_scatter_texture. Ignored if subsurf_scatter_skin_mode is true.

subsurf_scatter_transmittance_depth.description: The depth of the subsurface scattering transmittance effect.

subsurf_scatter_transmittance_boost.description: The intensity of the subsurface scattering transmittance effect.

backlight_enabled.description: If true, the backlight effect is enabled. See also subsurf_scatter_transmittance_enabled.

backlight.description: The color used by the backlight effect. Represents the light passing through an object.

backlight_texture.description: Texture used to control the backlight effect per-pixel. Added to backlight.

refraction_enabled.description:
If true, the refraction effect is enabled. Distorts transparency based on light from behind the object.
			Note: Refraction is implemented using the screen texture. Only opaque materials will appear in the refraction, since transparent materials do not appear in the screen texture.

refraction_scale.description: The strength of the refraction effect.

refraction_texture.description: Texture that controls the strength of the refraction per-pixel. Multiplied by refraction_scale.

refraction_texture_channel.description: Specifies the channel of the refraction_texture in which the refraction information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored refraction in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.

detail_enabled.description: If true, enables the detail overlay. Detail is a second texture that gets mixed over the surface of the object based on detail_mask and detail_albedo's alpha channel. This can be used to add variation to objects, or to blend between two different albedo/normal textures.

detail_mask.description: Texture used to specify how the detail textures get blended with the base textures. detail_mask can be used together with detail_albedo's alpha channel (if any).

detail_blend_mode.description: Specifies how the detail_albedo should blend with the current ALBEDO.

detail_uv_layer.description: Specifies whether to use UV or UV2 for the detail layer.

detail_albedo.description:
Texture that specifies the color of the detail overlay. detail_albedo's alpha channel is used as a mask, even when the material is opaque. To use a dedicated texture as a mask, see detail_mask.
			Note: detail_albedo is not modulated by albedo_color.

detail_normal.description:
Texture that specifies the per-pixel normal of the detail overlay. The detail_normal texture only uses the red and green channels; the blue and alpha channels are ignored. The normal read from detail_normal is oriented around the surface normal provided by the .
			Note: Godot expects the normal map to use X+, Y+, and Z+ coordinates. See this page for a comparison of normal map coordinates expected by popular engines.

uv1_scale.description: How much to scale the UV coordinates. This is multiplied by UV in the vertex function. The Z component is used when uv1_triplanar is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.

uv1_offset.description: How much to offset the UV coordinates. This amount will be added to UV in the vertex function. This can be used to offset a texture. The Z component is used when uv1_triplanar is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.

uv1_triplanar.description: If true, instead of using UV textures will use a triplanar texture lookup to determine how to apply textures. Triplanar uses the orientation of the object's surface to blend between texture coordinates. It reads from the source texture 3 times, once for each axis and then blends between the results based on how closely the pixel aligns with each axis. This is often used for natural features to get a realistic blend of materials. Because triplanar texturing requires many more texture reads per-pixel it is much slower than normal UV texturing. Additionally, because it is blending the texture between the three axes, it is unsuitable when you are trying to achieve crisp texturing.

uv1_triplanar_sharpness.description:
A lower number blends the texture more softly while a higher number blends the texture more sharply.
			Note: uv1_triplanar_sharpness is clamped between 0.0 and 150.0 (inclusive) as values outside that range can look broken depending on the mesh.

uv1_world_triplanar.description: If true, triplanar mapping for UV is calculated in world space rather than object local space. See also uv1_triplanar.

uv2_scale.description: How much to scale the UV2 coordinates. This is multiplied by UV2 in the vertex function. The Z component is used when uv2_triplanar is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.

uv2_offset.description: How much to offset the UV2 coordinates. This amount will be added to UV2 in the vertex function. This can be used to offset a texture. The Z component is used when uv2_triplanar is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.

uv2_triplanar.description: If true, instead of using UV2 textures will use a triplanar texture lookup to determine how to apply textures. Triplanar uses the orientation of the object's surface to blend between texture coordinates. It reads from the source texture 3 times, once for each axis and then blends between the results based on how closely the pixel aligns with each axis. This is often used for natural features to get a realistic blend of materials. Because triplanar texturing requires many more texture reads per-pixel it is much slower than normal UV texturing. Additionally, because it is blending the texture between the three axes, it is unsuitable when you are trying to achieve crisp texturing.

uv2_triplanar_sharpness.description:
A lower number blends the texture more softly while a higher number blends the texture more sharply.
			Note: uv2_triplanar_sharpness is clamped between 0.0 and 150.0 (inclusive) as values outside that range can look broken depending on the mesh.

uv2_world_triplanar.description: If true, triplanar mapping for UV2 is calculated in world space rather than object local space. See also uv2_triplanar.

texture_filter.description:
Filter flags for the texture.
			Note: heightmap_texture is always sampled with linear filtering, even if nearest-neighbor filtering is selected here. This is to ensure the heightmap effect looks as intended. If you need sharper height transitions between pixels, resize the heightmap texture in an image editor with nearest-neighbor filtering.

texture_repeat.description: If true, the texture repeats when exceeding the texture's size. See .

disable_receive_shadows.description: If true, the object receives no shadow that would otherwise be cast onto it.

shadow_to_opacity.description: If true, enables the "shadow to opacity" render mode where lighting modifies the alpha so shadowed areas are opaque and non-shadowed areas are transparent. Useful for overlaying shadows onto a camera feed in AR.

billboard_mode.description:
Controls how the object faces the camera.
			Note: Billboard mode is not suitable for VR because the left-right vector of the camera is not horizontal when the screen is attached to your head instead of on the table. See GitHub issue #41567 for details.

billboard_keep_scale.description: If true, the shader will keep the scale set for the mesh. Otherwise, the scale is lost when billboarding. Only applies when billboard_mode is not .

particles_anim_h_frames.description: The number of horizontal frames in the particle sprite sheet. Only enabled when using . See billboard_mode.

particles_anim_v_frames.description: The number of vertical frames in the particle sprite sheet. Only enabled when using . See billboard_mode.

particles_anim_loop.description: If true, particle animations are looped. Only enabled when using . See billboard_mode.

grow.description:
If true, enables the vertex grow setting. This can be used to create mesh-based outlines using a second material pass and its cull_mode set to . See also grow_amount.
			Note: Vertex growth cannot create new vertices, which means that visible gaps may occur in sharp corners. This can be alleviated by designing the mesh to use smooth normals exclusively using face weighted normals in the 3D authoring software. In this case, grow will be able to join every outline together, just like in the original mesh.

grow_amount.description: Grows object vertices in the direction of their normals. Only effective if grow is true.

fixed_size.description: If true, the object is rendered at the same size regardless of distance. The object's size on screen is the same as if the camera was 1.0 units away from the object's origin, regardless of the actual distance from the camera. The 's field of view (or Camera3D.size when in orthogonal/frustum mode) still affects the size the object is drawn at.

use_point_size.description:
If true, render point size can be changed.
			Note: This is only effective for objects whose geometry is point-based rather than triangle-based. See also point_size.

point_size.description: The point size in pixels. See use_point_size.

use_particle_trails.description: If true, enables parts of the shader required for  trails to function. This also requires using a mesh with appropriate skinning, such as  or . Enabling this feature outside of materials used in  meshes will break material rendering.

use_z_clip_scale.description: If true use z_clip_scale to scale the object being rendered towards the camera to avoid clipping into things like walls.

z_clip_scale.description: Scales the object being rendered towards the camera to avoid clipping into things like walls. This is intended to be used for objects that are fixed with respect to the camera like player arms, tools, etc. Lighting and shadows will continue to work correctly when this setting is adjusted, but screen-space effects like SSAO and SSR may break with lower scales. Therefore, try to keep this setting as close to 1.0 as possible.

use_fov_override.description: If true use fov_override to override the 's field of view angle.

fov_override.description:
Overrides the 's field of view angle (in degrees).
			Note: This behaves as if the field of view is set on a  with Camera3D.keep_aspect set to . Additionally, it may not look correct on a non-perspective camera where the field of view setting is ignored.

proximity_fade_enabled.description: If true, the proximity fade effect is enabled. The proximity fade effect fades out each pixel based on its distance to another object.

proximity_fade_distance.description: Distance over which the fade effect takes place. The larger the distance the longer it takes for an object to fade.

msdf_pixel_range.description: The width of the range around the shape between the minimum and maximum representable signed distance.

msdf_outline_size.description: The width of the shape outline.

distance_fade_mode.description: Specifies which type of fade to use. Can be any of the s.

distance_fade_min_distance.description:
Distance at which the object starts to become visible. If the object is less than this distance away, it will be invisible.
			Note: If distance_fade_min_distance is greater than distance_fade_max_distance, the behavior will be reversed. The object will start to fade away at distance_fade_max_distance and will fully disappear once it reaches distance_fade_min_distance.

distance_fade_max_distance.description:
Distance at which the object appears fully opaque.
			Note: If distance_fade_max_distance is less than distance_fade_min_distance, the behavior will be reversed. The object will start to fade away at distance_fade_max_distance and will fully disappear once it reaches distance_fade_min_distance.

stencil_flags.description: The flags dictating how the stencil operation behaves.

stencil_compare.description: The comparison operator to use for stencil masking operations.

stencil_reference.description: The stencil reference value (0-255). Typically a power of 2.

stencil_color.description: The primary color of the stencil effect.

BitMap.description: A two-dimensional array of boolean values, can be used to efficiently store a binary matrix (every matrix element takes only one bit) and query the values using natural cartesian coordinates.

create.description: Creates a bitmap with the specified size, filled with false.

create_from_image_alpha.description: Creates a bitmap that matches the given image dimensions, every element of the bitmap is set to false if the alpha value of the image at that position is equal to threshold or less, and true in other case.

set_bitv.description: Sets the bitmap's element at the specified position, to the specified value.

set_bit.description: Sets the bitmap's element at the specified position, to the specified value.

get_bitv.description: Returns bitmap's value at the specified position.

get_bit.description: Returns bitmap's value at the specified position.

set_bit_rect.description: Sets a rectangular portion of the bitmap to the specified value.

get_true_bit_count.description: Returns the number of bitmap elements that are set to true.

grow_mask.description: Applies morphological dilation or erosion to the bitmap. If pixels is positive, dilation is applied to the bitmap. If pixels is negative, erosion is applied to the bitmap. rect defines the area where the morphological operation is applied. Pixels located outside the rect are unaffected by grow_mask.

convert_to_image.description: Returns an image of the same size as the bitmap and with an  of type . true bits of the bitmap are being converted into white pixels, and false bits into black.

opaque_to_polygons.description:
Creates an  of polygons covering a rectangular portion of the bitmap. It uses a marching squares algorithm, followed by Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP) reduction of the number of vertices. Each polygon is described as a  of its vertices.
				To get polygons covering the whole bitmap, pass:
				
				Rect2(Vector2(), get_size())
				
				epsilon is passed to RDP to control how accurately the polygons cover the bitmap: a lower epsilon corresponds to more points in the polygons.

Bone2D.brief_description: A joint used with  to control and animate other nodes.
Bone2D.description:
A hierarchy of s can be bound to a  to control and animate other  nodes.
		You can use  and  nodes to animate 2D meshes created with the  UV editor.
		Each bone has a rest transform that you can reset to with apply_rest. These rest poses are relative to the bone's parent.
		If in the editor, you can set the rest pose of an entire skeleton using a menu option, from the code, you need to iterate over the bones to set their individual rest poses.

apply_rest.description: Resets the bone to the rest pose. This is equivalent to setting Node2D.transform to rest.

get_skeleton_rest.description: Returns the node's rest  if it doesn't have a parent, or its rest pose relative to its parent.

get_index_in_skeleton.description: Returns the node's index as part of the entire skeleton. See .

set_autocalculate_length_and_angle.description: When set to true, the  node will attempt to automatically calculate the bone angle and length using the first child  node, if one exists. If none exist, the  cannot automatically calculate these values and will print a warning.

get_autocalculate_length_and_angle.description: Returns whether this  is going to autocalculate its length and bone angle using its first  child node, if one exists. If there are no  children, then it cannot autocalculate these values and will print a warning.

set_length.description: Sets the length of the bone in the .

get_length.description: Returns the length of the bone in the  node.

set_bone_angle.description:
Sets the bone angle for the . This is typically set to the rotation from the  to a child  node.
				Note: This is different from the 's rotation. The bone's angle is the rotation of the bone shown by the gizmo, which is unaffected by the 's Node2D.transform.

get_bone_angle.description:
Returns the angle of the bone in the .
				Note: This is different from the 's rotation. The bone's angle is the rotation of the bone shown by the gizmo, which is unaffected by the 's Node2D.transform.

rest.description: Rest transform of the bone. You can reset the node's transforms to this value using apply_rest.

BoneAttachment3D.brief_description: А node that dynamically copies or overrides the 3D transform of a bone in its parent .
BoneAttachment3D.description: This node selects a bone in a  and attaches to it. This means that the  node will either dynamically copy or override the 3D transform of the selected bone.

get_skeleton.description: Returns the parent or external  node if it exists, otherwise returns null.

on_skeleton_update.description: A function that is called automatically when the  is updated. This function is where the  node updates its position so it is correctly bound when it is not set to override the bone pose.

bone_name.description: The name of the attached bone.

bone_idx.description: The index of the attached bone.

override_pose.description:
Whether the  node will override the bone pose of the bone it is attached to. When set to true, the  node can change the pose of the bone. When set to false, the  will always be set to the bone's transform.
			Note: This override performs interruptively in the skeleton update process using signals due to the old design. It may cause unintended behavior when used at the same time with .

use_external_skeleton.description: Whether the  node will use an external  node rather than attempting to use its parent node as the . When set to true, the  node will use the external  node set in external_skeleton.

BoneConstraint3D.brief_description: A node that may modify Skeleton3D's bone with associating the two bones.
BoneConstraint3D.description: Base class of  that modifies the bone set in set_apply_bone based on the transform of the bone retrieved by get_reference_bone.

set_amount.description: Sets the apply amount of the setting at index to amount.

get_amount.description: Returns the apply amount of the setting at index.

set_apply_bone_name.description: Sets the apply bone of the setting at index to bone_name. This bone will be modified.

get_apply_bone_name.description: Returns the apply bone name of the setting at index. This bone will be modified.

set_apply_bone.description: Sets the apply bone of the setting at index to bone. This bone will be modified.

get_apply_bone.description: Returns the apply bone of the setting at index. This bone will be modified.

set_reference_type.description: Sets the reference target type of the setting at index to type. See also .

get_reference_type.description: Returns the reference target type of the setting at index. See also .

set_reference_bone_name.description:
Sets the reference bone of the setting at index to bone_name.
				This bone will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

get_reference_bone_name.description:
Returns the reference bone name of the setting at index.
				This bone will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

set_reference_bone.description:
Sets the reference bone of the setting at index to bone.
				This bone will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

get_reference_bone.description:
Returns the reference bone of the setting at index.
				This bone will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

set_reference_node.description:
Sets the reference node path of the setting at index to node.
				This node will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

get_reference_node.description:
Returns the reference node path of the setting at index.
				This node will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

set_setting_count.description: Sets the number of settings in the modifier.

get_setting_count.description: Returns the number of settings in the modifier.

BoneMap.brief_description: Describes a mapping of bone names for retargeting  into common names defined by a .
BoneMap.description:
This class contains a dictionary that uses a list of bone names in  as key names.
		By assigning the actual  bone name as the key value, it maps the  to the .

get_skeleton_bone_name.description:
Returns a skeleton bone name is mapped to profile_bone_name.
				In the retargeting process, the returned bone name is the bone name of the source skeleton.

set_skeleton_bone_name.description:
Maps a skeleton bone name to profile_bone_name.
				In the retargeting process, the setting bone name is the bone name of the source skeleton.

find_profile_bone_name.description:
Returns a profile bone name having skeleton_bone_name. If not found, an empty  will be returned.
				In the retargeting process, the returned bone name is the bone name of the target skeleton.

profile.description: A  of the mapping target. Key names in the  are synchronized with it.

BoneTwistDisperser3D.brief_description: A node that propagates and disperses the child bone's twist to the parent bones.
BoneTwistDisperser3D.description:
This  allows for smooth twist interpolation between multiple bones by dispersing the end bone's twist to the parents. This only changes the twist without changing the global position of each joint.
		This is useful for smoothly twisting bones in combination with  and IK.
		Note: If an extracted twist is greater than 180 degrees, flipping occurs. This is similar to .

set_root_bone_name.description: Sets the root bone name of the bone chain.

get_root_bone_name.description: Returns the root bone name of the bone chain.

set_root_bone.description: Sets the root bone index of the bone chain.

get_root_bone.description: Returns the root bone index of the bone chain.

set_end_bone_name.description:
Sets the end bone name of the bone chain.
				Note: The end bone must be a child of the root bone.

get_end_bone_name.description: Returns the end bone name of the bone chain.

set_end_bone.description: Sets the end bone index of the bone chain.

get_end_bone.description: Returns the end bone index of the bone chain.

get_reference_bone_name.description:
Returns the reference bone name to extract twist of the setting at index.
				This bone is either the end of the chain or its parent, depending on is_end_bone_extended.

get_reference_bone.description:
Returns the reference bone to extract twist of the setting at index.
				This bone is either the end of the chain or its parent, depending on is_end_bone_extended.

set_extend_end_bone.description:
If enabled is true, the end bone is extended to have a tail.
				If enabled is false, get_reference_bone becomes a parent of the end bone and it uses the vector to the end bone as a twist axis.

is_end_bone_extended.description: Returns true if the end bone is extended to have a tail.

set_end_bone_direction.description: Sets the end bone tail direction of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended is true.

get_end_bone_direction.description: Returns the tail direction of the end bone of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended is true.

set_twist_from_rest.description:
If enabled is true, it extracts the twist amount from the difference between the bone rest and the current bone pose.
				If enabled is false, it extracts the twist amount from the difference between get_twist_from and the current bone pose. See also set_twist_from.

is_twist_from_rest.description: Returns true if extracting the twist amount from the difference between the bone rest and the current bone pose.

set_twist_from.description:
Sets the rotation to an arbitrary state before twisting for the current bone pose to extract the twist when is_twist_from_rest is false.
				In other words, by calling set_twist_from by  of a specific , you can extract only the twists generated by modifiers processed after that but before this .

get_twist_from.description: Returns the rotation to an arbitrary state before twisting for the current bone pose to extract the twist when is_twist_from_rest is false.

set_disperse_mode.description: Sets whether to use automatic amount assignment or to allow manual assignment.

get_disperse_mode.description: Returns whether to use automatic amount assignment or to allow manual assignment.

set_weight_position.description:
Sets the position at which to divide the segment between joints for weight assignment when get_disperse_mode is .
				For example, when weight_position is 0.5, if two bone segments with a length of 1.0 exist between three joints, weights are assigned to each joint from root to end at ratios of 0.5, 1.0, and 0.5. Then amounts become 0.25, 0.75, and 1.0 respectively.

get_weight_position.description: Returns the position at which to divide the segment between joints for weight assignment when get_disperse_mode is .

set_damping_curve.description: Sets the damping curve when get_disperse_mode is .

get_damping_curve.description: Returns the damping curve when get_disperse_mode is .

get_joint_bone_name.description: Returns the bone name at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

get_joint_bone.description: Returns the bone index at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

get_joint_twist_amount.description: Returns the twist amount at joint in the bone chain's joint list when get_disperse_mode is .

set_joint_twist_amount.description: Sets the twist amount at joint in the bone chain's joint list when get_disperse_mode is .

get_joint_count.description: Returns the joint count of the bone chain's joint list.

mutable_bone_axes.description:
If true, the solver retrieves the bone axis from the bone pose every frame.
			If false, the solver retrieves the bone axis from the bone rest and caches it.

BoxContainer.brief_description: A container that arranges its child controls horizontally or vertically.
BoxContainer.description: A container that arranges its child controls horizontally or vertically, rearranging them automatically when their minimum size changes.

add_spacer.description: Adds a  node to the box as a spacer. If begin is true, it will insert the  node in front of all other children.

alignment.description: The alignment of the container's children (must be one of , , or ).

vertical.description:
If true, the  will arrange its children vertically, rather than horizontally.
			Can't be changed when using  and .

BoxMesh.description:
Generate an axis-aligned box .
		The box's UV layout is arranged in a 3×2 layout that allows texturing each face individually. To apply the same texture on all faces, change the material's UV property to Vector3(3, 2, 1). This is equivalent to adding UV *= vec2(3.0, 2.0) in a vertex shader.
		Note: When using a large textured  (e.g. as a floor), you may stumble upon UV jittering issues depending on the camera angle. To solve this, increase subdivide_depth, subdivide_height and subdivide_width until you no longer notice UV jittering.

size.description: The box's width, height and depth.

subdivide_width.description: Number of extra edge loops inserted along the X axis.

subdivide_height.description: Number of extra edge loops inserted along the Y axis.

subdivide_depth.description: Number of extra edge loops inserted along the Z axis.

BoxOccluder3D.brief_description: Cuboid shape for use with occlusion culling in .
BoxOccluder3D.description:
stores a cuboid shape that can be used by the engine's occlusion culling system.
		See 's documentation for instructions on setting up occlusion culling.

size.description: The box's size in 3D units.

BoxShape3D.brief_description: A 3D box shape used for physics collision.
BoxShape3D.description:
A 3D box shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a .
		Performance:  is fast to check collisions against. It is faster than  and , but slower than .

size.description: The box's width, height and depth.

Button.brief_description: A themed button that can contain text and an icon.

text.description: The button's text that will be displayed inside the button's area.

icon.description:
Button's icon, if text is present the icon will be placed before the text.
			To edit margin and spacing of the icon, use  theme property and content_margin_* properties of the used es.

alignment.description: Text alignment policy for the button's text.

text_overrun_behavior.description: Sets the clipping behavior when the text exceeds the node's bounding rectangle.

autowrap_mode.description: If set to something other than , the text gets wrapped inside the node's bounding rectangle.

autowrap_trim_flags.description: Autowrap space trimming flags. See  and  for more info.

clip_text.description: If true, text that is too large to fit the button is clipped horizontally. If false, the button will always be wide enough to hold the text. The text is not vertically clipped, and the button's height is not affected by this property.

icon_alignment.description: Specifies if the icon should be aligned horizontally to the left, right, or center of a button. Uses the same  constants as the text alignment. If centered horizontally and vertically, text will draw on top of the icon.

vertical_icon_alignment.description: Specifies if the icon should be aligned vertically to the top, bottom, or center of a button. Uses the same  constants as the text alignment. If centered horizontally and vertically, text will draw on top of the icon.

expand_icon.description: When enabled, the button's icon will expand/shrink to fit the button's size while keeping its aspect. See also .

language.description: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.

ButtonGroup.brief_description: A group of buttons that doesn't allow more than one button to be pressed at a time.
ButtonGroup.description:
A group of -derived buttons. The buttons in a  are treated like radio buttons: No more than one button can be pressed at a time. Some types of buttons (such as ) may have a special appearance in this state.
		Every member of a  should have BaseButton.toggle_mode set to true.

get_buttons.description: Returns an  of s who have this as their  (see BaseButton.button_group).

allow_unpress.description: If true, it is possible to unpress all buttons in this .

CCDIK3D.brief_description: Rotation based cyclic coordinate descent inverse kinematics solver.
CCDIK3D.description:
is rotation based IK, enabling fast and effective tracking even with large joint rotations. It's especially suitable for chains with limitations, providing smoother and more stable target tracking compared to .
		The resulting twist around the forward vector will always be kept from the previous pose.
		Note: When the target is close to the root, it can cause unnatural movement, including joint flips and oscillations.

CPUParticles2D.description:
CPU-based 2D particle node used to create a variety of particle systems and effects.
		See also , which provides the same functionality with hardware acceleration, but may not run on older devices.

request_particles_process.description:
Requests the particles to process for extra process time during a single frame.
				Useful for particle playback, if used in combination with use_fixed_seed or by calling restart with parameter keep_seed set to true.

restart.description:
Restarts the particle emitter.
				If keep_seed is true, the current random seed will be preserved. Useful for seeking and playback.

set_param_min.description: Sets the minimum value for the given parameter.

get_param_min.description: Returns the minimum value range for the given parameter.

set_param_max.description: Sets the maximum value for the given parameter.

get_param_max.description: Returns the maximum value range for the given parameter.

set_param_curve.description: Sets the  of the parameter specified by . Should be a unit .

get_param_curve.description: Returns the  of the parameter specified by .

set_particle_flag.description: Enables or disables the given particle flag.

get_particle_flag.description: Returns the enabled state of the given particle flag.

convert_from_particles.description: Sets this node's properties to match a given  node with an assigned .

emitting.description: If true, particles are being emitted. emitting can be used to start and stop particles from emitting. However, if one_shot is true setting emitting to true will not restart the emission cycle until after all active particles finish processing. You can use the  signal to be notified once all active particles finish processing.

amount.description: Number of particles emitted in one emission cycle.

texture.description: Particle texture. If null, particles will be squares.

lifetime.description: Amount of time each particle will exist.

one_shot.description: If true, only one emission cycle occurs. If set true during a cycle, emission will stop at the cycle's end.

preprocess.description: Particle system starts as if it had already run for this many seconds.

speed_scale.description: Particle system's running speed scaling ratio. A value of 0 can be used to pause the particles.

explosiveness.description: How rapidly particles in an emission cycle are emitted. If greater than 0, there will be a gap in emissions before the next cycle begins.

use_fixed_seed.description: If true, particles will use the same seed for every simulation using the seed defined in seed. This is useful for situations where the visual outcome should be consistent across replays, for example when using Movie Maker mode.

seed.description: Sets the random seed used by the particle system. Only effective if use_fixed_seed is true.

fixed_fps.description: The particle system's frame rate is fixed to a value. For example, changing the value to 2 will make the particles render at 2 frames per second. Note this does not slow down the simulation of the particle system itself.

fract_delta.description: If true, results in fractional delta calculation which has a smoother particles display effect.

local_coords.description: If true, particles use the parent node's coordinate space (known as local coordinates). This will cause particles to move and rotate along the  node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated. If false, particles use global coordinates; they will not move or rotate along the  node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated.

emission_shape.description: Particles will be emitted inside this region.

emission_sphere_radius.description: The sphere's radius if emission_shape is set to .

emission_rect_extents.description: The rectangle's extents if emission_shape is set to .

emission_points.description: Sets the initial positions to spawn particles when using  or .

emission_normals.description: Sets the direction the particles will be emitted in when using .

emission_colors.description: Sets the s to modulate particles by when using  or .

emission_ring_inner_radius.description: The ring's inner radius if emission_shape is set to .

emission_ring_radius.description: The ring's outer radius if emission_shape is set to .

particle_flag_align_y.description: Align Y axis of particle with the direction of its velocity.

direction.description: Unit vector specifying the particles' emission direction.

spread.description: Each particle's initial direction range from +spread to -spread degrees.

initial_velocity_max.description: Maximum initial velocity magnitude for each particle. Direction comes from direction and spread.

angular_velocity_max.description: Maximum initial angular velocity (rotation speed) applied to each particle in degrees per second.

angular_velocity_curve.description: Each particle's angular velocity will vary along this . Should be a unit .

orbit_velocity_max.description: Maximum orbital velocity applied to each particle. Makes the particles circle around origin. Specified in number of full rotations around origin per second.

orbit_velocity_curve.description: Each particle's orbital velocity will vary along this . Should be a unit .

linear_accel_max.description: Maximum linear acceleration applied to each particle in the direction of motion.

linear_accel_curve.description: Each particle's linear acceleration will vary along this . Should be a unit .

radial_accel_max.description: Maximum radial acceleration applied to each particle. Makes particle accelerate away from the origin or towards it if negative.

radial_accel_curve.description: Each particle's radial acceleration will vary along this . Should be a unit .

tangential_accel_max.description: Maximum tangential acceleration applied to each particle. Tangential acceleration is perpendicular to the particle's velocity giving the particles a swirling motion.

tangential_accel_curve.description: Each particle's tangential acceleration will vary along this . Should be a unit .

damping_max.description: The maximum rate at which particles lose velocity. For example value of 100 means that the particle will go from 100 velocity to 0 in 1 second.

damping_curve.description: Damping will vary along this . Should be a unit .

angle_max.description: Maximum initial rotation applied to each particle, in degrees.

angle_curve.description: Each particle's rotation will be animated along this . Should be a unit .

scale_amount_max.description: Maximum initial scale applied to each particle.

scale_amount_curve.description: Each particle's scale will vary along this . Should be a unit .

split_scale.description: If true, the scale curve will be split into x and y components. See scale_curve_x and scale_curve_y.

scale_curve_x.description:
Each particle's horizontal scale will vary along this . Should be a unit .
			split_scale must be enabled.

scale_curve_y.description:
Each particle's vertical scale will vary along this . Should be a unit .
			split_scale must be enabled.

color.description: Each particle's initial color. If texture is defined, it will be multiplied by this color.

color_ramp.description: Each particle's color will vary along this  over its lifetime (multiplied with color).

color_initial_ramp.description: Each particle's initial color will vary along this  (multiplied with color).

hue_variation_max.description: Maximum initial hue variation applied to each particle. It will shift the particle color's hue.

hue_variation_curve.description: Each particle's hue will vary along this . Should be a unit .

anim_speed_max.description:
Maximum particle animation speed. Animation speed of 1 means that the particles will make full 0 to 1 offset cycle during lifetime, 2 means 2 cycles etc.
			With animation speed greater than 1, remember to enable CanvasItemMaterial.particles_anim_loop property if you want the animation to repeat.

anim_speed_curve.description: Each particle's animation speed will vary along this . Should be a unit .

anim_offset_max.description: Maximum animation offset that corresponds to frame index in the texture. 0 is the first frame, 1 is the last one. See CanvasItemMaterial.particles_animation.

anim_offset_curve.description: Each particle's animation offset will vary along this . Should be a unit .

CPUParticles3D.description:
CPU-based 3D particle node used to create a variety of particle systems and effects.
		See also , which provides the same functionality with hardware acceleration, but may not run on older devices.

restart.description:
Restarts the particle emitter.
				If keep_seed is true, the current random seed will be preserved. Useful for seeking and playback.

request_particles_process.description:
Requests the particles to process for extra process time during a single frame.
				Useful for particle playback, if used in combination with use_fixed_seed or by calling restart with parameter keep_seed set to true.

capture_aabb.description: Returns the axis-aligned bounding box that contains all the particles that are active in the current frame.

set_param_min.description: Sets the minimum value for the given parameter.

get_param_min.description: Returns the minimum value range for the given parameter.

set_param_max.description: Sets the maximum value for the given parameter.

get_param_max.description: Returns the maximum value range for the given parameter.

set_param_curve.description: Sets the  of the parameter specified by . Should be a unit .

get_param_curve.description: Returns the  of the parameter specified by .

set_particle_flag.description: Enables or disables the given particle flag.

get_particle_flag.description: Returns the enabled state of the given particle flag.

convert_from_particles.description: Sets this node's properties to match a given  node with an assigned .

emitting.description: If true, particles are being emitted. emitting can be used to start and stop particles from emitting. However, if one_shot is true setting emitting to true will not restart the emission cycle until after all active particles finish processing. You can use the  signal to be notified once all active particles finish processing.

amount.description: Number of particles emitted in one emission cycle.

lifetime.description: Amount of time each particle will exist.

one_shot.description: If true, only one emission cycle occurs. If set true during a cycle, emission will stop at the cycle's end.

preprocess.description: Particle system starts as if it had already run for this many seconds.

speed_scale.description: Particle system's running speed scaling ratio. A value of 0 can be used to pause the particles.

explosiveness.description: How rapidly particles in an emission cycle are emitted. If greater than 0, there will be a gap in emissions before the next cycle begins.

use_fixed_seed.description: If true, particles will use the same seed for every simulation using the seed defined in seed. This is useful for situations where the visual outcome should be consistent across replays, for example when using Movie Maker mode.

seed.description: Sets the random seed used by the particle system. Only effective if use_fixed_seed is true.

fixed_fps.description: The particle system's frame rate is fixed to a value. For example, changing the value to 2 will make the particles render at 2 frames per second. Note this does not slow down the particle system itself.

fract_delta.description: If true, results in fractional delta calculation which has a smoother particles display effect.

visibility_aabb.description:
The  that determines the node's region which needs to be visible on screen for the particle system to be active.
			Grow the box if particles suddenly appear/disappear when the node enters/exits the screen. The  can be grown via code or with the Particles → Generate AABB editor tool.

local_coords.description: If true, particles use the parent node's coordinate space (known as local coordinates). This will cause particles to move and rotate along the  node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated. If false, particles use global coordinates; they will not move or rotate along the  node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated.

mesh.description: The  used for each particle. If null, particles will be spheres.

emission_shape.description: Particles will be emitted inside this region.

emission_sphere_radius.description: The sphere's radius if  is set to .

emission_box_extents.description: The rectangle's extents if emission_shape is set to .

emission_points.description: Sets the initial positions to spawn particles when using  or .

emission_normals.description: Sets the direction the particles will be emitted in when using .

emission_colors.description:
Sets the s to modulate particles by when using  or .
			Note: emission_colors multiplies the particle mesh's vertex colors. To have a visible effect on a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALBEDO *= COLOR.rgb; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function. Otherwise, emission_colors will have no visible effect.

emission_ring_axis.description: The axis of the ring when using the emitter .

emission_ring_height.description: The height of the ring when using the emitter .

emission_ring_radius.description: The radius of the ring when using the emitter .

emission_ring_inner_radius.description: The inner radius of the ring when using the emitter .

emission_ring_cone_angle.description:
The angle of the cone when using the emitter . The default angle of 90 degrees results in a ring, while an angle of 0 degrees results in a cone. Intermediate values will result in a ring where one end is larger than the other.
			Note: Depending on emission_ring_height, the angle may be clamped if the ring's end is reached to form a perfect cone.

particle_flag_align_y.description: Align Y axis of particle with the direction of its velocity.

particle_flag_rotate_y.description: If true, particles rotate around Y axis by angle_min.

particle_flag_disable_z.description: If true, particles will not move on the Z axis.

direction.description: Unit vector specifying the particles' emission direction.

spread.description: Each particle's initial direction range from +spread to -spread degrees. Applied to X/Z plane and Y/Z planes.

flatness.description: Amount of spread in Y/Z plane. A value of 1 restricts particles to X/Z plane.

initial_velocity_min.description: Minimum value of the initial velocity.

initial_velocity_max.description: Maximum value of the initial velocity.

angular_velocity_min.description: Minimum initial angular velocity (rotation speed) applied to each particle in degrees per second.

angular_velocity_max.description: Maximum initial angular velocity (rotation speed) applied to each particle in degrees per second.

angular_velocity_curve.description: Each particle's angular velocity (rotation speed) will vary along this  over its lifetime. Should be a unit .

orbit_velocity_curve.description: Each particle's orbital velocity will vary along this . Should be a unit .

linear_accel_curve.description: Each particle's linear acceleration will vary along this . Should be a unit .

radial_accel_curve.description: Each particle's radial acceleration will vary along this . Should be a unit .

tangential_accel_curve.description: Each particle's tangential acceleration will vary along this . Should be a unit .

damping_curve.description: Damping will vary along this . Should be a unit .

angle_curve.description: Each particle's rotation will be animated along this . Should be a unit .

scale_amount_curve.description: Each particle's scale will vary along this . Should be a unit .

split_scale.description: If set to true, three different scale curves can be specified, one per scale axis.

scale_curve_x.description: Curve for the scale over life, along the x axis.

scale_curve_y.description: Curve for the scale over life, along the y axis.

scale_curve_z.description: Curve for the scale over life, along the z axis.

color.description:
Each particle's initial color.
			Note: color multiplies the particle mesh's vertex colors. To have a visible effect on a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALBEDO *= COLOR.rgb; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function. Otherwise, color will have no visible effect.

color_ramp.description:
Each particle's color will vary along this  over its lifetime (multiplied with color).
			Note: color_ramp multiplies the particle mesh's vertex colors. To have a visible effect on a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALBEDO *= COLOR.rgb; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function. Otherwise, color_ramp will have no visible effect.

color_initial_ramp.description:
Each particle's initial color will vary along this  (multiplied with color).
			Note: color_initial_ramp multiplies the particle mesh's vertex colors. To have a visible effect on a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALBEDO *= COLOR.rgb; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function. Otherwise, color_initial_ramp will have no visible effect.

hue_variation_curve.description: Each particle's hue will vary along this . Should be a unit .

anim_speed_curve.description: Each particle's animation speed will vary along this . Should be a unit .

anim_offset_curve.description: Each particle's animation offset will vary along this . Should be a unit .

CallbackTweener.brief_description: Calls the specified method after optional delay.
CallbackTweener.description:
is used to call a method in a tweening sequence. See Tween.tween_callback for more usage information.
		The tweener will finish automatically if the callback's target object is freed.
		Note: Tween.tween_callback is the only correct way to create . Any  created manually will not function correctly.

set_delay.description:
Makes the callback call delayed by given time in seconds.
				Example: Call Node.queue_free after 2 seconds:
				
				var tween = get_tree().create_tween()
				tween.tween_callback(queue_free).set_delay(2)

Camera2D.description:
Camera node for 2D scenes. It forces the screen (current layer) to scroll following this node. This makes it easier (and faster) to program scrollable scenes than manually changing the position of -based nodes.
		Cameras register themselves in the nearest  node (when ascending the tree). Only one camera can be active per viewport. If no viewport is available ascending the tree, the camera will register in the global viewport.
		This node is intended to be a simple helper to get things going quickly, but more functionality may be desired to change how the camera works. To make your own custom camera node, inherit it from  and change the transform of the canvas by setting Viewport.canvas_transform in  (you can obtain the current  by using Node.get_viewport).
		Note that the  node's Node2D.global_position doesn't represent the actual position of the screen, which may differ due to applied smoothing or limits. You can use get_screen_center_position to get the real position. Same for the node's Node2D.global_rotation which may be different due to applied rotation smoothing. You can use get_screen_rotation to get the current rotation of the screen.

make_current.description: Forces this  to become the current active one. enabled must be true.

is_current.description: Returns true if this  is the active camera (see Viewport.get_camera_2d).

set_limit.description: Sets the camera limit for the specified . See also limit_bottom, limit_top, limit_left, and limit_right.

get_limit.description: Returns the camera limit for the specified . See also limit_bottom, limit_top, limit_left, and limit_right.

set_drag_margin.description: Sets the specified 's margin. See also drag_bottom_margin, drag_top_margin, drag_left_margin, and drag_right_margin.

get_drag_margin.description: Returns the specified 's margin. See also drag_bottom_margin, drag_top_margin, drag_left_margin, and drag_right_margin.

get_target_position.description:
Returns this camera's target position, in global coordinates.
				Note: The returned value is not the same as Node2D.global_position, as it is affected by the drag properties. It is also not the same as the current position if position_smoothing_enabled is true (see get_screen_center_position).

get_screen_center_position.description:
Returns the center of the screen from this camera's point of view, in global coordinates.
				Note: The exact targeted position of the camera may be different. See get_target_position.

get_screen_rotation.description:
Returns the current screen rotation from this camera's point of view.
				Note: The screen rotation can be different from Node2D.global_rotation if the camera is rotating smoothly due to rotation_smoothing_enabled.

force_update_scroll.description: Forces the camera to update scroll immediately.

reset_smoothing.description:
Sets the camera's position immediately to its current smoothing destination.
				This method has no effect if position_smoothing_enabled is false.

align.description:
Aligns the camera to the tracked node.
				Note: Calling force_update_scroll after this method is not required.

offset.description: The camera's relative offset. Useful for looking around or camera shake animations. The offsetted camera can go past the limits defined in limit_top, limit_bottom, limit_left and limit_right.

ignore_rotation.description: If true, the camera's rendered view is not affected by its Node2D.rotation and Node2D.global_rotation.

enabled.description:
Controls whether the camera can be active or not. If true, the  will become the main camera when it enters the scene tree and there is no active camera currently (see Viewport.get_camera_2d).
			When the camera is currently active and enabled is set to false, the next enabled  in the scene tree will become active.

zoom.description:
The camera's zoom. Higher values are more zoomed in. For example, a zoom of Vector2(2.0, 2.0) will be twice as zoomed in on each axis (the view covers an area four times smaller). In contrast, a zoom of Vector2(0.5, 0.5) will be twice as zoomed out on each axis (the view covers an area four times larger). The X and Y components should generally always be set to the same value, unless you wish to stretch the camera view.
			Note: FontFile.oversampling does not take  zoom into account. This means that zooming in/out will cause bitmap fonts and rasterized (non-MSDF) dynamic fonts to appear blurry or pixelated unless the font is part of a  that makes it ignore camera zoom. To ensure text remains crisp regardless of zoom, you can enable MSDF font rendering by enabling ProjectSettings.gui/theme/default_font_multichannel_signed_distance_field (applies to the default project font only), or enabling Multichannel Signed Distance Field in the import options of a DynamicFont for custom fonts. On system fonts, SystemFont.multichannel_signed_distance_field can be enabled in the inspector.

custom_viewport.description: The custom  node attached to the . If null or not a , uses the default viewport instead.

limit_enabled.description: If true, the limits will be enabled. Disabling this will allow the camera to focus anywhere, when the four limit_* properties will not work.

limit_left.description: Left scroll limit in pixels. The camera stops moving when reaching this value, but offset can push the view past the limit.

limit_top.description: Top scroll limit in pixels. The camera stops moving when reaching this value, but offset can push the view past the limit.

limit_right.description: Right scroll limit in pixels. The camera stops moving when reaching this value, but offset can push the view past the limit.

limit_bottom.description: Bottom scroll limit in pixels. The camera stops moving when reaching this value, but offset can push the view past the limit.

limit_smoothed.description:
If true, the camera smoothly stops when reaches its limits.
			This property has no effect if position_smoothing_enabled is false.
			Note: To immediately update the camera's position to be within limits without smoothing, even with this setting enabled, invoke reset_smoothing.

position_smoothing_enabled.description: If true, the camera's view smoothly moves towards its target position at position_smoothing_speed.

position_smoothing_speed.description: Speed in pixels per second of the camera's smoothing effect when position_smoothing_enabled is true.

rotation_smoothing_enabled.description:
If true, the camera's view smoothly rotates, via asymptotic smoothing, to align with its target rotation at rotation_smoothing_speed.
			Note: This property has no effect if ignore_rotation is true.

rotation_smoothing_speed.description: The angular, asymptotic speed of the camera's rotation smoothing effect when rotation_smoothing_enabled is true.

drag_horizontal_enabled.description: If true, the camera only moves when reaching the horizontal (left and right) drag margins. If false, the camera moves horizontally regardless of margins.

drag_vertical_enabled.description: If true, the camera only moves when reaching the vertical (top and bottom) drag margins. If false, the camera moves vertically regardless of the drag margins.

drag_horizontal_offset.description:
The relative horizontal drag offset of the camera between the right (-1) and left (1) drag margins.
			Note: Used to set the initial horizontal drag offset; determine the current offset; or force the current offset. It's not automatically updated when drag_horizontal_enabled is true or the drag margins are changed.

drag_vertical_offset.description:
The relative vertical drag offset of the camera between the bottom (-1) and top (1) drag margins.
			Note: Used to set the initial vertical drag offset; determine the current offset; or force the current offset. It's not automatically updated when drag_vertical_enabled is true or the drag margins are changed.

drag_left_margin.description: Left margin needed to drag the camera. A value of 1 makes the camera move only when reaching the left edge of the screen.

drag_top_margin.description: Top margin needed to drag the camera. A value of 1 makes the camera move only when reaching the top edge of the screen.

drag_right_margin.description: Right margin needed to drag the camera. A value of 1 makes the camera move only when reaching the right edge of the screen.

drag_bottom_margin.description: Bottom margin needed to drag the camera. A value of 1 makes the camera move only when reaching the bottom edge of the screen.

editor_draw_screen.description: If true, draws the camera's screen rectangle in the editor.

editor_draw_limits.description: If true, draws the camera's limits rectangle in the editor.

editor_draw_drag_margin.description: If true, draws the camera's drag margin rectangle in the editor.

Camera3D.brief_description: Camera node, displays from a point of view.
Camera3D.description: is a special node that displays what is visible from its current location. Cameras register themselves in the nearest  node (when ascending the tree). Only one camera can be active per viewport. If no viewport is available ascending the tree, the camera will register in the global viewport. In other words, a camera just provides 3D display capabilities to a , and, without one, a scene registered in that  (or higher viewports) can't be displayed.

project_ray_normal.description: Returns a normal vector in world space, that is the result of projecting a point on the  rectangle by the inverse camera projection. This is useful for casting rays in the form of (origin, normal) for object intersection or picking.

project_local_ray_normal.description: Returns a normal vector from the screen point location directed along the camera. Orthogonal cameras are normalized. Perspective cameras account for perspective, screen width/height, etc.

project_ray_origin.description: Returns a 3D position in world space, that is the result of projecting a point on the  rectangle by the inverse camera projection. This is useful for casting rays in the form of (origin, normal) for object intersection or picking.

unproject_position.description:
Returns the 2D coordinate in the  rectangle that maps to the given 3D point in world space.
				Note: When using this to position GUI elements over a 3D viewport, use is_position_behind to prevent them from appearing if the 3D point is behind the camera:
				
				# This code block is part of a script that inherits from Node3D.
				# `control` is a reference to a node inheriting from Control.
				control.visible = not get_viewport().get_camera_3d().is_position_behind(global_transform.origin)
				control.position = get_viewport().get_camera_3d().unproject_position(global_transform.origin)

is_position_behind.description:
Returns true if the given position is behind the camera (the blue part of the linked diagram). See this diagram for an overview of position query methods.
				Note: A position which returns false may still be outside the camera's field of view.

project_position.description: Returns the 3D point in world space that maps to the given 2D coordinate in the  rectangle on a plane that is the given z_depth distance into the scene away from the camera.

set_perspective.description: Sets the camera projection to perspective mode (see ), by specifying a fov (field of view) angle in degrees, and the z_near and z_far clip planes in world space units.

set_orthogonal.description:
Sets the camera projection to orthogonal mode (see ), by specifying a size, and the z_near and z_far clip planes in world space units.
				As a hint, 3D games that look 2D often use this projection, with size specified in pixels.

set_frustum.description: Sets the camera projection to frustum mode (see ), by specifying a size, an offset, and the z_near and z_far clip planes in world space units. See also frustum_offset.

make_current.description: Makes this camera the current camera for the  (see class description). If the camera node is outside the scene tree, it will attempt to become current once it's added.

clear_current.description: If this is the current camera, remove it from being current. If enable_next is true, request to make the next camera current, if any.

get_camera_transform.description: Returns the transform of the camera plus the vertical (v_offset) and horizontal (h_offset) offsets; and any other adjustments made to the position and orientation of the camera by subclassed cameras such as .

get_camera_projection.description: Returns the projection matrix that this camera uses to render to its associated viewport. The camera must be part of the scene tree to function.

get_frustum.description: Returns the camera's frustum planes in world space units as an array of s in the following order: near, far, left, top, right, bottom. Not to be confused with frustum_offset.

is_position_in_frustum.description: Returns true if the given position is inside the camera's frustum (the green part of the linked diagram). See this diagram for an overview of position query methods.

get_camera_rid.description: Returns the camera's RID from the .

get_pyramid_shape_rid.description: Returns the RID of a pyramid shape encompassing the camera's view frustum, ignoring the camera's near plane. The tip of the pyramid represents the position of the camera.

set_cull_mask_value.description: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the cull_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 20.

get_cull_mask_value.description: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the cull_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 20.

keep_aspect.description: The axis to lock during fov/size adjustments. Can be either  or .

cull_mask.description:
The culling mask that describes which VisualInstance3D.layers are rendered by this camera. By default, all 20 user-visible layers are rendered.
			Note: Since the cull_mask allows for 32 layers to be stored in total, there are an additional 12 layers that are only used internally by the engine and aren't exposed in the editor. Setting cull_mask using a script allows you to toggle those reserved layers, which can be useful for editor plugins.
			To adjust cull_mask more easily using a script, use get_cull_mask_value and set_cull_mask_value.
			Note: , SDFGI and  will always take all layers into account to determine what contributes to global illumination. If this is an issue, set GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode to  for meshes and Light3D.light_bake_mode to  for lights to exclude them from global illumination.

environment.description: The  to use for this camera.

attributes.description: The  to use for this camera.

compositor.description: The  to use for this camera.

h_offset.description: The horizontal (X) offset of the camera viewport.

v_offset.description: The vertical (Y) offset of the camera viewport.

doppler_tracking.description:
If not , this camera will simulate the Doppler effect for objects changed in particular _process methods.
			Note: The Doppler effect will only be heard on s if AudioStreamPlayer3D.doppler_tracking is not set to .

projection.description: The camera's projection mode. In  mode, objects' Z distance from the camera's local space scales their perceived size.

current.description:
If true, the ancestor  is currently using this camera.
			If multiple cameras are in the scene, one will always be made current. For example, if two  nodes are present in the scene and only one is current, setting one camera's current to false will cause the other camera to be made current.

fov.description:
The camera's field of view angle (in degrees). Only applicable in perspective mode. Since keep_aspect locks one axis, fov sets the other axis' field of view angle.
			For reference, the default vertical field of view value (75.0) is equivalent to a horizontal FOV of:
			- ~91.31 degrees in a 4:3 viewport
			- ~101.67 degrees in a 16:10 viewport
			- ~107.51 degrees in a 16:9 viewport
			- ~121.63 degrees in a 21:9 viewport

size.description: The camera's size in meters measured as the diameter of the width or height, depending on keep_aspect. Only applicable in orthogonal and frustum modes.

frustum_offset.description:
The camera's frustum offset. This can be changed from the default to create "tilted frustum" effects such as Y-shearing.
			Note: Only effective if projection is .

near.description: The distance to the near culling boundary for this camera relative to its local Z axis. Lower values allow the camera to see objects more up close to its origin, at the cost of lower precision across the entire range. Values lower than the default can lead to increased Z-fighting.

far.description: The distance to the far culling boundary for this camera relative to its local Z axis. Higher values allow the camera to see further away, while decreasing far can improve performance if it results in objects being partially or fully culled.

CameraAttributes.description:
Controls camera-specific attributes such as depth of field and exposure override.
		When used in a  it provides default settings for exposure, auto-exposure, and depth of field that will be used by all cameras without their own , including the editor camera. When used in a  it will override any  set in the . When used in  or , only the exposure settings will be used.
		See also  for general 3D environment settings.
		This is a pure virtual class that is inherited by  and .

exposure_sensitivity.description:
Sensitivity of camera sensors, measured in ISO. A higher sensitivity results in a brighter image.
			If auto_exposure_enabled is true, this can be used as a method of exposure compensation, doubling the value will increase the exposure value (measured in EV100) by 1 stop.
			Note: Only available when ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units is enabled.

exposure_multiplier.description: Multiplier for the exposure amount. A higher value results in a brighter image.

auto_exposure_enabled.description: If true, enables the tonemapping auto exposure mode of the scene renderer. If true, the renderer will automatically determine the exposure setting to adapt to the scene's illumination and the observed light.

auto_exposure_scale.description: The scale of the auto exposure effect. Affects the intensity of auto exposure.

auto_exposure_speed.description: The speed of the auto exposure effect. Affects the time needed for the camera to perform auto exposure.

CameraAttributesPhysical.description:
is used to set rendering settings based on a physically-based camera's settings. It is responsible for exposure, auto-exposure, and depth of field.
		When used in a  it provides default settings for exposure, auto-exposure, and depth of field that will be used by all cameras without their own , including the editor camera. When used in a  it will override any  set in the  and will override the s Camera3D.far, Camera3D.near, Camera3D.fov, and Camera3D.keep_aspect properties. When used in  or , only the exposure settings will be used.
		The default settings are intended for use in an outdoor environment, tips for settings for use in an indoor environment can be found in each setting's documentation.
		Note: Depth of field blur is only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility.

get_fov.description: Returns the vertical field of view that corresponds to the frustum_focal_length. This value is calculated internally whenever frustum_focal_length is changed.

frustum_focus_distance.description: Distance from camera of object that will be in focus, measured in meters. Internally this will be clamped to be at least 1 millimeter larger than frustum_focal_length.

frustum_focal_length.description: Distance between camera lens and camera aperture, measured in millimeters. Controls field of view and depth of field. A larger focal length will result in a smaller field of view and a narrower depth of field meaning fewer objects will be in focus. A smaller focal length will result in a wider field of view and a larger depth of field meaning more objects will be in focus.
