				Note: On macOS, returned value is inaccurate if fractional display scaling mode is used.
				Note: On Android devices, the actual screen densities are grouped into six generalized densities:
				
				   ldpi - 120 dpi
				   mdpi - 160 dpi
				   hdpi - 240 dpi
				  xhdpi - 320 dpi
				 xxhdpi - 480 dpi
				xxxhdpi - 640 dpi
				
				Note: This method is implemented on Android, iOS, Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS, Web, and Windows. On other platforms, this method always returns 72.

screen_get_scale.description:
Returns the scale factor of the specified screen by index. Returns 1.0 if screen is invalid.
				Note: One of the following constants can be used as screen: , , , or .
				Note: On macOS, the returned value is 2.0 for hiDPI (Retina) screens, and 1.0 for all other cases.
				Note: On Linux (Wayland), the returned value is accurate only when screen is . Due to API limitations, passing a direct index will return a rounded-up integer, if the screen has a fractional scale (e.g. 1.25 would get rounded up to 2.0).
				Note: This method is implemented on Android, iOS, Web, macOS, and Linux (Wayland). On other platforms, this method always returns 1.0.

is_touchscreen_available.description: Returns true if touch events are available (Android or iOS), the capability is detected on the Web platform or if ProjectSettings.input_devices/pointing/emulate_touch_from_mouse is true.

screen_get_max_scale.description:
Returns the greatest scale factor of all screens.
				Note: On macOS returned value is 2.0 if there is at least one hiDPI (Retina) screen in the system, and 1.0 in all other cases.
				Note: This method is implemented only on macOS.

screen_get_refresh_rate.description:
Returns the current refresh rate of the specified screen. When V-Sync is enabled, this returns the maximum framerate the project can effectively reach. Returns -1.0 if screen is invalid or the  fails to find the refresh rate for the specified screen.
				To fallback to a default refresh rate if the method fails, try:
				
				var refresh_rate = DisplayServer.screen_get_refresh_rate()
				if refresh_rate < 0:
					refresh_rate = 60.0
				
				Note: One of the following constants can be used as screen: , , , or .
				Note: This method is implemented on Android, iOS, macOS, Linux (X11 and Wayland), and Windows. On other platforms, this method always returns -1.0.

screen_get_pixel.description:
Returns the color of the pixel at the given screen position. On multi-monitor setups, the screen position is relative to the virtual desktop area.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11, excluding XWayland), macOS, and Windows. On other platforms, this method always returns Color(0, 0, 0, 1).
				Note: On macOS, this method requires the "Screen Recording" permission. If permission is not granted, this method returns a color from a screenshot that will not include other application windows or OS elements not related to the application.

screen_get_image.description:
Returns a screenshot of the screen. Returns null if screen is invalid or the  fails to capture screenshot.
				Note: One of the following constants can be used as screen: , , , or .
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11, excluding XWayland), macOS, and Windows. On other platforms, this method always returns null.
				Note: On macOS, this method requires the "Screen Recording" permission. If permission is not granted, this method returns a screenshot that will not include other application windows or OS elements not related to the application.

screen_get_image_rect.description:
Returns a screenshot of the screen region defined by rect. Returns null if rect is outside screen bounds or the  fails to capture screenshot.
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS and Windows. On other platforms, this method always returns null.
				Note: On macOS, this method requires the "Screen Recording" permission. If permission is not granted, this method returns a screenshot that will not include other application windows or OS elements not related to the application.

screen_set_orientation.description:
Sets the screen's orientation. See also screen_get_orientation.
				Note: One of the following constants can be used as screen: , , , or .
				Note: This method is implemented on Android and iOS.
				Note: On iOS, this method has no effect if ProjectSettings.display/window/handheld/orientation is not set to .

screen_get_orientation.description:
Returns the screen's current orientation. See also screen_set_orientation. Returns  if screen is invalid.
				Note: One of the following constants can be used as screen: , , , or .
				Note: This method is implemented on Android and iOS. On other platforms, this method always returns .

screen_set_keep_on.description: Sets whether the screen should never be turned off by the operating system's power-saving measures. See also screen_is_kept_on.

screen_is_kept_on.description: Returns true if the screen should never be turned off by the operating system's power-saving measures. See also screen_set_keep_on.

get_window_list.description:
Returns the list of Godot window IDs belonging to this process.
				Note: Native dialogs are not included in this list.

get_window_at_screen_position.description:
Returns the ID of the window at the specified screen position (in pixels). On multi-monitor setups, the screen position is relative to the virtual desktop area. On multi-monitor setups with different screen resolutions or orientations, the origin may be located outside any display like this:
				
				* (0, 0)        +-------+
				                |       |
				+-------------+ |       |
				|             | |       |
				|             | |       |
				+-------------+ +-------+

window_get_native_handle.description:
Returns internal structure pointers for use in plugins.
				Note: This method is implemented on Android, Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS, and Windows.

window_get_active_popup.description: Returns ID of the active popup window, or  if there is none.

window_set_popup_safe_rect.description: Sets the bounding box of control, or menu item that was used to open the popup window, in the screen coordinate system. Clicking this area will not auto-close this popup.

window_get_popup_safe_rect.description: Returns the bounding box of control, or menu item that was used to open the popup window, in the screen coordinate system.

window_set_title.description:
Sets the title of the given window to title.
				Note: It's recommended to change this value using Window.title instead.
				Note: Avoid changing the window title every frame, as this can cause performance issues on certain window managers. Try to change the window title only a few times per second at most.

window_get_title_size.description:
Returns the estimated window title bar size (including text and window buttons) for the window specified by window_id (in pixels). This method does not change the window title.
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS and Windows.

window_get_current_screen.description:
Returns the screen the window specified by window_id is currently positioned on. If the screen overlaps multiple displays, the screen where the window's center is located is returned. See also window_set_current_screen. Returns  if window_id is invalid.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux/X11, macOS, and Windows. On other platforms, this method always returns 0.

window_set_current_screen.description:
Moves the window specified by window_id to the specified screen. See also window_get_current_screen.
				Note: One of the following constants can be used as screen: , , , or .
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux/X11, macOS, and Windows.

window_get_position.description: Returns the position of the client area of the given window on the screen.

window_get_position_with_decorations.description: Returns the position of the given window on the screen including the borders drawn by the operating system. See also window_get_position.

window_set_position.description:
Sets the position of the given window to position. On multi-monitor setups, the screen position is relative to the virtual desktop area. On multi-monitor setups with different screen resolutions or orientations, the origin may be located outside any display like this:
				
				* (0, 0)        +-------+
				                |       |
				+-------------+ |       |
				|             | |       |
				|             | |       |
				+-------------+ +-------+
				
				See also window_get_position and window_set_size.
				Note: It's recommended to change this value using Window.position instead.
				Note: On Linux (Wayland): this method is a no-op.

window_get_size.description: Returns the size of the window specified by window_id (in pixels), excluding the borders drawn by the operating system. This is also called the "client area". See also window_get_size_with_decorations, window_set_size and window_get_position.

window_set_size.description:
Sets the size of the given window to size (in pixels). See also window_get_size and window_get_position.
				Note: It's recommended to change this value using Window.size instead.

window_set_rect_changed_callback.description:
Sets the callback that will be called when the window specified by window_id is moved or resized.
				Warning: Advanced users only! Adding such a callback to a  node will override its default implementation, which can introduce bugs.

window_set_window_event_callback.description:
Sets the callback that will be called when an event occurs in the window specified by window_id.
				Warning: Advanced users only! Adding such a callback to a  node will override its default implementation, which can introduce bugs.

window_set_input_event_callback.description:
Sets the callback that should be called when any  is sent to the window specified by window_id.
				Warning: Advanced users only! Adding such a callback to a  node will override its default implementation, which can introduce bugs.

window_set_input_text_callback.description:
Sets the callback that should be called when text is entered using the virtual keyboard to the window specified by window_id.
				Warning: Advanced users only! Adding such a callback to a  node will override its default implementation, which can introduce bugs.

window_set_drop_files_callback.description:
Sets the callback that should be called when files are dropped from the operating system's file manager to the window specified by window_id. callback should take one  argument, which is the list of dropped files.
				Warning: Advanced users only! Adding such a callback to a  node will override its default implementation, which can introduce bugs.
				Note: This method is implemented on Windows, macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland), and Web.

window_get_attached_instance_id.description: Returns the Object.get_instance_id of the  the window_id is attached to.

window_get_max_size.description: Returns the window's maximum size (in pixels). See also window_set_max_size.

window_set_max_size.description:
Sets the maximum size of the window specified by window_id in pixels. Normally, the user will not be able to drag the window to make it larger than the specified size. See also window_get_max_size.
				Note: It's recommended to change this value using Window.max_size instead.
				Note: Using third-party tools, it is possible for users to disable window geometry restrictions and therefore bypass this limit.

window_get_min_size.description: Returns the window's minimum size (in pixels). See also window_set_min_size.

window_set_min_size.description:
Sets the minimum size for the given window to min_size in pixels. Normally, the user will not be able to drag the window to make it smaller than the specified size. See also window_get_min_size.
				Note: It's recommended to change this value using Window.min_size instead.
				Note: By default, the main window has a minimum size of Vector2i(64, 64). This prevents issues that can arise when the window is resized to a near-zero size.
				Note: Using third-party tools, it is possible for users to disable window geometry restrictions and therefore bypass this limit.

window_get_size_with_decorations.description: Returns the size of the window specified by window_id (in pixels), including the borders drawn by the operating system. See also window_get_size.

window_get_mode.description: Returns the mode of the given window.

window_set_mode.description:
Sets window mode for the given window to mode.
				Note: On Android, setting it to  or  will enable immersive mode.
				Note: Setting the window to full screen forcibly sets the borderless flag to true, so make sure to set it back to false when not wanted.

window_set_flag.description: Enables or disables the given window's given flag.

window_get_flag.description: Returns the current value of the given window's flag.

window_set_window_buttons_offset.description:
When  flag is set, set offset to the center of the first titlebar button.
				Note: This flag is implemented only on macOS.

window_get_safe_title_margins.description: Returns left margins (x), right margins (y) and height (z) of the title that are safe to use (contains no buttons or other elements) when  flag is set.

window_request_attention.description: Makes the window specified by window_id request attention, which is materialized by the window title and taskbar entry blinking until the window is focused. This usually has no visible effect if the window is currently focused. The exact behavior varies depending on the operating system.

window_move_to_foreground.description: Moves the window specified by window_id to the foreground, so that it is visible over other windows.

window_is_focused.description: Returns true if the window specified by window_id is focused.

window_can_draw.description: Returns true if anything can be drawn in the window specified by window_id, false otherwise. Using the --disable-render-loop command line argument or a headless build will return false.

window_set_transient.description:
Sets window transient parent. Transient window will be destroyed with its transient parent and will return focus to their parent when closed. The transient window is displayed on top of a non-exclusive full-screen parent window. Transient windows can't enter full-screen mode.
				Note: It's recommended to change this value using Window.transient instead.
				Note: The behavior might be different depending on the platform.

window_set_exclusive.description:
If set to true, this window will always stay on top of its parent window, parent window will ignore input while this window is opened.
				Note: On macOS, exclusive windows are confined to the same space (virtual desktop or screen) as the parent window.
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS and Windows.

window_set_ime_active.description: Sets whether Input Method Editor should be enabled for the window specified by window_id. See also window_set_ime_position.

window_set_ime_position.description: Sets the position of the Input Method Editor popup for the specified window_id. Only effective if window_set_ime_active was set to true for the specified window_id.

window_set_vsync_mode.description:
Sets the V-Sync mode of the given window. See also ProjectSettings.display/window/vsync/vsync_mode.
				Depending on the platform and used renderer, the engine will fall back to  if the desired mode is not supported.
				Note: V-Sync modes other than  are only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility.

window_get_vsync_mode.description: Returns the V-Sync mode of the given window.

window_is_maximize_allowed.description: Returns true if the given window can be maximized (the maximize button is enabled).

window_maximize_on_title_dbl_click.description:
Returns true if double-clicking on a window's title should maximize it.
				Note: This method is implemented only on macOS.

window_minimize_on_title_dbl_click.description:
Returns true if double-clicking on a window's title should minimize it.
				Note: This method is implemented only on macOS.

window_start_drag.description:
Starts an interactive drag operation on the window with the given window_id, using the current mouse position. Call this method when handling a mouse button being pressed to simulate a pressed event on the window's title bar. Using this method allows the window to participate in space switching, tiling, and other system features.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS, and Windows.

window_start_resize.description:
Starts an interactive resize operation on the window with the given window_id, using the current mouse position. Call this method when handling a mouse button being pressed to simulate a pressed event on the window's edge.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS, and Windows.

window_set_color.description:
Sets the background color of the root window.
				Note: This method is implemented only on Android.

accessibility_should_increase_contrast.description:
Returns 1 if a high-contrast user interface theme should be used, 0 otherwise. Returns -1 if status is unknown.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland, GNOME), macOS, and Windows.

accessibility_should_reduce_animation.description:
Returns 1 if flashing, blinking, and other moving content that can cause seizures in users with photosensitive epilepsy should be disabled, 0 otherwise. Returns -1 if status is unknown.
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS and Windows.

accessibility_should_reduce_transparency.description:
Returns 1 if background images, transparency, and other features that can reduce the contrast between the foreground and background should be disabled, 0 otherwise. Returns -1 if status is unknown.
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS and Windows.

accessibility_screen_reader_active.description:
Returns 1 if a screen reader, Braille display or other assistive app is active, 0 otherwise. Returns -1 if status is unknown.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
				Note: Accessibility debugging tools, such as Accessibility Insights for Windows, Accessibility Inspector (macOS), or AT-SPI Browser (Linux/BSD), do not count as assistive apps and will not affect this value. To test your project with these tools, set ProjectSettings.accessibility/general/accessibility_support to 1.

accessibility_create_element.description:
Creates a new, empty accessibility element resource.
				Note: An accessibility element is created and freed automatically for each . In general, this function should not be called manually.

accessibility_create_sub_element.description: Creates a new, empty accessibility sub-element resource. Sub-elements can be used to provide accessibility information for objects which are not s, such as list items, table cells, or menu items. Sub-elements are freed automatically when the parent element is freed, or can be freed early using the accessibility_free_element method.

accessibility_create_sub_text_edit_eleme.description:
Creates a new, empty accessibility sub-element from the shaped text buffer. Sub-elements are freed automatically when the parent element is freed, or can be freed early using the accessibility_free_element method.
				If is_last_line is true, no trailing newline is appended to the text content. Set to true for the last line in multi-line text fields and for single-line text fields.

accessibility_has_element.description: Returns true if id is a valid accessibility element.

accessibility_free_element.description: Frees the accessibility element id created by accessibility_create_element, accessibility_create_sub_element, or accessibility_create_sub_text_edit_elements.

accessibility_element_set_meta.description: Sets the metadata of the accessibility element id to meta.

accessibility_element_get_meta.description: Returns the metadata of the accessibility element id.

accessibility_set_window_rect.description:
Sets window outer (with decorations) and inner (without decorations) bounds for assistive apps.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
				Note: Advanced users only!  objects call this method automatically.

accessibility_set_window_focused.description:
Sets the window focused state for assistive apps.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
				Note: Advanced users only!  objects call this method automatically.

accessibility_get_window_root.description: Returns the main accessibility element of the OS native window.

accessibility_update_set_extra_info.description: Sets element accessibility extra information added to the element name.

accessibility_update_set_bounds.description: Sets element bounding box, relative to the node position.

accessibility_update_add_child.description:
Adds a child accessibility element.
				Note:  children and sub-elements are added to the child list automatically.

accessibility_update_add_related_control.description: Adds an element that is controlled by this element.

accessibility_update_add_related_details.description: Adds an element that details this element.

accessibility_update_add_related_describ.description: Adds an element that describes this element.

accessibility_update_add_related_flow_to.description: Adds an element that this element flow into.

accessibility_update_add_related_labeled.description: Adds an element that labels this element.

accessibility_update_add_related_radio_g.description:
Adds an element that is part of the same radio group.
				Note: This method should be called on each element of the group, using all other elements as related_id.

accessibility_update_set_active_descenda.description: Adds an element that is an active descendant of this element.

accessibility_update_set_next_on_line.description: Sets next element on the line.

accessibility_update_set_previous_on_lin.description: Sets previous element on the line.

accessibility_update_set_member_of.description: Sets the element to be a member of the group.

accessibility_update_set_in_page_link_ta.description: Sets target element for the link.

accessibility_update_set_error_message.description: Sets an element which contains an error message for this element.

accessibility_update_set_live.description: Sets the priority of the live region updates.

accessibility_update_add_action.description: Adds a callback for the accessibility action (action which can be performed by using a special screen reader command or buttons on the Braille display), and marks this action as supported. The action callback receives one  argument, which value depends on action type.

accessibility_update_add_custom_action.description: Adds support for a custom accessibility action. action_id is passed as an argument to the callback of  action.

accessibility_update_set_table_row_count.description: Sets number of rows in the table.

accessibility_update_set_table_column_co.description: Sets number of columns in the table.

accessibility_update_set_table_row_index.description: Sets position of the row in the table.

accessibility_update_set_table_cell_posi.description: Sets cell position in the table.

accessibility_update_set_list_item_count.description: Sets number of items in the list.

accessibility_update_set_list_item_index.description: Sets the position of the element in the list.

accessibility_update_set_list_item_level.description: Sets the hierarchical level of the element in the list.

accessibility_update_set_popup_type.description: Sets popup type for popup buttons.

accessibility_update_set_text_selection.description: Sets text selection to the text field. text_start_id and text_end_id should be elements created by accessibility_create_sub_text_edit_elements. Character offsets are relative to the corresponding element.

accessibility_update_set_list_orientatio.description: Sets the orientation of the list elements.

accessibility_update_set_shortcut.description: Sets the list of keyboard shortcuts used by element.

accessibility_update_set_role_descriptio.description: Sets element accessibility role description text.

accessibility_update_set_state_descripti.description: Sets human-readable description of the current checked state.

ime_get_selection.description:
Returns the text selection in the Input Method Editor composition string, with the 's x component being the caret position and y being the length of the selection.
				Note: This method is implemented only on macOS.

ime_get_text.description:
Returns the composition string contained within the Input Method Editor window.
				Note: This method is implemented only on macOS.

virtual_keyboard_show.description:
Shows the virtual keyboard if the platform has one.
				existing_text parameter is useful for implementing your own  or , as it tells the virtual keyboard what text has already been typed (the virtual keyboard uses it for auto-correct and predictions).
				position parameter is the screen space  of the edited text.
				type parameter allows configuring which type of virtual keyboard to show.
				max_length limits the number of characters that can be entered if different from -1.
				cursor_start can optionally define the current text cursor position if cursor_end is not set.
				cursor_start and cursor_end can optionally define the current text selection.
				Note: This method is implemented on Android, iOS and Web.

virtual_keyboard_hide.description: Hides the virtual keyboard if it is shown, does nothing otherwise.

virtual_keyboard_get_height.description:
Returns the on-screen keyboard's height in pixels. Returns 0 if there is no keyboard or if it is currently hidden.
				Note: On Android 7 and 8, the keyboard height may return 0 the first time the keyboard is opened in non-immersive mode. This behavior does not occur in immersive mode.

has_hardware_keyboard.description:
Returns true if a hardware keyboard is connected.
				Note: This method is implemented on Android and iOS. On other platforms, this method always returns true.

set_hardware_keyboard_connection_change_.description:
Sets the callback that should be called when a hardware keyboard is connected or disconnected. callable should accept a single  argument indicating whether the keyboard has been connected (true) or disconnected (false).
				Note: This method is only implemented on Android.

cursor_set_shape.description: Sets the default mouse cursor shape. The cursor's appearance will vary depending on the user's operating system and mouse cursor theme. See also cursor_get_shape and cursor_set_custom_image.

cursor_get_shape.description: Returns the default mouse cursor shape set by cursor_set_shape.

cursor_set_custom_image.description:
Sets a custom mouse cursor image for the given shape. This means the user's operating system and mouse cursor theme will no longer influence the mouse cursor's appearance.
				cursor can be either a  or an , and it should not be larger than 256×256 to display correctly. Optionally, hotspot can be set to offset the image's position relative to the click point. By default, hotspot is set to the top-left corner of the image. See also cursor_set_shape.
				Note: On Web, calling this method every frame can cause the cursor to flicker.

get_swap_cancel_ok.description:
Returns true if positions of OK and Cancel buttons are swapped in dialogs. This is enabled by default on Windows to follow interface conventions, and be toggled by changing ProjectSettings.gui/common/swap_cancel_ok.
				Note: This doesn't affect native dialogs such as the ones spawned by DisplayServer.dialog_show.

enable_for_stealing_focus.description:
Allows the process_id PID to steal focus from this window. In other words, this disables the operating system's focus stealing protection for the specified PID.
				Note: This method is implemented only on Windows.

dialog_show.description:
Shows a text dialog which uses the operating system's native look-and-feel. callback should accept a single  parameter which corresponds to the index of the pressed button.
				Note: This method is implemented if the display server has the  feature. Supported platforms include macOS, Windows, and Android.

dialog_input_text.description:
Shows a text input dialog which uses the operating system's native look-and-feel. callback should accept a single  parameter which contains the text field's contents.
				Note: This method is implemented if the display server has the  feature. Supported platforms include macOS, Windows, and Android.

file_dialog_show.description:
Displays OS native dialog for selecting files or directories in the file system.
				Each filter string in the filters array should be formatted like this: *.png,*.jpg,*.jpeg;Image Files;image/png,image/jpeg. The description text of the filter is optional and can be omitted. It is recommended to set both file extension and MIME type. See also FileDialog.filters.
				Callbacks have the following arguments: status: bool, selected_paths: PackedStringArray, selected_filter_index: int. On Android, the third callback argument (selected_filter_index) is always 0.
				Note: This method is implemented if the display server has the  feature. Supported platforms include Linux (X11/Wayland), Windows, macOS, and Android (API level 29+).
				Note: current_directory might be ignored.
				Note: Embedded file dialogs and Windows file dialogs support only file extensions, while Android, Linux, and macOS file dialogs also support MIME types.
				Note: On Android and Linux, show_hidden is ignored.
				Note: On Android and macOS, native file dialogs have no title.
				Note: On macOS, sandboxed apps will save security-scoped bookmarks to retain access to the opened folders across multiple sessions. Use OS.get_granted_permissions to get a list of saved bookmarks.
				Note: On Android, this method uses the Android Storage Access Framework (SAF).
				The file picker returns a URI instead of a filesystem path. This URI can be passed directly to  to perform read/write operations.
				When using , it returns a tree URI that grants full access to the selected directory. File operations inside this directory can be performed by passing a path on the form treeUri#relative/path/to/file to .
				To avoid opening the file picker again after each app restart, you can take persistable URI permission as follows:
				
				
				val uri = "content://com.android..." # URI of the selected file or folder.
				val persist = true # Set to false to release the persistable permission.
				var android_runtime = Engine.get_singleton("AndroidRuntime")
				android_runtime.updatePersistableUriPermission(uri, persist)
				
				
				The persistable URI permission remains valid across app restarts as long as the directory is not moved, renamed, or deleted.

file_dialog_with_options_show.description:
Displays OS native dialog for selecting files or directories in the file system with additional user selectable options.
				Each filter string in the filters array should be formatted like this: *.png,*.jpg,*.jpeg;Image Files;image/png,image/jpeg. The description text of the filter is optional and can be omitted. It is recommended to set both file extension and MIME type. See also FileDialog.filters.
				options is array of s with the following keys:
				- "name" - option's name .
				- "values" -  of values. If empty, boolean option (check box) is used.
				- "default" - default selected option index () or default boolean value ().
				Callbacks have the following arguments: status: bool, selected_paths: PackedStringArray, selected_filter_index: int, selected_option: Dictionary.
				Note: This method is implemented if the display server has the  feature. Supported platforms include Linux (X11/Wayland), Windows, and macOS.
				Note: current_directory might be ignored.
				Note: Embedded file dialogs and Windows file dialogs support only file extensions, while Android, Linux, and macOS file dialogs also support MIME types.
				Note: On Linux (X11), show_hidden is ignored.
				Note: On macOS, native file dialogs have no title.
				Note: On macOS, sandboxed apps will save security-scoped bookmarks to retain access to the opened folders across multiple sessions. Use OS.get_granted_permissions to get a list of saved bookmarks.

beep.description:
Plays the beep sound from the operative system, if possible. Because it comes from the OS, the beep sound will be audible even if the application is muted. It may also be disabled for the entire OS by the user.
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS, Linux (X11/Wayland), and Windows.

keyboard_get_layout_count.description:
Returns the number of keyboard layouts.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS and Windows.

keyboard_get_current_layout.description:
Returns active keyboard layout index.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS, and Windows.

keyboard_set_current_layout.description:
Sets the active keyboard layout.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS and Windows.

keyboard_get_layout_language.description:
Returns the ISO-639/BCP-47 language code of the keyboard layout at position index.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS and Windows.

keyboard_get_layout_name.description:
Returns the localized name of the keyboard layout at position index.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS and Windows.

keyboard_get_keycode_from_physical.description:
Converts a physical (US QWERTY) keycode to one in the active keyboard layout.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS and Windows.

keyboard_get_label_from_physical.description:
Converts a physical (US QWERTY) keycode to localized label printed on the key in the active keyboard layout.
				Note: This method is implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland), macOS and Windows.

show_emoji_and_symbol_picker.description:
Opens system emoji and symbol picker.
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS and Windows.

color_picker.description:
Displays OS native color picker.
				Callbacks have the following arguments: status: bool, color: Color.
				Note: This method is implemented if the display server has the  feature.
				Note: This method is only implemented on Linux (X11/Wayland).

process_events.description: Perform window manager processing, including input flushing. See also force_process_and_drop_events, Input.flush_buffered_events and Input.use_accumulated_input.

force_process_and_drop_events.description:
Forces window manager processing while ignoring all s. See also process_events.
				Note: This method is implemented on Windows and macOS.

set_native_icon.description:
Sets the window icon (usually displayed in the top-left corner) in the operating system's native format. The file at filename must be in .ico format on Windows or .icns on macOS. By using specially crafted .ico or .icns icons, set_native_icon allows specifying different icons depending on the size the icon is displayed at. This size is determined by the operating system and user preferences (including the display scale factor). To use icons in other formats, use set_icon instead.
				Note: Requires support for .

set_icon.description:
Sets the window icon (usually displayed in the top-left corner) with an . To use icons in the operating system's native format, use set_native_icon instead.
				Note: Requires support for .

create_status_indicator.description:
Creates a new application status indicator with the specified icon, tooltip, and activation callback.
				callback should take two arguments: the pressed mouse button (one of the  constants) and the click position in screen coordinates (a ).

status_indicator_set_icon.description:
Sets the application status indicator icon.
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS and Windows.

status_indicator_set_tooltip.description:
Sets the application status indicator tooltip.
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS and Windows.

status_indicator_set_menu.description:
Sets the application status indicator native popup menu.
				Note: On macOS, the menu is activated by any mouse button. Its activation callback is not triggered.
				Note: On Windows, the menu is activated by the right mouse button, selecting the status icon and pressing Shift + F10, or the applications key. The menu's activation callback for the other mouse buttons is still triggered.
				Note: Native popup is only supported if  supports the  feature.

status_indicator_set_callback.description:
Sets the application status indicator activation callback. callback should take two arguments:  mouse button index (one of  values) and  click position in screen coordinates.
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS and Windows.

status_indicator_get_rect.description:
Returns the rectangle for the given status indicator id in screen coordinates. If the status indicator is not visible, returns an empty .
				Note: This method is implemented on macOS and Windows.

tablet_get_driver_count.description:
Returns the total number of available tablet drivers.
				Note: This method is implemented only on Windows.

tablet_get_driver_name.description:
Returns the tablet driver name for the given index.
				Note: This method is implemented only on Windows.

tablet_get_current_driver.description:
Returns current active tablet driver name.
				Note: This method is implemented only on Windows.

tablet_set_current_driver.description:
Set active tablet driver name.
				Supported drivers:
				- winink: Windows Ink API, default.
				- wintab: Wacom Wintab API (compatible device driver required).
				- dummy: Dummy driver, tablet input is disabled.
				Note: This method is implemented only on Windows.

is_window_transparency_available.description: Returns true if the window background can be made transparent. This method returns false if ProjectSettings.display/window/per_pixel_transparency/allowed is set to false, or if transparency is not supported by the renderer or OS compositor.

register_additional_output.description:
Registers an  which represents an additional output that will be rendered too, beyond normal windows. The  is only used as an identifier, which can be later passed to unregister_additional_output.
				This can be used to prevent Godot from skipping rendering when no normal windows are visible.

unregister_additional_output.description: Unregisters an  representing an additional output, that was registered via register_additional_output.

has_additional_outputs.description: Returns true if any additional outputs have been registered via register_additional_output.

add_command.description:
Adds a custom command to EditorCommandPalette.
				- command_name:  (Name of the Command. This is displayed to the user.)
				- key_name:  (Name of the key for a particular Command. This is used to uniquely identify the Command.)
				- binded_callable:  (Callable of the Command. This will be executed when the Command is selected.)
				- shortcut_text:  (Shortcut text of the Command if available.)

remove_command.description:
Removes the custom command from EditorCommandPalette.
				- key_name:  (Name of the key for a particular Command.)

EditorContextMenuPlugin.brief_description: Plugin for adding custom context menus in the editor.
EditorContextMenuPlugin.description:
allows for the addition of custom options in the editor's context menu.
		Currently, context menus are supported for three commonly used areas: the file system, scene tree, and editor script list panel.

_popup_menu.description: Called when creating a context menu, custom options can be added by using the add_context_menu_item or add_context_menu_item_from_shortcut functions. paths contains currently selected paths (depending on menu), which can be used to conditionally add options.

add_context_menu_item.description:
Add custom option to the context menu of the plugin's specified slot. When the option is activated, callback will be called. Callback should take single  argument; array contents depend on context menu slot.
				
				func _popup_menu(paths):
					add_context_menu_item("File Custom options", handle, ICON)
				
				If you want to assign shortcut to the menu item, use add_context_menu_item_from_shortcut instead.

add_context_submenu_item.description:
Add a submenu to the context menu of the plugin's specified slot. The submenu is not automatically handled, you need to connect to its signals yourself. Also the submenu is freed on every popup, so provide a new  every time.
				
				func _popup_menu(paths):
					var popup_menu = PopupMenu.new()
					popup_menu.add_item("Blue")
					popup_menu.add_item("White")
					popup_menu.id_pressed.connect(_on_color_submenu_option)

					add_context_submenu_item("Set Node Color", popup_menu)

EditorDebuggerPlugin.brief_description: A base class to implement debugger plugins.

_setup_session.description: Override this method to be notified whenever a new  is created. Note that the session may be inactive during this stage.

_has_capture.description: Override this method to enable receiving messages from the debugger. If capture is "my_message" then messages starting with "my_message:" will be passed to the _capture method.

_capture.description: Override this method to process incoming messages. The session_id is the ID of the  that received the message. Use get_session to retrieve the session. This method should return true if the message is recognized.

_goto_script_line.description: Override this method to be notified when a breakpoint line has been clicked in the debugger breakpoint panel.

_breakpoints_cleared_in_tree.description: Override this method to be notified when all breakpoints are cleared in the editor.

_breakpoint_set_in_tree.description: Override this method to be notified when a breakpoint is set in the editor.

get_session.description: Returns the  with the given id.

get_sessions.description:
Returns an array of  currently available to this debugger plugin.
				Note: Sessions in the array may be inactive, check their state via EditorDebuggerSession.is_active.

EditorDebuggerSession.brief_description: A class to interact with the editor debugger.
EditorDebuggerSession.description:
This class cannot be directly instantiated and must be retrieved via an .
		You can add tabs to the session UI via add_session_tab, send messages via send_message, and toggle s via toggle_profiler.

send_message.description: Sends the given message to the attached remote instance, optionally passing additionally data. See  for how to retrieve those messages.

toggle_profiler.description: Toggle the given profiler on the attached remote instance, optionally passing additionally data. See  for more details.

is_breaked.description: Returns true if the attached remote instance is currently in the debug loop.

is_debuggable.description: Returns true if the attached remote instance can be debugged.

is_active.description: Returns true if the debug session is currently attached to a remote instance.

add_session_tab.description: Adds the given control to the debug session UI in the debugger bottom panel. The control's node name will be used as the tab title.

remove_session_tab.description: Removes the given control from the debug session UI in the debugger bottom panel.

set_breakpoint.description: Enables or disables a specific breakpoint based on enabled, updating the Editor Breakpoint Panel accordingly.

EditorDock.description:
EditorDock is a  node that can be docked in one of the editor's dock slots. Docks are added by plugins to provide space for controls related to an . The editor comes with a few built-in docks, such as the Scene dock, FileSystem dock, etc.
		You can add a dock by using EditorPlugin.add_dock. The dock can be customized by changing its properties.
		
		@tool
		extends EditorPlugin

		# Dock reference.
		var dock

		# Plugin initialization.
		func _enter_tree():
			dock = EditorDock.new()
			dock.title = "My Dock"
			dock.dock_icon = preload("./dock_icon.png")
			dock.default_slot = EditorDock.DOCK_SLOT_RIGHT_UL
			var dock_content = preload("./dock_content.tscn").instantiate()
			dock.add_child(dock_content)
			add_dock(dock)

		# Plugin clean-up.
		func _exit_tree():
			remove_dock(dock)
			dock.queue_free()
			dock = null

_save_layout_to_config.description: Implement this method to handle saving this dock's layout. It's equivalent to EditorPlugin._get_window_layout. section is a unique section based on layout_key.

_load_layout_from_config.description: Implement this method to handle loading this dock's layout. It's equivalent to EditorPlugin._set_window_layout. section is a unique section based on layout_key.

open.description:
Opens the dock. It will appear in the last used dock slot. If the dock has no default slot, it will be opened floating.
				Note: This does not focus the dock. If you want to open and focus the dock, use make_visible.

make_visible.description: Focuses the dock's tab (or window if it's floating). If the dock was closed, it will be opened. If it's a bottom dock, makes the bottom panel visible.

close.description: Closes the dock, making its tab hidden.

title.description: The title of the dock's tab. If empty, the dock's Node.name will be used. If the name is auto-generated (contains @), the first child's name will be used instead.

layout_key.description: The key representing this dock in the editor's layout file. If empty, the dock's displayed name will be used instead.

global.description: If true, the dock appears in the Editor > Editor Docks menu and can be closed. Non-global docks can still be closed using close or when closable is true.

transient.description: If true, the dock is not automatically opened or closed when loading an editor layout, only moved. It also can't be opened using a shortcut. This is meant for docks that are opened and closed in specific cases, such as when selecting a  or  node.

closable.description: If true, the dock can be closed with the Close button in the context popup. Docks with global enabled are always closable.

icon_name.description: The icon for the dock, as a name from the EditorIcons theme type in the editor theme. You can find the list of available icons here.

dock_icon.description: The icon for the dock, as a texture. If specified, it will override icon_name.

force_show_icon.description: If true, the dock will always display an icon, regardless of EditorSettings.interface/editor/dock_tab_style or EditorSettings.interface/editor/bottom_dock_tab_style.

title_color.description: The color of the dock tab's title. If its alpha is 0.0, the default font color will be used.

dock_shortcut.description: The shortcut used to open the dock.

default_slot.description:
The default dock slot used when adding the dock with EditorPlugin.add_dock.
			After the dock is added, it can be moved to a different slot and the editor will automatically remember its position between sessions. If you remove and re-add the dock, it will be reset to default.

available_layouts.description: The available layouts for this dock, as a bitmask. By default, the dock allows vertical and floating layouts.

EditorExportPlatform.brief_description: Identifies a supported export platform, and internally provides the functionality of exporting to that platform.
EditorExportPlatform.description:
Base resource that provides the functionality of exporting a release build of a project to a platform, from the editor. Stores platform-specific metadata such as the name and supported features of the platform, and performs the exporting of projects, PCK files, and ZIP files. Uses an export template for the platform provided at the time of project exporting.
		Used in scripting by  to configure platform-specific customization of scenes and resources. See EditorExportPlugin._begin_customize_scenes and EditorExportPlugin._begin_customize_resources for more details.

get_os_name.description: Returns the name of the export operating system handled by this  class, as a friendly string. Possible return values are Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, iOS, and Web.

create_preset.description: Create a new preset for this platform.

find_export_template.description: Locates export template for the platform, and returns  with the following keys: path: String and error: String. This method is provided for convenience and custom export platforms aren't required to use it or keep export templates stored in the same way official templates are.

get_current_presets.description: Returns array of s for this platform.

save_pack.description:
Saves PCK archive and returns  with the following keys: result: Error, so_files: Array (array of the shared/static objects which contains dictionaries with the following keys: path: String, tags: PackedStringArray, and target_folder: String).
				If embed is true, PCK content is appended to the end of path file and return  additionally include following keys: embedded_start: int (embedded PCK offset) and embedded_size: int (embedded PCK size).

save_zip.description: Saves ZIP archive and returns  with the following keys: result: Error, so_files: Array (array of the shared/static objects which contains dictionaries with the following keys: path: String, tags: PackedStringArray, and target_folder: String).

save_pack_patch.description: Saves patch PCK archive and returns  with the following keys: result: Error, so_files: Array (array of the shared/static objects which contains dictionaries with the following keys: path: String, tags: PackedStringArray, and target_folder: String).

save_zip_patch.description: Saves patch ZIP archive and returns  with the following keys: result: Error, so_files: Array (array of the shared/static objects which contains dictionaries with the following keys: path: String, tags: PackedStringArray, and target_folder: String).

gen_export_flags.description: Generates array of command line arguments for the default export templates for the debug flags and editor settings.

export_project_files.description:
Exports project files for the specified preset. This method can be used to implement custom export format, other than PCK and ZIP. One of the callbacks is called for each exported file.
				save_cb is called for all exported files and have the following arguments: file_path: String, file_data: PackedByteArray, file_index: int, file_count: int, encryption_include_filters: PackedStringArray, encryption_exclude_filters: PackedStringArray, encryption_key: PackedByteArray.
				shared_cb is called for exported native shared/static libraries and have the following arguments: file_path: String, tags: PackedStringArray, target_folder: String.
				Note: file_index and file_count are intended for progress tracking only and aren't necessarily unique and precise.

export_project.description: Creates a full project at path for the specified preset.

export_pack.description: Creates a PCK archive at path for the specified preset.

export_zip.description: Create a ZIP archive at path for the specified preset.

export_pack_patch.description:
Creates a patch PCK archive at path for the specified preset, containing only the files that have changed since the last patch.
				Note: patches is an optional override of the set of patches defined in the export preset. When empty the patches defined in the export preset will be used instead.

export_zip_patch.description:
Create a patch ZIP archive at path for the specified preset, containing only the files that have changed since the last patch.
				Note: patches is an optional override of the set of patches defined in the export preset. When empty the patches defined in the export preset will be used instead.

add_message.description: Adds a message to the export log that will be displayed when exporting ends.

get_message_count.description: Returns the number of messages in the export log.

get_message_type.description: Returns the type for the message with the given index.

get_message_category.description: Returns the message category for the message with the given index.

get_message_text.description: Returns the text for the message with the given index.

get_worst_message_type.description: Returns most severe message type currently present in the export log.

ssh_run_on_remote.description: Executes specified command on the remote host via SSH protocol and returns command output in the output.

ssh_run_on_remote_no_wait.description: Executes specified command on the remote host via SSH protocol and returns process ID (on the remote host) without waiting for command to finish.

ssh_push_to_remote.description: Uploads specified file over SCP protocol to the remote host.

get_internal_export_files.description: Returns additional files that should always be exported regardless of preset configuration, and are not part of the project source. The returned  contains filename keys () and their corresponding raw data ().

get_forced_export_files.description: Returns array of core file names that always should be exported regardless of preset config.

EditorExportPlatformAppleEmbedded.brief_description: Base class for the Apple embedded platform exporters (iOS and visionOS).
EditorExportPlatformAppleEmbedded.description: The base class for Apple embedded platform exporters. These include iOS and visionOS, but not macOS. See the classes inheriting from this one for more details.

EditorExportPlatformExtension.description:
External  implementations should inherit from this class.
		To use , register it using the EditorPlugin.add_export_platform method first.

_get_preset_features.description: Returns array of platform specific features for the specified preset.

_is_executable.description: Returns true if specified file is a valid executable (native executable or script) for the target platform.

_get_export_options.description:
Returns a property list, as an  of dictionaries. Each  must at least contain the name: StringName and type: Variant.Type entries.
				Additionally, the following keys are supported:
				- hint: PropertyHint
				- hint_string: String
				- usage: PropertyUsageFlags
				- class_name: StringName
				- default_value: Variant, default value of the property.
				- update_visibility: bool, if set to true, _get_export_option_visibility is called for each property when this property is changed.
				- required: bool, if set to true, this property warnings are critical, and should be resolved to make export possible. This value is a hint for the _has_valid_export_configuration implementation, and not used by the engine directly.
				See also Object._get_property_list.

_should_update_export_options.description: Returns true if export options list is changed and presets should be updated.

_get_export_option_visibility.description: Validates option and returns visibility for the specified preset. Default implementation return true for all options.

_get_export_option_warning.description: Validates option and returns warning message for the specified preset. Default implementation return empty string for all options.

_get_logo.description: Returns the platform logo displayed in the export dialog. The logo should be 32×32 pixels, adjusted for the current editor scale (see EditorInterface.get_editor_scale).

_poll_export.description: Returns true if one-click deploy options are changed and editor interface should be updated.

_get_options_count.description: Returns the number of devices (or other options) available in the one-click deploy menu.

_get_options_tooltip.description: Returns tooltip of the one-click deploy menu button.

_get_option_icon.description: Returns the item icon for the specified device in the one-click deploy menu. The icon should be 16×16 pixels, adjusted for the current editor scale (see EditorInterface.get_editor_scale).

_get_option_label.description: Returns one-click deploy menu item label for the specified device.

_get_option_tooltip.description: Returns one-click deploy menu item tooltip for the specified device.

_get_device_architecture.description: Returns device architecture for one-click deploy.

_cleanup.description: Called by the editor before platform is unregistered.

_run.description:
This method is called when device one-click deploy menu option is selected.
				Implementation should export project to a temporary location, upload and run it on the specific device, or perform another action associated with the menu item.

_get_run_icon.description: Returns the icon of the one-click deploy menu button. The icon should be 16×16 pixels, adjusted for the current editor scale (see EditorInterface.get_editor_scale).

_can_export.description:
Returns true if the specified preset is valid and can be exported. Use set_config_error and set_config_missing_templates to set error details.
				Usual implementations call _has_valid_export_configuration and _has_valid_project_configuration to determine if exporting is possible.

_has_valid_export_configuration.description: Returns true if export configuration is valid.

_has_valid_project_configuration.description: Returns true if project configuration is valid.

_get_binary_extensions.description: Returns array of supported binary extensions for the full project export.

_export_project.description:
Creates a full project at path for the specified preset.
				This method is called when "Export" button is pressed in the export dialog.
				This method implementation can call EditorExportPlatform.save_pack or EditorExportPlatform.save_zip to use default PCK/ZIP export process, or calls EditorExportPlatform.export_project_files and implement custom callback for processing each exported file.

_export_pack.description:
Creates a PCK archive at path for the specified preset.
				This method is called when "Export PCK/ZIP" button is pressed in the export dialog, with "Export as Patch" disabled, and PCK is selected as a file type.

_export_zip.description:
Create a ZIP archive at path for the specified preset.
				This method is called when "Export PCK/ZIP" button is pressed in the export dialog, with "Export as Patch" disabled, and ZIP is selected as a file type.

_export_pack_patch.description:
Creates a patch PCK archive at path for the specified preset, containing only the files that have changed since the last patch.
				This method is called when "Export PCK/ZIP" button is pressed in the export dialog, with "Export as Patch" enabled, and PCK is selected as a file type.
				Note: The patches provided in patches have already been loaded when this method is called and are merely provided as context. When empty the patches defined in the export preset have been loaded instead.

_export_zip_patch.description:
Create a ZIP archive at path for the specified preset, containing only the files that have changed since the last patch.
				This method is called when "Export PCK/ZIP" button is pressed in the export dialog, with "Export as Patch" enabled, and ZIP is selected as a file type.
				Note: The patches provided in patches have already been loaded when this method is called and are merely provided as context. When empty the patches defined in the export preset have been loaded instead.

_get_platform_features.description: Returns array of platform specific features.

_get_debug_protocol.description: Returns protocol used for remote debugging. Default implementation return tcp://.

_initialize.description: Initializes the plugin. Called by the editor when platform is registered.

set_config_error.description: Sets current configuration error message text. This method should be called only from the _can_export, _has_valid_export_configuration, or _has_valid_project_configuration implementations.

get_config_error.description: Returns current configuration error message text. This method should be called only from the _can_export, _has_valid_export_configuration, or _has_valid_project_configuration implementations.

set_config_missing_templates.description: Set to true is export templates are missing from the current configuration. This method should be called only from the _can_export, _has_valid_export_configuration, or _has_valid_project_configuration implementations.

get_config_missing_templates.description: Returns true is export templates are missing from the current configuration. This method should be called only from the _can_export, _has_valid_export_configuration, or _has_valid_project_configuration implementations.

EditorExportPlatformPC.brief_description: Base class for the desktop platform exporter (Windows and Linux/BSD).
EditorExportPlatformPC.description: The base class for the desktop platform exporters. These include Windows and Linux/BSD, but not macOS. See the classes inheriting from this one for more details.

EditorExportPlugin.brief_description: A script that is executed when exporting the project.
EditorExportPlugin.description:
s are automatically invoked whenever the user exports the project. Their most common use is to determine what files are being included in the exported project. For each plugin, _export_begin is called at the beginning of the export process and then _export_file is called for each exported file.
		To use , register it using the EditorPlugin.add_export_plugin method first.

_export_file.description:
Virtual method to be overridden by the user. Called for each exported file before _customize_resource and _customize_scene. The arguments can be used to identify the file. path is the path of the file, type is the  represented by the file (e.g. ), and features is the list of features for the export.
				Calling skip inside this callback will make the file not included in the export.

_export_begin.description: Virtual method to be overridden by the user. It is called when the export starts and provides all information about the export. features is the list of features for the export, is_debug is true for debug builds, path is the target path for the exported project. flags is only used when running a runnable profile, e.g. when using native run on Android.

_export_end.description: Virtual method to be overridden by the user. Called when the export is finished.

_begin_customize_resources.description:
Return true if this plugin will customize resources based on the platform and features used.
				When enabled, _get_customization_configuration_hash and _customize_resource will be called and must be implemented.

_customize_resource.description:
Customize a resource. If changes are made to it, return the same or a new resource. Otherwise, return null. When a new resource is returned, resource will be replaced by a copy of the new resource.
				The path argument is only used when customizing an actual file, otherwise this means that this resource is part of another one and it will be empty.
				Implementing this method is required if _begin_customize_resources returns true.
				Note: When customizing any of the following types and returning another resource, the other resource should not be skipped using skip in _export_file:
				- 
				- 
				- 
				- 
				- 
				-

_begin_customize_scenes.description:
Return true if this plugin will customize scenes based on the platform and features used.
				When enabled, _get_customization_configuration_hash and _customize_scene will be called and must be implemented.
				Note: _customize_scene will only be called for scenes that have been modified since the last export.

_customize_scene.description:
Customize a scene. If changes are made to it, return the same or a new scene. Otherwise, return null. If a new scene is returned, it is up to you to dispose of the old one.
				Implementing this method is required if _begin_customize_scenes returns true.

_get_customization_configuration_hash.description:
Return a hash based on the configuration passed (for both scenes and resources). This helps keep separate caches for separate export configurations.
				Implementing this method is required if _begin_customize_resources returns true.

_end_customize_scenes.description: This is called when the customization process for scenes ends.

_end_customize_resources.description: This is called when the customization process for resources ends.

_get_export_options.description:
Return a list of export options that can be configured for this export plugin.
				Each element in the return value is a  with the following keys:
				- option: A dictionary with the structure documented by Object.get_property_list, but all keys are optional.
				- default_value: The default value for this option.
				- update_visibility: An optional boolean value. If set to true, the preset will emit  when the option is changed.

_should_update_export_options.description: Return true if the result of _get_export_options has changed and the export options of the preset corresponding to platform should be updated.

_get_export_option_visibility.description: Validates option and returns the visibility for the specified platform. The default implementation returns true for all options.

_get_export_option_warning.description:
Check the requirements for the given option and return a non-empty warning string if they are not met.
				Note: Use get_option to check the value of the export options.

_get_export_features.description: Return a  of additional features this preset, for the given platform, should have.

_get_name.description:
Return the name identifier of this plugin (for future identification by the exporter). The plugins are sorted by name before exporting.
				Implementing this method is required.

_supports_platform.description: Return true if the plugin supports the given platform.

_get_android_dependencies.description:
Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is called to retrieve the set of Android dependencies provided by this plugin. Each returned Android dependency should have the format of an Android remote binary dependency: org.godot.example:my-plugin:0.0.0
				For more information see Android documentation on dependencies.
				Note: Only supported on Android and requires EditorExportPlatformAndroid.gradle_build/use_gradle_build to be enabled.

_get_android_dependencies_maven_repos.description:
Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is called to retrieve the URLs of Maven repositories for the set of Android dependencies provided by this plugin.
				For more information see Gradle documentation on dependency management.
				Note: Google's Maven repo and the Maven Central repo are already included by default.
				Note: Only supported on Android and requires EditorExportPlatformAndroid.gradle_build/use_gradle_build to be enabled.

_get_android_libraries.description:
Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is called to retrieve the local paths of the Android libraries archive (AAR) files provided by this plugin.
				Note: Relative paths must be relative to Godot's res://addons/ directory. For example, an AAR file located under res://addons/hello_world_plugin/HelloWorld.release.aar can be returned as an absolute path using res://addons/hello_world_plugin/HelloWorld.release.aar or a relative path using hello_world_plugin/HelloWorld.release.aar.
				Note: Only supported on Android and requires EditorExportPlatformAndroid.gradle_build/use_gradle_build to be enabled.

_get_android_manifest_activity_element_c.description:
Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is used at export time to update the contents of the activity element in the generated Android manifest.
				Note: Only supported on Android and requires EditorExportPlatformAndroid.gradle_build/use_gradle_build to be enabled.

_get_android_manifest_application_elemen.description:
Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is used at export time to update the contents of the application element in the generated Android manifest.
				Note: Only supported on Android and requires EditorExportPlatformAndroid.gradle_build/use_gradle_build to be enabled.

_get_android_manifest_element_contents.description:
Virtual method to be overridden by the user. This is used at export time to update the contents of the manifest element in the generated Android manifest.
				Note: Only supported on Android and requires EditorExportPlatformAndroid.gradle_build/use_gradle_build to be enabled.

_update_android_prebuilt_manifest.description:
Provide access to the Android prebuilt manifest and allows the plugin to modify it if needed.
				Implementers of this virtual method should take the binary manifest data from manifest_data, copy it, modify it, and then return it with the modifications.
				If no modifications are needed, then an empty  should be returned.

add_shared_object.description:
Adds a shared object or a directory containing only shared objects with the given tags and destination path.
				Note: In case of macOS exports, those shared objects will be added to Frameworks directory of app bundle.
				In case of a directory code-sign will error if you place non code object in directory.

add_file.description:
Adds a custom file to be exported. path is the virtual path that can be used to load the file, file is the binary data of the file.
				When called inside _export_file and remap is true, the current file will not be exported, but instead remapped to this custom file. remap is ignored when called in other places.
				file will not be imported, so consider using _customize_resource to remap imported resources.

add_apple_embedded_platform_project_stat.description: Adds a static library from the given path to the Apple embedded platform project.

add_apple_embedded_platform_framework.description: Adds a static library (*.a) or a dynamic library (*.dylib, *.framework) to the Linking Phase to the Apple embedded platform's Xcode project.

add_apple_embedded_platform_embedded_fra.description:
Adds a dynamic library (*.dylib, *.framework) to the Linking Phase in the Apple embedded platform's Xcode project and embeds it into the resulting binary.
				Note: For static libraries (*.a), this works in the same way as add_apple_embedded_platform_framework.
				Note: This method should not be used for System libraries as they are already present on the device.

add_apple_embedded_platform_plist_conten.description: Adds additional fields to the Apple embedded platform's project Info.plist file.

add_apple_embedded_platform_linker_flags.description: Adds linker flags for the Apple embedded platform export.

add_apple_embedded_platform_bundle_file.description: Adds an Apple embedded platform bundle file from the given path to the exported project.

add_apple_embedded_platform_cpp_code.description: Adds C++ code to the Apple embedded platform export. The final code is created from the code appended by each active export plugin.

add_ios_project_static_lib.description: Adds a static library from the given path to the iOS project.

add_ios_framework.description: Adds a static library (*.a) or a dynamic library (*.dylib, *.framework) to the Linking Phase to the iOS Xcode project.

add_ios_embedded_framework.description:
Adds a dynamic library (*.dylib, *.framework) to Linking Phase in iOS's Xcode project and embeds it into resulting binary.
				Note: For static libraries (*.a), this works the in same way as add_apple_embedded_platform_framework.
				Note: This method should not be used for System libraries as they are already present on the device.

add_ios_plist_content.description: Adds additional fields to the iOS project Info.plist file.

add_ios_linker_flags.description: Adds linker flags for the iOS export.

add_ios_bundle_file.description: Adds an iOS bundle file from the given path to the exported project.

add_ios_cpp_code.description: Adds C++ code to the iOS export. The final code is created from the code appended by each active export plugin.

add_macos_plugin_file.description:
Adds file or directory matching path to PlugIns directory of macOS app bundle.
				Note: This is useful only for macOS exports.

skip.description: To be called inside _export_file. Skips the current file, so it's not included in the export.

get_option.description: Returns the current value of an export option supplied by _get_export_options.

EditorExportPreset.description: Represents the configuration of an export preset, as created by the editor's export dialog. An  instance is intended to be used a read-only configuration passed to the  methods when exporting the project.

has.description: Returns true if the preset has the property named property.

get_files_to_export.description: Returns array of files to export.

get_customized_files.description: Returns a dictionary of files selected in the "Resources" tab of the export dialog. The dictionary's keys are file paths, and its values are the corresponding export modes: "strip", "keep", or "remove". See also get_file_export_mode.

get_customized_files_count.description: Returns the number of files selected in the "Resources" tab of the export dialog.

has_export_file.description: Returns true if the file at the specified path will be exported.

get_file_export_mode.description: Returns file export mode for the specified file.

get_project_setting.description: Returns the value of the setting identified by name using export preset feature tag overrides instead of current OS features.

is_runnable.description: Returns true if the "Runnable" toggle is enabled in the export dialog.

are_advanced_options_enabled.description: Returns true if the "Advanced" toggle is enabled in the export dialog.

is_dedicated_server.description: Returns true if the dedicated server export mode is selected in the export dialog.

get_export_filter.description: Returns export file filter mode selected in the "Resources" tab of the export dialog.

get_include_filter.description: Returns file filters to include during export.

get_exclude_filter.description: Returns file filters to exclude during export.

get_custom_features.description: Returns a comma-separated list of custom features added to this preset, as a string. See Feature tags in the documentation for more information.

get_patches.description: Returns the list of packs on which to base a patch export on.

get_encryption_in_filter.description: Returns file filters to include during PCK encryption.

get_encryption_ex_filter.description: Returns file filters to exclude during PCK encryption.

get_encrypt_pck.description: Returns true if PCK encryption is enabled in the export dialog.

get_encrypt_directory.description: Returns true if PCK directory encryption is enabled in the export dialog.

get_script_export_mode.description: Returns the export mode used by GDScript files. 0 for "Text", 1 for "Binary tokens", and 2 for "Compressed binary tokens (smaller files)".

get_or_env.description: Returns export option value or value of environment variable if it is set.

get_version.description:
Returns the preset's version number, or fall back to the ProjectSettings.application/config/version project setting if set to an empty string.
				If windows_version is true, formats the returned version number to be compatible with Windows executable metadata.

EditorFeatureProfile.brief_description: An editor feature profile which can be used to disable specific features.
EditorFeatureProfile.description:
An editor feature profile can be used to disable specific features of the Godot editor. When disabled, the features won't appear in the editor, which makes the editor less cluttered. This is useful in education settings to reduce confusion or when working in a team. For example, artists and level designers could use a feature profile that disables the script editor to avoid accidentally making changes to files they aren't supposed to edit.
		To manage editor feature profiles visually, use Editor > Manage Feature Profiles... at the top of the editor window.

set_disable_class.description: If disable is true, disables the class specified by class_name. When disabled, the class won't appear in the Create New Node dialog.

is_class_disabled.description: Returns true if the class specified by class_name is disabled. When disabled, the class won't appear in the Create New Node dialog.

set_disable_class_editor.description: If disable is true, disables editing for the class specified by class_name. When disabled, the class will still appear in the Create New Node dialog but the Inspector will be read-only when selecting a node that extends the class.

is_class_editor_disabled.description: Returns true if editing for the class specified by class_name is disabled. When disabled, the class will still appear in the Create New Node dialog but the Inspector will be read-only when selecting a node that extends the class.

set_disable_class_property.description: If disable is true, disables editing for property in the class specified by class_name. When a property is disabled, it won't appear in the Inspector when selecting a node that extends the class specified by class_name.

is_class_property_disabled.description: Returns true if property is disabled in the class specified by class_name. When a property is disabled, it won't appear in the Inspector when selecting a node that extends the class specified by class_name.

set_disable_feature.description: If disable is true, disables the editor feature specified in feature. When a feature is disabled, it will disappear from the editor entirely.

is_feature_disabled.description: Returns true if the feature is disabled. When a feature is disabled, it will disappear from the editor entirely.

get_feature_name.description: Returns the specified feature's human-readable name.

save_to_file.description:
Saves the editor feature profile to a file in JSON format. It can then be imported using the feature profile manager's Import button or the load_from_file method.
				Note: Feature profiles created via the user interface are saved in the feature_profiles directory, as a file with the .profile extension. The editor configuration folder can be found by using EditorPaths.get_config_dir.

load_from_file.description:
Loads an editor feature profile from a file. The file must follow the JSON format obtained by using the feature profile manager's Export button or the save_to_file method.
				Note: Feature profiles created via the user interface are loaded from the feature_profiles directory, as a file with the .profile extension. The editor configuration folder can be found by using EditorPaths.get_config_dir.

EditorFileDialog.brief_description: A modified version of  used by the editor.
EditorFileDialog.description:
is a  tweaked to work in the editor. It automatically handles favorite and recent directory lists, and synchronizes some properties with their corresponding editor settings.
		 will automatically show a native dialog based on the EditorSettings.interface/editor/use_native_file_dialogs editor setting and ignores FileDialog.use_native_dialog.
		Note:  is invisible by default. To make it visible, call one of the popup_* methods from  on the node, such as Window.popup_centered_clamped.

add_side_menu.description: This method is kept for compatibility and does nothing. As an alternative, you can display another dialog after showing the file dialog.

disable_overwrite_warning.description: If true, the  will not warn the user before overwriting files.

EditorFileSystem.brief_description: Resource filesystem, as the editor sees it.
EditorFileSystem.description:
This object holds information of all resources in the filesystem, their types, etc.
		Note: This class shouldn't be instantiated directly. Instead, access the singleton using EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem.

is_scanning.description: Returns true if the filesystem is being scanned.
