		Note:  is invisible by default. To make it visible, call one of the popup_* methods from  on the node, such as Window.popup_centered_clamped.

clear_filters.description: Clear all the added filters in the dialog.

add_filter.description:
Adds a comma-separated file extension filter and comma-separated MIME type mime_type option to the  with an optional description, which restricts what files can be picked.
				A filter should be of the form "filename.extension", where filename and extension can be * to match any string. Filters starting with . (i.e. empty filenames) are not allowed.
				For example, a filter of "*.png, *.jpg", a mime_type of image/png, image/jpeg, and a description of "Images" results in filter text "Images (*.png, *.jpg)".
				Note: Embedded file dialogs and Windows file dialogs support only file extensions, while Android, Linux, and macOS file dialogs also support MIME types.

clear_filename_filter.description: Clear the filter for file names.

get_option_name.description: Returns the name of the  or  with index option.

get_option_values.description: Returns an array of values of the  with index option.

get_option_default.description: Returns the default value index of the  or  with index option.

set_option_name.description: Sets the name of the  or  with index option.

set_option_values.description: Sets the option values of the  with index option.

set_option_default.description: Sets the default value index of the  or  with index option.

add_option.description:
Adds an additional  to the file dialog. If values is empty, a  is added instead.
				default_value_index should be an index of the value in the values. If values is empty it should be either 1 (checked), or 0 (unchecked).

get_selected_options.description: Returns a  with the selected values of the additional s and/or es.  keys are names and values are selected value indices.

get_vbox.description:
Returns the vertical box container of the dialog, custom controls can be added to it.
				Warning: This is a required internal node, removing and freeing it may cause a crash. If you wish to hide it or any of its children, use their CanvasItem.visible property.
				Note: Changes to this node are ignored by native file dialogs, use add_option to add custom elements to the dialog instead.

get_line_edit.description:
Returns the LineEdit for the selected file.
				Warning: This is a required internal node, removing and freeing it may cause a crash. If you wish to hide it or any of its children, use their CanvasItem.visible property.

set_customization_flag_enabled.description: Sets the specified customization flag, allowing to customize the features available in this .

is_customization_flag_enabled.description: Returns true if the provided flag is enabled.

deselect_all.description: Clear all currently selected items in the dialog.

set_favorite_list.description:
Sets the list of favorite directories, which is shared by all  nodes. Useful to restore the list of favorites saved with get_favorite_list. This method can be called only from the main thread.
				Note:  will update its internal  of favorites when its visibility changes. Be sure to call this method earlier if you want your changes to have effect.

get_favorite_list.description: Returns the list of favorite directories, which is shared by all  nodes. Useful to store the list of favorites between project sessions. This method can be called only from the main thread.

set_recent_list.description:
Sets the list of recent directories, which is shared by all  nodes. Useful to restore the list of recents saved with set_recent_list. This method can be called only from the main thread.
				Note:  will update its internal  of recent directories when its visibility changes. Be sure to call this method earlier if you want your changes to have effect.

get_recent_list.description: Returns the list of recent directories, which is shared by all  nodes. Useful to store the list of recents between project sessions. This method can be called only from the main thread.

set_get_icon_callback.description: Sets the callback used by the  nodes to get a file icon, when  mode is used. The callback should take a single  argument (file path), and return a . If an invalid texture is returned, the  icon will be used instead.

popup_file_dialog.description: Shows the  using the default size and position for file dialogs, and selects the file name if there is a current file.

invalidate.description:
Invalidates and updates this dialog's content list.
				Note: This method does nothing on native file dialogs.

mode_overrides_title.description: If true, changing the file_mode property will set the window title accordingly (e.g. setting file_mode to  will change the window title to "Open a File").

file_mode.description: The dialog's open or save mode, which affects the selection behavior.

display_mode.description: Display mode of the dialog's file list.

access.description:
The file system access scope.
			Warning: In Web builds, FileDialog cannot access the host file system. In sandboxed Linux and macOS environments, use_native_dialog is automatically used to allow limited access to host file system.

root_subfolder.description:
If non-empty, the given sub-folder will be "root" of this , i.e. user won't be able to go to its parent directory.
			Note: This property is ignored by native file dialogs.

filters.description:
The available file type filters. Each filter string in the array should be formatted like this: *.png,*.jpg,*.jpeg;Image Files;image/png,image/jpeg. The description text of the filter is optional and can be omitted. Both file extensions and MIME type should be always set.
			Note: Embedded file dialogs and Windows file dialogs support only file extensions, while Android, Linux, and macOS file dialogs also support MIME types.

filename_filter.description:
The filter for file names (case-insensitive). When set to a non-empty string, only files that contains the substring will be shown. filename_filter can be edited by the user with the filter button at the top of the file dialog.
			See also filters, which should be used to restrict the file types that can be selected instead of filename_filter which is meant to be set by the user.

show_hidden_files.description:
If true, the dialog will show hidden files.
			Note: This property is ignored by native file dialogs on Android and Linux.

use_native_dialog.description:
If true, and if supported by the current , OS native dialog will be used instead of custom one.
			Note: On Android, it is only supported for Android 10+ devices and when using . For access mode  and , the system will fall back to custom FileDialog.
			Note: On Linux and macOS, sandboxed apps always use native dialogs to access the host file system.
			Note: On macOS, sandboxed apps will save security-scoped bookmarks to retain access to the opened folders across multiple sessions. Use OS.get_granted_permissions to get a list of saved bookmarks.
			Note: Native dialogs are isolated from the base process, file dialog properties can't be modified once the dialog is shown.
			Note: This property is ignored in .

option_count.description: The number of additional s and es in the dialog.

hidden_files_toggle_enabled.description: If true, shows the toggle hidden files button.

file_filter_toggle_enabled.description: If true, shows the toggle file filter button.

file_sort_options_enabled.description: If true, shows the file sorting options button.

folder_creation_enabled.description: If true, shows the button for creating new directories (when using , , or ), and the context menu will have the "New Folder..." option.

favorites_enabled.description: If true, shows the toggle favorite button and favorite list on the left side of the dialog.

recent_list_enabled.description: If true, shows the recent directories list on the left side of the dialog.

layout_toggle_enabled.description: If true, shows the layout switch buttons (list/thumbnails).

overwrite_warning_enabled.description: If true, the  will warn the user before overwriting files in save mode.

deleting_enabled.description: If true, the context menu will show the "Delete" option, which allows moving files and folders to trash.

current_dir.description:
The current working directory of the file dialog.
			Note: For native file dialogs, this property is only treated as a hint and may not be respected by specific OS implementations.

current_file.description: The currently selected file of the file dialog.

current_path.description: The currently selected file path of the file dialog.

FileSystemDock.brief_description: Godot editor's dock for managing files in the project.
FileSystemDock.description:
This class is available only in s and can't be instantiated. You can access it using EditorInterface.get_file_system_dock.
		While  doesn't expose any methods for file manipulation, it can listen for various file-related signals.

navigate_to_path.description: Sets the given path as currently selected, ensuring that the selected file/directory is visible.

remove_resource_tooltip_plugin.description: Removes an . Fails if the plugin wasn't previously added.

FlowContainer.brief_description: A container that arranges its child controls horizontally or vertically and wraps them around at the borders.
FlowContainer.description: A container that arranges its child controls horizontally or vertically and wraps them around at the borders. This is similar to how text in a book wraps around when no more words can fit on a line.

alignment.description: The alignment of the container's children (must be one of , , or ).

last_wrap_alignment.description: The wrap behavior of the last, partially filled row or column (must be one of , , , or ).

vertical.description:
If true, the  will arrange its children vertically, rather than horizontally.
			Can't be changed when using  and .

reverse_fill.description:
If true, reverses fill direction. Horizontal s will fill rows bottom to top, vertical s will fill columns right to left.
			When using a vertical  with a right to left Control.layout_direction, columns will fill left to right instead.

FogMaterial.brief_description: A material that controls how volumetric fog is rendered, to be assigned to a .
FogMaterial.description:
A  resource that can be used by s to draw volumetric effects.
		If you need more advanced effects, use a custom fog shader.

density.description:
The density of the . Denser objects are more opaque, but may suffer from under-sampling artifacts that look like stripes. Negative values can be used to subtract fog from other s or global volumetric fog.
			Note: Due to limited precision, density values between -0.001 and 0.001 (exclusive) act like 0.0. This does not apply to Environment.volumetric_fog_density.

albedo.description: The single-scattering  of the . Internally, albedo is converted into single-scattering, which is additively blended with other s and the Environment.volumetric_fog_albedo.

emission.description: The  of the light emitted by the . Emitted light will not cast light or shadows on other objects, but can be useful for modulating the  of the  independently from light sources.

height_falloff.description: The rate by which the height-based fog decreases in density as height increases in world space. A high falloff will result in a sharp transition, while a low falloff will result in a smoother transition. A value of 0.0 results in uniform-density fog. The height threshold is determined by the height of the associated .

edge_fade.description: The hardness of the edges of the . A higher value will result in softer edges, while a lower value will result in harder edges.

density_texture.description: The 3D texture that is used to scale the density of the . This can be used to vary fog density within the  with any kind of static pattern. For animated effects, consider using a custom fog shader.

FogVolume.brief_description: A region that contributes to the default volumetric fog from the world environment.
FogVolume.description:
s are used to add localized fog into the global volumetric fog effect. s can also remove volumetric fog from specific areas if using a  with a negative FogMaterial.density.
		Performance of s is directly related to their relative size on the screen and the complexity of their attached . It is best to keep s relatively small and simple where possible.
		Note: s only have a visible effect if Environment.volumetric_fog_enabled is true. If you don't want fog to be globally visible (but only within  nodes), set Environment.volumetric_fog_density to 0.0.

size.description:
The size of the  when shape is , ,  or .
			Note: Thin fog volumes may appear to flicker when the camera moves or rotates. This can be alleviated by increasing ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/volumetric_fog/volume_depth (at a performance cost) or by decreasing Environment.volumetric_fog_length (at no performance cost, but at the cost of lower fog range). Alternatively, the  can be made thicker and use a lower density in the material.
			Note: If shape is  or , the cone/cylinder will be adjusted to fit within the size. Non-uniform scaling of cone/cylinder shapes via the size property is not supported, but you can scale the  node instead.

shape.description: The shape of the . This can be set to either , , ,  or .

material.description: The  used by the . Can be either a built-in  or a custom .

FoldableContainer.brief_description: A container that can be expanded/collapsed.
FoldableContainer.description:
A container that can be expanded/collapsed, with a title that can be filled with controls, such as buttons. This is also called an accordion.
		The title can be positioned at the top or bottom of the container. The container can be expanded or collapsed by clicking the title or by pressing ui_accept when focused. Child control nodes are hidden when the container is collapsed. Ignores non-control children.
		A FoldableContainer can be grouped with other FoldableContainers so that only one of them can be opened at a time; see foldable_group and .

add_title_bar_control.description:
Adds a  that will be placed next to the container's title, obscuring the clickable area. Prime usage is adding  nodes, but it can be any .
				The control will be added as a child of this container and removed from previous parent if necessary. The controls will be placed aligned to the right, with the first added control being the leftmost one.

remove_title_bar_control.description: Removes a  added with add_title_bar_control. The node is not freed automatically, you need to use Node.queue_free.

folded.description: If true, the container will becomes folded and will hide all its children.

title_text_overrun_behavior.description: Defines the behavior of the title when the text is longer than the available space.

foldable_group.description: The  associated with the container. When multiple  nodes share the same group, only one of them is allowed to be unfolded.

language.description: Language code used for text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.

FoldableGroup.brief_description: A group of foldable containers that doesn't allow more than one container to be expanded at a time.
FoldableGroup.description: A group of -derived nodes. Only one container can be expanded at a time.

get_containers.description: Returns an  of s that have this as their FoldableGroup (see FoldableContainer.foldable_group). This is equivalent to  but for FoldableContainers.

allow_folding_all.description: If true, it is possible to fold all containers in this FoldableGroup.

Font.brief_description: Abstract base class for fonts and font variations.
Font.description: Abstract base class for different font types. It has methods for drawing text and font character introspection.

find_variation.description: Returns  RID of the font cache for specific variation.

get_rids.description: Returns  of valid  s, which can be passed to the  methods.

get_height.description:
Returns the total average font height (ascent plus descent) in pixels.
				Note: Real height of the string is context-dependent and can be significantly different from the value returned by this function. Use it only as rough estimate (e.g. as the height of empty line).

get_ascent.description:
Returns the average font ascent (number of pixels above the baseline).
				Note: Real ascent of the string is context-dependent and can be significantly different from the value returned by this function. Use it only as rough estimate (e.g. as the ascent of empty line).

get_descent.description:
Returns the average font descent (number of pixels below the baseline).
				Note: Real descent of the string is context-dependent and can be significantly different from the value returned by this function. Use it only as rough estimate (e.g. as the descent of empty line).

get_underline_position.description:
Returns average pixel offset of the underline below the baseline.
				Note: Real underline position of the string is context-dependent and can be significantly different from the value returned by this function. Use it only as rough estimate.

get_underline_thickness.description:
Returns average thickness of the underline.
				Note: Real underline thickness of the string is context-dependent and can be significantly different from the value returned by this function. Use it only as rough estimate.

get_ot_name_strings.description: Returns  with OpenType font name strings (localized font names, version, description, license information, sample text, etc.).

get_font_weight.description: Returns weight (boldness) of the font. A value in the 100...999 range, normal font weight is 400, bold font weight is 700.

get_font_stretch.description: Returns font stretch amount, compared to a normal width. A percentage value between 50% and 200%.

get_spacing.description: Returns the amount of spacing for the given spacing type.

get_opentype_features.description: Returns a set of OpenType feature tags. More info: OpenType feature tags.

set_cache_capacity.description: Sets LRU cache capacity for draw_* methods.

get_multiline_string_size.description:
Returns the size of a bounding box of a string broken into the lines, taking kerning and advance into account.
				See also draw_multiline_string.

draw_string.description:
Draw text into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color, optionally clipping the width and aligning horizontally. pos specifies the baseline, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
				See also CanvasItem.draw_string.

draw_multiline_string.description:
Breaks text into lines using rules specified by brk_flags and draws it into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color, optionally clipping the width and aligning horizontally. pos specifies the baseline of the first line, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
				See also CanvasItem.draw_multiline_string.

draw_string_outline.description:
Draw text outline into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color and size outline size, optionally clipping the width and aligning horizontally. pos specifies the baseline, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
				See also CanvasItem.draw_string_outline.

draw_multiline_string_outline.description:
Breaks text to the lines using rules specified by brk_flags and draws text outline into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color and size outline size, optionally clipping the width and aligning horizontally. pos specifies the baseline of the first line, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
				See also CanvasItem.draw_multiline_string_outline.

get_char_size.description:
Returns the size of a character. Does not take kerning into account.
				Note: Do not use this function to calculate width of the string character by character, use get_string_size or  instead. The height returned is the font height (see also get_height) and has no relation to the glyph height.

draw_char.description:
Draw a single Unicode character char into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color. pos specifies the baseline, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
				Note: Do not use this function to draw strings character by character, use draw_string or  instead.

draw_char_outline.description:
Draw a single Unicode character char outline into a canvas item using the font, at a given position, with modulate color and size outline size. pos specifies the baseline, not the top. To draw from the top, ascent must be added to the Y axis. If oversampling is greater than zero, it is used as font oversampling factor, otherwise viewport oversampling settings are used.
				Note: Do not use this function to draw strings character by character, use draw_string or  instead.

has_char.description: Returns true if a Unicode char is available in the font.

get_supported_chars.description:
Returns a string containing all the characters available in the font.
				If a given character is included in more than one font data source, it appears only once in the returned string.

is_language_supported.description: Returns true if the font supports the given language (as a ISO 639 code).

is_script_supported.description: Returns true if the font supports the given script (as a ISO 15924 code).

get_supported_feature_list.description: Returns list of OpenType features supported by font.

get_face_count.description: Returns number of faces in the TrueType / OpenType collection.

fallbacks.description:
Array of fallback s to use as a substitute if a glyph is not found in this current .
			If this array is empty in a , the FontVariation.base_font's fallbacks are used instead.

FontFile.brief_description: Holds font source data and prerendered glyph cache, imported from a dynamic or a bitmap font.
FontFile.description:
contains a set of glyphs to represent Unicode characters imported from a font file, as well as a cache of rasterized glyphs, and a set of fallback s to use.
		Use  to access specific OpenType variation of the font, create simulated bold / slanted version, and draw lines of text.
		For more complex text processing, use  in conjunction with  or .
		Supported font formats:
		- Dynamic font importer: TrueType (.ttf), TrueType collection (.ttc), OpenType (.otf), OpenType collection (.otc), WOFF (.woff), WOFF2 (.woff2), Type 1 (.pfb, .pfm).
		- Bitmap font importer: AngelCode BMFont (.fnt, .font), text and binary (version 3) format variants.
		- Monospace image font importer: All supported image formats.
		Note: A character is a symbol that represents an item (letter, digit etc.) in an abstract way.
		Note: A glyph is a bitmap or a shape used to draw one or more characters in a context-dependent manner. Glyph indices are bound to the specific font data source.
		Note: If none of the font data sources contain glyphs for a character used in a string, the character in question will be replaced with a box displaying its hexadecimal code.
		
		
		var f = load("res://BarlowCondensed-Bold.ttf")
		$Label.add_theme_font_override("font", f)
		$Label.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 64)
		
		
		var f = ResourceLoader.Load<FontFile>("res://BarlowCondensed-Bold.ttf");
		GetNode("Label").AddThemeFontOverride("font", f);
		GetNode("Label").AddThemeFontSizeOverride("font_size", 64);

load_bitmap_font.description:
Loads an AngelCode BMFont (.fnt, .font) bitmap font from file path.
				Warning: This method should only be used in the editor or in cases when you need to load external fonts at run-time, such as fonts located at the user:// directory.

load_dynamic_font.description:
Loads a TrueType (.ttf), OpenType (.otf), WOFF (.woff), WOFF2 (.woff2) or Type 1 (.pfb, .pfm) dynamic font from file path.
				Warning: This method should only be used in the editor or in cases when you need to load external fonts at run-time, such as fonts located at the user:// directory.

get_cache_count.description: Returns number of the font cache entries.

get_size_cache_list.description: Returns list of the font sizes in the cache. Each size is  with font size and outline size.

clear_size_cache.description: Removes all font sizes from the cache entry.

remove_size_cache.description: Removes specified font size from the cache entry.

set_variation_coordinates.description: Sets variation coordinates for the specified font cache entry. See Font.get_supported_variation_list for more info.

get_variation_coordinates.description: Returns variation coordinates for the specified font cache entry. See Font.get_supported_variation_list for more info.

set_embolden.description: Sets embolden strength, if is not equal to zero, emboldens the font outlines. Negative values reduce the outline thickness.

get_embolden.description: Returns embolden strength, if is not equal to zero, emboldens the font outlines. Negative values reduce the outline thickness.

set_transform.description: Sets 2D transform, applied to the font outlines, can be used for slanting, flipping, and rotating glyphs.

get_transform.description: Returns 2D transform, applied to the font outlines, can be used for slanting, flipping and rotating glyphs.

set_extra_spacing.description: Sets the spacing for spacing to value in pixels (not relative to the font size).

get_extra_spacing.description: Returns spacing for spacing in pixels (not relative to the font size).

set_extra_baseline_offset.description: Sets extra baseline offset (as a fraction of font height).

get_extra_baseline_offset.description: Returns extra baseline offset (as a fraction of font height).

set_face_index.description: Sets an active face index in the TrueType / OpenType collection.

get_face_index.description: Returns an active face index in the TrueType / OpenType collection.

set_cache_ascent.description: Sets the font ascent (number of pixels above the baseline).

get_cache_ascent.description: Returns the font ascent (number of pixels above the baseline).

set_cache_descent.description: Sets the font descent (number of pixels below the baseline).

get_cache_descent.description: Returns the font descent (number of pixels below the baseline).

set_cache_underline_position.description: Sets pixel offset of the underline below the baseline.

get_cache_underline_position.description: Returns pixel offset of the underline below the baseline.

set_cache_underline_thickness.description: Sets thickness of the underline in pixels.

get_cache_underline_thickness.description: Returns thickness of the underline in pixels.

set_cache_scale.description: Sets scaling factor of the color bitmap font.

get_cache_scale.description: Returns scaling factor of the color bitmap font.

get_texture_count.description: Returns number of textures used by font cache entry.

clear_textures.description:
Removes all textures from font cache entry.
				Note: This function will not remove glyphs associated with the texture, use remove_glyph to remove them manually.

remove_texture.description:
Removes specified texture from the cache entry.
				Note: This function will not remove glyphs associated with the texture. Remove them manually using remove_glyph.

get_texture_image.description: Returns a copy of the font cache texture image.

set_texture_offsets.description: Sets array containing glyph packing data.

get_texture_offsets.description: Returns a copy of the array containing glyph packing data.

get_glyph_list.description: Returns list of rendered glyphs in the cache entry.

clear_glyphs.description:
Removes all rendered glyph information from the cache entry.
				Note: This function will not remove textures associated with the glyphs, use remove_texture to remove them manually.

remove_glyph.description:
Removes specified rendered glyph information from the cache entry.
				Note: This function will not remove textures associated with the glyphs, use remove_texture to remove them manually.

set_glyph_advance.description:
Sets glyph advance (offset of the next glyph).
				Note: Advance for glyphs outlines is the same as the base glyph advance and is not saved.

get_glyph_advance.description:
Returns glyph advance (offset of the next glyph).
				Note: Advance for glyphs outlines is the same as the base glyph advance and is not saved.

set_glyph_offset.description: Sets glyph offset from the baseline.

get_glyph_offset.description: Returns glyph offset from the baseline.

set_glyph_uv_rect.description: Sets rectangle in the cache texture containing the glyph.

get_glyph_uv_rect.description: Returns rectangle in the cache texture containing the glyph.

set_glyph_texture_idx.description: Sets index of the cache texture containing the glyph.

get_glyph_texture_idx.description: Returns index of the cache texture containing the glyph.

get_kerning_list.description: Returns list of the kerning overrides.

remove_kerning.description: Removes kerning override for the pair of glyphs.

set_kerning.description: Sets kerning for the pair of glyphs.

get_kerning.description: Returns kerning for the pair of glyphs.

render_range.description: Renders the range of characters to the font cache texture.

render_glyph.description: Renders specified glyph to the font cache texture.

get_language_support_override.description: Returns true if support override is enabled for the language.

get_language_support_overrides.description: Returns list of language support overrides.

get_script_support_override.description: Returns true if support override is enabled for the script.

get_script_support_overrides.description: Returns list of script support overrides.

get_glyph_index.description: Returns the glyph index of a char, optionally modified by the variation_selector.

get_char_from_glyph_index.description: Returns character code associated with glyph_index, or 0 if glyph_index is invalid. See get_glyph_index.

data.description: Contents of the dynamic font source file.

generate_mipmaps.description: If set to true, generate mipmaps for the font textures.

disable_embedded_bitmaps.description: If set to true, embedded font bitmap loading is disabled (bitmap-only and color fonts ignore this property).

font_weight.description: Weight (boldness) of the font. A value in the 100...999 range, normal font weight is 400, bold font weight is 700.

font_stretch.description: Font stretch amount, compared to a normal width. A percentage value between 50% and 200%.

subpixel_positioning.description: Font glyph subpixel positioning mode. Subpixel positioning provides shaper text and better kerning for smaller font sizes, at the cost of higher memory usage and lower font rasterization speed. Use  to automatically enable it based on the font size.

keep_rounding_remainders.description: If set to true, when aligning glyphs to the pixel boundaries rounding remainders are accumulated to ensure more uniform glyph distribution. This setting has no effect if subpixel positioning is enabled.

multichannel_signed_distance_field.description:
If set to true, glyphs of all sizes are rendered using single multichannel signed distance field (MSDF) generated from the dynamic font vector data. Since this approach does not rely on rasterizing the font every time its size changes, this allows for resizing the font in real-time without any performance penalty. Text will also not look grainy for s that are scaled down (or for s viewed from a long distance). As a downside, font hinting is not available with MSDF. The lack of font hinting may result in less crisp and less readable fonts at small sizes.
			Note: If using font outlines, msdf_pixel_range must be set to at least twice the size of the largest font outline.
			Note: MSDF font rendering does not render glyphs with overlapping shapes correctly. Overlapping shapes are not valid per the OpenType standard, but are still commonly found in many font files, especially those converted by Google Fonts. To avoid issues with overlapping glyphs, consider downloading the font file directly from the type foundry instead of relying on Google Fonts.

msdf_pixel_range.description: The width of the range around the shape between the minimum and maximum representable signed distance. If using font outlines, msdf_pixel_range must be set to at least twice the size of the largest font outline. The default msdf_pixel_range value of 16 allows outline sizes up to 8 to look correct.

msdf_size.description: Source font size used to generate MSDF textures. Higher values allow for more precision, but are slower to render and require more memory. Only increase this value if you notice a visible lack of precision in glyph rendering.

allow_system_fallback.description: If set to true, system fonts can be automatically used as fallbacks.

force_autohinter.description: If set to true, auto-hinting is supported and preferred over font built-in hinting. Used by dynamic fonts only (MSDF fonts don't support hinting).

modulate_color_glyphs.description: If set to true, color modulation is applied when drawing colored glyphs, otherwise it's applied to the monochrome glyphs only.

hinting.description: Font hinting mode. Used by dynamic fonts only.

fixed_size.description: Font size, used only for the bitmap fonts.

fixed_size_scale_mode.description: Scaling mode, used only for the bitmap fonts with fixed_size greater than zero.

oversampling.description: If set to a positive value, overrides the oversampling factor of the viewport this font is used in. See Viewport.oversampling. This value doesn't override the oversampling parameter of draw_* methods.

FontVariation.brief_description: A variation of a font with additional settings.

set_spacing.description: Sets the spacing for spacing to value in pixels (not relative to the font size).

base_font.description: Base font used to create a variation. If not set, default  font is used.

variation_opentype.description:
Font OpenType variation coordinates. More info: OpenType variation tags.
			Note: This  uses OpenType tags as keys. Variation axes can be identified both by tags (, e.g. 0x77678674) and names (, e.g. wght). Some axes might be accessible by multiple names. For example, wght refers to the same axis as weight. Tags on the other hand are unique. To convert between names and tags, use TextServer.name_to_tag and TextServer.tag_to_name.
			Note: To get available variation axes of a font, use Font.get_supported_variation_list.

variation_face_index.description: Active face index in the TrueType / OpenType collection file.

variation_embolden.description:
If is not equal to zero, emboldens the font outlines. Negative values reduce the outline thickness.
			Note: Emboldened fonts might have self-intersecting outlines, which will prevent MSDF fonts and  from working correctly.

variation_transform.description:
2D transform, applied to the font outlines, can be used for slanting, flipping and rotating glyphs.
			For example, to simulate italic typeface by slanting, apply the following transform Transform2D(1.0, slant, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0).

opentype_features.description: A set of OpenType feature tags. More info: OpenType feature tags.

spacing_space.description: Extra width of the space glyphs.

spacing_top.description: Extra spacing at the top of the line in pixels.

spacing_bottom.description: Extra spacing at the bottom of the line in pixels.

baseline_offset.description: Extra baseline offset (as a fraction of font height).

FramebufferCacheRD.brief_description: Framebuffer cache manager for Rendering Device based renderers.
FramebufferCacheRD.description: Framebuffer cache manager for -based renderers. Provides a way to create a framebuffer and reuse it in subsequent calls for as long as the used textures exists. Framebuffers will automatically be cleaned up when dependent objects are freed.

get_cache_multipass.description: Creates, or obtains a cached, framebuffer. textures lists textures accessed. passes defines the subpasses and texture allocation, if left empty a single pass is created and textures are allocated depending on their usage flags. views defines the number of views used when rendering.

GDExtension.description:
The  resource type represents a shared library which can expand the functionality of the engine. The  singleton is responsible for loading, reloading, and unloading  resources.
		Note: GDExtension itself is not a scripting language and has no relation to  resources.

is_library_open.description: Returns true if this extension's library has been opened.

get_minimum_library_initialization_level.description: Returns the lowest level required for this extension to be properly initialized (see the  enum).

GDExtensionManager.description:
The GDExtensionManager loads, initializes, and keeps track of all available  libraries in the project.
		Note: Do not worry about GDExtension unless you know what you are doing.

load_extension.description: Loads an extension by absolute file path. The path needs to point to a valid . Returns  if successful.

load_extension_from_function.description: Loads the extension already in address space via the given path and initialization function. The path needs to be unique and start with "libgodot://". Returns  if successful.

reload_extension.description:
Reloads the extension at the given file path. The path needs to point to a valid , otherwise this method may return either  or .
				Note: You can only reload extensions in the editor. In release builds, this method always fails and returns .

unload_extension.description: Unloads an extension by file path. The path needs to point to an already loaded , otherwise this method returns .

is_extension_loaded.description: Returns true if the extension at the given file path has already been loaded successfully. See also get_loaded_extensions.

get_loaded_extensions.description: Returns the file paths of all currently loaded extensions.

get_extension.description: Returns the  at the given file path, or null if it has not been loaded or does not exist.

GPUParticles2D.description:
2D particle node used to create a variety of particle systems and effects.  features an emitter that generates some number of particles at a given rate.
		Use the process_material property to add a  to configure particle appearance and behavior. Alternatively, you can add a  which will be applied to all particles.
		2D particles can optionally collide with , but they don't collide with  nodes.

request_particles_process.description:
Requests the particles to process for extra process time during a single frame.
				Useful for particle playback, if used in combination with use_fixed_seed or by calling restart with parameter keep_seed set to true.

capture_rect.description:
Returns a rectangle containing the positions of all existing particles.
				Note: When using threaded rendering this method synchronizes the rendering thread. Calling it often may have a negative impact on performance.

restart.description:
Restarts the particle emission cycle, clearing existing particles. To avoid particles vanishing from the viewport, wait for the  signal before calling.
				Note: The  signal is only emitted by one_shot emitters.
				If keep_seed is true, the current random seed will be preserved. Useful for seeking and playback.

emit_particle.description:
Emits a single particle. Whether xform, velocity, color and custom are applied depends on the value of flags. See .
				The default ParticleProcessMaterial will overwrite color and use the contents of custom as (rotation, age, animation, lifetime).
				Note: emit_particle is only supported on the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility.

convert_from_particles.description: Sets this node's properties to match a given  node.

emitting.description:
If true, particles are being emitted. emitting can be used to start and stop particles from emitting. However, if one_shot is true setting emitting to true will not restart the emission cycle unless all active particles have finished processing. Use the  signal to be notified once all active particles finish processing.
			Note: For one_shot emitters, due to the particles being computed on the GPU, there may be a short period after receiving the  signal during which setting this to true will not restart the emission cycle.
			Tip: If your one_shot emitter needs to immediately restart emitting particles once  signal is received, consider calling restart instead of setting emitting.

amount.description:
The number of particles to emit in one emission cycle. The effective emission rate is (amount * amount_ratio) / lifetime particles per second. Higher values will increase GPU requirements, even if not all particles are visible at a given time or if amount_ratio is decreased.
			Note: Changing this value will cause the particle system to restart. To avoid this, change amount_ratio instead.

amount_ratio.description:
The ratio of particles that should actually be emitted. If set to a value lower than 1.0, this will set the amount of emitted particles throughout the lifetime to amount * amount_ratio. Unlike changing amount, changing amount_ratio while emitting does not affect already-emitted particles and doesn't cause the particle system to restart. amount_ratio can be used to create effects that make the number of emitted particles vary over time.
			Note: Reducing the amount_ratio has no performance benefit, since resources need to be allocated and processed for the total amount of particles regardless of the amount_ratio. If you don't intend to change the number of particles emitted while the particles are emitting, make sure amount_ratio is set to 1 and change amount to your liking instead.

sub_emitter.description:
Path to another  node that will be used as a subemitter (see ParticleProcessMaterial.sub_emitter_mode). Subemitters can be used to achieve effects such as fireworks, sparks on collision, bubbles popping into water drops, and more.
			Note: When sub_emitter is set, the target  node will no longer emit particles on its own.

texture.description:
Particle texture. If null, particles will be squares with a size of 1×1 pixels.
			Note: To use a flipbook texture, assign a new  to the 's CanvasItem.material property, then enable CanvasItemMaterial.particles_animation and set CanvasItemMaterial.particles_anim_h_frames, CanvasItemMaterial.particles_anim_v_frames, and CanvasItemMaterial.particles_anim_loop to match the flipbook texture.

lifetime.description: The amount of time each particle will exist (in seconds). The effective emission rate is (amount * amount_ratio) / lifetime particles per second.

interp_to_end.description:
Causes all the particles in this node to interpolate towards the end of their lifetime.
			Note: This only works when used with a . It needs to be manually implemented for custom process shaders.

one_shot.description: If true, only one emission cycle occurs. If set true during a cycle, emission will stop at the cycle's end.

preprocess.description:
Particle system starts as if it had already run for this many seconds.
			Note: This can be very expensive if set to a high number as it requires running the particle shader a number of times equal to the fixed_fps (or 30, if fixed_fps is 0) for every second. In extreme cases it can even lead to a GPU crash due to the volume of work done in a single frame.

speed_scale.description: Particle system's running speed scaling ratio. A value of 0 can be used to pause the particles.

explosiveness.description: How rapidly particles in an emission cycle are emitted. If greater than 0, there will be a gap in emissions before the next cycle begins.

use_fixed_seed.description: If true, particles will use the same seed for every simulation using the seed defined in seed. This is useful for situations where the visual outcome should be consistent across replays, for example when using Movie Maker mode.

seed.description: Sets the random seed used by the particle system. Only effective if use_fixed_seed is true.

fixed_fps.description: The particle system's frame rate is fixed to a value. For example, changing the value to 2 will make the particles render at 2 frames per second. Note this does not slow down the simulation of the particle system itself.

interpolate.description: Enables particle interpolation, which makes the particle movement smoother when their fixed_fps is lower than the screen refresh rate.

fract_delta.description: If true, results in fractional delta calculation which has a smoother particles display effect.

collision_base_size.description:
Multiplier for particle's collision radius. 1.0 corresponds to the size of the sprite. If particles appear to sink into the ground when colliding, increase this value. If particles appear to float when colliding, decrease this value. Only effective if ParticleProcessMaterial.collision_mode is  or .
			Note: Particles always have a spherical collision shape.

visibility_rect.description:
The  that determines the node's region which needs to be visible on screen for the particle system to be active.
			Grow the rect if particles suddenly appear/disappear when the node enters/exits the screen. The  can be grown via code or with the Particles → Generate Visibility Rect editor tool.

local_coords.description: If true, particles use the parent node's coordinate space (known as local coordinates). This will cause particles to move and rotate along the  node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated. If false, particles use global coordinates; they will not move or rotate along the  node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated.

trail_enabled.description:
If true, enables particle trails using a mesh skinning system.
			Note: Unlike , the number of trail sections and subdivisions is set with the trail_sections and trail_section_subdivisions properties.

trail_lifetime.description: The amount of time the particle's trail should represent (in seconds). Only effective if trail_enabled is true.

trail_sections.description: The number of sections to use for the particle trail rendering. Higher values can result in smoother trail curves, at the cost of performance due to increased mesh complexity. See also trail_section_subdivisions. Only effective if trail_enabled is true.

trail_section_subdivisions.description: The number of subdivisions to use for the particle trail rendering. Higher values can result in smoother trail curves, at the cost of performance due to increased mesh complexity. See also trail_sections. Only effective if trail_enabled is true.

process_material.description: for processing particles. Can be a  or a .

		Use process_material to add a  to configure particle appearance and behavior. Alternatively, you can add a  which will be applied to all particles.

set_draw_pass_mesh.description: Sets the  that is drawn at index pass.

get_draw_pass_mesh.description: Returns the  that is drawn at index pass.

			Note: This only works when used with a . It needs to be manually implemented for custom process shaders.

collision_base_size.description:
The base diameter for particle collision in meters. If particles appear to sink into the ground when colliding, increase this value. If particles appear to float when colliding, decrease this value. Only effective if ParticleProcessMaterial.collision_mode is  or .
			Note: Particles always have a spherical collision shape.

visibility_aabb.description:
The  that determines the node's region which needs to be visible on screen for the particle system to be active. GeometryInstance3D.extra_cull_margin is added on each of the AABB's axes. Particle collisions and attraction will only occur within this area.
			Grow the box if particles suddenly appear/disappear when the node enters/exits the screen. The  can be grown via code or with the Particles → Generate AABB editor tool.
			Note: visibility_aabb is overridden by GeometryInstance3D.custom_aabb if that property is set to a non-default value.
