scroll_hint_mode.description: The way which scroll hints (indicators that show that the content can still be scrolled in a certain direction) will be shown.

tile_scroll_hint.description: If true, the scroll hint texture will be tiled instead of stretched. See scroll_hint_mode.

item_count.description: The number of items currently in the list.

max_columns.description:
Maximum columns the list will have.
			If greater than zero, the content will be split among the specified columns.
			A value of zero means unlimited columns, i.e. all items will be put in the same row.

same_column_width.description:
Whether all columns will have the same width.
			If true, the width is equal to the largest column width of all columns.

fixed_column_width.description:
The width all columns will be adjusted to.
			A value of zero disables the adjustment, each item will have a width equal to the width of its content and the columns will have an uneven width.

icon_mode.description: The icon position, whether above or to the left of the text. See the  constants.

icon_scale.description: The scale of icon applied after fixed_icon_size and transposing takes effect.

fixed_icon_size.description:
The size all icons will be adjusted to.
			If either X or Y component is not greater than zero, icon size won't be affected.

IterateIK3D.brief_description: A  to approach the goal by repeating small rotations.
IterateIK3D.description:
Base class of  to approach the goal by repeating small rotations.
		Each bone chain (setting) has one effector, which is processed in order of the setting list. You can set some limitations for each joint.

set_target_node.description: Sets the target node that the end bone is trying to reach.

get_target_node.description: Returns the target node that the end bone is trying to reach.

set_joint_rotation_axis.description:
Sets the rotation axis at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
				The axes are based on the Skeleton3D.get_bone_rest's space, if axis is , you can specify any axis.
				Note: The rotation axis and the forward vector shouldn't be colinear to avoid unintended rotation since  does not factor in twisting forces.

get_joint_rotation_axis.description: Returns the rotation axis at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

set_joint_rotation_axis_vector.description:
Sets the rotation axis vector for the specified joint in the bone chain.
				This vector is normalized by an internal process and represents the axis around which the bone chain can rotate.
				If the vector length is 0, it is considered synonymous with .

get_joint_rotation_axis_vector.description:
Returns the rotation axis vector for the specified joint in the bone chain. This vector represents the axis around which the joint can rotate. It is determined based on the rotation axis set for the joint.
				If get_joint_rotation_axis is , this method returns Vector3(0, 0, 0).

set_joint_limitation.description: Sets the joint limitation at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

get_joint_limitation.description: Returns the joint limitation at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

set_joint_limitation_right_axis.description: Sets the joint limitation right axis at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

get_joint_limitation_right_axis.description: Returns the joint limitation right axis at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

set_joint_limitation_right_axis_vector.description: Sets the optional joint limitation right axis vector at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

get_joint_limitation_right_axis_vector.description:
Returns the joint limitation right axis vector at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
				If get_joint_limitation_right_axis is , this method returns Vector3(0, 0, 0).

set_joint_limitation_rotation_offset.description:
Sets the joint limitation rotation offset at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
				Rotation is done in the local space which is constructed by the bone direction (in general parent to child) as the +Y axis and get_joint_limitation_right_axis_vector as the +X axis.
				If the +X and +Y axes are not orthogonal, the +X axis is implicitly modified to make it orthogonal.
				Also, if the length of get_joint_limitation_right_axis_vector is zero, the space is created by rotating the bone rest using the shortest arc that rotates the +Y axis of the bone rest to match the bone direction.

get_joint_limitation_rotation_offset.description:
Returns the joint limitation rotation offset at joint in the bone chain's joint list.
				Rotation is done in the local space which is constructed by the bone direction (in general parent to child) as the +Y axis and get_joint_limitation_right_axis_vector as the +X axis.
				If the +X and +Y axes are not orthogonal, the +X axis is implicitly modified to make it orthogonal.
				Also, if the length of get_joint_limitation_right_axis_vector is zero, the space is created by rotating the bone rest using the shortest arc that rotates the +Y axis of the bone rest to match the bone direction.

max_iterations.description: The number of iteration loops used by the IK solver to produce more accurate results.

min_distance.description: The minimum distance between the end bone and the target. If the distance is below this value, the IK solver stops any further iterations.

angular_delta_limit.description:
The maximum amount each bone can rotate in a single iteration.
			Note: This limitation is applied during each iteration. For example, if max_iterations is 4 and angular_delta_limit is 5 degrees, the maximum rotation possible in a single frame is 20 degrees.

deterministic.description:
If false, the result is calculated from the previous frame's  result as the initial state.
			If true, the previous frame's  result is discarded. At this point, the new result is calculated from the bone pose excluding the  as the initial state. This means the result will be always equal as long as the target position and the previous bone pose are the same. However, if angular_delta_limit and max_iterations are set too small, the end bone of the chain will never reach the target.

JNISingleton.brief_description: Singleton that connects the engine with Android plugins to interface with native Android code.
JNISingleton.description: The JNISingleton is implemented only in the Android export. It's used to call methods and connect signals from an Android plugin written in Java or Kotlin. Methods and signals can be called and connected to the JNISingleton as if it is a Node. See Java Native Interface - Wikipedia for more information.

has_java_method.description: Returns true if the given method name exists in the JNISingleton's Java methods.

JSON.brief_description: Helper class for creating and parsing JSON data.
JSON.description:
The  class enables all data types to be converted to and from a JSON string. This is useful for serializing data, e.g. to save to a file or send over the network.
		stringify is used to convert any data type into a JSON string.
		parse is used to convert any existing JSON data into a  that can be used within Godot. If successfully parsed, use data to retrieve the , and use @GlobalScope.typeof to check if the Variant's type is what you expect. JSON Objects are converted into a , but JSON data can be used to store s, numbers, s and even just a boolean.
		
		var data_to_send = ["a", "b", "c"]
		var json_string = JSON.stringify(data_to_send)
		# Save data
		# ...
		# Retrieve data
		var json = JSON.new()
		var error = json.parse(json_string)
		if error == OK:
			var data_received = json.data
			if typeof(data_received) == TYPE_ARRAY:
				print(data_received) # Prints the array.
			else:
				print("Unexpected data")
		else:
			print("JSON Parse Error: ", json.get_error_message(), " in ", json_string, " at line ", json.get_error_line())
		
		Alternatively, you can parse strings using the static parse_string method, but it doesn't handle errors.
		
		var data = JSON.parse_string(json_string) # Returns null if parsing failed.
		
		Note: Both parse methods do not fully comply with the JSON specification:
		- Trailing commas in arrays or objects are ignored, instead of causing a parser error.
		- New line and tab characters are accepted in string literals, and are treated like their corresponding escape sequences \n and \t.
		- Numbers are parsed using String.to_float which is generally more lax than the JSON specification.
		- Certain errors, such as invalid Unicode sequences, do not cause a parser error. Instead, the string is cleaned up and an error is logged to the console.

parse_string.description: Attempts to parse the json_string provided and returns the parsed data. Returns null if parse failed.

parse.description:
Attempts to parse the json_text provided.
				Returns an . If the parse was successful, it returns  and the result can be retrieved using data. If unsuccessful, use get_error_line and get_error_message to identify the source of the failure.
				Non-static variant of parse_string, if you want custom error handling.
				The optional keep_text argument instructs the parser to keep a copy of the original text. This text can be obtained later by using the get_parsed_text function and is used when saving the resource (instead of generating new text from data).

get_parsed_text.description: Return the text parsed by parse (requires passing keep_text to parse).

get_error_line.description: Returns 0 if the last call to parse was successful, or the line number where the parse failed.

get_error_message.description: Returns an empty string if the last call to parse was successful, or the error message if it failed.

data.description: Contains the parsed JSON data in  form.

JSONRPC.brief_description: A helper to handle dictionaries which look like JSONRPC documents.
JSONRPC.description: JSON-RPC is a standard which wraps a method call in a  object. The object has a particular structure and identifies which method is called, the parameters to that function, and carries an ID to keep track of responses. This class implements that standard on top of ; you will have to convert between a  and  with other functions.

set_method.description:
Registers a callback for the given method name.
				- name: The name that clients can use to access the callback.
				- callback: The callback which will handle the specified method.

process_action.description:
Given a Dictionary which takes the form of a JSON-RPC request: unpack the request and run it. Methods are resolved by looking at the field called "method" and looking for an equivalently named function in the JSONRPC object. If one is found that method is called.
				To add new supported methods extend the JSONRPC class and call process_action on your subclass.
				action: The action to be run, as a Dictionary in the form of a JSON-RPC request or notification.

make_request.description:
Returns a dictionary in the form of a JSON-RPC request. Requests are sent to a server with the expectation of a response. The ID field is used for the server to specify which exact request it is responding to.
				- method: Name of the method being called.
				- params: An array or dictionary of parameters being passed to the method.
				- id: Uniquely identifies this request. The server is expected to send a response with the same ID.

make_response.description:
When a server has received and processed a request, it is expected to send a response. If you did not want a response then you need to have sent a Notification instead.
				- result: The return value of the function which was called.
				- id: The ID of the request this response is targeted to.

make_notification.description:
Returns a dictionary in the form of a JSON-RPC notification. Notifications are one-shot messages which do not expect a response.
				- method: Name of the method being called.
				- params: An array or dictionary of parameters being passed to the method.

make_response_error.description:
Creates a response which indicates a previous reply has failed in some way.
				- code: The error code corresponding to what kind of error this is. See the  constants.
				- message: A custom message about this error.
				- id: The request this error is a response to.

JacobianIK3D.brief_description: Jacobian transpose based inverse kinematics solver.
JacobianIK3D.description:
calculates rotations for all joints simultaneously, producing natural and smooth movement. It is particularly suited for biological animations.
		The resulting twist around the forward vector will always be kept from the previous pose.
		Note: It converges more slowly than other IK solvers, leading to gentler and less immediate tracking of targets.

JavaClass.brief_description: Represents a class from the Java Native Interface.
JavaClass.description:
Represents a class from the Java Native Interface. It is returned from JavaClassWrapper.wrap.
		Note: This class only works on Android. On any other platform, this class does nothing.
		Note: This class is not to be confused with .

get_java_method_list.description: Returns the object's Java methods and their signatures as an  of dictionaries, in the same format as Object.get_method_list.

get_java_parent_class.description: Returns a  representing the Java parent class of this class.

has_java_method.description: Returns true if the given method name exists in the object's Java methods.

JavaClassWrapper.brief_description: Provides access to the Java Native Interface.

get_exception.description:
Returns the Java exception from the last call into a Java class. If there was no exception, it will return null.
				Note: This method only works on Android. On every other platform, this method will always return null.

JavaObject.brief_description: Represents an object from the Java Native Interface.
JavaObject.description:
Represents an object from the Java Native Interface. It can be returned from Java methods called on  or other s. See  for an example.
		Note: This class only works on Android. On any other platform, this class does nothing.
		Note: This class is not to be confused with .

get_java_class.description: Returns the  that this object is an instance of.

has_java_method.description: Returns true if the given method name exists in the object's Java methods.

JavaScriptBridge.brief_description: Singleton that connects the engine with the browser's JavaScript context in Web export.
JavaScriptBridge.description:
The JavaScriptBridge singleton is implemented only in the Web export. It's used to access the browser's JavaScript context. This allows interaction with embedding pages or calling third-party JavaScript APIs.
		Note: This singleton can be disabled at build-time to improve security. By default, the JavaScriptBridge singleton is enabled. Official export templates also have the JavaScriptBridge singleton enabled. See Compiling for the Web in the documentation for more information.

eval.description:
Execute the string code as JavaScript code within the browser window. This is a call to the actual global JavaScript function eval().
				If use_global_execution_context is true, the code will be evaluated in the global execution context. Otherwise, it is evaluated in the execution context of a function within the engine's runtime environment.

get_interface.description: Returns an interface to a JavaScript object that can be used by scripts. The interface must be a valid property of the JavaScript window. The callback must accept a single  argument, which will contain the JavaScript arguments. See  for usage.

create_callback.description:
Creates a reference to a  that can be used as a callback by JavaScript. The reference must be kept until the callback happens, or it won't be called at all. See  for usage.
				Note: The callback function must take exactly one  argument, which is going to be the JavaScript arguments object converted to an array.

is_js_buffer.description: Returns true if the given javascript_object is of type ArrayBuffer, DataView, or one of the many typed array objects.

js_buffer_to_packed_byte_array.description: Returns a copy of javascript_buffer's contents as a . See also is_js_buffer.

create_object.description: Creates a new JavaScript object using the new constructor. The object must a valid property of the JavaScript window. See  for usage.

download_buffer.description:
Prompts the user to download a file containing the specified buffer. The file will have the given name and mime type.
				Note: The browser may override the MIME type provided based on the file name's extension.
				Note: Browsers might block the download if download_buffer is not being called from a user interaction (e.g. button click).
				Note: Browsers might ask the user for permission or block the download if multiple download requests are made in a quick succession.

pwa_needs_update.description:
Returns true if a new version of the progressive web app is waiting to be activated.
				Note: Only relevant when exported as a Progressive Web App.

pwa_update.description:
Performs the live update of the progressive web app. Forcing the new version to be installed and the page to be reloaded.
				Note: Your application will be reloaded in all browser tabs.
				Note: Only relevant when exported as a Progressive Web App and pwa_needs_update returns true.

force_fs_sync.description:
Force synchronization of the persistent file system (when enabled).
				Note: This is only useful for modules or extensions that can't use  to write files.

JavaScriptObject.brief_description: A wrapper class for web native JavaScript objects.
JavaScriptObject.description:
JavaScriptObject is used to interact with JavaScript objects retrieved or created via JavaScriptBridge.get_interface, JavaScriptBridge.create_object, or JavaScriptBridge.create_callback.
		
		extends Node

		var _my_js_callback = JavaScriptBridge.create_callback(myCallback) # This reference must be kept
		var console = JavaScriptBridge.get_interface("console")

		func _init():
			var buf = JavaScriptBridge.create_object("ArrayBuffer", 10) # new ArrayBuffer(10)
			print(buf) # Prints 
			var uint8arr = JavaScriptBridge.create_object("Uint8Array", buf) # new Uint8Array(buf)
			uint8arr = 255
			prints(uint8arr, uint8arr.byteLength) # Prints "255 10"

			# Prints "Uint8Array(10) [ 0, 255, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 ]" in the browser's console.
			console.log(uint8arr)

			# Equivalent of JavaScriptBridge: Array.from(uint8arr).forEach(myCallback)
			JavaScriptBridge.get_interface("Array").from(uint8arr).forEach(_my_js_callback)

		func myCallback(args):
			# Will be called with the parameters passed to the "forEach" callback
			# ]
			# ]
			# ...
			# ]
			print(args)
		
		Note: Only available in the Web platform.

Joint2D.brief_description: Abstract base class for all 2D physics joints.
Joint2D.description: Abstract base class for all joints in 2D physics. 2D joints bind together two physics bodies (node_a and node_b) and apply a constraint.

get_rid.description: Returns the joint's internal  from the .

node_a.description: Path to the first body (A) attached to the joint. The node must inherit .

node_b.description: Path to the second body (B) attached to the joint. The node must inherit .

bias.description:
When node_a and node_b move in different directions the bias controls how fast the joint pulls them back to their original position. The lower the bias the more the two bodies can pull on the joint.
			When set to 0, the default value from ProjectSettings.physics/2d/solver/default_constraint_bias is used.

disable_collision.description: If true, the two bodies bound together do not collide with each other.

Joint3D.brief_description: Abstract base class for all 3D physics joints.
Joint3D.description: Abstract base class for all joints in 3D physics. 3D joints bind together two physics bodies (node_a and node_b) and apply a constraint. If only one body is defined, it is attached to a fixed  without collision shapes.

get_rid.description: Returns the joint's internal  from the .

node_a.description:
Path to the first node (A) attached to the joint. The node must inherit .
			If left empty and node_b is set, the body is attached to a fixed  without collision shapes.

node_b.description:
Path to the second node (B) attached to the joint. The node must inherit .
			If left empty and node_a is set, the body is attached to a fixed  without collision shapes.

solver_priority.description: The priority used to define which solver is executed first for multiple joints. The lower the value, the higher the priority.

exclude_nodes_from_collision.description: If true, the two bodies bound together do not collide with each other.

JointLimitation3D.brief_description: A base class of the limitation that interacts with .
JointLimitation3D.description: The limitation is attached to each joint and limits the rotation of the bone.

JointLimitationCone3D.brief_description: A cone shape limitation that interacts with .
JointLimitationCone3D.description: A cone shape limitation that interacts with .

angle.description:
The radius range of the hole made by the cone.
			0 degrees makes a sphere without hole, 180 degrees makes a hemisphere, and 360 degrees become empty (no limitation).

KinematicCollision2D.brief_description: Holds collision data from the movement of a .
KinematicCollision2D.description:
Holds collision data from the movement of a , usually from PhysicsBody2D.move_and_collide. When a  is moved, it stops if it detects a collision with another body. If a collision is detected, a  object is returned.
		The collision data includes the colliding object, the remaining motion, and the collision position. This data can be used to determine a custom response to the collision.

get_position.description: Returns the point of collision in global coordinates.

get_normal.description: Returns the colliding body's shape's normal at the point of collision.

get_travel.description: Returns the moving object's travel before collision.

get_remainder.description: Returns the moving object's remaining movement vector.

get_angle.description: Returns the collision angle according to up_direction, which is  by default. This value is always positive.

get_depth.description: Returns the colliding body's length of overlap along the collision normal.

get_local_shape.description: Returns the moving object's colliding shape.

get_collider_id.description: Returns the unique instance ID of the colliding body's attached . See Object.get_instance_id.

get_collider_rid.description: Returns the colliding body's  used by the .

get_collider_shape_index.description: Returns the colliding body's shape index. See .

KinematicCollision3D.brief_description: Holds collision data from the movement of a .
KinematicCollision3D.description:
Holds collision data from the movement of a , usually from PhysicsBody3D.move_and_collide. When a  is moved, it stops if it detects a collision with another body. If a collision is detected, a  object is returned.
		The collision data includes the colliding object, the remaining motion, and the collision position. This data can be used to determine a custom response to the collision.

get_travel.description: Returns the moving object's travel before collision.

get_remainder.description: Returns the moving object's remaining movement vector.

get_depth.description: Returns the colliding body's length of overlap along the collision normal.

get_collision_count.description: Returns the number of detected collisions.

get_position.description: Returns the point of collision in global coordinates given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).

get_normal.description: Returns the colliding body's shape's normal at the point of collision given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).

get_angle.description: Returns the collision angle according to up_direction, which is  by default. This value is always positive.

get_local_shape.description: Returns the moving object's colliding shape given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).

get_collider.description: Returns the colliding body's attached  given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).

get_collider_id.description: Returns the unique instance ID of the colliding body's attached  given a collision index (the deepest collision by default). See Object.get_instance_id.

get_collider_rid.description: Returns the colliding body's  used by the  given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).

get_collider_shape.description: Returns the colliding body's shape given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).

get_collider_shape_index.description: Returns the colliding body's shape index given a collision index (the deepest collision by default). See .

get_collider_velocity.description: Returns the colliding body's velocity given a collision index (the deepest collision by default).

Label.brief_description: A control for displaying plain text.
Label.description:
A control for displaying plain text. It gives you control over the horizontal and vertical alignment and can wrap the text inside the node's bounding rectangle. It doesn't support bold, italics, or other rich text formatting. For that, use  instead.
		Note: A single Label node is not designed to display huge amounts of text. To display large amounts of text in a single node, consider using  instead as it supports features like an integrated scroll bar and threading.  generally performs better when displaying large amounts of text (several pages or more).

get_line_height.description:
Returns the height of the line line.
				If line is set to -1, returns the biggest line height.
				If there are no lines, returns font size in pixels.

get_line_count.description: Returns the number of lines of text the Label has.

get_visible_line_count.description: Returns the number of lines shown. Useful if the 's height cannot currently display all lines.

get_total_character_count.description: Returns the total number of printable characters in the text (excluding spaces and newlines).

get_character_bounds.description: Returns the bounding rectangle of the character at position pos in the label's local coordinate system. If the character is a non-visual character or pos is outside the valid range, an empty  is returned. If the character is a part of a composite grapheme, the bounding rectangle of the whole grapheme is returned.

text.description: The text to display on screen.

label_settings.description: A  resource that can be shared between multiple  nodes. Takes priority over theme properties.

horizontal_alignment.description: Controls the text's horizontal alignment. Supports left, center, right, and fill (also known as justify).

vertical_alignment.description: Controls the text's vertical alignment. Supports top, center, bottom, and fill.

autowrap_mode.description: If set to something other than , the text gets wrapped inside the node's bounding rectangle. If you resize the node, it will change its height automatically to show all the text.

autowrap_trim_flags.description: Autowrap space trimming flags. See  and  for more info.

paragraph_separator.description: String used as a paragraph separator. Each paragraph is processed independently, in its own BiDi context.

clip_text.description: If true, the Label only shows the text that fits inside its bounding rectangle and will clip text horizontally.

text_overrun_behavior.description: The clipping behavior when the text exceeds the node's bounding rectangle.

ellipsis_char.description: Ellipsis character used for text clipping.

uppercase.description: If true, all the text displays as UPPERCASE.

tab_stops.description: Aligns text to the given tab-stops.

lines_skipped.description: The number of the lines ignored and not displayed from the start of the text value.

max_lines_visible.description: Limits the lines of text the node shows on screen.

visible_characters.description:
The number of characters to display. If set to -1, all characters are displayed. This can be useful when animating the text appearing in a dialog box.
			Note: Setting this property updates visible_ratio accordingly.
			Note: Characters are counted as Unicode codepoints. A single visible grapheme may contain multiple codepoints (e.g. certain emoji use three codepoints). A single codepoint may contain two UTF-16 characters, which are used in C# strings.

visible_characters_behavior.description: The clipping behavior when visible_characters or visible_ratio is set.

visible_ratio.description:
The fraction of characters to display, relative to the total number of characters (see get_total_character_count). If set to 1.0, all characters are displayed. If set to 0.5, only half of the characters will be displayed. This can be useful when animating the text appearing in a dialog box.
			Note: Setting this property updates visible_characters accordingly.

language.description: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.

structured_text_bidi_override.description: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text.

structured_text_bidi_override_options.description: Set additional options for BiDi override.

Label3D.brief_description: A node for displaying plain text in 3D space.
Label3D.description: A node for displaying plain text in 3D space. By adjusting various properties of this node, you can configure things such as the text's appearance and whether it always faces the camera.

set_draw_flag.description: If true, the specified flag will be enabled.

get_draw_flag.description: Returns the value of the specified flag.

generate_triangle_mesh.description: Returns a  with the label's vertices following its current configuration (such as its pixel_size).

pixel_size.description: The size of one pixel's width on the label to scale it in 3D. To make the font look more detailed when up close, increase font_size while decreasing pixel_size at the same time.

billboard.description: The billboard mode to use for the label.

shaded.description: If true, the  in the  has effects on the label.

double_sided.description: If true, text can be seen from the back as well, if false, it is invisible when looking at it from behind.

no_depth_test.description: If true, depth testing is disabled and the object will be drawn in render order.

fixed_size.description: If true, the label is rendered at the same size regardless of distance. The label's size on screen is the same as if the camera was 1.0 units away from the label's origin, regardless of the actual distance from the camera. The 's field of view (or Camera3D.size when in orthogonal/frustum mode) still affects the size the label is drawn at.

alpha_cut.description: The alpha cutting mode to use for the sprite.

alpha_scissor_threshold.description: Threshold at which the alpha scissor will discard values.

alpha_hash_scale.description: The hashing scale for Alpha Hash. Recommended values between 0 and 2.

alpha_antialiasing_mode.description: The type of alpha antialiasing to apply.

alpha_antialiasing_edge.description: Threshold at which antialiasing will be applied on the alpha channel.

render_priority.description:
Sets the render priority for the text. Higher priority objects will be sorted in front of lower priority objects.
			Note: This only applies if alpha_cut is set to  (default value).
			Note: This only applies to sorting of transparent objects. This will not impact how transparent objects are sorted relative to opaque objects. This is because opaque objects are not sorted, while transparent objects are sorted from back to front (subject to priority).

outline_render_priority.description:
Sets the render priority for the text outline. Higher priority objects will be sorted in front of lower priority objects.
			Note: This only applies if alpha_cut is set to  (default value).
			Note: This only applies to sorting of transparent objects. This will not impact how transparent objects are sorted relative to opaque objects. This is because opaque objects are not sorted, while transparent objects are sorted from back to front (subject to priority).

text.description: The text to display on screen.

font.description: Font configuration used to display text.

font_size.description:
Font size of the 's text. To make the font look more detailed when up close, increase font_size while decreasing pixel_size at the same time.
			Higher font sizes require more time to render new characters, which can cause stuttering during gameplay.

horizontal_alignment.description: Controls the text's horizontal alignment. Supports left, center, right, and fill (also known as justify).

vertical_alignment.description: Controls the text's vertical alignment. Supports top, center, and bottom.

uppercase.description: If true, all the text displays as UPPERCASE.

line_spacing.description: Additional vertical spacing between lines (in pixels), spacing is added to line descent. This value can be negative.

autowrap_mode.description: If set to something other than , the text gets wrapped inside the node's bounding rectangle. If you resize the node, it will change its height automatically to show all the text.

autowrap_trim_flags.description: Autowrap space trimming flags. See  and  for more info.

width.description: Text width (in pixels), used for autowrap and fill alignment.

language.description: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.

structured_text_bidi_override.description: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text.

structured_text_bidi_override_options.description: Set additional options for BiDi override.

LabelSettings.brief_description: Provides common settings to customize the text in a .
LabelSettings.description: is a resource that provides common settings to customize the text in a . It will take priority over the properties defined in Control.theme. The resource can be shared between multiple labels and changed on the fly, so it's convenient and flexible way to setup text style.

add_stacked_outline.description: Adds a new stacked outline to the label at the given index. If index is -1, the new stacked outline will be added at the end of the list.

move_stacked_outline.description: Moves the stacked outline at index from_index to the given position to_position in the array.

remove_stacked_outline.description: Removes the stacked outline at index index.

set_stacked_outline_size.description: Sets the size of the stacked outline identified by the given index to size.

get_stacked_outline_size.description: Returns the size of the stacked outline at index.

set_stacked_outline_color.description: Sets the color of the stacked outline identified by the given index to color.

get_stacked_outline_color.description: Returns the color of the stacked outline at index.

add_stacked_shadow.description: Adds a new stacked shadow to the label at the given index. If index is -1, the new stacked shadow will be added at the end of the list.

move_stacked_shadow.description: Moves the stacked shadow at index from_index to the given position to_position in the array.

remove_stacked_shadow.description: Removes the stacked shadow at index index.

set_stacked_shadow_offset.description: Sets the offset of the stacked shadow identified by the given index to offset.

get_stacked_shadow_offset.description: Returns the offset of the stacked shadow at index.

set_stacked_shadow_color.description: Sets the color of the stacked shadow identified by the given index to color.

get_stacked_shadow_color.description: Returns the color of the stacked shadow at index.

set_stacked_shadow_outline_size.description: Sets the outline size of the stacked shadow identified by the given index to size.

get_stacked_shadow_outline_size.description: Returns the outline size of the stacked shadow at index.

line_spacing.description: Additional vertical spacing between lines (in pixels), spacing is added to line descent. This value can be negative.

paragraph_spacing.description: Vertical space between paragraphs. Added on top of line_spacing.

shadow_color.description: Color of the shadow effect. If alpha is 0, no shadow will be drawn.

shadow_offset.description: Offset of the shadow effect, in pixels.

Light2D.description: Casts light in a 2D environment. A light is defined as a color, an energy value, a mode (see constants), and various other parameters (range and shadows-related).

set_height.description: Sets the light's height, which is used in 2D normal mapping. See PointLight2D.height and DirectionalLight2D.height.

get_height.description: Returns the light's height, which is used in 2D normal mapping. See PointLight2D.height and DirectionalLight2D.height.

enabled.description: If true, Light2D will emit light.

editor_only.description: If true, Light2D will only appear when editing the scene.

energy.description: The Light2D's energy value. The larger the value, the stronger the light.

range_z_min.description: Minimum z value of objects that are affected by the Light2D.

range_z_max.description: Maximum z value of objects that are affected by the Light2D.

range_layer_min.description: Minimum layer value of objects that are affected by the Light2D.

range_layer_max.description: Maximum layer value of objects that are affected by the Light2D.

range_item_cull_mask.description:
The layer mask. Only objects with a matching CanvasItem.light_mask will be affected by the Light2D. See also shadow_item_cull_mask, which affects which objects can cast shadows.
			Note: range_item_cull_mask is ignored by , which will always light a 2D node regardless of the 2D node's CanvasItem.light_mask.

shadow_enabled.description: If true, the Light2D will cast shadows.

shadow_color.description: of shadows cast by the Light2D.

shadow_filter_smooth.description: Smoothing value for shadows. Higher values will result in softer shadows, at the cost of visible streaks that can appear in shadow rendering. shadow_filter_smooth only has an effect if shadow_filter is  or .

shadow_item_cull_mask.description: The shadow mask. Used with  to cast shadows. Only occluders with a matching CanvasItem.light_mask will cast shadows. See also range_item_cull_mask, which affects which objects can receive the light.

Light3D.brief_description: Provides a base class for different kinds of light nodes.
Light3D.description: Light3D is the abstract base class for light nodes. As it can't be instantiated, it shouldn't be used directly. Other types of light nodes inherit from it. Light3D contains the common variables and parameters used for lighting.

set_param.description: Sets the value of the specified  parameter.

get_param.description: Returns the value of the specified  parameter.

get_correlated_color.description: Returns the  of an idealized blackbody at the given light_temperature. This value is calculated internally based on the light_temperature. This  is multiplied by light_color before being sent to the .

light_intensity_lumens.description:
Used by positional lights ( and ) when ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units is true. Sets the intensity of the light source measured in Lumens. Lumens are a measure of luminous flux, which is the total amount of visible light emitted by a light source per unit of time.
			For s, we assume that the area outside the visible cone is surrounded by a perfect light absorbing material. Accordingly, the apparent brightness of the cone area does not change as the cone increases and decreases in size.
			A typical household lightbulb can range from around 600 lumens to 1,200 lumens, a candle is about 13 lumens, while a streetlight can be approximately 60,000 lumens.

light_intensity_lux.description:
Used by s when ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units is true. Sets the intensity of the light source measured in Lux. Lux is a measure of luminous flux per unit area, it is equal to one lumen per square meter. Lux is the measure of how much light hits a surface at a given time.
			On a clear sunny day a surface in direct sunlight may be approximately 100,000 lux, a typical room in a home may be approximately 50 lux, while the moonlit ground may be approximately 0.1 lux.

light_temperature.description:
Sets the color temperature of the light source, measured in Kelvin. This is used to calculate a correlated color temperature which tints the light_color.
			The sun on a cloudy day is approximately 6500 Kelvin, on a clear day it is between 5500 to 6000 Kelvin, and on a clear day at sunrise or sunset it ranges to around 1850 Kelvin.

light_color.description: The light's color in nonlinear sRGB encoding. An overbright color can be used to achieve a result equivalent to increasing the light's light_energy.

light_energy.description: The light's strength multiplier (this is not a physical unit). For  and , changing this value will only change the light color's intensity, not the light's radius.

light_indirect_energy.description:
Secondary multiplier used with indirect light (light bounces). Used with  and SDFGI (see Environment.sdfgi_enabled).
			Note: This property is ignored if light_energy is equal to 0.0, as the light won't be present at all in the GI shader.

light_volumetric_fog_energy.description:
Secondary multiplier multiplied with light_energy then used with the 's volumetric fog (if enabled). If set to 0.0, computing volumetric fog will be skipped for this light, which can improve performance for large amounts of lights when volumetric fog is enabled.
			Note: To prevent short-lived dynamic light effects from poorly interacting with volumetric fog, lights used in those effects should have light_volumetric_fog_energy set to 0.0 unless Environment.volumetric_fog_temporal_reprojection_enabled is disabled (or unless the reprojection amount is significantly lowered).

light_projector.description:
projected by light. shadow_enabled must be on for the projector to work. Light projectors make the light appear as if it is shining through a colored but transparent object, almost like light shining through stained-glass.
			Note: Unlike  whose filter mode can be adjusted on a per-material basis, the filter mode for light projector textures is set globally with ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/light_projectors/filter.
			Note: Light projector textures are only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility.

light_size.description:
The size of the light in Godot units. Only available for s and s. Increasing this value will make the light fade out slower and shadows appear blurrier (also called percentage-closer soft shadows, or PCSS). This can be used to simulate area lights to an extent. Increasing this value above 0.0 for lights with shadows enabled will have a noticeable performance cost due to PCSS.
			Note: light_size is not affected by Node3D.scale (the light's scale or its parent's scale).
			Note: PCSS for positional lights is only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility.

light_angular_distance.description:
The light's angular size in degrees. Increasing this will make shadows softer at greater distances (also called percentage-closer soft shadows, or PCSS). Only available for s. For reference, the Sun from the Earth is approximately 0.5. Increasing this value above 0.0 for lights with shadows enabled will have a noticeable performance cost due to PCSS.
			Note: light_angular_distance is not affected by Node3D.scale (the light's scale or its parent's scale).
			Note: PCSS for directional lights is only supported in the Forward+ rendering method, not Mobile or Compatibility.

light_negative.description: If true, the light's effect is reversed, darkening areas and casting bright shadows.

light_specular.description: The intensity of the specular blob in objects affected by the light. At 0, the light becomes a pure diffuse light. When not baking emission, this can be used to avoid unrealistic reflections when placing lights above an emissive surface.

light_bake_mode.description:
The light's bake mode. This will affect the global illumination techniques that have an effect on the light's rendering.
			Note: Meshes' global illumination mode will also affect the global illumination rendering. See GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode.

light_cull_mask.description:
The light will affect objects in the selected layers.
			Note: The light cull mask is ignored by , SDFGI, , and volumetric fog. These will always render lights in a way that ignores the cull mask. See also VisualInstance3D.layers.

shadow_enabled.description: If true, the light will cast real-time shadows. This has a significant performance cost. Only enable shadow rendering when it makes a noticeable difference in the scene's appearance, and consider using distance_fade_enabled to hide the light when far away from the .

shadow_bias.description: Used to adjust shadow appearance. Too small a value results in self-shadowing ("shadow acne"), while too large a value causes shadows to separate from casters ("peter-panning"). Adjust as needed.

shadow_normal_bias.description: Offsets the lookup into the shadow map by the object's normal. This can be used to reduce self-shadowing artifacts without using shadow_bias. In practice, this value should be tweaked along with shadow_bias to reduce artifacts as much as possible.

shadow_reverse_cull_face.description: If true, reverses the backface culling of the mesh. This can be useful when you have a flat mesh that has a light behind it. If you need to cast a shadow on both sides of the mesh, set the mesh to use double-sided shadows with .

shadow_opacity.description: The opacity to use when rendering the light's shadow map. Values lower than 1.0 make the light appear through shadows. This can be used to fake global illumination at a low performance cost.

shadow_blur.description: Blurs the edges of the shadow. Can be used to hide pixel artifacts in low-resolution shadow maps. A high value can impact performance, make shadows appear grainy and can cause other unwanted artifacts. Try to keep as near default as possible.

shadow_caster_mask.description: The light will only cast shadows using objects in the selected layers.

distance_fade_enabled.description:
If true, the light will smoothly fade away when far from the active  starting at distance_fade_begin. This acts as a form of level of detail (LOD). The light will fade out over distance_fade_begin + distance_fade_length, after which it will be culled and not sent to the shader at all. Use this to reduce the number of active lights in a scene and thus improve performance.
			Note: Only effective for  and .

distance_fade_begin.description:
The distance from the camera at which the light begins to fade away (in 3D units).
			Note: Only effective for  and .

distance_fade_shadow.description:
The distance from the camera at which the light's shadow cuts off (in 3D units). Set this to a value lower than distance_fade_begin + distance_fade_length to further improve performance, as shadow rendering is often more expensive than light rendering itself.
			Note: Only effective for  and , and only when shadow_enabled is true.

distance_fade_length.description:
Distance over which the light and its shadow fades. The light's energy and shadow's opacity is progressively reduced over this distance and is completely invisible at the end.
			Note: Only effective for  and .

editor_only.description: If true, the light only appears in the editor and will not be visible at runtime. If true, the light will never be baked in  regardless of its light_bake_mode.

LightOccluder2D.brief_description: Occludes light cast by a Light2D, casting shadows.
LightOccluder2D.description: Occludes light cast by a Light2D, casting shadows. The LightOccluder2D must be provided with an  in order for the shadow to be computed.

occluder.description: The  used to compute the shadow.

sdf_collision.description: If enabled, the occluder will be part of a real-time generated signed distance field that can be used in custom shaders.

occluder_light_mask.description: The LightOccluder2D's occluder light mask. The LightOccluder2D will cast shadows only from Light2D(s) that have the same light mask(s).

LightmapGI.brief_description: Computes and stores baked lightmaps for fast global illumination.
LightmapGI.description:
The  node is used to compute and store baked lightmaps. Lightmaps are used to provide high-quality indirect lighting with very little light leaking.  can also provide rough reflections using spherical harmonics if directional is enabled. Dynamic objects can receive indirect lighting thanks to light probes, which can be automatically placed by setting generate_probes_subdiv to a value other than . Additional lightmap probes can also be added by creating  nodes. The downside is that lightmaps are fully static and cannot be baked in an exported project. Baking a  node is also slower compared to .
		Procedural generation: Lightmap baking functionality is only available in the editor. This means  is not suited to procedurally generated or user-built levels. For procedurally generated or user-built levels, use  or SDFGI instead (see Environment.sdfgi_enabled).
		Performance:  provides the best possible run-time performance for global illumination. It is suitable for low-end hardware including integrated graphics and mobile devices.
		Note: Due to how lightmaps work, most properties only have a visible effect once lightmaps are baked again.
		Note: Lightmap baking on s and es is not supported, as these cannot store UV2 data required for baking.
		Note: If no custom lightmappers are installed,  can only be baked from devices that support the Forward+ or Mobile renderers.
		Note: The  node only bakes light data for child nodes of its parent. Nodes further up the hierarchy of the scene will not be baked.

quality.description:
The quality preset to use when baking lightmaps. This affects bake times, but output file sizes remain mostly identical across quality levels.
			To further speed up bake times, decrease bounces, disable use_denoiser and/or decrease texel_scale.
			To further increase quality, enable supersampling and/or increase texel_scale.

supersampling.description:
If true, lightmaps are baked with the texel scale multiplied with supersampling_factor and downsampled before saving the lightmap (so the effective texel density is identical to having supersampling disabled).
			Supersampling provides increased lightmap quality with less noise, smoother shadows and better shadowing of small-scale features in objects. However, it may result in significantly increased bake times and memory usage while baking lightmaps. Padding is automatically adjusted to avoid increasing light leaking.

supersampling_factor.description:
The factor by which the texel density is multiplied for supersampling. For best results, use an integer value. While fractional values are allowed, they can result in increased light leaking and a blurry lightmap.
			Higher values may result in better quality, but also increase bake times and memory usage while baking.
			See supersampling for more information.

bounces.description: Number of light bounces that are taken into account during baking. Higher values result in brighter, more realistic lighting, at the cost of longer bake times. If set to 0, only environment lighting, direct light and emissive lighting is baked.

bounce_indirect_energy.description:
The energy multiplier for each bounce. Higher values will make indirect lighting brighter. A value of 1.0 represents physically accurate behavior, but higher values can be used to make indirect lighting propagate more visibly when using a low number of bounces. This can be used to speed up bake times by lowering the number of bounces then increasing bounce_indirect_energy.
			Note: bounce_indirect_energy only has an effect if bounces is set to a value greater than or equal to 1.

directional.description:
If true, bakes lightmaps to contain directional information as spherical harmonics. This results in more realistic lighting appearance, especially with normal mapped materials and for lights that have their direct light baked (Light3D.light_bake_mode set to  and with Light3D.editor_only set to false). The directional information is also used to provide rough reflections for static and dynamic objects. This has a small run-time performance cost as the shader has to perform more work to interpret the direction information from the lightmap. Directional lightmaps also take longer to bake and result in larger file sizes.
			Note: The property's name has no relationship with . directional works with all light types.

shadowmask_mode.description:
The shadowmasking policy to use for directional shadows on static objects that are baked with this  instance.
			Shadowmasking allows  nodes to cast shadows even outside the range defined by their DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_max_distance property. This is done by baking a texture that contains a shadowmap for the directional light, then using this texture according to the current shadowmask mode.
			Note: The shadowmask texture is only created if shadowmask_mode is not . To see a difference, you need to bake lightmaps again after switching from  to any other mode.

use_texture_for_bounces.description:
If true, a texture with the lighting information will be generated to speed up the generation of indirect lighting at the cost of some accuracy. The geometry might exhibit extra light leak artifacts when using low resolution lightmaps or UVs that stretch the lightmap significantly across surfaces. Leave use_texture_for_bounces at its default value of true if unsure.
			Note: use_texture_for_bounces only has an effect if bounces is set to a value greater than or equal to 1.

interior.description: If true, ignore environment lighting when baking lightmaps.

use_denoiser.description: If true, uses a GPU-based denoising algorithm on the generated lightmap. This eliminates most noise within the generated lightmap at the cost of longer bake times. File sizes are generally not impacted significantly by the use of a denoiser, although lossless compression may do a better job at compressing a denoised image.

denoiser_strength.description: The strength of denoising step applied to the generated lightmaps. Only effective if use_denoiser is true and ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/denoising/denoiser is set to JNLM.

denoiser_range.description: The distance in pixels from which the denoiser samples. Lower values preserve more details, but may give blotchy results if the lightmap quality is not high enough. Only effective if use_denoiser is true and ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/denoising/denoiser is set to JNLM.

bias.description: The bias to use when computing shadows. Increasing bias can fix shadow acne on the resulting baked lightmap, but can introduce peter-panning (shadows not connecting to their casters). Real-time  shadows are not affected by this bias property.

texel_scale.description:
Scales the lightmap texel density of all meshes for the current bake. This is a multiplier that builds upon the existing lightmap texel size defined in each imported 3D scene, along with the per-mesh density multiplier (which is designed to be used when the same mesh is used at different scales). Lower values will result in faster bake times.
			For example, doubling texel_scale doubles the lightmap texture resolution for all objects on each axis, so it will quadruple the texel count.

max_texture_size.description: The maximum texture size for the generated texture atlas. Higher values will result in fewer slices being generated, but may not work on all hardware as a result of hardware limitations on texture sizes. Leave max_texture_size at its default value of 16384 if unsure.

environment_mode.description: The environment mode to use when baking lightmaps.

environment_custom_sky.description: The sky to use as a source of environment lighting. Only effective if environment_mode is .

environment_custom_color.description: The color to use for environment lighting. Only effective if environment_mode is .

environment_custom_energy.description: The color multiplier to use for environment lighting. Only effective if environment_mode is .

camera_attributes.description: The  resource that specifies exposure levels to bake at. Auto-exposure and non exposure properties will be ignored. Exposure settings should be used to reduce the dynamic range present when baking. If exposure is too high, the  will have banding artifacts or may have over-exposure artifacts.

generate_probes_subdiv.description:
The level of subdivision to use when automatically generating s for dynamic object lighting. Higher values result in more accurate indirect lighting on dynamic objects, at the cost of longer bake times and larger file sizes.
			Note: Automatically generated s are not visible as nodes in the Scene tree dock, and cannot be modified this way after they are generated.
			Note: Regardless of generate_probes_subdiv, direct lighting on dynamic objects is always applied using  nodes in real-time.

light_data.description: The  associated to this  node. This resource is automatically created after baking, and is not meant to be created manually.

LightmapGIData.brief_description: Contains baked lightmap and dynamic object probe data for .
LightmapGIData.description: contains baked lightmap and dynamic object probe data for . It is replaced every time lightmaps are baked in .

set_uses_spherical_harmonics.description:
If uses_spherical_harmonics is true, tells the engine to treat the lightmap data as if it was baked with directional information.
				Note: Changing this value on already baked lightmaps will not cause them to be baked again. This means the material appearance will look incorrect until lightmaps are baked again, in which case the value set here is discarded as the entire  resource is replaced by the lightmapper.

is_using_spherical_harmonics.description: If true, lightmaps were baked with directional information. See also LightmapGI.directional.

add_user.description: Adds an object that is considered baked within this .

get_user_count.description: Returns the number of objects that are considered baked within this .

get_user_path.description: Returns the  of the baked object at index user_idx.

clear_users.description: Clear all objects that are considered baked within this .

lightmap_textures.description: The lightmap atlas textures generated by the lightmapper.

shadowmask_textures.description: The shadowmask atlas textures generated by the lightmapper.

light_texture.description: The lightmap atlas texture generated by the lightmapper.

LightmapProbe.brief_description: Represents a single manually placed probe for dynamic object lighting with .
LightmapProbe.description:
represents the position of a single manually placed probe for dynamic object lighting with . Lightmap probes affect the lighting of -derived nodes that have their GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode set to .
		Typically,  probes are placed automatically by setting LightmapGI.generate_probes_subdiv to a value other than . By creating  nodes before baking lightmaps, you can add more probes in specific areas for greater detail, or disable automatic generation and rely only on manually placed probes instead.
		Note:  nodes that are placed after baking lightmaps are ignored by dynamic objects. You must bake lightmaps again after creating or modifying s for the probes to be effective.

Lightmapper.brief_description: Abstract class extended by lightmappers, for use in .
Lightmapper.description:
This class should be extended by custom lightmapper classes. Lightmappers can then be used with  to provide fast baked global illumination in 3D.
		Godot contains a built-in GPU-based lightmapper  that uses compute shaders, but custom lightmappers can be implemented by C++ modules.

LightmapperRD.brief_description: The built-in GPU-based lightmapper for use with .
LightmapperRD.description:
LightmapperRD ("RD" stands for ) is the built-in GPU-based lightmapper for use with . On most dedicated GPUs, it can bake lightmaps much faster than most CPU-based lightmappers. LightmapperRD uses compute shaders to bake lightmaps, so it does not require CUDA or OpenCL libraries to be installed to be usable.
		Note: This lightmapper requires the GPU to support the  backend (Forward+ and Mobile renderers). When using the Compatibility renderer, baking will use a temporary . Support for  is not required to render lightmaps that were already baked beforehand.

LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D.description:
This modifier limits bone rotation angular velocity by comparing poses between previous and current frame.
		You can add bone chains by specifying their root and end bones, then add the bones between them to a list. Modifier processes either that list or the bones excluding those in the list depending on the option exclude.

set_root_bone_name.description: Sets the root bone name of the bone chain.

get_root_bone_name.description: Returns the root bone name of the bone chain.

set_root_bone.description: Sets the root bone index of the bone chain.

get_root_bone.description: Returns the root bone index of the bone chain.

set_end_bone_name.description:
Sets the end bone name of the bone chain.
				Note: End bone must be the root bone or a child of the root bone.

get_end_bone_name.description: Returns the end bone name of the bone chain.

set_end_bone.description: Sets the end bone index of the bone chain.

get_end_bone.description: Returns the end bone index of the bone chain.

reset.description: Sets the reference pose for angle comparison to the current pose with the influence of constraints removed. This function is automatically triggered when joints change or upon activation.

max_angular_velocity.description: The maximum angular velocity per second.

exclude.description:
If true, the modifier processes bones not included in the bone list.
			If false, the bones processed by the modifier are equal to the bone list.

joint_count.description: The number of joints in the list which created by chains dynamically.

Line2D.brief_description: A 2D polyline that can optionally be textured.
Line2D.description:
This node draws a 2D polyline, i.e. a shape consisting of several points connected by segments.  is not a mathematical polyline, i.e. the segments are not infinitely thin. It is intended for rendering and it can be colored and optionally textured.
		Warning: Certain configurations may be impossible to draw nicely, such as very sharp angles. In these situations, the node uses fallback drawing logic to look decent.
		Note:  is drawn using a 2D mesh.

set_point_position.description: Overwrites the position of the point at the given index with the supplied position.

get_point_position.description: Returns the position of the point at index index.

get_point_count.description: Returns the number of points in the polyline.

add_point.description:
Adds a point with the specified position relative to the polyline's own position. If no index is provided, the new point will be added to the end of the points array.
				If index is given, the new point is inserted before the existing point identified by index index. The indices of the points after the new point get increased by 1. The provided index must not exceed the number of existing points in the polyline. See get_point_count.

remove_point.description: Removes the point at index index from the polyline.

clear_points.description: Removes all points from the polyline, making it empty.

points.description: The points of the polyline, interpreted in local 2D coordinates. Segments are drawn between the adjacent points in this array.

closed.description:
If true and the polyline has more than 2 points, the last point and the first one will be connected by a segment.
			Note: The shape of the closing segment is not guaranteed to be seamless if a width_curve is provided.
			Note: The joint between the closing segment and the first segment is drawn first and it samples the gradient and the width_curve at the beginning. This is an implementation detail that might change in a future version.

width_curve.description: The polyline's width curve. The width of the polyline over its length will be equivalent to the value of the width curve over its domain. The width curve should be a unit .

default_color.description: The color of the polyline. Will not be used if a gradient is set.

gradient.description: The gradient is drawn through the whole line from start to finish. The default_color will not be used if this property is set.

texture.description: The texture used for the polyline. Uses texture_mode for drawing style.

texture_mode.description: The style to render the texture of the polyline.

joint_mode.description: The style of the connections between segments of the polyline.

begin_cap_mode.description: The style of the beginning of the polyline, if closed is false.

end_cap_mode.description: The style of the end of the polyline, if closed is false.

sharp_limit.description: Determines the miter limit of the polyline. Normally, when joint_mode is set to , sharp angles fall back to using the logic of  joints to prevent very long miters. Higher values of this property mean that the fallback to a bevel joint will happen at sharper angles.

round_precision.description: The smoothness used for rounded joints and caps. Higher values result in smoother corners, but are more demanding to render and update.

antialiased.description:
If true, the polyline's border will be anti-aliased.
			Note:  is not accelerated by batching when being anti-aliased.

LineEdit.brief_description: An input field for single-line text.
LineEdit.description:
provides an input field for editing a single line of text.
		- When the  control is focused using the keyboard arrow keys, it will only gain focus and not enter edit mode.
		- To enter edit mode, click on the control with the mouse, see also keep_editing_on_text_submit.
		- To exit edit mode, press ui_text_submit or ui_cancel (by default Escape) actions.
		- Check edit, unedit, is_editing, and  for more information.
		While entering text, it is possible to insert special characters using Unicode, OEM or Windows alt codes:
		- To enter Unicode codepoints, hold Alt and type the codepoint on the numpad. For example, to enter the character á (U+00E1), hold Alt and type +E1 on the numpad (the leading zeroes can be omitted).
		- To enter OEM codepoints, hold Alt and type the code on the numpad. For example, to enter the character á (OEM 160), hold Alt and type 160 on the numpad.
		- To enter Windows codepoints, hold Alt and type the code on the numpad. For example, to enter the character á (Windows 0225), hold Alt and type 0, 2, 2, 5 on the numpad. The leading zero here must not be omitted, as this is how Windows codepoints are distinguished from OEM codepoints.
		Important:
		- Focusing the  with ui_focus_next (by default Tab) or ui_focus_prev (by default Shift + Tab) or Control.grab_focus still enters edit mode (for compatibility).
		 features many built-in shortcuts that are always available (Ctrl here maps to Cmd on macOS):
		- Ctrl + C: Copy
		- Ctrl + X: Cut
		- Ctrl + V or Ctrl + Y: Paste/"yank"
		- Ctrl + Z: Undo
		- Ctrl + ~: Swap input direction.
		- Ctrl + Shift + Z: Redo
		- Ctrl + U: Delete text from the caret position to the beginning of the line
		- Ctrl + K: Delete text from the caret position to the end of the line
		- Ctrl + A: Select all text
		- Up Arrow/Down Arrow: Move the caret to the beginning/end of the line
		On macOS, some extra keyboard shortcuts are available:
		- Cmd + F: Same as Right Arrow, move the caret one character right
		- Cmd + B: Same as Left Arrow, move the caret one character left
		- Cmd + P: Same as Up Arrow, move the caret to the previous line
		- Cmd + N: Same as Down Arrow, move the caret to the next line
		- Cmd + D: Same as Delete, delete the character on the right side of caret
		- Cmd + H: Same as Backspace, delete the character on the left side of the caret
		- Cmd + A: Same as Home, move the caret to the beginning of the line
		- Cmd + E: Same as End, move the caret to the end of the line
		- Cmd + Left Arrow: Same as Home, move the caret to the beginning of the line
		- Cmd + Right Arrow: Same as End, move the caret to the end of the line
		Note: Caret movement shortcuts listed above are not affected by shortcut_keys_enabled.

has_ime_text.description: Returns true if the user has text in the Input Method Editor (IME).

cancel_ime.description: Closes the Input Method Editor (IME) if it is open. Any text in the IME will be lost.

apply_ime.description: Applies text from the Input Method Editor (IME) and closes the IME if it is open.

edit.description:
Allows entering edit mode whether the  is focused or not. If hide_focus is true, the focused state will not be shown (see Control.grab_focus).
				See also keep_editing_on_text_submit.

unedit.description: Allows exiting edit mode while preserving focus.

is_editing.description: Returns whether the  is being edited.

clear.description: Erases the 's text.

select.description:
Selects characters inside  between from and to. By default, from is at the beginning and to at the end.
				
				
				text = "Welcome"
				select() # Will select "Welcome".
				select(4) # Will select "ome".
				select(2, 5) # Will select "lco".
				
				
				Text = "Welcome";
				Select(); // Will select "Welcome".
				Select(4); // Will select "ome".
				Select(2, 5); // Will select "lco".

has_undo.description: Returns true if an "undo" action is available.

has_redo.description: Returns true if a "redo" action is available.

has_selection.description: Returns true if the user has selected text.

get_selected_text.description: Returns the text inside the selection.

get_next_composite_character_column.description:
Returns the correct column at the end of a composite character like ❤️‍🩹 (mending heart; Unicode: U+2764 U+FE0F U+200D U+1FA79) which is comprised of more than one Unicode code point, if the caret is at the start of the composite character. Also returns the correct column with the caret at mid grapheme and for non-composite characters.
				Note: To check at caret location use get_next_composite_character_column(get_caret_column())

get_previous_composite_character_column.description:
Returns the correct column at the start of a composite character like ❤️‍🩹 (mending heart; Unicode: U+2764 U+FE0F U+200D U+1FA79) which is comprised of more than one Unicode code point, if the caret is at the end of the composite character. Also returns the correct column with the caret at mid grapheme and for non-composite characters.
				Note: To check at caret location use get_previous_composite_character_column(get_caret_column())

get_scroll_offset.description: Returns the scroll offset due to caret_column, as a number of characters.

insert_text_at_caret.description: Inserts text at the caret. If the resulting value is longer than max_length, nothing happens.

delete_char_at_caret.description: Deletes one character at the caret's current position (equivalent to pressing Delete).

delete_text.description: Deletes a section of the text going from position from_column to to_column. Both parameters should be within the text's length.

menu_option.description: Executes a given action as defined in the  enum.

is_menu_visible.description: Returns whether the menu is visible. Use this instead of get_menu().visible to improve performance (so the creation of the menu is avoided).

text.description:
String value of the .
			Note: Changing text using this property won't emit the  signal.

placeholder_text.description: Text shown when the  is empty. It is not the 's default value (see text).

editable.description: If false, existing text cannot be modified and new text cannot be added.

keep_editing_on_text_submit.description: If true, the  will not exit edit mode when text is submitted by pressing ui_text_submit action (by default: Enter or Kp Enter).

expand_to_text_length.description: If true, the  width will increase to stay longer than the text. It will not compress if the text is shortened.

context_menu_enabled.description: If true, the context menu will appear when right-clicked.

emoji_menu_enabled.description: If true, "Emoji and Symbols" menu is enabled.

backspace_deletes_composite_character_en.description: If true and caret_mid_grapheme is false, backspace deletes an entire composite character such as ❤️‍🩹, instead of deleting part of the composite character.

clear_button_enabled.description: If true, the  will show a clear button if text is not empty, which can be used to clear the text quickly.

shortcut_keys_enabled.description: If true, shortcut keys for context menu items are enabled, even if the context menu is disabled.

middle_mouse_paste_enabled.description:
If false, using middle mouse button to paste clipboard will be disabled.
			Note: This method is only implemented on Linux.

selecting_enabled.description: If false, it's impossible to select the text using mouse nor keyboard.

deselect_on_focus_loss_enabled.description: If true, the selected text will be deselected when focus is lost.

drag_and_drop_selection_enabled.description: If true, allow drag and drop of selected text.

flat.description: If true, the  doesn't display decoration.

draw_control_chars.description: If true, control characters are displayed.

select_all_on_focus.description: If true, the  will select the whole text when it gains focus.

virtual_keyboard_enabled.description: If true, the native virtual keyboard is enabled on platforms that support it.

virtual_keyboard_show_on_focus.description: If true, the native virtual keyboard is shown on focus events on platforms that support it.

virtual_keyboard_type.description: Specifies the type of virtual keyboard to show.

caret_blink.description: If true, makes the caret blink.

caret_blink_interval.description: The interval at which the caret blinks (in seconds).

caret_column.description: The caret's column position inside the . When set, the text may scroll to accommodate it.
