		This class does not store the untranslated strings for optimization purposes. Therefore, Translation.get_message_list always returns an empty array, and Translation.get_message_count always returns 0.

generate.description:
Generates and sets an optimized translation from the given  resource.
				Note: Messages in from should not use context or plural forms.
				Note: This method is intended to be used in the editor. It does nothing when called from an exported project.

OptionButton.brief_description: A button that brings up a dropdown with selectable options when pressed.
OptionButton.description:
is a type of button that brings up a dropdown with selectable items when pressed. The item selected becomes the "current" item and is displayed as the button text.
		See also  which contains common properties and methods associated with this node.
		Note: The IDs used for items are limited to signed 32-bit integers, not the full 64 bits of . These have a range of -2^31 to 2^31 - 1, that is, -2147483648 to 2147483647.
		Note: The Button.text and Button.icon properties are set automatically based on the selected item. They shouldn't be changed manually.

add_item.description:
Adds an item, with text label and (optionally) id. If no id is passed, the item index will be used as the item's ID. New items are appended at the end.
				Note: The item will be selected if there are no other items.

add_icon_item.description:
Adds an item, with a texture icon, text label and (optionally) id. If no id is passed, the item index will be used as the item's ID. New items are appended at the end.
				Note: The item will be selected if there are no other items.

set_item_text.description: Sets the text of the item at index idx.

set_item_icon.description: Sets the icon of the item at index idx.

set_item_disabled.description:
Sets whether the item at index idx is disabled.
				Disabled items are drawn differently in the dropdown and are not selectable by the user. If the current selected item is set as disabled, it will remain selected.

set_item_id.description: Sets the ID of the item at index idx.

set_item_metadata.description: Sets the metadata of an item. Metadata may be of any type and can be used to store extra information about an item, such as an external string ID.

set_item_tooltip.description: Sets the tooltip of the item at index idx.

set_item_auto_translate_mode.description:
Sets the auto translate mode of the item at index idx.
				Items use  by default, which uses the same auto translate mode as the  itself.

get_item_text.description: Returns the text of the item at index idx.

get_item_icon.description: Returns the icon of the item at index idx.

get_item_id.description: Returns the ID of the item at index idx.

get_item_index.description: Returns the index of the item with the given id.

get_item_metadata.description: Retrieves the metadata of an item. Metadata may be any type and can be used to store extra information about an item, such as an external string ID.

get_item_tooltip.description: Returns the tooltip of the item at index idx.

get_item_auto_translate_mode.description: Returns the auto translate mode of the item at index idx.

is_item_disabled.description: Returns true if the item at index idx is disabled.

is_item_separator.description: Returns true if the item at index idx is marked as a separator.

add_separator.description: Adds a separator to the list of items. Separators help to group items, and can optionally be given a text header. A separator also gets an index assigned, and is appended at the end of the item list.

clear.description: Clears all the items in the .

select.description:
Selects an item by index and makes it the current item. This will work even if the item is disabled.
				Passing -1 as the index deselects any currently selected item.

get_selected_id.description: Returns the ID of the selected item, or -1 if no item is selected.

get_selected_metadata.description: Gets the metadata of the selected item. Metadata for items can be set using set_item_metadata.

remove_item.description: Removes the item at index idx.

get_popup.description:
Returns the  contained in this button.
				Warning: This is a required internal node, removing and freeing it may cause a crash. If you wish to hide it or any of its children, use their Window.visible property.

show_popup.description: Adjusts popup position and sizing for the , then shows the . Prefer this over using get_popup().popup().

has_selectable_items.description: Returns true if this button contains at least one item which is not disabled, or marked as a separator.

get_selectable_item.description:
Returns the index of the first item which is not disabled, or marked as a separator. If from_last is true, the items will be searched in reverse order.
				Returns -1 if no item is found.

set_disable_shortcuts.description: If true, shortcuts are disabled and cannot be used to trigger the button.

selected.description: The index of the currently selected item, or -1 if no item is selected.

fit_to_longest_item.description:
If true, minimum size will be determined by the longest item's text, instead of the currently selected one's.
			Note: For performance reasons, the minimum size doesn't update immediately when adding, removing or modifying items.

allow_reselect.description: If true, the currently selected item can be selected again.

item_count.description: The number of items to select from.

PCKPacker.brief_description: Creates packages that can be loaded into a running project.

pck_start.description: Creates a new PCK file at the file path pck_path. The .pck file extension isn't added automatically, so it should be part of pck_path (even though it's not required).

add_file.description: Adds the source_path file to the current PCK package at the target_path internal path. The res:// prefix for target_path is optional and stripped internally. File content is immediately written to the PCK.

add_file_removal.description: Registers a file removal of the target_path internal path to the PCK. This is mainly used for patches. If the file at this path has been loaded from a previous PCK, it will be removed. The res:// prefix for target_path is optional and stripped internally.

flush.description:
Writes the file directory and closes the PCK. If verbose is true, a list of files added will be printed to the console for easier debugging.
				Note:  will automatically flush when it's freed, which happens when it goes out of scope or when it gets assigned with null. In C# the reference must be disposed after use, either with the using statement or by calling the Dispose method directly.

PackedDataContainer.description:
can be used to efficiently store data from untyped containers. The data is packed into raw bytes and can be saved to file. Only  and  can be stored this way.
		You can retrieve the data by iterating on the container, which will work as if iterating on the packed data itself. If the packed container is a , the data can be retrieved by key names (/ only).
		
		var data = { "key": "value", "another_key": 123, "lock": Vector2() }
		var packed = PackedDataContainer.new()
		packed.pack(data)
		ResourceSaver.save(packed, "packed_data.res")
		
		
		var container = load("packed_data.res")
		for key in container:
			prints(key, container)
		
		Prints:
		
		key value
		lock (0, 0)
		another_key 123
		
		Nested containers will be packed recursively. While iterating, they will be returned as .

pack.description:
Packs the given container into a binary representation. The value must be either  or , any other type will result in invalid data error.
				Note: Subsequent calls to this method will overwrite the existing data.

size.description: Returns the size of the packed container (see Array.size and Dictionary.size).

PackedDataContainerRef.brief_description: An internal class used by  to pack nested arrays and dictionaries.
PackedDataContainerRef.description:
When packing nested containers using , they are recursively packed into  (only applies to  and ). Their data can be retrieved the same way as from .
		
		var packed = PackedDataContainer.new()
		packed.pack(, 4, 5, 6])

		for element in packed:
			if element is PackedDataContainerRef:
				for subelement in element:
					print("::", subelement)
			else:
				print(element)
		
		Prints:
		
		1
		2
		3
		::nested1
		::nested2
		4
		5
		6

size.description: Returns the size of the packed container (see Array.size and Dictionary.size).

PackedScene.brief_description: An abstraction of a serialized scene.

pack.description: Packs the path node, and all owned sub-nodes, into this . Any existing data will be cleared. See Node.owner.

instantiate.description: Instantiates the scene's node hierarchy. Triggers child scene instantiation(s). Triggers a  notification on the root node.

can_instantiate.description: Returns true if the scene file has nodes.

get_state.description: Returns the  representing the scene file contents.

PacketPeer.brief_description: Abstraction and base class for packet-based protocols.
PacketPeer.description:
PacketPeer is an abstraction and base class for packet-based protocols (such as UDP). It provides an API for sending and receiving packets both as raw data or variables. This makes it easy to transfer data over a protocol, without having to encode data as low-level bytes or having to worry about network ordering.
		Note: When exporting to Android, make sure to enable the INTERNET permission in the Android export preset before exporting the project or using one-click deploy. Otherwise, network communication of any kind will be blocked by Android.

get_var.description:
Gets a Variant. If allow_objects is true, decoding objects is allowed.
				Internally, this uses the same decoding mechanism as the @GlobalScope.bytes_to_var method.
				Warning: Deserialized objects can contain code which gets executed. Do not use this option if the serialized object comes from untrusted sources to avoid potential security threats such as remote code execution.

put_var.description:
Sends a  as a packet. If full_objects is true, encoding objects is allowed (and can potentially include code).
				Internally, this uses the same encoding mechanism as the @GlobalScope.var_to_bytes method.

get_packet_error.description: Returns the error state of the last packet received (via get_packet and get_var).

get_available_packet_count.description: Returns the number of packets currently available in the ring-buffer.

encode_buffer_max_size.description:
Maximum buffer size allowed when encoding s. Raise this value to support heavier memory allocations.
			The put_var method allocates memory on the stack, and the buffer used will grow automatically to the closest power of two to match the size of the . If the  is bigger than encode_buffer_max_size, the method will error out with .

PacketPeerDTLS.description:
This class represents a DTLS peer connection. It can be used to connect to a DTLS server, and is returned by DTLSServer.take_connection.
		Note: When exporting to Android, make sure to enable the INTERNET permission in the Android export preset before exporting the project or using one-click deploy. Otherwise, network communication of any kind will be blocked by Android.
		Warning: TLS certificate revocation and certificate pinning are currently not supported. Revoked certificates are accepted as long as they are otherwise valid. If this is a concern, you may want to use automatically managed certificates with a short validity period.

poll.description: Poll the connection to check for incoming packets. Call this frequently to update the status and keep the connection working.

connect_to_peer.description: Connects a packet_peer beginning the DTLS handshake using the underlying  which must be connected (see PacketPeerUDP.connect_to_host). You can optionally specify the client_options to be used while verifying the TLS connections. See TLSOptions.client and TLSOptions.client_unsafe.

get_status.description: Returns the status of the connection.

disconnect_from_peer.description: Disconnects this peer, terminating the DTLS session.

PacketPeerStream.brief_description: Wrapper to use a PacketPeer over a StreamPeer.
PacketPeerStream.description:
PacketStreamPeer provides a wrapper for working using packets over a stream. This allows for using packet based code with StreamPeers. PacketPeerStream implements a custom protocol over the StreamPeer, so the user should not read or write to the wrapped StreamPeer directly.
		Note: When exporting to Android, make sure to enable the INTERNET permission in the Android export preset before exporting the project or using one-click deploy. Otherwise, network communication of any kind will be blocked by Android.

bind.description:
Binds this  to the specified port and bind_address with a buffer size recv_buf_size, allowing it to receive incoming packets.
				If bind_address is set to "*" (default), the peer will be bound on all available addresses (both IPv4 and IPv6).
				If bind_address is set to "0.0.0.0" (for IPv4) or "::" (for IPv6), the peer will be bound to all available addresses matching that IP type.
				If bind_address is set to any valid address (e.g. "192.168.1.101", "::1", etc.), the peer will only be bound to the interface with that address (or fail if no interface with the given address exists).

is_bound.description: Returns whether this  is bound to an address and can receive packets.

connect_to_host.description:
Calling this method connects this UDP peer to the given host/port pair. UDP is in reality connectionless, so this option only means that incoming packets from different addresses are automatically discarded, and that outgoing packets are always sent to the connected address (future calls to set_dest_address are not allowed). This method does not send any data to the remote peer, to do that, use PacketPeer.put_var or PacketPeer.put_packet as usual. See also .
				Note: Connecting to the remote peer does not help to protect from malicious attacks like IP spoofing, etc. Think about using an encryption technique like TLS or DTLS if you feel like your application is transferring sensitive information.

is_socket_connected.description: Returns true if the UDP socket is open and has been connected to a remote address. See connect_to_host.

get_packet_ip.description: Returns the IP of the remote peer that sent the last packet(that was received with PacketPeer.get_packet or PacketPeer.get_var).

get_packet_port.description: Returns the port of the remote peer that sent the last packet(that was received with PacketPeer.get_packet or PacketPeer.get_var).

get_local_port.description: Returns the local port to which this peer is bound.

set_dest_address.description:
Sets the destination address and port for sending packets and variables. A hostname will be resolved using DNS if needed.
				Note: set_broadcast_enabled must be enabled before sending packets to a broadcast address (e.g. 255.255.255.255).

set_broadcast_enabled.description:
Enable or disable sending of broadcast packets (e.g. set_dest_address("255.255.255.255", 4343). This option is disabled by default.
				Note: Some Android devices might require the CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE permission and this option to be enabled to receive broadcast packets too.

join_multicast_group.description:
Joins the multicast group specified by multicast_address using the interface identified by interface_name.
				You can join the same multicast group with multiple interfaces. Use IP.get_local_interfaces to know which are available.
				Note: Some Android devices might require the CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE permission for multicast to work.

leave_multicast_group.description: Removes the interface identified by interface_name from the multicast group specified by multicast_address.

Panel.brief_description: A GUI control that displays a .
Panel.description: is a GUI control that displays a . See also .

PanelContainer.brief_description: A container that keeps its child controls within the area of a .
PanelContainer.description: A container that keeps its child controls within the area of a . Useful for giving controls an outline.

PanoramaSkyMaterial.brief_description: A material that provides a special texture to a , usually an HDR panorama.
PanoramaSkyMaterial.description:
A resource referenced in a  that is used to draw a background.  functions similar to skyboxes in other engines, except it uses an equirectangular sky map instead of a .
		Using an HDR panorama is strongly recommended for accurate, high-quality reflections. Godot supports the Radiance HDR (.hdr) and OpenEXR (.exr) image formats for this purpose.
		You can use this tool to convert a cubemap to an equirectangular sky map.

filter.description: A boolean value to determine if the background texture should be filtered or not.

energy_multiplier.description: The sky's overall brightness multiplier. Higher values result in a brighter sky.

Parallax2D.brief_description: A node used to create a parallax scrolling background.
Parallax2D.description:
A  is used to create a parallax effect. It can move at a different speed relative to the camera movement using scroll_scale. This creates an illusion of depth in a 2D game. If manual scrolling is desired, the  position can be ignored with ignore_camera_scroll.
		Note: Any changes to this node's position made after it enters the scene tree will be overridden if ignore_camera_scroll is false or screen_offset is modified.

scroll_scale.description:
Multiplier to the final 's offset. Can be used to simulate distance from the camera.
			For example, a value of 1 scrolls at the same speed as the camera. A value greater than 1 scrolls faster, making objects appear closer. Less than 1 scrolls slower, making objects appear further, and a value of 0 stops the objects completely.

scroll_offset.description:
The 's offset. Similar to screen_offset and Node2D.position, but will not be overridden.
			Note: Values will loop if repeat_size is set higher than 0.

repeat_size.description: Repeats the  of each of this node's children and offsets them by this value. When scrolling, the node's position loops, giving the illusion of an infinite scrolling background if the values are larger than the screen size. If an axis is set to 0, the  will not be repeated.

autoscroll.description: Velocity at which the offset scrolls automatically, in pixels per second.

repeat_times.description: Overrides the amount of times the texture repeats. Each texture copy spreads evenly from the original by repeat_size. Useful for when zooming out with a camera.

limit_begin.description: Top-left limits for scrolling to begin. If the camera is outside of this limit, the  stops scrolling. Must be lower than limit_end minus the viewport size to work.

limit_end.description: Bottom-right limits for scrolling to end. If the camera is outside of this limit, the  will stop scrolling. Must be higher than limit_begin and the viewport size combined to work.

follow_viewport.description: If true, this  is offset by the current camera's position. If the  is in a  separate from the current camera, it may be desired to match the value with CanvasLayer.follow_viewport_enabled.

ignore_camera_scroll.description: If true, 's position is not affected by the position of the camera.

screen_offset.description: Offset used to scroll this . This value is updated automatically unless ignore_camera_scroll is true.

ParallaxBackground.brief_description: A node used to create a parallax scrolling background.
ParallaxBackground.description:
A ParallaxBackground uses one or more  child nodes to create a parallax effect. Each  can move at a different speed using ParallaxLayer.motion_offset. This creates an illusion of depth in a 2D game. If not used with a , you must manually calculate the scroll_offset.
		Note: Each  is drawn on one specific  and cannot be shared between multiple s, see CanvasLayer.custom_viewport. When using multiple s, for example in a split-screen game, you need create an individual  for each  you want it to be drawn on.

scroll_offset.description: The ParallaxBackground's scroll value. Calculated automatically when using a , but can be used to manually manage scrolling when no camera is present.

scroll_base_offset.description: The base position offset for all  children.

scroll_base_scale.description: The base motion scale for all  children.

scroll_limit_begin.description: Top-left limits for scrolling to begin. If the camera is outside of this limit, the background will stop scrolling. Must be lower than scroll_limit_end to work.

scroll_limit_end.description: Bottom-right limits for scrolling to end. If the camera is outside of this limit, the background will stop scrolling. Must be higher than scroll_limit_begin to work.

scroll_ignore_camera_zoom.description: If true, elements in  child aren't affected by the zoom level of the camera.

ParallaxLayer.brief_description: A parallax scrolling layer to be used with .
ParallaxLayer.description:
A ParallaxLayer must be the child of a  node. Each ParallaxLayer can be set to move at different speeds relative to the camera movement or the ParallaxBackground.scroll_offset value.
		This node's children will be affected by its scroll offset.
		Note: Any changes to this node's position and scale made after it enters the scene will be ignored.

motion_scale.description: Multiplies the ParallaxLayer's motion. If an axis is set to 0, it will not scroll.

motion_offset.description: The ParallaxLayer's offset relative to the parent ParallaxBackground's ParallaxBackground.scroll_offset.

motion_mirroring.description:
The interval, in pixels, at which the  is drawn repeatedly. Useful for creating an infinitely scrolling background. If an axis is set to 0, the  will be drawn only once along that direction.
			Note: If you want the repetition to pixel-perfect match a  displayed by a child node, you should account for any scale applied to the texture when defining this interval. For example, if you use a child  scaled to 0.5 to display a 600x600 texture, and want this sprite to be repeated continuously horizontally, you should set the mirroring to Vector2(300, 0).
			Note: If the length of the viewport axis is bigger than twice the repeated axis size, it will not repeat infinitely, as the parallax layer only draws 2 instances of the layer at any given time. The visibility window is calculated from the parent 's position, not the layer's own position. So, if you use mirroring, do not change the  position relative to its parent. Instead, if you need to adjust the background's position, set the CanvasLayer.offset property in the parent .
			Note: Despite the name, the layer will not be mirrored, it will only be repeated.

ParticleProcessMaterial.brief_description: Holds a particle configuration for  or  nodes.
ParticleProcessMaterial.description: defines particle properties and behavior. It is used in the process_material of the  and  nodes. Some of this material's properties are applied to each particle when emitted, while others can have a  or a  applied to vary numerical or color values over the lifetime of the particle.

set_param.description:
Sets the minimum and maximum values of the given param.
				The x component of the argument vector corresponds to minimum and the y component corresponds to maximum.

get_param.description:
Returns the minimum and maximum values of the given param as a vector.
				The x component of the returned vector corresponds to minimum and the y component corresponds to maximum.

set_param_min.description: Sets the minimum value range for the given parameter.

get_param_min.description: Returns the minimum value range for the given parameter.

set_param_max.description: Sets the maximum value range for the given parameter.

get_param_max.description: Returns the maximum value range for the given parameter.

get_param_texture.description: Returns the  used by the specified parameter.

get_particle_flag.description: Returns true if the specified particle flag is enabled.

lifetime_randomness.description: Particle lifetime randomness ratio. The equation for the lifetime of a particle is lifetime * (1.0 - randf() * lifetime_randomness). For example, a lifetime_randomness of 0.4 scales the lifetime between 0.6 to 1.0 of its original value.

particle_flag_align_y.description: Align Y axis of particle with the direction of its velocity.

particle_flag_rotate_y.description: If true, particles rotate around Y axis by angle_min.

particle_flag_disable_z.description: If true, particles will not move on the z axis.

particle_flag_damping_as_friction.description: Changes the behavior of the damping properties from a linear deceleration to a deceleration based on speed percentage.

emission_shape_offset.description: The offset for the emission_shape, in local space.

emission_shape_scale.description: The scale of the emission_shape, in local space.

emission_shape.description: Particles will be emitted inside this region.

emission_sphere_radius.description: The sphere's radius if emission_shape is set to .

emission_box_extents.description:
The box's extents if emission_shape is set to .
			Note: emission_box_extents starts from the center point and applies the X, Y, and Z values in both directions. The size is twice the area of the extents.

emission_point_texture.description: Particles will be emitted at positions determined by sampling this texture at a random position. Used with  and . Can be created automatically from mesh or node by selecting "Create Emission Points from Mesh/Node" under the "Particles" tool in the toolbar.

emission_normal_texture.description: Particle velocity and rotation will be set by sampling this texture at the same point as the emission_point_texture. Used only in . Can be created automatically from mesh or node by selecting "Create Emission Points from Mesh/Node" under the "Particles" tool in the toolbar.

emission_color_texture.description:
Particle color will be modulated by color determined by sampling this texture at the same point as the emission_point_texture.
			Note: emission_color_texture multiplies the particle mesh's vertex colors. To have a visible effect on a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALBEDO *= COLOR.rgb; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function. Otherwise, emission_color_texture will have no visible effect.

emission_point_count.description: The number of emission points if emission_shape is set to  or .

emission_ring_axis.description: The axis of the ring when using the emitter .

emission_ring_height.description: The height of the ring when using the emitter .

emission_ring_radius.description: The radius of the ring when using the emitter .

emission_ring_inner_radius.description: The inner radius of the ring when using the emitter .

emission_ring_cone_angle.description:
The angle of the cone when using the emitter . The default angle of 90 degrees results in a ring, while an angle of 0 degrees results in a cone. Intermediate values will result in a ring where one end is larger than the other.
			Note: Depending on emission_ring_height, the angle may be clamped if the ring's end is reached to form a perfect cone.

angle_max.description:
Maximum initial rotation applied to each particle, in degrees.
			Only applied when particle_flag_disable_z or particle_flag_rotate_y are true or the  being used to draw the particle is using .

angle_curve.description: Each particle's rotation will be animated along this .

inherit_velocity_ratio.description: Percentage of the velocity of the respective  or  inherited by each particle when spawning.

velocity_pivot.description: A pivot point used to calculate radial and orbital velocity of particles.

direction.description: Unit vector specifying the particles' emission direction.

spread.description: Each particle's initial direction range from +spread to -spread degrees.

flatness.description: Amount of spread along the Y axis.

initial_velocity_max.description: Maximum initial velocity magnitude for each particle. Direction comes from direction and spread.

angular_velocity_max.description:
Maximum initial angular velocity (rotation speed) applied to each particle in degrees per second.
			Only applied when particle_flag_disable_z or particle_flag_rotate_y are true or the  being used to draw the particle is using .

angular_velocity_curve.description: Each particle's angular velocity (rotation speed) will vary along this  over its lifetime.

directional_velocity_min.description:
Minimum directional velocity value, which is multiplied by directional_velocity_curve.
			Note: Animated velocities will not be affected by damping, use velocity_limit_curve instead.

directional_velocity_max.description:
Maximum directional velocity value, which is multiplied by directional_velocity_curve.
			Note: Animated velocities will not be affected by damping, use velocity_limit_curve instead.

directional_velocity_curve.description:
A curve that specifies the velocity along each of the axes of the particle system along its lifetime.
			Note: Animated velocities will not be affected by damping, use velocity_limit_curve instead.

orbit_velocity_min.description:
Minimum equivalent of orbit_velocity_max.
			Note: Animated velocities will not be affected by damping, use velocity_limit_curve instead.

orbit_velocity_max.description:
Maximum orbital velocity applied to each particle. Makes the particles circle around origin. Specified in number of full rotations around origin per second.
			Note: Animated velocities will not be affected by damping, use velocity_limit_curve instead.

orbit_velocity_curve.description:
Each particle's orbital velocity will vary along this .
			Note: For 3D orbital velocity, use a .
			Note: Animated velocities will not be affected by damping, use velocity_limit_curve instead.

radial_velocity_min.description:
Minimum radial velocity applied to each particle. Makes particles move away from the velocity_pivot, or toward it if negative.
			Note: Animated velocities will not be affected by damping, use velocity_limit_curve instead.

radial_velocity_max.description:
Maximum radial velocity applied to each particle. Makes particles move away from the velocity_pivot, or toward it if negative.
			Note: Animated velocities will not be affected by damping, use velocity_limit_curve instead.

radial_velocity_curve.description:
A  that defines the velocity over the particle's lifetime away (or toward) the velocity_pivot.
			Note: Animated velocities will not be affected by damping, use velocity_limit_curve instead.

velocity_limit_curve.description: A  that defines the maximum velocity of a particle during its lifetime.

linear_accel_max.description: Maximum linear acceleration applied to each particle in the direction of motion.

linear_accel_curve.description: Each particle's linear acceleration will vary along this .

radial_accel_max.description: Maximum radial acceleration applied to each particle. Makes particle accelerate away from the origin or towards it if negative.

radial_accel_curve.description: Each particle's radial acceleration will vary along this .

tangential_accel_max.description: Maximum tangential acceleration applied to each particle. Tangential acceleration is perpendicular to the particle's velocity giving the particles a swirling motion.

tangential_accel_curve.description: Each particle's tangential acceleration will vary along this .

damping_max.description: The maximum rate at which particles lose velocity. For example value of 100 means that the particle will go from 100 velocity to 0 in 1 second.

attractor_interaction_enabled.description: If true, interaction with particle attractors is enabled. In 3D, attraction only occurs within the area defined by the  node's GPUParticles3D.visibility_aabb.

scale_max.description: Maximum initial scale applied to each particle.

scale_curve.description: Each particle's scale will vary along this  over its lifetime. If a  is supplied instead, the scale will be separated per-axis.

scale_over_velocity_min.description:
Minimum velocity value reference for scale_over_velocity_curve.
			scale_over_velocity_curve will be interpolated between scale_over_velocity_min and scale_over_velocity_max.

scale_over_velocity_max.description:
Maximum velocity value reference for scale_over_velocity_curve.
			scale_over_velocity_curve will be interpolated between scale_over_velocity_min and scale_over_velocity_max.

scale_over_velocity_curve.description: Either a  or a  that scales each particle based on its velocity.

color.description:
Each particle's initial color. If the 's texture is defined, it will be multiplied by this color.
			Note: color multiplies the particle mesh's vertex colors. To have a visible effect on a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALBEDO *= COLOR.rgb; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function. Otherwise, color will have no visible effect.

color_ramp.description:
Each particle's color will vary along this  over its lifetime (multiplied with color).
			Note: color_ramp multiplies the particle mesh's vertex colors. To have a visible effect on a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALBEDO *= COLOR.rgb; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function. Otherwise, color_ramp will have no visible effect.

color_initial_ramp.description:
Each particle's initial color will vary along this  (multiplied with color).
			Note: color_initial_ramp multiplies the particle mesh's vertex colors. To have a visible effect on a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALBEDO *= COLOR.rgb; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function. Otherwise, color_initial_ramp will have no visible effect.

alpha_curve.description:
The alpha value of each particle's color will be multiplied by this  over its lifetime.
			Note: alpha_curve multiplies the particle mesh's vertex colors. To have a visible effect on a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALPHA *= COLOR.a; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function. Otherwise, alpha_curve will have no visible effect.

emission_curve.description:
Each particle's color will be multiplied by this  over its lifetime.
			Note: emission_curve multiplies the particle mesh's vertex colors. To have a visible effect on a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALBEDO *= COLOR.rgb; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function. Otherwise, emission_curve will have no visible effect.

hue_variation_max.description: Maximum initial hue variation applied to each particle. It will shift the particle color's hue.

hue_variation_curve.description: Each particle's hue will vary along this .

anim_speed_max.description:
Maximum particle animation speed. Animation speed of 1 means that the particles will make full 0 to 1 offset cycle during lifetime, 2 means 2 cycles etc.
			With animation speed greater than 1, remember to enable CanvasItemMaterial.particles_anim_loop property if you want the animation to repeat.

anim_speed_curve.description: Each particle's animation speed will vary along this .

anim_offset_max.description: Maximum animation offset that corresponds to frame index in the texture. 0 is the first frame, 1 is the last one. See CanvasItemMaterial.particles_animation.

anim_offset_curve.description: Each particle's animation offset will vary along this .

turbulence_enabled.description:
If true, enables turbulence for the particle system. Turbulence can be used to vary particle movement according to its position (based on a 3D noise pattern). In 3D,  with  can be used as an alternative to turbulence that works in world space and with multiple particle systems reacting in the same way.
			Note: Enabling turbulence has a high performance cost on the GPU. Only enable turbulence on a few particle systems at once at most, and consider disabling it when targeting mobile/web platforms.

turbulence_noise_strength.description: The turbulence noise strength. Increasing this will result in a stronger, more contrasting, flow pattern.

turbulence_noise_scale.description:
This value controls the overall scale/frequency of the turbulence noise pattern.
			A small scale will result in smaller features with more detail while a high scale will result in smoother noise with larger features.

turbulence_noise_speed.description:
A scrolling velocity for the turbulence field. This sets a directional trend for the pattern to move in over time.
			The default value of Vector3(0, 0, 0) turns off the scrolling.

turbulence_noise_speed_random.description:
The in-place rate of change of the turbulence field. This defines how quickly the noise pattern varies over time.
			A value of 0.0 will result in a fixed pattern.

turbulence_influence_min.description:
Minimum turbulence influence on each particle.
			The actual amount of turbulence influence on each particle is calculated as a random value between turbulence_influence_min and turbulence_influence_max and multiplied by the amount of turbulence influence from turbulence_influence_over_life.

turbulence_influence_max.description:
Maximum turbulence influence on each particle.
			The actual amount of turbulence influence on each particle is calculated as a random value between turbulence_influence_min and turbulence_influence_max and multiplied by the amount of turbulence influence from turbulence_influence_over_life.

turbulence_initial_displacement_min.description:
Minimum displacement of each particle's spawn position by the turbulence.
			The actual amount of displacement will be a factor of the underlying turbulence multiplied by a random value between turbulence_initial_displacement_min and turbulence_initial_displacement_max.

turbulence_initial_displacement_max.description:
Maximum displacement of each particle's spawn position by the turbulence.
			The actual amount of displacement will be a factor of the underlying turbulence multiplied by a random value between turbulence_initial_displacement_min and turbulence_initial_displacement_max.

turbulence_influence_over_life.description: Each particle's amount of turbulence will be influenced along this  over its life time.

collision_mode.description:
The particles' collision mode.
			Note: 3D Particles can only collide with  nodes, not  nodes. To make particles collide with various objects, you can add  nodes as children of  nodes. In 3D, collisions only occur within the area defined by the  node's GPUParticles3D.visibility_aabb.
			Note: 2D Particles can only collide with  nodes, not  nodes.

collision_friction.description: The particles' friction. Values range from 0 (frictionless) to 1 (maximum friction). Only effective if collision_mode is .

collision_bounce.description: The particles' bounciness. Values range from 0 (no bounce) to 1 (full bounciness). Only effective if collision_mode is .

collision_use_scale.description: If true, GPUParticles3D.collision_base_size is multiplied by the particle's effective scale (see scale_min, scale_max, scale_curve, and scale_over_velocity_curve).

sub_emitter_mode.description: The particle subemitter mode (see GPUParticles2D.sub_emitter and GPUParticles3D.sub_emitter).

sub_emitter_frequency.description:
The frequency at which particles should be emitted from the subemitter node. One particle will be spawned every sub_emitter_frequency seconds.
			Note: This value shouldn't exceed GPUParticles2D.amount or GPUParticles3D.amount defined on the subemitter node (not the main node), relative to the subemitter's particle lifetime. If the number of particles is exceeded, no new particles will spawn from the subemitter until enough particles have expired.

sub_emitter_amount_at_end.description:
The amount of particles to spawn from the subemitter node when the particle expires.
			Note: This value shouldn't exceed GPUParticles2D.amount or GPUParticles3D.amount defined on the subemitter node (not the main node), relative to the subemitter's particle lifetime. If the number of particles is exceeded, no new particles will spawn from the subemitter until enough particles have expired.

sub_emitter_amount_at_collision.description:
The amount of particles to spawn from the subemitter node when a collision occurs. When combined with  on the main particles material, this can be used to achieve effects such as raindrops hitting the ground.
			Note: This value shouldn't exceed GPUParticles2D.amount or GPUParticles3D.amount defined on the subemitter node (not the main node), relative to the subemitter's particle lifetime. If the number of particles is exceeded, no new particles will spawn from the subemitter until enough particles have expired.

sub_emitter_amount_at_start.description:
The amount of particles to spawn from the subemitter node when the particle spawns.
			Note: This value shouldn't exceed GPUParticles2D.amount or GPUParticles3D.amount defined on the subemitter node (not the main node), relative to the subemitter's particle lifetime. If the number of particles is exceeded, no new particles will spawn from the subemitter until enough particles have expired.

sub_emitter_keep_velocity.description: If true, the subemitter inherits the parent particle's velocity when it spawns.

Path2D.brief_description: Contains a  path for  nodes to follow.
Path2D.description:
Can have  child nodes moving along the . See  for more information on usage.
		Note: The path is considered as relative to the moved nodes (children of ). As such, the curve should usually start with a zero vector ((0, 0)).

Path3D.brief_description: Contains a  path for  nodes to follow.
Path3D.description:
Can have  child nodes moving along the . See  for more information on the usage.
		Note that the path is considered as relative to the moved nodes (children of ). As such, the curve should usually start with a zero vector (0, 0, 0).

debug_custom_color.description: The custom color used to draw the path in the editor. If set to  (as by default), the color set in ProjectSettings.debug/shapes/paths/geometry_color is used.

PathFollow2D.description:
This node takes its parent , and returns the coordinates of a point within it, given a distance from the first vertex.
		It is useful for making other nodes follow a path, without coding the movement pattern. For that, the nodes must be children of this node. The descendant nodes will then move accordingly when setting the progress in this node.

progress.description: The distance along the path, in pixels. Changing this value sets this node's position to a point within the path.

progress_ratio.description:
The distance along the path as a number in the range 0.0 (for the first vertex) to 1.0 (for the last). This is just another way of expressing the progress within the path, as the offset supplied is multiplied internally by the path's length.
			It can be set or get only if the  is the child of a  which is part of the scene tree, and that this  has a  with a non-zero length. Otherwise, trying to set this field will print an error, and getting this field will return 0.0.

h_offset.description: The node's offset along the curve.

v_offset.description: The node's offset perpendicular to the curve.

rotates.description: If true, this node rotates to follow the path, with the +X direction facing forward on the path.

cubic_interp.description:
If true, the position between two cached points is interpolated cubically, and linearly otherwise.
			The points along the  of the  are precomputed before use, for faster calculations. The point at the requested offset is then calculated interpolating between two adjacent cached points. This may present a problem if the curve makes sharp turns, as the cached points may not follow the curve closely enough.
			There are two answers to this problem: either increase the number of cached points and increase memory consumption, or make a cubic interpolation between two points at the cost of (slightly) slower calculations.

loop.description: If true, any offset outside the path's length will wrap around, instead of stopping at the ends. Use it for cyclic paths.

PathFollow3D.description:
This node takes its parent , and returns the coordinates of a point within it, given a distance from the first vertex.
		It is useful for making other nodes follow a path, without coding the movement pattern. For that, the nodes must be children of this node. The descendant nodes will then move accordingly when setting the progress in this node.

correct_posture.description: Correct the transform. rotation_mode implicitly specifies how posture (forward, up and sideway direction) is calculated.

progress.description: The distance from the first vertex, measured in 3D units along the path. Changing this value sets this node's position to a point within the path.

progress_ratio.description:
The distance from the first vertex, considering 0.0 as the first vertex and 1.0 as the last. This is just another way of expressing the progress within the path, as the progress supplied is multiplied internally by the path's length.
			It can be set or get only if the  is the child of a  which is part of the scene tree, and that this  has a  with a non-zero length. Otherwise, trying to set this field will print an error, and getting this field will return 0.0.

h_offset.description: The node's offset along the curve.

v_offset.description: The node's offset perpendicular to the curve.

rotation_mode.description: Allows or forbids rotation on one or more axes, depending on the  constants being used.

use_model_front.description: If true, the node moves on the travel path with orienting the +Z axis as forward. See also  and .

cubic_interp.description:
If true, the position between two cached points is interpolated cubically, and linearly otherwise.
			The points along the  of the  are precomputed before use, for faster calculations. The point at the requested offset is then calculated interpolating between two adjacent cached points. This may present a problem if the curve makes sharp turns, as the cached points may not follow the curve closely enough.
			There are two answers to this problem: either increase the number of cached points and increase memory consumption, or make a cubic interpolation between two points at the cost of (slightly) slower calculations.

loop.description: If true, any offset outside the path's length will wrap around, instead of stopping at the ends. Use it for cyclic paths.

tilt_enabled.description: If true, the tilt property of  takes effect.

Performance.description:
This class provides access to a number of different monitors related to performance, such as memory usage, draw calls, and FPS. These are the same as the values displayed in the Monitor tab in the editor's Debugger panel. By using the get_monitor method of this class, you can access this data from your code.
		You can add custom monitors using the add_custom_monitor method. Custom monitors are available in Monitor tab in the editor's Debugger panel together with built-in monitors.
		Note: Some of the built-in monitors are only available in debug mode and will always return 0 when used in a project exported in release mode.
		Note: Some of the built-in monitors are not updated in real-time for performance reasons, so there may be a delay of up to 1 second between changes.
		Note: Custom monitors do not support negative values. Negative values are clamped to 0.

get_monitor.description:
Returns the value of one of the available built-in monitors. You should provide one of the  constants as the argument, like this:
				
				
				print(Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_FPS)) # Prints the FPS to the console.
				
				
				GD.Print(Performance.GetMonitor(Performance.Monitor.TimeFps)); // Prints the FPS to the console.
				
				
				See get_custom_monitor to query custom performance monitors' values.

remove_custom_monitor.description: Removes the custom monitor with given id. Prints an error if the given id is already absent.

has_custom_monitor.description: Returns true if custom monitor with the given id is present, false otherwise.

get_custom_monitor.description: Returns the value of custom monitor with given id. The callable is called to get the value of custom monitor. See also has_custom_monitor. Prints an error if the given id is absent.

get_monitor_modification_time.description: Returns the last tick in which custom monitor was added/removed (in microseconds since the engine started). This is set to Time.get_ticks_usec when the monitor is updated.

get_custom_monitor_names.description: Returns the names of active custom monitors in an .

get_custom_monitor_types.description: Returns the  values of active custom monitors in an .

PhysicalBone2D.brief_description: A -derived node used to make s in a  react to physics.
PhysicalBone2D.description:
The  node is a -based node that can be used to make s in a  react to physics.
		Note: To make the s visually follow the  node, use a  modification on the  parent.
		Note: The  node does not automatically create a  node to keep  nodes together. They must be created manually. For most cases, you want to use a  node. The  node will automatically configure the  node once it's been added as a child node.

get_joint.description: Returns the first  child node, if one exists. This is mainly a helper function to make it easier to get the  that the  is autoconfiguring.

is_simulating_physics.description: Returns a boolean that indicates whether the  is running and simulating using the Godot 2D physics engine. When true, the PhysicalBone2D node is using physics.

bone2d_nodepath.description: The  to the  that this  should simulate.

bone2d_index.description: The index of the  that this  should simulate.

auto_configure_joint.description: If true, the  will automatically configure the first  child node. The automatic configuration is limited to setting up the node properties and positioning the .

simulate_physics.description:
If true, the  will start simulating using physics. If false, the  will follow the transform of the  node.
			Note: To have the s visually follow the , use a  modification on the  node with the  nodes.

follow_bone_when_simulating.description: If true, the  will keep the transform of the bone it is bound to when simulating physics.

PhysicalBone3D.brief_description: A physics body used to make bones in a  react to physics.
PhysicalBone3D.description:
The  node is a physics body that can be used to make bones in a  react to physics.
		Note: In order to detect physical bones with raycasts, the SkeletonModifier3D.active property of the parent  must be true and the 's bone must be assigned to  correctly; it means that get_bone_id should return a valid id (>= 0).

_integrate_forces.description: Called during physics processing, allowing you to read and safely modify the simulation state for the object. By default, it is called before the standard force integration, but the custom_integrator property allows you to disable the standard force integration and do fully custom force integration for a body.

apply_central_impulse.description:
Applies a directional impulse without affecting rotation.
				An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_integrate_forces" functions otherwise).
				This is equivalent to using apply_impulse at the body's center of mass.

apply_impulse.description:
Applies a positioned impulse to the PhysicsBone3D.
				An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_integrate_forces" functions otherwise).
				position is the offset from the PhysicsBone3D origin in global coordinates.

get_simulate_physics.description: Returns true if the PhysicsBone3D is allowed to simulate physics.

is_simulating_physics.description: Returns true if the PhysicsBone3D is currently simulating physics.

get_bone_id.description: Returns the unique identifier of the PhysicsBone3D.

joint_rotation.description: Sets the joint's rotation in radians.

friction.description: The body's friction, from 0 (frictionless) to 1 (max friction).

bounce.description:
The body's bounciness. Values range from 0 (no bounce) to 1 (full bounciness).
			Note: Even with bounce set to 1.0, some energy will be lost over time due to linear and angular damping. To have a  that preserves all its energy over time, set bounce to 1.0, linear_damp_mode to , linear_damp to 0.0, angular_damp_mode to , and angular_damp to 0.0.

gravity_scale.description: This is multiplied by ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_gravity to produce this body's gravity. For example, a value of 1.0 will apply normal gravity, 2.0 will apply double the gravity, and 0.5 will apply half the gravity to this body.

custom_integrator.description:
If true, the standard force integration (like gravity or damping) will be disabled for this body. Other than collision response, the body will only move as determined by the _integrate_forces method, if that virtual method is overridden.
			Setting this property will call the method PhysicsServer3D.body_set_omit_force_integration internally.

linear_damp.description:
Damps the body's movement. By default, the body will use ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_linear_damp or any value override set by an  the body is in. Depending on linear_damp_mode, linear_damp may be added to or replace the body's damping value.
			See ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_linear_damp for more details about damping.

angular_damp.description:
Damps the body's rotation. By default, the body will use the ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_angular_damp project setting or any value override set by an  the body is in. Depending on angular_damp_mode, you can set angular_damp to be added to or to replace the body's damping value.
			See ProjectSettings.physics/3d/default_angular_damp for more details about damping.

linear_velocity.description: The body's linear velocity in units per second. Can be used sporadically, but don't set this every frame, because physics may run in another thread and runs at a different granularity. Use _integrate_forces as your process loop for precise control of the body state.

angular_velocity.description: The PhysicalBone3D's rotational velocity in radians per second.

can_sleep.description: If true, the body is deactivated when there is no movement, so it will not take part in the simulation until it is awakened by an external force.

PhysicalBoneSimulator3D.brief_description: Node that can be the parent of  and can apply the simulation results to .
PhysicalBoneSimulator3D.description: Node that can be the parent of  and can apply the simulation results to .

is_simulating_physics.description: Returns a boolean that indicates whether the  is running and simulating.

physical_bones_stop_simulation.description: Tells the  nodes in the Skeleton to stop simulating.

physical_bones_start_simulation.description:
Tells the  nodes in the Skeleton to start simulating and reacting to the physics world.
				Optionally, a list of bone names can be passed-in, allowing only the passed-in bones to be simulated.

physical_bones_add_collision_exception.description:
Adds a collision exception to the physical bone.
				Works just like the  node.

physical_bones_remove_collision_exceptio.description:
Removes a collision exception to the physical bone.
				Works just like the  node.

PhysicalSkyMaterial.brief_description: A material that defines a sky for a  resource by a set of physical properties.
PhysicalSkyMaterial.description:
The  uses the Preetham analytic daylight model to draw a sky based on physical properties. This results in a substantially more realistic sky than the , but it is slightly slower and less flexible.
		The  only supports one sun. The color, energy, and direction of the sun are taken from the first  in the scene tree.

rayleigh_coefficient.description: Controls the strength of the Rayleigh scattering. Rayleigh scattering results from light colliding with small particles. It is responsible for the blue color of the sky.

rayleigh_color.description: Controls the  of the Rayleigh scattering. While not physically accurate, this allows for the creation of alien-looking planets. For example, setting this to a red  results in a Mars-looking atmosphere with a corresponding blue sunset.

mie_coefficient.description: Controls the strength of Mie scattering for the sky. Mie scattering results from light colliding with larger particles (like water). On earth, Mie scattering results in a whitish color around the sun and horizon.

mie_eccentricity.description: Controls the direction of the Mie scattering. A value of 1 means that when light hits a particle it's passing through straight forward. A value of -1 means that all light is scatter backwards.

mie_color.description: Controls the  of the Mie scattering effect. While not physically accurate, this allows for the creation of alien-looking planets.

turbidity.description: Sets the thickness of the atmosphere. High turbidity creates a foggy-looking atmosphere, while a low turbidity results in a clearer atmosphere.

sun_disk_scale.description: Sets the size of the sun disk. Default value is based on Sol's perceived size from Earth.

ground_color.description: Modulates the  on the bottom half of the sky to represent the ground.

energy_multiplier.description: The sky's overall brightness multiplier. Higher values result in a brighter sky.

use_debanding.description: If true, enables debanding. Debanding adds a small amount of noise which helps reduce banding that appears from the smooth changes in color in the sky.

night_sky.description: for the night sky. This is added to the sky, so if it is bright enough, it may be visible during the day.

PhysicsBody2D.brief_description: Abstract base class for 2D game objects affected by physics.
PhysicsBody2D.description: is an abstract base class for 2D game objects affected by physics. All 2D physics bodies inherit from it.

move_and_collide.description:
Moves the body along the vector motion. In order to be frame rate independent in Node._physics_process or Node._process, motion should be computed using delta.
				Returns a , which contains information about the collision when stopped, or when touching another body along the motion.
				If test_only is true, the body does not move but the would-be collision information is given.
				safe_margin is the extra margin used for collision recovery (see CharacterBody2D.safe_margin for more details).
				If recovery_as_collision is true, any depenetration from the recovery phase is also reported as a collision; this is used e.g. by  for improving floor detection during floor snapping.

test_move.description:
Checks for collisions without moving the body. In order to be frame rate independent in Node._physics_process or Node._process, motion should be computed using delta.
				Virtually sets the node's position, scale and rotation to that of the given , then tries to move the body along the vector motion. Returns true if a collision would stop the body from moving along the whole path.
				collision is an optional object of type , which contains additional information about the collision when stopped, or when touching another body along the motion.
				safe_margin is the extra margin used for collision recovery (see CharacterBody2D.safe_margin for more details).
				If recovery_as_collision is true, any depenetration from the recovery phase is also reported as a collision; this is useful for checking whether the body would touch any other bodies.

get_gravity.description: Returns the gravity vector computed from all sources that can affect the body, including all gravity overrides from  nodes and the global world gravity.

get_collision_exceptions.description: Returns an array of nodes that were added as collision exceptions for this body.

add_collision_exception_with.description: Adds a body to the list of bodies that this body can't collide with.

remove_collision_exception_with.description: Removes a body from the list of bodies that this body can't collide with.

PhysicsBody3D.brief_description: Abstract base class for 3D game objects affected by physics.
PhysicsBody3D.description:
is an abstract base class for 3D game objects affected by physics. All 3D physics bodies inherit from it.
		Warning: With a non-uniform scale, this node will likely not behave as expected. It is advised to keep its scale the same on all axes and adjust its collision shape(s) instead.

move_and_collide.description:
Moves the body along the vector motion. In order to be frame rate independent in Node._physics_process or Node._process, motion should be computed using delta.
				The body will stop if it collides. Returns a , which contains information about the collision when stopped, or when touching another body along the motion.
				If test_only is true, the body does not move but the would-be collision information is given.
				safe_margin is the extra margin used for collision recovery (see CharacterBody3D.safe_margin for more details).
				If recovery_as_collision is true, any depenetration from the recovery phase is also reported as a collision; this is used e.g. by  for improving floor detection during floor snapping.
				max_collisions allows to retrieve more than one collision result.

test_move.description:
Checks for collisions without moving the body. In order to be frame rate independent in Node._physics_process or Node._process, motion should be computed using delta.
				Virtually sets the node's position, scale and rotation to that of the given , then tries to move the body along the vector motion. Returns true if a collision would stop the body from moving along the whole path.
				collision is an optional object of type , which contains additional information about the collision when stopped, or when touching another body along the motion.
				safe_margin is the extra margin used for collision recovery (see CharacterBody3D.safe_margin for more details).
				If recovery_as_collision is true, any depenetration from the recovery phase is also reported as a collision; this is useful for checking whether the body would touch any other bodies.
				max_collisions allows to retrieve more than one collision result.

get_gravity.description: Returns the gravity vector computed from all sources that can affect the body, including all gravity overrides from  nodes and the global world gravity.

set_axis_lock.description: Locks or unlocks the specified linear or rotational axis depending on the value of lock.

get_axis_lock.description: Returns true if the specified linear or rotational axis is locked.

get_collision_exceptions.description: Returns an array of nodes that were added as collision exceptions for this body.

add_collision_exception_with.description: Adds a body to the list of bodies that this body can't collide with.

remove_collision_exception_with.description: Removes a body from the list of bodies that this body can't collide with.

axis_lock_linear_x.description: Lock the body's linear movement in the X axis.

axis_lock_linear_y.description: Lock the body's linear movement in the Y axis.

axis_lock_linear_z.description: Lock the body's linear movement in the Z axis.

axis_lock_angular_x.description: Lock the body's rotation in the X axis.

axis_lock_angular_y.description: Lock the body's rotation in the Y axis.

axis_lock_angular_z.description: Lock the body's rotation in the Z axis.

PhysicsDirectBodyState2D.brief_description: Provides direct access to a physics body in the .
PhysicsDirectBodyState2D.description: Provides direct access to a physics body in the , allowing safe changes to physics properties. This object is passed via the direct state callback of , and is intended for changing the direct state of that body. See RigidBody2D._integrate_forces.

get_velocity_at_local_position.description: Returns the body's velocity at the given relative position, including both translation and rotation.

apply_central_impulse.description:
Applies a directional impulse without affecting rotation.
				An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).
				This is equivalent to using apply_impulse at the body's center of mass.

apply_torque_impulse.description:
Applies a rotational impulse to the body without affecting the position.
				An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).
				Note: inverse_inertia is required for this to work. To have inverse_inertia, an active  must be a child of the node, or you can manually set inverse_inertia.

apply_impulse.description:
Applies a positioned impulse to the body.
				An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).
				position is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

apply_central_force.description:
Applies a directional force without affecting rotation. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
				This is equivalent to using apply_force at the body's center of mass.

apply_force.description:
Applies a positioned force to the body. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
				position is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

apply_torque.description:
Applies a rotational force without affecting position. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
				Note: inverse_inertia is required for this to work. To have inverse_inertia, an active  must be a child of the node, or you can manually set inverse_inertia.

add_constant_central_force.description:
Adds a constant directional force without affecting rotation that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_force = Vector2(0, 0).
				This is equivalent to using add_constant_force at the body's center of mass.

add_constant_force.description:
Adds a constant positioned force to the body that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_force = Vector2(0, 0).
				position is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

add_constant_torque.description: Adds a constant rotational force without affecting position that keeps being applied over time until cleared with constant_torque = 0.

set_constant_force.description:
Sets the body's total constant positional forces applied during each physics update.
				See add_constant_force and add_constant_central_force.

get_constant_force.description:
Returns the body's total constant positional forces applied during each physics update.
				See add_constant_force and add_constant_central_force.

set_constant_torque.description:
Sets the body's total constant rotational forces applied during each physics update.
				See add_constant_torque.

get_constant_torque.description:
Returns the body's total constant rotational forces applied during each physics update.
				See add_constant_torque.

get_contact_count.description:
Returns the number of contacts this body has with other bodies.
				Note: By default, this returns 0 unless bodies are configured to monitor contacts. See RigidBody2D.contact_monitor.

get_contact_local_position.description: Returns the position of the contact point on the body in the global coordinate system.

get_contact_local_normal.description: Returns the local normal at the contact point.

get_contact_local_shape.description: Returns the local shape index of the collision.

get_contact_local_velocity_at_position.description: Returns the velocity vector at the body's contact point.

get_contact_collider_position.description: Returns the position of the contact point on the collider in the global coordinate system.

get_contact_collider_object.description: Returns the collider object. This depends on how it was created (will return a scene node if such was used to create it).

get_contact_collider_velocity_at_positio.description: Returns the velocity vector at the collider's contact point.

get_contact_impulse.description: Returns the impulse created by the contact.

integrate_forces.description: Updates the body's linear and angular velocity by applying gravity and damping for the equivalent of one physics tick.

get_space_state.description: Returns the current state of the space, useful for queries.

step.description: The timestep (delta) used for the simulation.

inverse_mass.description: The inverse of the mass of the body.

inverse_inertia.description: The inverse of the inertia of the body.

total_angular_damp.description: The rate at which the body stops rotating, if there are not any other forces moving it.

total_linear_damp.description: The rate at which the body stops moving, if there are not any other forces moving it.

total_gravity.description: The total gravity vector being currently applied to this body.

center_of_mass.description: The body's center of mass position relative to the body's center in the global coordinate system.

center_of_mass_local.description: The body's center of mass position in the body's local coordinate system.

angular_velocity.description: The body's rotational velocity in radians per second.

linear_velocity.description: The body's linear velocity in pixels per second.

sleeping.description: If true, this body is currently sleeping (not active).

PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D.brief_description: Provides direct access to a physics space in the .
PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D.description:
Provides direct access to a physics space in the . It's used mainly to do queries against objects and areas residing in a given space.
		Note: This class is not meant to be instantiated directly. Use World2D.direct_space_state to get the world's physics 2D space state.

intersect_point.description:
Checks whether a point is inside any solid shape. Position and other parameters are defined through . The shapes the point is inside of are returned in an array containing dictionaries with the following fields:
				collider: The colliding object.
				collider_id: The colliding object's ID.
				rid: The intersecting object's .
				shape: The shape index of the colliding shape.
				The number of intersections can be limited with the max_results parameter, to reduce the processing time.
				Note: s and s in Segments build mode are not solid shapes. Therefore, they will not be detected.

intersect_ray.description:
Intersects a ray in a given space. Ray position and other parameters are defined through . The returned object is a dictionary with the following fields:
				collider: The colliding object.
				collider_id: The colliding object's ID.
				normal: The object's surface normal at the intersection point, or Vector2(0, 0) if the ray starts inside the shape and PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D.hit_from_inside is true.
				position: The intersection point.
				rid: The intersecting object's .
				shape: The shape index of the colliding shape.
				If the ray did not intersect anything, then an empty dictionary is returned instead.

intersect_shape.description:
Checks the intersections of a shape, given through a  object, against the space. The intersected shapes are returned in an array containing dictionaries with the following fields:
				collider: The colliding object.
				collider_id: The colliding object's ID.
				rid: The intersecting object's .
				shape: The shape index of the colliding shape.
				The number of intersections can be limited with the max_results parameter, to reduce the processing time.

cast_motion.description:
Checks how far a  can move without colliding. All the parameters for the query, including the shape and the motion, are supplied through a  object.
				Returns an array with the safe and unsafe proportions (between 0 and 1) of the motion. The safe proportion is the maximum fraction of the motion that can be made without a collision. The unsafe proportion is the minimum fraction of the distance that must be moved for a collision. If no collision is detected a result of  will be returned.
				Note: Any s that the shape is already colliding with e.g. inside of, will be ignored. Use collide_shape to determine the s that the shape is already colliding with.

collide_shape.description:
Checks the intersections of a shape, given through a  object, against the space. The resulting array contains a list of points where the shape intersects another. Like with intersect_shape, the number of returned results can be limited to save processing time.
				Returned points are a list of pairs of contact points. For each pair the first one is in the shape passed in  object, second one is in the collided shape from the physics space.

get_rest_info.description:
Checks the intersections of a shape, given through a  object, against the space. If it collides with more than one shape, the nearest one is selected. The returned object is a dictionary containing the following fields:
				collider_id: The colliding object's ID.
				linear_velocity: The colliding object's velocity . If the object is an , the result is (0, 0).
				normal: The collision normal of the query shape at the intersection point, pointing away from the intersecting object.
				point: The intersection point.
				rid: The intersecting object's .
				shape: The shape index of the colliding shape.
				If the shape did not intersect anything, then an empty dictionary is returned instead.

				normal: The object's surface normal at the intersection point, or Vector3(0, 0, 0) if the ray starts inside the shape and PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.hit_from_inside is true.
				position: The intersection point.
				face_index: The face index at the intersection point.
				Note: Returns a valid number only if the intersected shape is a . Otherwise, -1 is returned.
				rid: The intersecting object's .
				shape: The shape index of the colliding shape.
				If the ray did not intersect anything, then an empty dictionary is returned instead.

intersect_shape.description:
Checks the intersections of a shape, given through a  object, against the space. The intersected shapes are returned in an array containing dictionaries with the following fields:
				collider: The colliding object.
				collider_id: The colliding object's ID.
				rid: The intersecting object's .
				shape: The shape index of the colliding shape.
				The number of intersections can be limited with the max_results parameter, to reduce the processing time.
				Note: This method does not take into account the motion property of the object.

cast_motion.description:
Checks how far a  can move without colliding. All the parameters for the query, including the shape and the motion, are supplied through a  object.
				Returns an array with the safe and unsafe proportions (between 0 and 1) of the motion. The safe proportion is the maximum fraction of the motion that can be made without a collision. The unsafe proportion is the minimum fraction of the distance that must be moved for a collision. If no collision is detected a result of  will be returned.
				Note: Any s that the shape is already colliding with e.g. inside of, will be ignored. Use collide_shape to determine the s that the shape is already colliding with.

collide_shape.description:
Checks the intersections of a shape, given through a  object, against the space. The resulting array contains a list of points where the shape intersects another. Like with intersect_shape, the number of returned results can be limited to save processing time.
				Returned points are a list of pairs of contact points. For each pair the first one is in the shape passed in  object, second one is in the collided shape from the physics space.
				Note: This method does not take into account the motion property of the object.

get_rest_info.description:
Checks the intersections of a shape, given through a  object, against the space. If it collides with more than one shape, the nearest one is selected. The returned object is a dictionary containing the following fields:
				collider_id: The colliding object's ID.
				linear_velocity: The colliding object's velocity . If the object is an , the result is (0, 0, 0).
				normal: The collision normal of the query shape at the intersection point, pointing away from the intersecting object.
				point: The intersection point.
				rid: The intersecting object's .
				shape: The shape index of the colliding shape.
				If the shape did not intersect anything, then an empty dictionary is returned instead.
				Note: This method does not take into account the motion property of the object.

PhysicsMaterial.description: Holds physics-related properties of a surface, namely its roughness and bounciness. This class is used to apply these properties to a physics body.

friction.description: The body's friction. Values range from 0 (frictionless) to 1 (maximum friction).

rough.description: If true, the physics engine will use the friction of the object marked as "rough" when two objects collide. If false, the physics engine will use the lowest friction of all colliding objects instead. If true for both colliding objects, the physics engine will use the highest friction.

bounce.description:
The body's bounciness. Values range from 0 (no bounce) to 1 (full bounciness).
			Note: Even with bounce set to 1.0, some energy will be lost over time due to linear and angular damping. To have a physics body that preserves all its energy over time, set bounce to 1.0, the body's linear damp mode to Replace (if applicable), its linear damp to 0.0, its angular damp mode to Replace (if applicable), and its angular damp to 0.0.

absorbent.description: If true, subtracts the bounciness from the colliding object's bounciness instead of adding it.
