			Generally the  used is an , though it can be any , including an .

Skeleton2D.brief_description: The parent of a hierarchy of s, used to create a 2D skeletal animation.
Skeleton2D.description:
parents a hierarchy of  nodes. It holds a reference to each 's rest pose and acts as a single point of access to its bones.
		To set up different types of inverse kinematics for the given Skeleton2D, a  should be created. The inverse kinematics be applied by increasing SkeletonModificationStack2D.modification_count and creating the desired number of modifications.

get_bone_count.description: Returns the number of  nodes in the node hierarchy parented by Skeleton2D.

get_bone.description: Returns a  from the node hierarchy parented by Skeleton2D. The object to return is identified by the parameter idx. Bones are indexed by descending the node hierarchy from top to bottom, adding the children of each branch before moving to the next sibling.

get_skeleton.description: Returns the  of a Skeleton2D instance.

set_modification_stack.description: Sets the  attached to this skeleton.

get_modification_stack.description: Returns the  attached to this skeleton, if one exists.

execute_modifications.description: Executes all the modifications on the , if the Skeleton2D has one assigned.

set_bone_local_pose_override.description:
Sets the local pose transform, override_pose, for the bone at bone_idx.
				strength is the interpolation strength that will be used when applying the pose, and persistent determines if the applied pose will remain.
				Note: The pose transform needs to be a local transform relative to the  node at bone_idx!

get_bone_local_pose_override.description: Returns the local pose override transform for bone_idx.

Skeleton3D.brief_description: A node containing a bone hierarchy, used to create a 3D skeletal animation.
Skeleton3D.description:
provides an interface for managing a hierarchy of bones, including pose, rest and animation (see ). It can also use ragdoll physics.
		The overall transform of a bone with respect to the skeleton is determined by bone pose. Bone rest defines the initial transform of the bone pose.
		Note that "global pose" below refers to the overall transform of the bone with respect to skeleton, so it is not the actual global/world transform of the bone.

add_bone.description:
Adds a new bone with the given name. Returns the new bone's index, or -1 if this method fails.
				Note: Bone names should be unique, non empty, and cannot include the : and / characters.

find_bone.description: Returns the bone index that matches name as its name. Returns -1 if no bone with this name exists.

get_bone_name.description: Returns the name of the bone at index bone_idx.

set_bone_name.description: Sets the bone name, name, for the bone at bone_idx.

get_bone_meta.description: Returns the metadata with the given key for the bone at index bone_idx.

get_bone_meta_list.description: Returns the list of all metadata keys for the bone at index bone_idx.

has_bone_meta.description: Returns true if the bone at index bone_idx has metadata with the given key.

set_bone_meta.description: Sets the metadata with the given key to value for the bone at index bone_idx.

get_concatenated_bone_names.description:
Returns all bone names concatenated with commas (,) as a single .
				It is useful to set it as a hint for the enum property.

get_bone_parent.description:
Returns the bone index which is the parent of the bone at bone_idx. If -1, then bone has no parent.
				Note: The parent bone returned will always be less than bone_idx.

set_bone_parent.description:
Sets the bone index parent_idx as the parent of the bone at bone_idx. If -1, then bone has no parent.
				Note: parent_idx must be less than bone_idx.

get_bone_count.description: Returns the number of bones in the skeleton.

get_version.description:
Returns the number of times the bone hierarchy has changed within this skeleton, including renames.
				The Skeleton version is not serialized: only use within a single instance of Skeleton3D.
				Use for invalidating caches in IK solvers and other nodes which process bones.

unparent_bone_and_rest.description: Unparents the bone at bone_idx and sets its rest position to that of its parent prior to being reset.

get_bone_children.description: Returns an array containing the bone indexes of all the child node of the passed in bone, bone_idx.

get_parentless_bones.description: Returns an array with all of the bones that are parentless. Another way to look at this is that it returns the indexes of all the bones that are not dependent or modified by other bones in the Skeleton.

get_bone_rest.description: Returns the rest transform for a bone bone_idx.

set_bone_rest.description: Sets the rest transform for bone bone_idx.

get_bone_global_rest.description: Returns the global rest transform for bone_idx.

register_skin.description: Binds the given Skin to the Skeleton.

localize_rests.description: Returns all bones in the skeleton to their rest poses.

clear_bones.description: Clear all the bones in this skeleton.

get_bone_pose.description:
Returns the pose transform of the specified bone.
				Note: This is the pose you set to the skeleton in the process, the final pose can get overridden by modifiers in the deferred process, if you want to access the final pose, use .

set_bone_pose.description: Sets the pose transform, pose, for the bone at bone_idx.

set_bone_pose_position.description: Sets the pose position of the bone at bone_idx to position. position is a  describing a position local to the  node.

set_bone_pose_rotation.description: Sets the pose rotation of the bone at bone_idx to rotation. rotation is a  describing a rotation in the bone's local coordinate space with respect to the rotation of any parent bones.

set_bone_pose_scale.description: Sets the pose scale of the bone at bone_idx to scale.

get_bone_pose_position.description: Returns the pose position of the bone at bone_idx. The returned  is in the local coordinate space of the  node.

get_bone_pose_rotation.description: Returns the pose rotation of the bone at bone_idx. The returned  is local to the bone with respect to the rotation of any parent bones.

get_bone_pose_scale.description: Returns the pose scale of the bone at bone_idx.

reset_bone_pose.description: Sets the bone pose to rest for bone_idx.

reset_bone_poses.description: Sets all bone poses to rests.

is_bone_enabled.description: Returns whether the bone pose for the bone at bone_idx is enabled.

set_bone_enabled.description: Disables the pose for the bone at bone_idx if false, enables the bone pose if true.

get_bone_global_pose.description:
Returns the overall transform of the specified bone, with respect to the skeleton. Being relative to the skeleton frame, this is not the actual "global" transform of the bone.
				Note: This is the global pose you set to the skeleton in the process, the final global pose can get overridden by modifiers in the deferred process, if you want to access the final global pose, use .

set_bone_global_pose.description:
Sets the global pose transform, pose, for the bone at bone_idx.
				Note: If other bone poses have been changed, this method executes a dirty poses recalculation and will cause performance to deteriorate. If you know that multiple global poses will be applied, consider using set_bone_pose with precalculation.

force_update_all_bone_transforms.description: Force updates the bone transforms/poses for all bones in the skeleton.

force_update_bone_child_transform.description: Force updates the bone transform for the bone at bone_idx and all of its children.

advance.description:
Manually advance the child s by the specified time (in seconds).
				Note: The delta is temporarily accumulated in the , and the deferred process uses the accumulated value to process the modification.

clear_bones_global_pose_override.description: Removes the global pose override on all bones in the skeleton.

set_bone_global_pose_override.description:
Sets the global pose transform, pose, for the bone at bone_idx.
				amount is the interpolation strength that will be used when applying the pose, and persistent determines if the applied pose will remain.
				Note: The pose transform needs to be a global pose! To convert a world transform from a  to a global bone pose, multiply the Transform3D.affine_inverse of the node's Node3D.global_transform by the desired world transform.

get_bone_global_pose_override.description: Returns the global pose override transform for bone_idx.

get_bone_global_pose_no_override.description: Returns the overall transform of the specified bone, with respect to the skeleton, but without any global pose overrides. Being relative to the skeleton frame, this is not the actual "global" transform of the bone.

physical_bones_stop_simulation.description: Tells the  nodes in the Skeleton to stop simulating.

physical_bones_start_simulation.description:
Tells the  nodes in the Skeleton to start simulating and reacting to the physics world.
				Optionally, a list of bone names can be passed-in, allowing only the passed-in bones to be simulated.

physical_bones_add_collision_exception.description:
Adds a collision exception to the physical bone.
				Works just like the  node.

physical_bones_remove_collision_exceptio.description:
Removes a collision exception to the physical bone.
				Works just like the  node.

motion_scale.description:
Multiplies the 3D position track animation.
			Note: Unless this value is 1.0, the key value in animation will not match the actual position value.

show_rest_only.description: If true, forces the bones in their default rest pose, regardless of their values. In the editor, this also prevents the bones from being edited.

modifier_callback_mode_process.description: Sets the processing timing for the Modifier.

animate_physical_bones.description:
If you follow the recommended workflow and explicitly have  as a child of , you can control whether it is affected by raycasting without running physical_bones_start_simulation, by its SkeletonModifier3D.active.
			However, for old (deprecated) configurations,  has an internal virtual  for compatibility. This property controls the internal virtual 's SkeletonModifier3D.active.

SkeletonIK3D.brief_description: A node used to rotate all bones of a  bone chain a way that places the end bone at a desired 3D position.
SkeletonIK3D.description:
SkeletonIK3D is used to rotate all bones of a  bone chain a way that places the end bone at a desired 3D position. A typical scenario for IK in games is to place a character's feet on the ground or a character's hands on a currently held object. SkeletonIK uses FabrikInverseKinematic internally to solve the bone chain and applies the results to the  bones_global_pose_override property for all affected bones in the chain. If fully applied, this overwrites any bone transform from s or bone custom poses set by users. The applied amount can be controlled with the SkeletonModifier3D.influence property.
		
		# Apply IK effect automatically on every new frame (not the current)
		skeleton_ik_node.start()

		# Apply IK effect only on the current frame
		skeleton_ik_node.start(true)

		# Stop IK effect and reset bones_global_pose_override on Skeleton
		skeleton_ik_node.stop()

		# Apply full IK effect
		skeleton_ik_node.set_influence(1.0)

		# Apply half IK effect
		skeleton_ik_node.set_influence(0.5)

		# Apply zero IK effect (a value at or below 0.01 also removes bones_global_pose_override on Skeleton)
		skeleton_ik_node.set_influence(0.0)

get_parent_skeleton.description: Returns the parent  node that was present when SkeletonIK entered the scene tree. Returns null if the parent node was not a  node when SkeletonIK3D entered the scene tree.

is_running.description: Returns true if SkeletonIK is applying IK effects on continues frames to the  bones. Returns false if SkeletonIK is stopped or start was used with the one_time parameter set to true.

start.description: Starts applying IK effects on each frame to the  bones but will only take effect starting on the next frame. If one_time is true, this will take effect immediately but also reset on the next frame.

stop.description: Stops applying IK effects on each frame to the  bones and also calls Skeleton3D.clear_bones_global_pose_override to remove existing overrides on all bones.

root_bone.description: The name of the current root bone, the first bone in the IK chain.

tip_bone.description: The name of the current tip bone, the last bone in the IK chain placed at the target transform (or target_node if defined).

target.description: First target of the IK chain where the tip bone is placed and, if override_tip_basis is true, how the tip bone is rotated. If a target_node path is available the nodes transform is used instead and this property is ignored.

override_tip_basis.description: If true overwrites the rotation of the tip bone with the rotation of the target (or target_node if defined).

use_magnet.description: If true, instructs the IK solver to consider the secondary magnet target (pole target) when calculating the bone chain. Use the magnet position (pole target) to control the bending of the IK chain.

magnet.description: Secondary target position (first is target property or target_node) for the IK chain. Use magnet position (pole target) to control the bending of the IK chain. Only works if the bone chain has more than 2 bones. The middle chain bone position will be linearly interpolated with the magnet position.

target_node.description: Target node  for the IK chain. If available, the node's current  is used instead of the target property.

min_distance.description: The minimum distance between bone and goal target. If the distance is below this value, the IK solver stops further iterations.

max_iterations.description: Number of iteration loops used by the IK solver to produce more accurate (and elegant) bone chain results.

interpolation.description: Interpolation value for how much the IK results are applied to the current skeleton bone chain. A value of 1.0 will overwrite all skeleton bone transforms completely while a value of 0.0 will visually disable the SkeletonIK.

SkeletonModification2D.brief_description: Base class for resources that operate on s in a .
SkeletonModification2D.description:
This resource provides an interface that can be expanded so code that operates on  nodes in a  can be mixed and matched together to create complex interactions.
		This is used to provide Godot with a flexible and powerful Inverse Kinematics solution that can be adapted for many different uses.

_execute.description: Executes the given modification. This is where the modification performs whatever function it is designed to do.

_setup_modification.description: Called when the modification is setup. This is where the modification performs initialization.

_draw_editor_gizmo.description:
Used for drawing editor-only modification gizmos. This function will only be called in the Godot editor and can be overridden to draw custom gizmos.
				Note: You will need to use the Skeleton2D from SkeletonModificationStack2D.get_skeleton and it's draw functions, as the  resource cannot draw on its own.

get_modification_stack.description: Returns the  that this modification is bound to. Through the modification stack, you can access the Skeleton2D the modification is operating on.

set_is_setup.description: Manually allows you to set the setup state of the modification. This function should only rarely be used, as the  the modification is bound to should handle setting the modification up.

get_is_setup.description: Returns whether this modification has been successfully setup or not.

SkeletonModification2DCCDIK.brief_description: A modification that uses CCDIK to manipulate a series of bones to reach a target in 2D.
SkeletonModification2DCCDIK.description:
This  uses an algorithm called Cyclic Coordinate Descent Inverse Kinematics, or CCDIK, to manipulate a chain of bones in a  so it reaches a defined target.
		CCDIK works by rotating a set of bones, typically called a "bone chain", on a single axis. Each bone is rotated to face the target from the tip (by default), which over a chain of bones allow it to rotate properly to reach the target. Because the bones only rotate on a single axis, CCDIK can look more robotic than other IK solvers.
		Note: The CCDIK modifier has ccdik_joints, which are the data objects that hold the data for each joint in the CCDIK chain. This is different from a bone! CCDIK joints hold the data needed for each bone in the bone chain used by CCDIK.
		CCDIK also fully supports angle constraints, allowing for more control over how a solution is met.

SkeletonModification2DFABRIK.brief_description: A modification that uses FABRIK to manipulate a series of  nodes to reach a target.
SkeletonModification2DFABRIK.description:
This  uses an algorithm called Forward And Backward Reaching Inverse Kinematics, or FABRIK, to rotate a bone chain so that it reaches a target.
		FABRIK works by knowing the positions and lengths of a series of bones, typically called a "bone chain". It first starts by running a forward pass, which places the final bone at the target's position. Then all other bones are moved towards the tip bone, so they stay at the defined bone length away. Then a backwards pass is performed, where the root/first bone in the FABRIK chain is placed back at the origin. Then all other bones are moved so they stay at the defined bone length away. This positions the bone chain so that it reaches the target when possible, but all of the bones stay the correct length away from each other.
		Because of how FABRIK works, it often gives more natural results than those seen in .
		Note: The FABRIK modifier has fabrik_joints, which are the data objects that hold the data for each joint in the FABRIK chain. This is different from  nodes! FABRIK joints hold the data needed for each  in the bone chain used by FABRIK.
		To help control how the FABRIK joints move, a magnet vector can be passed, which can nudge the bones in a certain direction prior to solving, giving a level of control over the final result.

SkeletonModification2DJiggle.brief_description: A modification that jiggles  nodes as they move towards a target.
SkeletonModification2DJiggle.description:
This modification moves a series of bones, typically called a bone chain, towards a target. What makes this modification special is that it calculates the velocity and acceleration for each bone in the bone chain, and runs a very light physics-like calculation using the inputted values. This allows the bones to overshoot the target and "jiggle" around. It can be configured to act more like a spring, or sway around like cloth might.
		This modification is useful for adding additional motion to things like hair, the edges of clothing, and more. It has several settings to that allow control over how the joint moves when the target moves.
		Note: The Jiggle modifier has jiggle_joints, which are the data objects that hold the data for each joint in the Jiggle chain. This is different from than  nodes! Jiggle joints hold the data needed for each  in the bone chain used by the Jiggle modification.

SkeletonModification2DLookAt.description: This  rotates a bone to look a target. This is extremely helpful for moving character's head to look at the player, rotating a turret to look at a target, or any other case where you want to make a bone rotate towards something quickly and easily.

SkeletonModification2DTwoBoneIK.brief_description: A modification that rotates two bones using the law of cosines to reach the target.
SkeletonModification2DTwoBoneIK.description:
This  uses an algorithm typically called TwoBoneIK. This algorithm works by leveraging the law of cosines and the lengths of the bones to figure out what rotation the bones currently have, and what rotation they need to make a complete triangle, where the first bone, the second bone, and the target form the three vertices of the triangle. Because the algorithm works by making a triangle, it can only operate on two bones.
		TwoBoneIK is great for arms, legs, and really any joints that can be represented by just two bones that bend to reach a target. This solver is more lightweight than , but gives similar, natural looking results.

SkeletonModificationStack2D.brief_description: A resource that holds a stack of s.
SkeletonModificationStack2D.description:
This resource is used by the Skeleton and holds a stack of s.
		This controls the order of the modifications and how they are applied. Modification order is especially important for full-body IK setups, as you need to execute the modifications in the correct order to get the desired results. For example, you want to execute a modification on the spine before the arms on a humanoid skeleton.
		This resource also controls how strongly all of the modifications are applied to the .

setup.description: Sets up the modification stack so it can execute. This function should be called by  and shouldn't be manually called unless you know what you are doing.

execute.description:
Executes all of the s in the stack that use the same execution mode as the passed-in execution_mode, starting from index 0 to modification_count.
				Note: The order of the modifications can matter depending on the modifications. For example, modifications on a spine should operate before modifications on the arms in order to get proper results.

Sky.description: The  class uses a  to render a 3D environment's background and the light it emits by updating the reflection/radiance cubemaps.

The 's radiance map size. The higher the radiance map size, the more detailed the lighting from the  will be.

Slider.description: Abstract base class for sliders, used to adjust a value by moving a grabber along a horizontal or vertical axis. Sliders are -based controls.

editable.description: If true, the slider can be interacted with. If false, the value can be changed only by code.

scrollable.description: If true, the value can be changed using the mouse wheel.

tick_count.description: Number of ticks displayed on the slider, including border ticks. Ticks are uniformly-distributed value markers.

ticks_on_borders.description: If true, the slider will display ticks for minimum and maximum values.

ticks_position.description: Sets the position of the ticks. See  for details.

SliderJoint3D.brief_description: A physics joint that restricts the movement of a 3D physics body along an axis relative to another physics body.
SliderJoint3D.description: A physics joint that restricts the movement of a 3D physics body along an axis relative to another physics body. For example, Body A could be a  representing a piston base, while Body B could be a  representing the piston head, moving up and down.

set_param.description: Assigns value to the given parameter.

get_param.description: Returns the value of the given parameter.

SocketServer.brief_description: An abstract class for servers based on sockets.

is_connection_available.description: Returns true if a connection is available for taking.

is_listening.description: Returns true if the server is currently listening for connections.

take_socket_connection.description: If a connection is available, returns a StreamPeerSocket with the connection.

SoftBody3D.description:
A deformable 3D physics mesh. Used to create elastic or deformable objects such as cloth, rubber, or other flexible materials.
		Additionally,  is subject to wind forces defined in  (see Area3D.wind_source_path, Area3D.wind_force_magnitude, and Area3D.wind_attenuation_factor).
		Note: It's recommended to use Jolt Physics when using  instead of the default GodotPhysics3D, as Jolt Physics' soft body implementation is faster and more reliable. You can switch the physics engine using the ProjectSettings.physics/3d/physics_engine project setting.

get_physics_rid.description: Returns the internal  used by the  for this body.

set_collision_mask_value.description: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_mask, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.

get_collision_mask_value.description: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_mask is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.

set_collision_layer_value.description: Based on value, enables or disables the specified layer in the collision_layer, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.

get_collision_layer_value.description: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the collision_layer is enabled, given a layer_number between 1 and 32.

get_collision_exceptions.description: Returns an array of nodes that were added as collision exceptions for this body.

add_collision_exception_with.description: Adds a body to the list of bodies that this body can't collide with.

remove_collision_exception_with.description: Removes a body from the list of bodies that this body can't collide with.

get_point_transform.description: Returns local translation of a vertex in the surface array.

apply_impulse.description:
Applies an impulse to a point.
				An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).

apply_force.description: Applies a force to a point. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.

apply_central_impulse.description:
Distributes and applies an impulse to all points.
				An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).

apply_central_force.description: Distributes and applies a force to all points. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.

set_point_pinned.description: Sets the pinned state of a surface vertex. When set to true, the optional attachment_path can define a  the pinned vertex will be attached to.

is_point_pinned.description: Returns true if vertex is set to pinned.

collision_layer.description:
The physics layers this SoftBody3D is in. Collision objects can exist in one or more of 32 different layers. See also collision_mask.
			Note: Object A can detect a contact with object B only if object B is in any of the layers that object A scans. See Collision layers and masks in the documentation for more information.

collision_mask.description:
The physics layers this SoftBody3D scans. Collision objects can scan one or more of 32 different layers. See also collision_layer.
			Note: Object A can detect a contact with object B only if object B is in any of the layers that object A scans. See Collision layers and masks in the documentation for more information.

parent_collision_ignore.description: to a  this SoftBody3D should avoid clipping.

simulation_precision.description: Increasing this value will improve the resulting simulation, but can affect performance. Use with care.

linear_stiffness.description: Higher values will result in a stiffer body, while lower values will increase the body's ability to bend. The value can be between 0.0 and 1.0 (inclusive).

shrinking_factor.description:
Scales the rest lengths of 's edge constraints. Positive values shrink the mesh, while negative values expand it. For example, a value of 0.1 shortens the edges of the mesh by 10%, while -0.1 expands the edges by 10%.
			Note: shrinking_factor is best used on surface meshes with pinned points.

pressure_coefficient.description: The pressure coefficient of this soft body. Simulate pressure build-up from inside this body. Higher values increase the strength of this effect.

damping_coefficient.description: The body's damping coefficient. Higher values will slow down the body more noticeably when forces are applied.

drag_coefficient.description:
The body's drag coefficient. Higher values increase this body's air resistance.
			Note: This value is currently unused by Godot's default physics implementation.

ray_pickable.description: If true, the  will respond to s.

disable_mode.description: Defines the behavior in physics when Node.process_mode is set to .

radial_segments.description: Number of radial segments on the sphere.

rings.description: Number of segments along the height of the sphere.

is_hemisphere.description:
If true, a hemisphere is created rather than a full sphere.
			Note: To get a regular hemisphere, the height and radius of the sphere must be equal.

SphereOccluder3D.brief_description: Spherical shape for use with occlusion culling in .
SphereOccluder3D.description:
stores a sphere shape that can be used by the engine's occlusion culling system.
		See 's documentation for instructions on setting up occlusion culling.

SphereShape3D.brief_description: A 3D sphere shape used for physics collision.
SphereShape3D.description:
A 3D sphere shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a .
		Performance:  is fast to check collisions against. It is faster than , , and .

radius.description: The sphere's radius. The shape's diameter is double the radius.

apply.description: Applies the current value of this . This is equivalent to pressing Enter while editing the  used by the . This will cause  to be emitted and its currently contained expression to be evaluated.

get_line_edit.description:
Returns the  instance from this . You can use it to access properties and methods of .
				Warning: This is a required internal node, removing and freeing it may cause a crash. If you wish to hide it or any of its children, use their CanvasItem.visible property.

alignment.description: Changes the alignment of the underlying .

editable.description: If true, the  will be editable. Otherwise, it will be read only.

update_on_text_changed.description:
Sets the value of the  for this  when the  text is changed instead of submitted. See  and .
			Note: If set to true, this will interfere with entering mathematical expressions in the . The  will try to evaluate the expression as you type, which means symbols like a trailing + are removed immediately by the expression being evaluated.

prefix.description: Adds the specified prefix string before the numerical value of the .

suffix.description: Adds the specified suffix string after the numerical value of the .

custom_arrow_step.description:
If not 0, sets the step when interacting with the arrow buttons of the .
			Note: Range.value will still be rounded to a multiple of Range.step.

custom_arrow_round.description: If true, the value will be rounded to a multiple of custom_arrow_step when interacting with the arrow buttons. Otherwise, increments the value by custom_arrow_step and then rounds it according to Range.step.

select_all_on_focus.description: If true, the  will select the whole text when the  gains focus. Clicking the up and down arrows won't trigger this behavior.

SplineIK3D.brief_description: A  for aligning bones along a .
SplineIK3D.description:
A  for aligning bones along a . The smoothness of the fitting depends on the Curve3D.bake_interval.
		If you want the  to attach to a specific bone, it is recommended to place a  before the  in the  list (children of the ), and then place a  as the 's child.
		Bone twist is determined based on the Curve3D.get_point_tilt.
		If the root bone joint and the start point of the  are separated, it assumes that there is a linear line segment between them. This means that the vector pointing toward the start point of the  takes precedence over the shortest intersection point along the .
		If the end bone joint exceeds the path length, it is bent as close as possible to the end point of the .

set_path_3d.description: Sets the node path of the  which is describing the path.

get_path_3d.description: Returns the node path of the  which is describing the path.

set_tilt_enabled.description: Sets if the tilt property of the  should affect the bone twist.

is_tilt_enabled.description: Returns if the tilt property of the  affects the bone twist.

set_tilt_fade_in.description:
If size is greater than 0, the tilt is interpolated between size start bones from the start point of the  when they are apart.
				If size is equal 0, the tilts between the root bone head and the start point of the  are unified with a tilt of the start point of the .
				If size is less than 0, the tilts between the root bone and the start point of the  are 0.0.

get_tilt_fade_in.description: Returns the tilt interpolation method used between the root bone and the start point of the  when they are apart. See also set_tilt_fade_in.

set_tilt_fade_out.description:
If size is greater than 0, the tilt is interpolated between size end bones from the end point of the  when they are apart.
				If size is equal 0, the tilts between the end bone tail and the end point of the  are unified with a tilt of the end point of the .
				If size is less than 0, the tilts between the end bone and the end point of the  are 0.0.

get_tilt_fade_out.description: Returns the tilt interpolation method used between the end bone and the end point of the  when they are apart. See also set_tilt_fade_out.

SplitContainer.brief_description: A container that arranges child controls horizontally or vertically and provides grabbers for adjusting the split ratios between them.
SplitContainer.description: A container that arranges child controls horizontally or vertically and creates grabbers between them. The grabbers can be dragged around to change the size relations between the child controls.

clamp_split_offset.description: Clamps the split_offsets values to ensure they are within valid ranges and do not overlap with each other. When overlaps occur, this method prioritizes one split offset (at index priority_index) by clamping any overlapping split offsets to it.

get_drag_area_controls.description:
Returns an  of the drag area s. These are the interactable  nodes between each child. For example, this can be used to add a pre-configured button to a drag area  so that it rides along with the split bar. Try setting the  anchors to center prior to the Node.reparent call.
				
				$BarnacleButton.reparent($SplitContainer.get_drag_area_controls())
				
				Note: The drag area s are drawn over the 's children, so  draw objects called from a drag area and children added to it will also appear over the 's children. Try setting Control.mouse_filter of custom children to  to prevent blocking the mouse from dragging if desired.
				Warning: These are required internal nodes, removing or freeing them may cause a crash.

get_drag_area_control.description:
Returns the drag area . For example, you can move a pre-configured button into the drag area  so that it rides along with the split bar. Try setting the  anchors to center prior to the reparent() call.
				
				$BarnacleButton.reparent($SplitContainer.get_drag_area_control())
				
				Note: The drag area  is drawn over the 's children, so  draw objects called from the  and children added to the  will also appear over the 's children. Try setting Control.mouse_filter of custom children to  to prevent blocking the mouse from dragging if desired.
				Warning: This is a required internal node, removing and freeing it may cause a crash.

split_offsets.description:
Offsets for each dragger in pixels. Each one is the offset of the split between the  nodes before and after the dragger, with 0 being the default position. The default position is based on the  nodes expand flags and minimum sizes. See Control.size_flags_horizontal, Control.size_flags_vertical, and Control.size_flags_stretch_ratio.
			If none of the  nodes before the dragger are expanded, the default position will be at the start of the . If none of the  nodes after the dragger are expanded, the default position will be at the end of the . If the dragger is in between expanded  nodes, the default position will be in the middle, based on the Control.size_flags_stretch_ratios and minimum sizes.
			Note: If the split offsets cause  nodes to overlap, the first split will take priority when resolving the positions.

collapsed.description: If true, the draggers will be disabled and the children will be sized as if all split_offsets were 0.

dragger_visibility.description: Determines the dragger's visibility. This property does not determine whether dragging is enabled or not. Use dragging_enabled for that.

vertical.description:
If true, the  will arrange its children vertically, rather than horizontally.
			Can't be changed when using  and .

touch_dragger_enabled.description: If true, a touch-friendly drag handle will be enabled for better usability on smaller screens. Unlike the standard grabber, this drag handle overlaps the 's children and does not affect their minimum separation. The standard grabber will no longer be drawn when this option is enabled.

drag_area_margin_begin.description: Reduces the size of the drag area and split bar  at the beginning of the container.

drag_area_margin_end.description: Reduces the size of the drag area and split bar  at the end of the container.

drag_area_offset.description: Shifts the drag area in the axis of the container to prevent the drag area from overlapping the  or other selectable  of a child node.

drag_area_highlight_in_editor.description: Highlights the drag area  so you can see where it is during development. The drag area is gold if dragging_enabled is true, and red if false.

SpotLight3D.brief_description: A spotlight, such as a reflector spotlight or a lantern.
SpotLight3D.description:
A Spotlight is a type of  node that emits lights in a specific direction, in the shape of a cone. The light is attenuated through the distance. This attenuation can be configured by changing the energy, radius and attenuation parameters of .
		Light is emitted in the -Z direction of the node's global basis. For an unrotated light, this means that the light is emitted forwards, illuminating the front side of a 3D model (see  and ).
		Note: When using the Mobile rendering method, only 8 spot lights can be displayed on each mesh resource. Attempting to display more than 8 spot lights on a single mesh resource will result in spot lights flickering in and out as the camera moves. When using the Compatibility rendering method, only 8 spot lights can be displayed on each mesh resource by default, but this can be increased by adjusting ProjectSettings.rendering/limits/opengl/max_lights_per_object.
		Note: When using the Mobile or Compatibility rendering methods, spot lights will only correctly affect meshes whose visibility AABB intersects with the light's AABB. If using a shader to deform the mesh in a way that makes it go outside its AABB, GeometryInstance3D.extra_cull_margin must be increased on the mesh. Otherwise, the light may not be visible on the mesh.

spot_range.description:
The maximal range that can be reached by the spotlight. Note that the effectively lit area may appear to be smaller depending on the spot_attenuation in use. No matter the spot_attenuation in use, the light will never reach anything outside this range.
			Note: spot_range is not affected by Node3D.scale (the light's scale or its parent's scale).

spot_attenuation.description:
Controls the distance attenuation function for spotlights.
			A value of 0.0 will maintain a constant brightness through most of the range, but smoothly attenuate the light at the edge of the range. Use a value of 2.0 for physically accurate lights as it results in the proper inverse square attenutation.
			Note: Setting attenuation to 2.0 or higher may result in distant objects receiving minimal light, even within range. For example, with a range of 4096, an object at 100 units is attenuated by a factor of 0.0001. With a default brightness of 1, the light would not be visible at that distance.
			Note: Using negative or values higher than 10.0 may lead to unexpected results.

spot_angle.description:
The spotlight's angle in degrees. This is the angular radius, meaning the angle from the -Z axis, the cone's center, to the edge of the cone. The default angular radius of 45 degrees corresponds to a cone with an angular diameter of 90 degrees.
			Note: spot_angle is not affected by Node3D.scale (the light's scale or its parent's scale).

spot_angle_attenuation.description: The spotlight's angular attenuation curve. See also spot_attenuation.

SpringArm3D.brief_description: A 3D raycast that dynamically moves its children near the collision point.
SpringArm3D.description: casts a ray or a shape along its Z axis and moves all its direct children to the collision point, with an optional margin. This is useful for 3rd person cameras that move closer to the player when inside a tight space (you may need to exclude the player's collider from the 's collision check).

get_hit_length.description: Returns the spring arm's current length.

add_excluded_object.description: Adds the  object with the given  to the list of  objects excluded from the collision check.

remove_excluded_object.description: Removes the given  from the list of  objects excluded from the collision check.

clear_excluded_objects.description: Clears the list of  objects excluded from the collision check.

collision_mask.description: The layers against which the collision check will be done. See Collision layers and masks in the documentation for more information.

shape.description:
The  to use for the SpringArm3D.
			When the shape is set, the SpringArm3D will cast the  on its z axis instead of performing a ray cast.

spring_length.description:
The maximum extent of the SpringArm3D. This is used as a length for both the ray and the shape cast used internally to calculate the desired position of the SpringArm3D's child nodes.
			To know more about how to perform a shape cast or a ray cast, please consult the  documentation.

margin.description:
When the collision check is made, a candidate length for the SpringArm3D is given.
			The margin is then subtracted to this length and the translation is applied to the child objects of the SpringArm3D.
			This margin is useful for when the SpringArm3D has a  as a child node: without the margin, the  would be placed on the exact point of collision, while with the margin the  would be placed close to the point of collision.

SpringBoneCollision3D.brief_description: A base class of the collision that interacts with .
SpringBoneCollision3D.description:
A collision can be a child of . If it is not a child of , it has no effect.
		The colliding and sliding are done in the 's modification process in order of its collision list which is set by SpringBoneSimulator3D.set_collision_path. If SpringBoneSimulator3D.are_all_child_collisions_enabled is true, the order matches .
		If bone is set, it synchronizes with the bone pose of the ancestor , which is done in before the 's modification process as the pre-process.
		Warning: A scaled  will likely not behave as expected. Make sure that the parent  and its bones are not scaled.

get_skeleton.description: Get parent  node of the parent  if found.

bone_name.description: The name of the attached bone.

bone.description: The index of the attached bone.

position_offset.description: The offset of the position from 's bone pose position.

rotation_offset.description: The offset of the rotation from 's bone pose rotation.

SpringBoneCollisionCapsule3D.brief_description: A capsule shape collision that interacts with .
SpringBoneCollisionCapsule3D.description: A capsule shape collision that interacts with .

radius.description:
The capsule's radius.
			Note: The radius of a capsule cannot be greater than half of its height. Otherwise, the capsule becomes a sphere. If the radius is greater than half of the height, the properties adjust to a valid value.

height.description:
The capsule's full height, including the hemispheres.
			Note: The height of a capsule must be at least twice its radius. Otherwise, the capsule becomes a sphere. If the height is less than twice the radius, the properties adjust to a valid value.

mid_height.description: The capsule's height, excluding the hemispheres. This is the height of the central cylindrical part in the middle of the capsule, and is the distance between the centers of the two hemispheres. This is a wrapper for height.

inside.description: If true, the collision acts to trap the joint within the collision.

SpringBoneCollisionPlane3D.brief_description: An infinite plane collision that interacts with .
SpringBoneCollisionPlane3D.description: An infinite plane collision that interacts with . It is an infinite size XZ plane, and the +Y direction is treated as normal.

SpringBoneCollisionSphere3D.brief_description: A sphere shape collision that interacts with .
SpringBoneCollisionSphere3D.description: A sphere shape collision that interacts with .

inside.description: If true, the collision acts to trap the joint within the collision.

SpringBoneSimulator3D.brief_description: A  to apply inertial wavering to bone chains.
SpringBoneSimulator3D.description:
This  can be used to wiggle hair, cloth, and tails. This modifier behaves differently from  as it attempts to return the original pose after modification.
		If you setup set_root_bone and set_end_bone, it is treated as one bone chain. Note that it does not support a branched chain like Y-shaped chains.
		When a bone chain is created, an array is generated from the bones that exist in between and listed in the joint list.
		Several properties can be applied to each joint, such as set_joint_stiffness, set_joint_drag, and set_joint_gravity.
		For simplicity, you can set values to all joints at the same time by using a . If you want to specify detailed values individually, set set_individual_config to true.
		For physical simulation,  can have children as self-standing collisions that are not related to , see also .
		Warning: A scaled  will likely not behave as expected. Make sure that the parent  and its bones are not scaled.

set_root_bone_name.description: Sets the root bone name of the bone chain.

get_root_bone_name.description: Returns the root bone name of the bone chain.

set_root_bone.description: Sets the root bone index of the bone chain.

get_root_bone.description: Returns the root bone index of the bone chain.

set_end_bone_name.description:
Sets the end bone name of the bone chain.
				Note: End bone must be the root bone or a child of the root bone. If they are the same, the tail must be extended by set_extend_end_bone to jiggle the bone.

get_end_bone_name.description: Returns the end bone name of the bone chain.

set_end_bone.description: Sets the end bone index of the bone chain.

get_end_bone.description: Returns the end bone index of the bone chain.

set_extend_end_bone.description:
If enabled is true, the end bone is extended to have a tail.
				The extended tail config is allocated to the last element in the joint list. In other words, if you set enabled to false, the config of the last element in the joint list has no effect in the simulated result.

is_end_bone_extended.description: Returns true if the end bone is extended to have a tail.

set_end_bone_direction.description: Sets the end bone tail direction of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended is true.

get_end_bone_direction.description: Returns the tail direction of the end bone of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended is true.

set_end_bone_length.description: Sets the end bone tail length of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended is true.

get_end_bone_length.description: Returns the end bone tail length of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended is true.

set_center_from.description:
Sets what the center originates from in the bone chain.
				Bone movement is calculated based on the difference in relative distance between center and bone in the previous and next frames.
				For example, if the parent  is used as the center, the bones are considered to have not moved if the  moves in the world.
				In this case, only a change in the bone pose is considered to be a bone movement.

get_center_from.description: Returns what the center originates from in the bone chain.

set_center_node.description: Sets the center node path of the bone chain.

get_center_node.description: Returns the center node path of the bone chain.

set_center_bone_name.description: Sets the center bone name of the bone chain.

get_center_bone_name.description: Returns the center bone name of the bone chain.

set_center_bone.description: Sets the center bone index of the bone chain.

get_center_bone.description: Returns the center bone index of the bone chain.

set_radius.description:
Sets the joint radius of the bone chain. It is used to move and slide with the  in the collision list.
				The value is scaled by set_radius_damping_curve and cached in each joint setting in the joint list.

get_radius.description: Returns the joint radius of the bone chain.

set_rotation_axis.description:
Sets the rotation axis of the bone chain. If set to a specific axis, it acts like a hinge joint. The value is cached in each joint setting in the joint list.
				The axes are based on the Skeleton3D.get_bone_rest's space, if axis is , you can specify any axis.
				Note: The rotation axis vector and the forward vector shouldn't be colinear to avoid unintended rotation since  does not factor in twisting forces.

get_rotation_axis.description: Returns the rotation axis of the bone chain.

set_rotation_axis_vector.description:
Sets the rotation axis vector of the bone chain. The value is cached in each joint setting in the joint list.
				This vector is normalized by an internal process and represents the axis around which the bone chain can rotate.
				If the vector length is 0, it is considered synonymous with .

get_rotation_axis_vector.description:
Returns the rotation axis vector of the bone chain. This vector represents the axis around which the bone chain can rotate. It is determined based on the rotation axis set for the bone chain.
				If get_rotation_axis is , this method returns Vector3(0, 0, 0).

set_radius_damping_curve.description: Sets the joint radius damping curve of the bone chain.

get_radius_damping_curve.description: Returns the joint radius damping curve of the bone chain.

set_stiffness.description:
Sets the stiffness force of the bone chain. The greater the value, the faster it recovers to its initial pose.
				If stiffness is 0, the modified pose will not return to the original pose.
				The value is scaled by set_stiffness_damping_curve and cached in each joint setting in the joint list.

get_stiffness.description: Returns the stiffness force of the bone chain.

set_stiffness_damping_curve.description: Sets the stiffness force damping curve of the bone chain.

get_stiffness_damping_curve.description: Returns the stiffness force damping curve of the bone chain.

set_drag.description:
Sets the drag force of the bone chain. The greater the value, the more suppressed the wiggling.
				The value is scaled by set_drag_damping_curve and cached in each joint setting in the joint list.

get_drag.description: Returns the drag force damping curve of the bone chain.

set_drag_damping_curve.description: Sets the drag force damping curve of the bone chain.

get_drag_damping_curve.description: Returns the drag force damping curve of the bone chain.

set_gravity.description:
Sets the gravity amount of the bone chain. This value is not an acceleration, but a constant velocity of movement in set_gravity_direction.
				If gravity is not 0, the modified pose will not return to the original pose since it is always affected by gravity.
				The value is scaled by set_gravity_damping_curve and cached in each joint setting in the joint list.

get_gravity.description: Returns the gravity amount of the bone chain.

set_gravity_damping_curve.description: Sets the gravity amount damping curve of the bone chain.

get_gravity_damping_curve.description: Returns the gravity amount damping curve of the bone chain.

set_gravity_direction.description:
Sets the gravity direction of the bone chain. This value is internally normalized and then multiplied by set_gravity.
				The value is cached in each joint setting in the joint list.

get_gravity_direction.description: Returns the gravity direction of the bone chain.

set_individual_config.description: If enabled is true, the config can be edited individually for each joint.

is_config_individual.description: Returns true if the config can be edited individually for each joint.

get_joint_bone_name.description: Returns the bone name at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

get_joint_bone.description: Returns the bone index at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

set_joint_rotation_axis.description:
Sets the rotation axis at joint in the bone chain's joint list when is_config_individual is true.
				The axes are based on the Skeleton3D.get_bone_rest's space, if axis is , you can specify any axis.
				Note: The rotation axis and the forward vector shouldn't be colinear to avoid unintended rotation since  does not factor in twisting forces.

get_joint_rotation_axis.description: Returns the rotation axis at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

set_joint_rotation_axis_vector.description:
Sets the rotation axis vector for the specified joint in the bone chain.
				This vector is normalized by an internal process and represents the axis around which the bone chain can rotate.
				If the vector length is 0, it is considered synonymous with .

get_joint_rotation_axis_vector.description:
Returns the rotation axis vector for the specified joint in the bone chain. This vector represents the axis around which the joint can rotate. It is determined based on the rotation axis set for the joint.
				If get_joint_rotation_axis is , this method returns Vector3(0, 0, 0).

set_joint_radius.description: Sets the joint radius at joint in the bone chain's joint list when is_config_individual is true.

get_joint_radius.description: Returns the radius at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

set_joint_stiffness.description: Sets the stiffness force at joint in the bone chain's joint list when is_config_individual is true.

get_joint_stiffness.description: Returns the stiffness force at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

set_joint_drag.description: Sets the drag force at joint in the bone chain's joint list when is_config_individual is true.

get_joint_drag.description: Returns the drag force at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

set_joint_gravity.description: Sets the gravity amount at joint in the bone chain's joint list when is_config_individual is true.

get_joint_gravity.description: Returns the gravity amount at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

set_joint_gravity_direction.description: Sets the gravity direction at joint in the bone chain's joint list when is_config_individual is true.

get_joint_gravity_direction.description: Returns the gravity direction at joint in the bone chain's joint list.

get_joint_count.description: Returns the joint count of the bone chain's joint list.

set_enable_all_child_collisions.description:
If enabled is true, all child s are colliding and set_exclude_collision_path is enabled as an exclusion list at index in the settings.
				If enabled is false, you need to manually register all valid collisions with set_collision_path.

are_all_child_collisions_enabled.description: Returns true if all child s are contained in the collision list at index in the settings.

set_exclude_collision_path.description: Sets the node path of the  at collision in the bone chain's exclude collision list when are_all_child_collisions_enabled is true.

get_exclude_collision_path.description: Returns the node path of the  at collision in the bone chain's exclude collision list when are_all_child_collisions_enabled is true.

set_exclude_collision_count.description: Sets the number of exclude collisions in the exclude collision list at index in the settings when are_all_child_collisions_enabled is true.

get_exclude_collision_count.description: Returns the exclude collision count of the bone chain's exclude collision list when are_all_child_collisions_enabled is true.

clear_exclude_collisions.description: Clears all exclude collisions from the collision list at index in the settings when are_all_child_collisions_enabled is true.

set_collision_path.description: Sets the node path of the  at collision in the bone chain's collision list when are_all_child_collisions_enabled is false.

get_collision_path.description: Returns the node path of the  at collision in the bone chain's collision list when are_all_child_collisions_enabled is false.

set_collision_count.description: Sets the number of collisions in the collision list at index in the settings when are_all_child_collisions_enabled is false.

get_collision_count.description: Returns the collision count of the bone chain's collision list when are_all_child_collisions_enabled is false.

clear_collisions.description: Clears all collisions from the collision list at index in the settings when are_all_child_collisions_enabled is false.

reset.description:
Resets a simulating state with respect to the current bone pose.
				It is useful to prevent the simulation result getting violent. For example, calling this immediately after a call to AnimationPlayer.play without a fading, or within the previous  signal if it's condition changes significantly.

external_force.description:
The constant force that always affected bones. It is equal to the result when the parent  moves at this speed in the opposite direction.
			This is useful for effects such as wind and anti-gravity.

mutable_bone_axes.description:
If true, the solver retrieves the bone axis from the bone pose every frame.
			If false, the solver retrieves the bone axis from the bone rest and caches it, which increases performance slightly, but position changes in the bone pose made before processing this  are ignored.

Sprite2D.description: A node that displays a 2D texture. The texture displayed can be a region from a larger atlas texture, or a frame from a sprite sheet animation.

is_pixel_opaque.description: Returns true if the pixel at the given position is opaque, false otherwise. Also returns false if the given position is out of bounds or this sprite's texture is null. pos is in local coordinates.

centered.description:
If true, texture is centered.
			Note: For games with a pixel art aesthetic, textures may appear deformed when centered. This is caused by their position being between pixels. To prevent this, set this property to false, or consider enabling ProjectSettings.rendering/2d/snap/snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel and ProjectSettings.rendering/2d/snap/snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel.

offset.description:
The texture's drawing offset.
			Note: When you increase offset.y in Sprite2D, the sprite moves downward on screen (i.e., +Y is down).

flip_h.description: If true, texture is flipped horizontally.

flip_v.description: If true, texture is flipped vertically.

hframes.description: The number of columns in the sprite sheet. When this property is changed, frame is adjusted so that the same visual frame is maintained (same row and column). If that's impossible, frame is reset to 0.

vframes.description: The number of rows in the sprite sheet. When this property is changed, frame is adjusted so that the same visual frame is maintained (same row and column). If that's impossible, frame is reset to 0.

frame.description: Current frame to display from sprite sheet. hframes or vframes must be greater than 1. This property is automatically adjusted when hframes or vframes are changed to keep pointing to the same visual frame (same column and row). If that's impossible, this value is reset to 0.

frame_coords.description: Coordinates of the frame to display from sprite sheet. This is as an alias for the frame property. hframes or vframes must be greater than 1.

region_enabled.description:
If true, texture is cut from a larger atlas texture. See region_rect.
			Note: When using a custom  on a , the UV shader built-in will refer to the entire texture space. Use the REGION_RECT built-in to get the currently visible region defined in region_rect instead. See CanvasItem shaders for details.

region_rect.description: The region of the atlas texture to display. region_enabled must be true.

region_filter_clip_enabled.description: If true, the area outside of the region_rect is clipped to avoid bleeding of the surrounding texture pixels. region_enabled must be true.

Sprite3D.description: A node that displays a 2D texture in a 3D environment. The texture displayed can be a region from a larger atlas texture, or a frame from a sprite sheet animation. See also  where properties such as the billboard mode are defined.

texture.description: object to draw. If GeometryInstance3D.material_override is used, this will be overridden. The size information is still used.

hframes.description: The number of columns in the sprite sheet. When this property is changed, frame is adjusted so that the same visual frame is maintained (same row and column). If that's impossible, frame is reset to 0.

vframes.description: The number of rows in the sprite sheet. When this property is changed, frame is adjusted so that the same visual frame is maintained (same row and column). If that's impossible, frame is reset to 0.

frame.description: Current frame to display from sprite sheet. hframes or vframes must be greater than 1. This property is automatically adjusted when hframes or vframes are changed to keep pointing to the same visual frame (same column and row). If that's impossible, this value is reset to 0.

frame_coords.description: Coordinates of the frame to display from sprite sheet. This is as an alias for the frame property. hframes or vframes must be greater than 1.

region_enabled.description: If true, the sprite will use region_rect and display only the specified part of its texture.

region_rect.description: The region of the atlas texture to display. region_enabled must be true.

SpriteBase3D.description: A node that displays 2D texture information in a 3D environment. See also  where many other properties are defined.

set_draw_flag.description: If true, the specified flag will be enabled.

get_draw_flag.description: Returns the value of the specified flag.

get_item_rect.description: Returns the rectangle representing this sprite.

generate_triangle_mesh.description: Returns a  with the sprite's vertices following its current configuration (such as its axis and pixel_size).

centered.description: If true, texture will be centered.

offset.description:
The texture's drawing offset.
			Note: When you increase offset.y in Sprite3D, the sprite moves upward in world space (i.e., +Y is up).

flip_h.description: If true, texture is flipped horizontally.

flip_v.description: If true, texture is flipped vertically.

modulate.description:
A color value used to multiply the texture's colors. Can be used for mood-coloring or to simulate the color of ambient light.
			Note: Unlike CanvasItem.modulate for 2D, colors with values above 1.0 (overbright) are not supported.
			Note: If a GeometryInstance3D.material_override is defined on the , the material override must be configured to take vertex colors into account for albedo. Otherwise, the color defined in modulate will be ignored. For a , BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo must be true. For a , ALBEDO *= COLOR.rgb; must be inserted in the shader's fragment() function.

pixel_size.description: The size of one pixel's width on the sprite to scale it in 3D.

axis.description: The direction in which the front of the texture faces.

billboard.description:
The billboard mode to use for the sprite.
			Note: When billboarding is enabled and the material also casts shadows, billboards will face the camera in the scene when rendering shadows. In scenes with multiple cameras, the intended shadow cannot be determined and this will result in undefined behavior. See GitHub Pull Request #72638 for details.

transparent.description: If true, the texture's transparency and the opacity are used to make those parts of the sprite invisible.

shaded.description: If true, the  in the  has effects on the sprite.

double_sided.description: If true, texture can be seen from the back as well, if false, it is invisible when looking at it from behind.

no_depth_test.description: If true, depth testing is disabled and the object will be drawn in render order.

fixed_size.description: If true, the texture is rendered at the same size regardless of distance. The texture's size on screen is the same as if the camera was 1.0 units away from the texture's origin, regardless of the actual distance from the camera. The 's field of view (or Camera3D.size when in orthogonal/frustum mode) still affects the size the sprite is drawn at.

alpha_cut.description: The alpha cutting mode to use for the sprite.

alpha_scissor_threshold.description: Threshold at which the alpha scissor will discard values.

alpha_hash_scale.description: The hashing scale for Alpha Hash. Recommended values between 0 and 2.

alpha_antialiasing_mode.description: The type of alpha antialiasing to apply.

alpha_antialiasing_edge.description: Threshold at which antialiasing will be applied on the alpha channel.

texture_filter.description:
Filter flags for the texture.
			Note: Linear filtering may cause artifacts around the edges, which are especially noticeable on opaque textures. To prevent this, use textures with transparent or identical colors around the edges.

render_priority.description:
Sets the render priority for the sprite. Higher priority objects will be sorted in front of lower priority objects.
			Note: This only applies if alpha_cut is set to  (default value).
			Note: This only applies to sorting of transparent objects. This will not impact how transparent objects are sorted relative to opaque objects. This is because opaque objects are not sorted, while transparent objects are sorted from back to front (subject to priority).

SpriteFrames.brief_description: Sprite frame library for AnimatedSprite2D and AnimatedSprite3D.
SpriteFrames.description: Sprite frame library for an  or  node. Contains frames and animation data for playback.

add_animation.description: Adds a new anim animation to the library.

has_animation.description: Returns true if the anim animation exists.

duplicate_animation.description: Duplicates the animation anim_from to a new animation named anim_to. Fails if anim_to already exists, or if anim_from does not exist.

rename_animation.description: Changes the anim animation's name to newname.

get_animation_names.description: Returns an array containing the names associated to each animation. Values are placed in alphabetical order.

set_animation_speed.description: Sets the speed for the anim animation in frames per second.

get_animation_speed.description: Returns the speed in frames per second for the anim animation.

set_animation_loop.description: If loop is true, the anim animation will loop when it reaches the end, or the start if it is played in reverse.

get_animation_loop.description: Returns true if the given animation is configured to loop when it finishes playing. Otherwise, returns false.

add_frame.description: Adds a frame to the anim animation. If at_position is -1, the frame will be added to the end of the animation. duration specifies the relative duration, see get_frame_duration for details.

set_frame.description: Sets the texture and the duration of the frame idx in the anim animation. duration specifies the relative duration, see get_frame_duration for details.

remove_frame.description: Removes the anim animation's frame idx.

get_frame_count.description: Returns the number of frames for the anim animation.

get_frame_texture.description: Returns the texture of the frame idx in the anim animation.

get_frame_duration.description:
Returns a relative duration of the frame idx in the anim animation (defaults to 1.0). For example, a frame with a duration of 2.0 is displayed twice as long as a frame with a duration of 1.0. You can calculate the absolute duration (in seconds) of a frame using the following formula:
				
				absolute_duration = relative_duration / (animation_fps * abs(playing_speed))
				
				In this example, playing_speed refers to either AnimatedSprite2D.get_playing_speed or AnimatedSprite3D.get_playing_speed.

clear.description: Removes all frames from the anim animation.

clear_all.description: Removes all animations. An empty default animation will be created.

StandardMaterial3D.brief_description: A PBR (Physically Based Rendering) material to be used on 3D objects.
StandardMaterial3D.description: 's properties are inherited from .  uses separate textures for ambient occlusion, roughness and metallic maps. To use a single ORM map for all 3 textures, use an  instead.

StaticBody2D.brief_description: A 2D physics body that can't be moved by external forces. When moved manually, it doesn't affect other bodies in its path.
StaticBody2D.description:
A static 2D physics body. It can't be moved by external forces or contacts, but can be moved manually by other means such as code, s (with AnimationMixer.callback_mode_process set to ), and .
		When  is moved, it is teleported to its new position without affecting other physics bodies in its path. If this is not desired, use  instead.
		 is useful for completely static objects like floors and walls, as well as moving surfaces like conveyor belts and circular revolving platforms (by using constant_linear_velocity and constant_angular_velocity).

physics_material_override.description:
The physics material override for the body.
			If a material is assigned to this property, it will be used instead of any other physics material, such as an inherited one.

constant_linear_velocity.description: The body's constant linear velocity. This does not move the body, but affects touching bodies, as if it were moving.

constant_angular_velocity.description: The body's constant angular velocity. This does not rotate the body, but affects touching bodies, as if it were rotating.

StaticBody3D.brief_description: A 3D physics body that can't be moved by external forces. When moved manually, it doesn't affect other bodies in its path.
StaticBody3D.description:
A static 3D physics body. It can't be moved by external forces or contacts, but can be moved manually by other means such as code, s (with AnimationMixer.callback_mode_process set to ), and .
		When  is moved, it is teleported to its new position without affecting other physics bodies in its path. If this is not desired, use  instead.
		 is useful for completely static objects like floors and walls, as well as moving surfaces like conveyor belts and circular revolving platforms (by using constant_linear_velocity and constant_angular_velocity).

physics_material_override.description:
The physics material override for the body.
			If a material is assigned to this property, it will be used instead of any other physics material, such as an inherited one.

constant_linear_velocity.description: The body's constant linear velocity. This does not move the body, but affects touching bodies, as if it were moving.

constant_angular_velocity.description: The body's constant angular velocity. This does not rotate the body, but affects touching bodies, as if it were rotating.

StatusIndicator.brief_description:
Application status indicator (aka notification area icon).
		Note: Status indicator is implemented on macOS and Windows.

get_rect.description: Returns the status indicator rectangle in screen coordinates. If this status indicator is not visible, returns an empty .

menu.description:
Status indicator native popup menu. If this is set, the  signal is not emitted.
			Note: Native popup is only supported if  supports  feature.

visible.description: If true, the status indicator is visible.

StreamPeer.brief_description: Abstract base class for interacting with streams.
StreamPeer.description:
StreamPeer is an abstract base class mostly used for stream-based protocols (such as TCP). It provides an API for sending and receiving data through streams as raw data or strings.
		Note: When exporting to Android, make sure to enable the INTERNET permission in the Android export preset before exporting the project or using one-click deploy. Otherwise, network communication of any kind will be blocked by Android.

put_data.description: Sends a chunk of data through the connection, blocking if necessary until the data is done sending. This function returns an  code.

put_partial_data.description: Sends a chunk of data through the connection. If all the data could not be sent at once, only part of it will. This function returns two values, an  code and an integer, describing how much data was actually sent.

get_data.description: Returns a chunk data with the received bytes, as an  containing two elements: an  constant and a . bytes is the number of bytes to be received. If not enough bytes are available, the function will block until the desired amount is received.

get_partial_data.description: Returns a chunk data with the received bytes, as an  containing two elements: an  constant and a . bytes is the number of bytes to be received. If not enough bytes are available, the function will return how many were actually received.

get_available_bytes.description: Returns the number of bytes this  has available.

put_8.description: Puts a signed byte into the stream.

put_u8.description: Puts an unsigned byte into the stream.

put_16.description: Puts a signed 16-bit value into the stream.

put_u16.description: Puts an unsigned 16-bit value into the stream.

put_32.description: Puts a signed 32-bit value into the stream.

put_u32.description: Puts an unsigned 32-bit value into the stream.

put_64.description: Puts a signed 64-bit value into the stream.

put_u64.description: Puts an unsigned 64-bit value into the stream.

put_half.description: Puts a half-precision float into the stream.

put_float.description: Puts a single-precision float into the stream.

put_double.description: Puts a double-precision float into the stream.

put_string.description:
Puts a zero-terminated ASCII string into the stream prepended by a 32-bit unsigned integer representing its size.
				Note: To put an ASCII string without prepending its size, you can use put_data:
				
				
				put_data("Hello world".to_ascii_buffer())
				
				
				PutData("Hello World".ToAsciiBuffer());

put_utf8_string.description:
Puts a zero-terminated UTF-8 string into the stream prepended by a 32 bits unsigned integer representing its size.
				Note: To put a UTF-8 string without prepending its size, you can use put_data:
				
				
				put_data("Hello world".to_utf8_buffer())
				
				
				PutData("Hello World".ToUtf8Buffer());

put_var.description:
Puts a Variant into the stream. If full_objects is true encoding objects is allowed (and can potentially include code).
				Internally, this uses the same encoding mechanism as the @GlobalScope.var_to_bytes method.

get_8.description: Gets a signed byte from the stream.

get_u8.description: Gets an unsigned byte from the stream.

get_16.description: Gets a signed 16-bit value from the stream.

get_u16.description: Gets an unsigned 16-bit value from the stream.

get_32.description: Gets a signed 32-bit value from the stream.

get_u32.description: Gets an unsigned 32-bit value from the stream.

get_64.description: Gets a signed 64-bit value from the stream.

get_u64.description: Gets an unsigned 64-bit value from the stream.

get_half.description: Gets a half-precision float from the stream.

get_float.description: Gets a single-precision float from the stream.

get_double.description: Gets a double-precision float from the stream.

get_string.description: Gets an ASCII string with byte-length bytes from the stream. If bytes is negative (default) the length will be read from the stream using the reverse process of put_string.

get_utf8_string.description: Gets a UTF-8 string with byte-length bytes from the stream (this decodes the string sent as UTF-8). If bytes is negative (default) the length will be read from the stream using the reverse process of put_utf8_string.

get_var.description:
Gets a Variant from the stream. If allow_objects is true, decoding objects is allowed.
				Internally, this uses the same decoding mechanism as the @GlobalScope.bytes_to_var method.
				Warning: Deserialized objects can contain code which gets executed. Do not use this option if the serialized object comes from untrusted sources to avoid potential security threats such as remote code execution.

big_endian.description: If true, this  will using big-endian format for encoding and decoding.

StreamPeerBuffer.brief_description: A stream peer used to handle binary data streams.
StreamPeerBuffer.description:
A data buffer stream peer that uses a byte array as the stream. This object can be used to handle binary data from network sessions. To handle binary data stored in files,  can be used directly.
		A  object keeps an internal cursor which is the offset in bytes to the start of the buffer. Get and put operations are performed at the cursor position and will move the cursor accordingly.

seek.description: Moves the cursor to the specified position. position must be a valid index of data_array.

resize.description: Resizes the data_array. This doesn't update the cursor.

clear.description: Clears the data_array and resets the cursor.

duplicate.description: Returns a new  with the same data_array content.

data_array.description: The underlying data buffer. Setting this value resets the cursor.

StreamPeerGZIP.brief_description: A stream peer that handles GZIP and deflate compression/decompression.
StreamPeerGZIP.description:
This class allows to compress or decompress data using GZIP/deflate in a streaming fashion. This is particularly useful when compressing or decompressing files that have to be sent through the network without needing to allocate them all in memory.
		After starting the stream via start_compression (or start_decompression), calling StreamPeer.put_partial_data on this stream will compress (or decompress) the data, writing it to the internal buffer. Calling StreamPeer.get_available_bytes will return the pending bytes in the internal buffer, and StreamPeer.get_partial_data will retrieve the compressed (or decompressed) bytes from it. When the stream is over, you must call finish to ensure the internal buffer is properly flushed (make sure to call StreamPeer.get_available_bytes on last time to check if more data needs to be read after that).

start_compression.description: Start the stream in compression mode with the given buffer_size, if use_deflate is true uses deflate instead of GZIP.

start_decompression.description: Start the stream in decompression mode with the given buffer_size, if use_deflate is true uses deflate instead of GZIP.

finish.description:
Finalizes the stream, compressing any buffered chunk left.
				You must call it only when you are compressing.

clear.description: Clears this stream, resetting the internal state.

StreamPeerSocket.brief_description: Abstract base class for interacting with socket streams.
StreamPeerSocket.description: StreamPeerSocket is an abstract base class that defines common behavior for socket-based streams.

poll.description: Polls the socket, updating its state. See get_status.

get_status.description: Returns the status of the connection.
