paused.description: If true, the timer is paused. A paused timer does not process until this property is set back to false, even when start is called. See also stop.

ignore_time_scale.description: If true, the timer will ignore Engine.time_scale and update with the real, elapsed time.

time_left.description:
The timer's remaining time in seconds. This is always 0 if the timer is stopped.
			Note: This property is read-only and cannot be modified. It is based on wait_time.

inner_radius.description: The inner radius of the torus.

outer_radius.description: The outer radius of the torus.

rings.description: The number of slices the torus is constructed of.

ring_segments.description: The number of edges each ring of the torus is constructed of.

TouchScreenButton.brief_description: Button for touch screen devices for gameplay use.
TouchScreenButton.description:
TouchScreenButton allows you to create on-screen buttons for touch devices. It's intended for gameplay use, such as a unit you have to touch to move. Unlike , TouchScreenButton supports multitouch out of the box. Several TouchScreenButtons can be pressed at the same time with touch input.
		This node inherits from . Unlike with  nodes, you cannot set anchors on it. If you want to create menus or user interfaces, you may want to use  nodes instead. To make button nodes react to touch events, you can enable ProjectSettings.input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch in the Project Settings.
		You can configure TouchScreenButton to be visible only on touch devices, helping you develop your game both for desktop and mobile devices.

is_pressed.description: Returns true if this button is currently pressed.

texture_normal.description: The button's texture for the normal state.

texture_pressed.description: The button's texture for the pressed state.

shape_centered.description: If true, the button's shape is centered in the provided texture. If no texture is used, this property has no effect.

shape_visible.description: If true, the button's shape is visible in the editor.

passby_press.description:
If true, the  and  signals are emitted whenever a pressed finger goes in and out of the button, even if the pressure started outside the active area of the button.
			Note: This is a "pass-by" (not "bypass") press mode.

action.description: The button's action. Actions can be handled with .

Translation.brief_description: A language translation that maps a collection of strings to their individual translations.
Translation.description:
maps a collection of strings to their individual translations, and also provides convenience methods for pluralization.
		A  consists of messages. A message is identified by its context and untranslated string. Unlike gettext, using an empty context string in Godot means not using any context.

add_message.description:
Adds a message if nonexistent, followed by its translation.
				An additional context could be used to specify the translation context or differentiate polysemic words.

add_plural_message.description:
Adds a message involving plural translation if nonexistent, followed by its translation.
				An additional context could be used to specify the translation context or differentiate polysemic words.

get_plural_message.description:
Returns a message's translation involving plurals.
				The number n is the number or quantity of the plural object. It will be used to guide the translation system to fetch the correct plural form for the selected language.
				Note: Plurals are only supported in gettext-based translations (PO), not CSV.

get_message_count.description: Returns the number of existing messages.

plural_rules_override.description:
The plural rules string to enforce. See GNU gettext for examples and more info.
			If empty or invalid, default plural rules from TranslationServer.get_plural_rules are used. The English plural rules are used as a fallback.

TranslationDomain.description:
is a self-contained collection of  resources. Translations can be added to or removed from it.
		If you're working with the main translation domain, it is more convenient to use the wrap methods on .

get_translation_object.description: Returns the  instance that best matches locale. Returns null if there are no matches.

clear.description: Removes all translations.

get_translations.description: Returns all available  instances as added by add_translation.

has_translation_for_locale.description: Returns true if there are any  instances that match locale (see TranslationServer.compare_locales). If exact is true, only instances whose locale exactly equals locale are considered.

has_translation.description: Returns true if this translation domain contains the given translation.

find_translations.description: Returns the  instances that match locale (see TranslationServer.compare_locales). If exact is true, only instances whose locale exactly equals locale will be returned.

translate.description: Returns the current locale's translation for the given message and context.

translate_plural.description:
Returns the current locale's translation for the given message, plural message and context.
				The number n is the number or quantity of the plural object. It will be used to guide the translation system to fetch the correct plural form for the selected language.

get_locale_override.description: Returns the locale override of the domain. Returns an empty string if locale override is disabled.

set_locale_override.description:
Sets the locale override of the domain.
				If locale is an empty string, locale override is disabled. Otherwise, locale will be standardized to match known locales (e.g. en-US would be matched to en_US).
				Note: Calling this method does not automatically update texts in the scene tree. Please propagate the  signal manually.

pseudolocalize.description: Returns the pseudolocalized string based on the message passed in.

enabled.description: If true, translation is enabled. Otherwise, translate and translate_plural will return the input message unchanged regardless of the current locale.

pseudolocalization_enabled.description:
If true, enables pseudolocalization for the project. This can be used to spot untranslatable strings or layout issues that may occur once the project is localized to languages that have longer strings than the source language.
			Note: Updating this property does not automatically update texts in the scene tree. Please propagate the  notification manually after you have finished modifying pseudolocalization related options.

pseudolocalization_accents_enabled.description:
Replace all characters with their accented variants during pseudolocalization.
			Note: Updating this property does not automatically update texts in the scene tree. Please propagate the  notification manually after you have finished modifying pseudolocalization related options.

pseudolocalization_double_vowels_enabled.description:
Double vowels in strings during pseudolocalization to simulate the lengthening of text due to localization.
			Note: Updating this property does not automatically update texts in the scene tree. Please propagate the  notification manually after you have finished modifying pseudolocalization related options.

pseudolocalization_fake_bidi_enabled.description:
If true, emulate bidirectional (right-to-left) text when pseudolocalization is enabled. This can be used to spot issues with RTL layout and UI mirroring that will crop up if the project is localized to RTL languages such as Arabic or Hebrew.
			Note: Updating this property does not automatically update texts in the scene tree. Please propagate the  notification manually after you have finished modifying pseudolocalization related options.

pseudolocalization_override_enabled.description:
Replace all characters in the string with *. Useful for finding non-localizable strings.
			Note: Updating this property does not automatically update texts in the scene tree. Please propagate the  notification manually after you have finished modifying pseudolocalization related options.

pseudolocalization_skip_placeholders_ena.description:
Skip placeholders for string formatting like %s or %f during pseudolocalization. Useful to identify strings which need additional control characters to display correctly.
			Note: Updating this property does not automatically update texts in the scene tree. Please propagate the  notification manually after you have finished modifying pseudolocalization related options.

pseudolocalization_expansion_ratio.description:
The expansion ratio to use during pseudolocalization. A value of 0.3 is sufficient for most practical purposes, and will increase the length of each string by 30%.
			Note: Updating this property does not automatically update texts in the scene tree. Please propagate the  notification manually after you have finished modifying pseudolocalization related options.

pseudolocalization_prefix.description:
Prefix that will be prepended to the pseudolocalized string.
			Note: Updating this property does not automatically update texts in the scene tree. Please propagate the  notification manually after you have finished modifying pseudolocalization related options.

pseudolocalization_suffix.description:
Suffix that will be appended to the pseudolocalized string.
			Note: Updating this property does not automatically update texts in the scene tree. Please propagate the  notification manually after you have finished modifying pseudolocalization related options.

TranslationServer.brief_description: The server responsible for language translations.
TranslationServer.description:
The translation server is the API backend that manages all language translations.
		Translations are stored in s, which can be accessed by name. The most commonly used translation domain is the main translation domain. It always exists and can be accessed using an empty . The translation server provides wrapper methods for accessing the main translation domain directly, without having to fetch the translation domain first. Custom translation domains are mainly for advanced usages like editor plugins. Names starting with godot. are reserved for engine internals.

set_locale.description:
Sets the locale of the project. The locale string will be standardized to match known locales (e.g. en-US would be matched to en_US).
				If translations have been loaded beforehand for the new locale, they will be applied.

get_locale.description:
Returns the current locale of the project.
				See also OS.get_locale and OS.get_locale_language to query the locale of the user system.

get_tool_locale.description:
Returns the current locale of the editor.
				Note: When called from an exported project returns the same value as get_locale.

compare_locales.description: Compares two locales and returns a similarity score between 0 (no match) and 10 (full match).

standardize_locale.description: Returns a locale string standardized to match known locales (e.g. en-US would be matched to en_US). If add_defaults is true, the locale may have a default script or country added.

get_all_languages.description: Returns array of known language codes.

get_language_name.description: Returns a readable language name for the language code.

get_all_scripts.description: Returns an array of known script codes.

get_script_name.description: Returns a readable script name for the script code.

get_all_countries.description: Returns an array of known country codes.

get_country_name.description: Returns a readable country name for the country code.

get_locale_name.description: Returns a locale's language and its variant (e.g. "en_US" would return "English (United States)").

get_plural_rules.description: Returns the default plural rules for the locale.

translate.description:
Returns the current locale's translation for the given message and context.
				Note: This method always uses the main translation domain.

translate_plural.description:
Returns the current locale's translation for the given message, plural message and context.

				Note: This method always uses the main translation domain.

add_translation.description: Adds a translation to the main translation domain.

remove_translation.description: Removes the given translation from the main translation domain.

get_translation_object.description: Returns the  instance that best matches locale in the main translation domain. Returns null if there are no matches.

get_translations.description: Returns all available  instances in the main translation domain as added by add_translation.

has_translation.description: Returns true if the main translation domain contains the given translation.

has_domain.description: Returns true if a translation domain with the specified name exists.

get_or_add_domain.description: Returns the translation domain with the specified name. An empty translation domain will be created and added if it does not exist.

remove_domain.description:

get_loaded_locales.description: Returns an array of all loaded locales of the project.

format_number.description: Converts a number from Western Arabic (0..9) to the numeral system used in the given locale.

get_percent_sign.description: Returns the percent sign used in the given locale.

parse_number.description: Converts number from the numeral system used in the given locale to Western Arabic (0..9).

reload_pseudolocalization.description: Reparses the pseudolocalization options and reloads the translation for the main translation domain.

pseudolocalize.description:
Returns the pseudolocalized string based on the message passed in.

pseudolocalization_enabled.description: If true, enables the use of pseudolocalization on the main translation domain. See ProjectSettings.internationalization/pseudolocalization/use_pseudolocalization for details.

Tree.brief_description: A control used to show a set of internal s in a hierarchical structure.

create_item.description:

set_column_custom_minimum_width.description: Overrides the calculated minimum width of a column. It can be set to 0 to restore the default behavior. Columns that have the "Expand" flag will use their "min_width" in a similar fashion to Control.size_flags_stretch_ratio.

set_column_expand.description: If true, the column will have the "Expand" flag of . Columns that have the "Expand" flag will use their expand ratio in a similar fashion to Control.size_flags_stretch_ratio (see set_column_expand_ratio).

set_column_expand_ratio.description: Sets the relative expand ratio for a column. See set_column_expand.

set_column_clip_content.description: Allows to enable clipping for column's content, making the content size ignored.

is_column_expanding.description: Returns true if the column has enabled expanding (see set_column_expand).

is_column_clipping_content.description: Returns true if the column has enabled clipping (see set_column_clip_content).

get_column_width.description: Returns the column's width in pixels.

get_next_selected.description:

get_selected.description:
Returns the currently focused item, or null if no item is focused.

get_selected_column.description:
Returns the currently focused column, or -1 if no column is focused.
				In  mode, the focused column is the selected column. In  mode, the focused column is always 0 if any item is selected. In  mode, the focused column is the column under the focus cursor, and there are not necessarily any column selected.

deselect_all.description: Deselects all tree items (rows and columns). In  mode also removes selection cursor.

get_edited_column.description: Returns the column for the currently edited item.

edit_selected.description:
Edits the selected tree item as if it was clicked.

				Returns true if the item could be edited. Fails if no item is selected.

get_custom_popup_rect.description: Returns the rectangle for custom popups. Helper to create custom cell controls that display a popup. See TreeItem.set_cell_mode.

get_item_area_rect.description: Returns the rectangle area for the specified . If column is specified, only get the position and size of that column, otherwise get the rectangle containing all columns. If a button index is specified, the rectangle of that button will be returned.

get_item_at_position.description: Returns the tree item at the specified position (relative to the tree origin position).

get_column_at_position.description: Returns the column index at position, or -1 if no item is there.

get_drop_section_at_position.description:
Returns the drop section at position, or -100 if no item is there.
				Values -1, 0, or 1 will be returned for the "above item", "on item", and "below item" drop sections, respectively. See  for a description of each drop section.
				To get the item which the returned drop section is relative to, use get_item_at_position.

get_button_id_at_position.description: Returns the button ID at position, or -1 if no button is there.

ensure_cursor_is_visible.description:
Makes the currently focused cell visible.
				This will scroll the tree if necessary. In  mode, this will not do horizontal scrolling, as all the cells in the selected row is focused logically.
				Note: Despite the name of this method, the focus cursor itself is only visible in  mode.

set_column_title.description: Sets the title of a column.

set_column_title_tooltip_text.description: Sets the column title's tooltip text.

get_column_title_tooltip_text.description: Returns the column title's tooltip text.

set_column_title_alignment.description: Sets the column title alignment. Note that  is not supported for column titles.

set_column_title_direction.description: Sets column title base writing direction.

set_column_title_language.description: Sets the language code of the given column's title to language. This is used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If language is empty, the current locale is used.

scroll_to_item.description: Causes the  to jump to the specified .

column_titles_visible.description: If true, column titles are visible.

allow_reselect.description: If true, the currently selected cell may be selected again.

allow_rmb_select.description: If true, a right mouse button click can select items.

allow_search.description: If true, allows navigating the  with letter keys through incremental search.

hide_folding.description: If true, the folding arrow is hidden.

enable_recursive_folding.description: If true, recursive folding is enabled for this . Holding down Shift while clicking the fold arrow or using ui_right/ui_left shortcuts collapses or uncollapses the  and all its descendants.

enable_drag_unfolding.description: If true, tree items will unfold when hovered over during a drag-and-drop. The delay for when this happens is dictated by .

hide_root.description: If true, the tree's root is hidden.

drop_mode_flags.description:
The drop mode as an OR combination of flags. See  constants. Once dropping is done, reverts to . Setting this during Control._can_drop_data is recommended.

select_mode.description: Allows single or multiple selection. See the  constants.

auto_tooltip.description: If true, tree items with no tooltip assigned display their text as their tooltip. See also TreeItem.get_tooltip_text and TreeItem.get_button_tooltip_text.

scroll_hint_mode.description: The way which scroll hints (indicators that show that the content can still be scrolled in a certain direction) will be shown.

tile_scroll_hint.description: If true, the scroll hint texture will be tiled instead of stretched. See scroll_hint_mode.

TreeItem.brief_description: An internal control for a single item inside .
TreeItem.description:
A single item of a  control. It can contain other s as children, which allows it to create a hierarchy. It can also contain text and buttons.  is not a , it is internal to the .
		To create a , use Tree.create_item or TreeItem.create_child. To remove a , use Object.free.
		Note: The ID values used for buttons are 32-bit, unlike  which is always 64-bit. They go from -2147483648 to 2147483647.

set_cell_mode.description: Sets the given column's cell mode to mode. This determines how the cell is displayed and edited.

set_auto_translate_mode.description:
Sets the given column's auto translate mode to mode.
				All columns use  by default, which uses the same auto translate mode as the  itself.

get_auto_translate_mode.description: Returns the column's auto translate mode.

set_edit_multiline.description:
If multiline is true, the given column is multiline editable.
				Note: This option only affects the type of control ( or ) that appears when editing the column. You can set multiline values with set_text even if the column is not multiline editable.

is_edit_multiline.description: Returns true if the given column is multiline editable.

set_checked.description: If checked is true, the given column is checked. Clears column's indeterminate status.

set_indeterminate.description:
If indeterminate is true, the given column is marked indeterminate.
				Note: If set true from false, then column is cleared of checked status.

is_checked.description: Returns true if the given column is checked.

is_indeterminate.description: Returns true if the given column is indeterminate.

propagate_check.description: Propagates this item's checked status to its children and parents for the given column. It is possible to process the items affected by this method call by connecting to . The order that the items affected will be processed is as follows: the item invoking this method, children of that item, and finally parents of that item. If emit_signal is false, then  will not be emitted.

set_text.description: Sets the given column's text value.

set_description.description: Sets the given column's description for assistive apps.

get_description.description: Returns the given column's description for assistive apps.

set_text_direction.description: Sets item's text base writing direction.

get_text_direction.description: Returns item's text base writing direction.

set_autowrap_mode.description: Sets the autowrap mode in the given column. If set to something other than , the text gets wrapped inside the cell's bounding rectangle.

get_autowrap_mode.description: Returns the text autowrap mode in the given column. By default it is .

set_text_overrun_behavior.description: Sets the clipping behavior when the text exceeds the item's bounding rectangle in the given column.

get_text_overrun_behavior.description: Returns the clipping behavior when the text exceeds the item's bounding rectangle in the given column. By default it is .

set_structured_text_bidi_override.description: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text. Has effect for cells that display text.

get_structured_text_bidi_override.description: Returns the BiDi algorithm override set for this cell.

set_structured_text_bidi_override_option.description: Set additional options for BiDi override. Has effect for cells that display text.

get_structured_text_bidi_override_option.description: Returns the additional BiDi options set for this cell.

set_language.description: Sets the language code of the given column's text to language. This is used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If language is empty, the current locale is used.

set_suffix.description: Sets a string to be shown after a column's value (for example, a unit abbreviation).

get_suffix.description: Gets the suffix string shown after the column value.

set_icon.description: Sets the given cell's icon . If the cell is in  mode, the icon is displayed in the center of the cell. Otherwise, the icon is displayed before the cell's text.  does not display an icon.

get_icon.description: Returns the given column's icon . Error if no icon is set.

set_icon_overlay.description: Sets the given cell's icon overlay . The cell has to be in  mode, and icon has to be set. Overlay is drawn on top of icon, in the bottom left corner.

get_icon_overlay.description: Returns the given column's icon overlay .

set_icon_region.description: Sets the given column's icon's texture region.

set_icon_max_width.description: Sets the maximum allowed width of the icon in the given column. This limit is applied on top of the default size of the icon and on top of . The height is adjusted according to the icon's ratio.

get_icon_max_width.description: Returns the maximum allowed width of the icon in the given column.

set_icon_modulate.description: Modulates the given column's icon with modulate.

get_icon_modulate.description: Returns the  modulating the column's icon.

set_range.description: Sets the value of a  column.

get_range.description: Returns the value of a  column.

set_range_config.description:
Sets the range of accepted values for a column. The column must be in the  mode.
				If expr is true, the edit mode slider will use an exponential scale as with Range.exp_edit.

get_range_config.description: Returns a dictionary containing the range parameters for a given column. The keys are "min", "max", "step", and "expr".

set_metadata.description: Sets the metadata value for the given column, which can be retrieved later using get_metadata. This can be used, for example, to store a reference to the original data.

get_metadata.description: Returns the metadata value that was set for the given column using set_metadata.

set_custom_draw.description:
Sets the given column's custom draw callback to the callback method on object.
				The method named callback should accept two arguments: the  that is drawn and its position and size as a .

set_custom_draw_callback.description:
Sets the given column's custom draw callback. Use an empty  (Callable()) to clear the custom callback. The cell has to be in  to use this feature.
				The callback should accept two arguments: the  that is drawn and its position and size as a .

get_custom_draw_callback.description: Returns the custom callback of column column.

set_custom_stylebox.description:
Sets the given column's custom  used to draw the background.
				Note: If a custom background color is set, the  will be drawn in front of it.

get_custom_stylebox.description: Returns the given column's custom  used to draw the background.

set_collapsed_recursive.description: Collapses or uncollapses this  and all the descendants of this item.

is_any_collapsed.description:
Returns true if this , or any of its descendants, is collapsed.
				If only_visible is true it ignores non-visible s.

is_visible_in_tree.description: Returns true if visible is true and all its ancestors are also visible.

uncollapse_tree.description: Uncollapses all s necessary to reveal this , i.e. all ancestor s.

set_selectable.description: If selectable is true, the given column is selectable.

is_selectable.description: Returns true if the given column is selectable.

is_selected.description: Returns true if the given column is selected.

set_editable.description: If enabled is true, the given column is editable.

is_editable.description: Returns true if the given column is editable.

set_custom_color.description: Sets the given column's custom color.

get_custom_color.description: Returns the custom color of column column.

clear_custom_color.description: Resets the color for the given column to default.

set_custom_font.description: Sets custom font used to draw text in the given column.

get_custom_font.description: Returns custom font used to draw text in the column column.

set_custom_font_size.description: Sets custom font size used to draw text in the given column.

get_custom_font_size.description: Returns custom font size used to draw text in the column column.

set_custom_bg_color.description:
Sets the given column's custom background color and whether to just use it as an outline.
				Note: If a custom  is set, the background color will be drawn behind it.

clear_custom_bg_color.description: Resets the background color for the given column to default.

get_custom_bg_color.description: Returns the custom background color of column column.

set_custom_as_button.description: Makes a cell with  display as a non-flat button with a .

is_custom_set_as_button.description: Returns true if the cell was made into a button with set_custom_as_button.

clear_buttons.description: Removes all buttons from all columns of this item.

add_button.description: Adds a button with  button to the end of the cell at column column. The id is used to identify the button in the according  signal and can be different from the buttons index. If not specified, the next available index is used, which may be retrieved by calling get_button_count immediately before this method. Optionally, the button can be disabled and have a tooltip_text. description is used as the button description for assistive apps.

get_button_tooltip_text.description: Returns the tooltip text for the button at index button_index in column column.

get_button_id.description: Returns the ID for the button at index button_index in column column.

get_button_by_id.description: Returns the button index if there is a button with ID id in column column, otherwise returns -1.

get_button_color.description: Returns the color of the button with ID id in column column. If the specified button does not exist, returns .

get_button.description: Returns the  of the button at index button_index in column column.

set_button_tooltip_text.description: Sets the tooltip text for the button at index button_index in the given column.

set_button.description: Sets the given column's button  at index button_index to button.

erase_button.description: Removes the button at index button_index in column column.

set_button_description.description: Sets the given column's button description at index button_index for assistive apps.

set_button_disabled.description: If true, disables the button at index button_index in the given column.

is_button_disabled.description: Returns true if the button at index button_index for the given column is disabled.

set_tooltip_text.description: Sets the given column's tooltip text.

get_tooltip_text.description: Returns the given column's tooltip text.

set_text_alignment.description: Sets the given column's text alignment to text_alignment.

get_text_alignment.description: Returns the given column's text alignment.

set_expand_right.description: If enable is true, the given column is expanded to the right.

get_expand_right.description: Returns true if expand_right is set.

create_child.description:
Creates an item and adds it as a child.
				The new item will be inserted as position index (the default value -1 means the last position), or it will be the last child if index is higher than the child count.

add_child.description: Adds a previously unparented  as a direct child of this one. The child item must not be a part of any  or parented to any . See also remove_child.

remove_child.description:
Removes the given child  and all its children from the . Note that it doesn't free the item from memory, so it can be reused later (see add_child). To completely remove a  use Object.free.
				Note: If you want to move a child from one  to another, then instead of removing and adding it manually you can use move_before or move_after.

get_tree.description: Returns the  that owns this TreeItem.

get_next.description: Returns the next sibling TreeItem in the tree or a null object if there is none.

get_prev.description: Returns the previous sibling TreeItem in the tree or a null object if there is none.

get_parent.description: Returns the parent TreeItem or a null object if there is none.

get_next_in_tree.description:
Returns the next TreeItem in the tree (in the context of a depth-first search) or a null object if there is none.
				If wrap is enabled, the method will wrap around to the first element in the tree when called on the last element, otherwise it returns null.

get_prev_in_tree.description:
Returns the previous TreeItem in the tree (in the context of a depth-first search) or a null object if there is none.
				If wrap is enabled, the method will wrap around to the last element in the tree when called on the first visible element, otherwise it returns null.

get_next_visible.description:
Returns the next visible TreeItem in the tree (in the context of a depth-first search) or a null object if there is none.
				If wrap is enabled, the method will wrap around to the first visible element in the tree when called on the last visible element, otherwise it returns null.

get_prev_visible.description:
Returns the previous visible sibling TreeItem in the tree (in the context of a depth-first search) or a null object if there is none.
				If wrap is enabled, the method will wrap around to the last visible element in the tree when called on the first visible element, otherwise it returns null.

Returns a child item by its index (see get_child_count). This method is often used for iterating all children of an item.

get_index.description: Returns the node's order in the tree. For example, if called on the first child item the position is 0.

move_before.description:
Moves this TreeItem right before the given item.
				Note: You can't move to the root or move the root.

move_after.description:
Moves this TreeItem right after the given item.

call_recursive.description: Calls the method on the actual TreeItem and its children recursively. Pass parameters as a comma separated list.

collapsed.description: If true, the TreeItem is collapsed.

visible.description:
If true, the  is visible (default).
			Note that if a  is set to not be visible, none of its children will be visible either.

disable_folding.description: If true, folding is disabled for this TreeItem.

TriangleMesh.brief_description: Triangle geometry for efficient, physicsless intersection queries.
TriangleMesh.description:
Creates a bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) tree structure around triangle geometry.
		The triangle BVH tree can be used for efficient intersection queries without involving a physics engine.
		For example, this can be used in editor tools to select objects with complex shapes based on the mouse cursor position.
		Performance: Creating the BVH tree for complex geometry is a slow process and best done in a background thread.

create_from_faces.description:
Creates the BVH tree from an array of faces. Each 3 vertices of the input faces array represent one triangle (face).
				Returns true if the tree is successfully built, false otherwise.

get_faces.description: Returns a copy of the geometry faces. Each 3 vertices of the array represent one triangle (face).

intersect_segment.description:
Tests for intersection with a segment going from begin to end.
				If an intersection with a triangle happens returns a  with the following fields:
				position: The position on the intersected triangle.
				normal: The normal of the intersected triangle.
				face_index: The index of the intersected triangle.
				Returns an empty  if no intersection happens.
				See also intersect_ray, which is similar but uses an infinite-length ray.

intersect_ray.description:
Tests for intersection with a ray starting at begin and facing dir and extending toward infinity.
				If an intersection with a triangle happens, returns a  with the following fields:
				position: The position on the intersected triangle.
				normal: The normal of the intersected triangle.
				face_index: The index of the intersected triangle.
				Returns an empty  if no intersection happens.
				See also intersect_segment, which is similar but uses a finite-length segment.

TubeTrailMesh.brief_description: Represents a straight tube-shaped  with variable width.
TubeTrailMesh.description:
represents a straight tube-shaped mesh with variable width. The tube is composed of a number of cylindrical sections, each with the same section_length and number of section_rings. A curve is sampled along the total length of the tube, meaning that the curve determines the radius of the tube along its length.
		This primitive mesh is usually used for particle trails.

radius.description: The baseline radius of the tube. The radius of a particular section ring is obtained by multiplying this radius by the value of the curve at the given distance.

radial_steps.description: The number of sides on the tube. For example, a value of 5 means the tube will be pentagonal. Higher values result in a more detailed tube at the cost of performance.

sections.description: The total number of sections on the tube.

section_length.description: The length of a section of the tube.

section_rings.description: The number of rings in a section. The curve is sampled on each ring to determine its radius. Higher values result in a more detailed tube at the cost of performance.

cap_top.description: If true, generates a cap at the top of the tube. This can be set to false to speed up generation and rendering when the cap is never seen by the camera.

cap_bottom.description: If true, generates a cap at the bottom of the tube. This can be set to false to speed up generation and rendering when the cap is never seen by the camera.

curve.description: Determines the radius of the tube along its length. The radius of a particular section ring is obtained by multiplying the baseline radius by the value of this curve at the given distance. For values smaller than 0, the faces will be inverted. Should be a unit .

Tween.brief_description: Lightweight object used for general-purpose animation via script, using s.

tween_subtween.description:
Creates and appends a . This method can be used to nest subtween within this , allowing for the creation of more complex and composable sequences.
				
				# Subtween will rotate the object.
				var subtween = create_tween()
				subtween.tween_property(self, "rotation_degrees", 45.0, 1.0)
				subtween.tween_property(self, "rotation_degrees", 0.0, 1.0)

				# Parent tween will execute the subtween as one of its steps.
				var tween = create_tween()
				tween.tween_property(self, "position:x", 500, 3.0)
				tween.tween_subtween(subtween)
				tween.tween_property(self, "position:x", 300, 2.0)
				
				Note: The methods pause, stop, and set_loops can cause the parent  to get stuck on the subtween step; see the documentation for those methods for more information.
				Note: The pause and process modes set by set_pause_mode and set_process_mode on subtween will be overridden by the parent 's settings.

custom_step.description:
Processes the  by the given delta value, in seconds. This is mostly useful for manual control when the  is paused. It can also be used to end the  animation immediately, by setting delta longer than the whole duration of the  animation.
				Returns true if the  still has s that haven't finished.

stop.description:
Stops the tweening and resets the  to its initial state. This will not remove any appended s.
				Note: This does not reset targets of s to their values when the  first started.
				
				var tween = create_tween()

				# Will move from 0 to 500 over 1 second.
				position.x = 0.0
				tween.tween_property(self, "position:x", 500, 1.0)

				# Will be at (about) 250 when the timer finishes.
				await get_tree().create_timer(0.5).timeout

				# Will now move from (about) 250 to 500 over 1 second,
				# thus at half the speed as before.
				tween.stop()
				tween.play()
				
				Note: If a Tween is stopped and not bound to any node, it will exist indefinitely until manually started or invalidated. If you lose a reference to such Tween, you can retrieve it using SceneTree.get_processed_tweens.

pause.description:
Pauses the tweening. The animation can be resumed by using play.
				Note: If a Tween is paused and not bound to any node, it will exist indefinitely until manually started or invalidated. If you lose a reference to such Tween, you can retrieve it using SceneTree.get_processed_tweens.

kill.description: Aborts all tweening operations and invalidates the .

get_total_elapsed_time.description:
Returns the total time in seconds the  has been animating (i.e. the time since it started, not counting pauses etc.). The time is affected by set_speed_scale, and stop will reset it to 0.
				Note: As it results from accumulating frame deltas, the time returned after the  has finished animating will be slightly greater than the actual  duration.

is_running.description: Returns whether the  is currently running, i.e. it wasn't paused and it's not finished.

is_valid.description: Returns whether the  is valid. A valid  is a  contained by the scene tree (i.e. the array from SceneTree.get_processed_tweens will contain this ). A  might become invalid when it has finished tweening, is killed, or when created with Tween.new(). Invalid s can't have s appended.

bind_node.description:
Binds this  with the given node. s are processed directly by the , so they run independently of the animated nodes. When you bind a  with the , the  will halt the animation when the object is not inside tree and the  will be automatically killed when the bound object is freed. Also  will make the pausing behavior dependent on the bound node.
				For a shorter way to create and bind a , you can use Node.create_tween.

set_process_mode.description:
Determines whether the  should run after process frames (see Node._process) or physics frames (see Node._physics_process).
				Default value is .

set_pause_mode.description:
Determines the behavior of the  when the  is paused.
				Default value is .

set_ignore_time_scale.description: If ignore is true, the tween will ignore Engine.time_scale and update with the real, elapsed time. This affects all s and their delays. Default value is false.

set_parallel.description:
If parallel is true, the s appended after this method will by default run simultaneously, as opposed to sequentially.
				Note: Just like with parallel, the tweener added right before this method will also be part of the parallel step.
				
				tween.tween_property(self, "position", Vector2(300, 0), 0.5)
				tween.set_parallel()
				tween.tween_property(self, "modulate", Color.GREEN, 0.5) # Runs together with the position tweener.

set_loops.description:
Sets the number of times the tweening sequence will be repeated, i.e. set_loops(2) will run the animation twice.
				Calling this method without arguments will make the  run infinitely, until either it is killed with kill, the 's bound node is freed, or all the animated objects have been freed (which makes further animation impossible).
				Warning: Make sure to always add some duration/delay when using infinite loops. To prevent the game freezing, 0-duration looped animations (e.g. a single  with no delay) are stopped after a small number of loops, which may produce unexpected results. If a 's lifetime depends on some node, always use bind_node.

get_loops_left.description: Returns the number of remaining loops for this  (see set_loops). A return value of -1 indicates an infinitely looping , and a return value of 0 indicates that the  has already finished.

set_speed_scale.description: Scales the speed of tweening. This affects all s and their delays.

set_trans.description:
Sets the default transition type for s and s appended after this method.
				Before this method is called, the default transition type is .
				
				var tween = create_tween()
				tween.tween_property(self, "position", Vector2(300, 0), 0.5) # Uses TRANS_LINEAR.
				tween.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE)
				tween.tween_property(self, "rotation_degrees", 45.0, 0.5) # Uses TRANS_SINE.

set_ease.description:
Sets the default ease type for s and s appended after this method.
				Before this method is called, the default ease type is .
				
				var tween = create_tween()
				tween.tween_property(self, "position", Vector2(300, 0), 0.5) # Uses EASE_IN_OUT.
				tween.set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN)
				tween.tween_property(self, "rotation_degrees", 45.0, 0.5) # Uses EASE_IN.

interpolate_value.description:
This method can be used for manual interpolation of a value, when you don't want  to do animating for you. It's similar to @GlobalScope.lerp, but with support for custom transition and easing.
				initial_value is the starting value of the interpolation.
				delta_value is the change of the value in the interpolation, i.e. it's equal to final_value - initial_value.
				elapsed_time is the time in seconds that passed after the interpolation started and it's used to control the position of the interpolation. E.g. when it's equal to half of the duration, the interpolated value will be halfway between initial and final values. This value can also be greater than duration or lower than 0, which will extrapolate the value.
				duration is the total time of the interpolation.
				Note: If duration is equal to 0, the method will always return the final value, regardless of elapsed_time provided.

Tweener.brief_description: Abstract class for all Tweeners used by .
Tweener.description: Tweeners are objects that perform a specific animating task, e.g. interpolating a property or calling a method at a given time. A  can't be created manually, you need to use a dedicated method from .

TwoBoneIK3D.brief_description: Rotation based intersection of two circles inverse kinematics solver.
TwoBoneIK3D.description:
This  requires a pole target. It provides deterministic results by constructing a plane from each joint and pole target and finding the intersection of two circles (disks in 3D).
		This IK can handle twist by setting the pole direction. If there are more than one bone between each set bone, their rotations are ignored, and the straight line connecting the root-middle and middle-end joints are treated as virtual bones.

set_target_node.description: Sets the target node that the end bone is trying to reach.

get_target_node.description: Returns the target node that the end bone is trying to reach.

set_pole_node.description: Sets the pole target node that constructs a plane which the joints are all on and the pole is trying to direct.

get_pole_node.description: Returns the pole target node that constructs a plane which the joints are all on and the pole is trying to direct.

set_middle_bone_name.description:
Sets the middle bone name.
				Note: The middle bone must be a child of the root bone.

set_pole_direction.description:
Sets the pole direction.
				The pole is on the middle bone and will direct to the pole target.
				The rotation axis is a vector that is orthogonal to this and the forward vector.
				Note: The pole direction and the forward vector shouldn't be colinear to avoid unintended rotation.

set_pole_direction_vector.description:
Sets the pole direction vector.
				This vector is normalized by an internal process.
				If the vector length is 0, it is considered synonymous with .

get_pole_direction_vector.description:
Returns the pole direction vector.
				If get_pole_direction is , this method returns Vector3(0, 0, 0).

set_end_bone_name.description:
Sets the end bone name.
				Note: The end bone must be a child of the middle bone.

set_use_virtual_end.description: If enabled is true, the end bone is extended from the middle bone as a virtual bone.

is_using_virtual_end.description: Returns true if the end bone is extended from the middle bone as a virtual bone.

set_extend_end_bone.description: If enabled is true, the end bone is extended to have a tail.

is_end_bone_extended.description: Returns true if the end bone is extended to have a tail.

set_end_bone_direction.description: Sets the end bone tail direction when is_end_bone_extended is true.

get_end_bone_direction.description: Returns the end bone's tail direction when is_end_bone_extended is true.

set_end_bone_length.description: Sets the end bone tail length when is_end_bone_extended is true.

get_end_bone_length.description: Returns the end bone tail length of the bone chain when is_end_bone_extended is true.

UDPServer.brief_description: Helper class to implement a UDP server.

listen.description: Starts the server by opening a UDP socket listening on the given port. You can optionally specify a bind_address to only listen for packets sent to that address. See also PacketPeerUDP.bind.

poll.description: Call this method at regular intervals (e.g. inside Node._process) to process new packets. Any packet from a known address/port pair will be delivered to the appropriate , while any packet received from an unknown address/port pair will be added as a pending connection (see is_connection_available and take_connection). The maximum number of pending connections is defined via max_pending_connections.

is_connection_available.description: Returns true if a packet with a new address/port combination was received on the socket.

get_local_port.description: Returns the local port this server is listening to.

is_listening.description: Returns true if the socket is open and listening on a port.

take_connection.description: Returns the first pending connection (connected to the appropriate address/port). Will return null if no new connection is available. See also is_connection_available, PacketPeerUDP.connect_to_host.

stop.description: Stops the server, closing the UDP socket if open. Will close all connected  accepted via take_connection (remote peers will not be notified).

max_pending_connections.description: Define the maximum number of pending connections, during poll, any new pending connection exceeding that value will be automatically dropped. Setting this value to 0 effectively prevents any new pending connection to be accepted (e.g. when all your players have connected).

UDSServer.description:
A Unix Domain Socket (UDS) server. Listens to connections on a socket path and returns a  when it gets an incoming connection. Unix Domain Sockets provide inter-process communication on the same machine using the filesystem namespace.
		Note: Unix Domain Sockets are only available on Unix-like systems (Linux, macOS, etc.) and are not supported on Windows.

listen.description:
Listens on the socket at path. The socket file will be created at the specified path.
				Note: The socket file must not already exist at the specified path. You may need to remove any existing socket file before calling this method.

take_connection.description: If a connection is available, returns a StreamPeerUDS with the connection.

UndoRedo.brief_description: Provides a high-level interface for implementing undo and redo operations.

create_action.description:
Create a new action. After this is called, do all your calls to add_do_method, add_undo_method, add_do_property, and add_undo_property, then commit the action with commit_action.
				The way actions are merged is dictated by merge_mode.
				The way undo operation are ordered in actions is dictated by backward_undo_ops. When backward_undo_ops is false undo option are ordered in the same order they were added. Which means the first operation to be added will be the first to be undone.

commit_action.description: Commit the action. If execute is true (which it is by default), all "do" methods/properties are called/set when this function is called.

is_committing_action.description: Returns true if the  is currently committing the action, i.e. running its "do" method or property change (see commit_action).

add_do_method.description: Register a  that will be called when the action is committed.

add_undo_method.description: Register a  that will be called when the action is undone.

add_do_property.description: Register a property that would change its value to value when the action is committed.

add_undo_property.description: Register a property that would change its value to value when the action is undone.

add_do_reference.description:
Register a reference to an object that will be erased if the "do" history is deleted. This is useful for objects added by the "do" action and removed by the "undo" action.
				When the "do" history is deleted, if the object is a , it will be unreferenced. Otherwise, it will be freed. Do not use for resources.
				
				var node = Node2D.new()
				undo_redo.create_action("Add node")
				undo_redo.add_do_method(add_child.bind(node))
				undo_redo.add_do_reference(node)
				undo_redo.add_undo_method(remove_child.bind(node))
				undo_redo.commit_action()

add_undo_reference.description:
Register a reference to an object that will be erased if the "undo" history is deleted. This is useful for objects added by the "undo" action and removed by the "do" action.
				When the "undo" history is deleted, if the object is a , it will be unreferenced. Otherwise, it will be freed. Do not use for resources.
				
				var node = $Node2D
				undo_redo.create_action("Remove node")
				undo_redo.add_do_method(remove_child.bind(node))
				undo_redo.add_undo_method(add_child.bind(node))
				undo_redo.add_undo_reference(node)
				undo_redo.commit_action()

start_force_keep_in_merge_ends.description: Marks the next "do" and "undo" operations to be processed even if the action gets merged with another in the  mode. Return to normal operation using end_force_keep_in_merge_ends.

end_force_keep_in_merge_ends.description: Stops marking operations as to be processed even if the action gets merged with another in the  mode. See start_force_keep_in_merge_ends.

get_history_count.description: Returns how many elements are in the history.

get_current_action.description: Gets the index of the current action.

get_action_name.description: Gets the action name from its index.

clear_history.description:
Clear the undo/redo history and associated references.
				Passing false to increase_version will prevent the version number from increasing when the history is cleared.

get_current_action_name.description: Gets the name of the current action, equivalent to get_action_name(get_current_action()).

has_undo.description: Returns true if an "undo" action is available.

has_redo.description: Returns true if a "redo" action is available.

get_version.description:
Gets the version. Every time a new action is committed, the 's version number is increased automatically.
				This is useful mostly to check if something changed from a saved version.

max_steps.description: The maximum number of steps that can be stored in the undo/redo history. If the number of stored steps exceeds this limit, older steps are removed from history and can no longer be reached by calling undo. A value of 0 or lower means no limit.

UniformSetCacheRD.brief_description: Uniform set cache manager for Rendering Device based renderers.
UniformSetCacheRD.description: Uniform set cache manager for -based renderers. Provides a way to create a uniform set and reuse it in subsequent calls for as long as the uniform set exists. Uniform set will automatically be cleaned up when dependent objects are freed.

get_cache.description: Creates/returns a cached uniform set based on the provided uniforms for a given shader.

VBoxContainer.brief_description: A container that arranges its child controls vertically.
VBoxContainer.description: A variant of  that can only arrange its child controls vertically. Child controls are rearranged automatically when their minimum size changes.

VFlowContainer.brief_description: A container that arranges its child controls vertically and wraps them around at the borders.
VFlowContainer.description: A variant of  that can only arrange its child controls vertically, wrapping them around at the borders. This is similar to how text in a book wraps around when no more words can fit on a line, except vertically.

VScrollBar.brief_description: A vertical scrollbar that goes from top (min) to bottom (max).
VScrollBar.description: A vertical scrollbar, typically used to navigate through content that extends beyond the visible height of a control. It is a -based control and goes from top (min) to bottom (max). Note that this direction is the opposite of 's.

VSeparator.brief_description: A vertical line used for separating other controls.
VSeparator.description: A vertical separator used for separating other controls that are arranged horizontally.  is purely visual and normally drawn as a .

VSlider.brief_description: A vertical slider that goes from bottom (min) to top (max).
VSlider.description: A vertical slider, used to adjust a value by moving a grabber along a vertical axis. It is a -based control and goes from bottom (min) to top (max). Note that this direction is the opposite of 's.

VSplitContainer.brief_description: A container that splits two child controls vertically and provides a grabber for adjusting the split ratio.
VSplitContainer.description: A container that accepts only two child controls, then arranges them vertically and creates a divisor between them. The divisor can be dragged around to change the size relation between the child controls.

VehicleBody3D.brief_description: A 3D physics body that simulates the behavior of a car.
VehicleBody3D.description:
This physics body implements all the physics logic needed to simulate a car. It is based on the raycast vehicle system commonly found in physics engines. Aside from a  for the main body of the vehicle, you must also add a  node for each wheel. You should also add a  to this node for the 3D model of the vehicle, but this model should generally not include meshes for the wheels. You can control the vehicle by using the brake, engine_force, and steering properties. The position or orientation of this node shouldn't be changed directly.
		Note: The local forward for this node is .
		Note: The origin point of your VehicleBody3D will determine the center of gravity of your vehicle. To make the vehicle more grounded, the origin point is usually kept low, moving the  and  upwards.
		Note: This class has known issues and isn't designed to provide realistic 3D vehicle physics. If you want advanced vehicle physics, you may have to write your own physics integration using  or .

engine_force.description:
Accelerates the vehicle by applying an engine force. The vehicle is only sped up if the wheels that have VehicleWheel3D.use_as_traction set to true and are in contact with a surface. The RigidBody3D.mass of the vehicle has an effect on the acceleration of the vehicle. For a vehicle with a mass set to 1000, try a value in the 25 - 50 range for acceleration.
			Note: The simulation does not take the effect of gears into account, you will need to add logic for this if you wish to simulate gears.
			A negative value will result in the vehicle reversing.

brake.description: Slows down the vehicle by applying a braking force. The vehicle is only slowed down if the wheels are in contact with a surface. The force you need to apply to adequately slow down your vehicle depends on the RigidBody3D.mass of the vehicle. For a vehicle with a mass set to 1000, try a value in the 25 - 30 range for hard braking.

steering.description:
The steering angle for the vehicle. Setting this to a non-zero value will result in the vehicle turning when it's moving. Wheels that have VehicleWheel3D.use_as_steering set to true will automatically be rotated.
			Note: This property is edited in the inspector in degrees. In code the property is set in radians.

VehicleWheel3D.brief_description: A 3D physics body for a  that simulates the behavior of a wheel.
VehicleWheel3D.description:
A node used as a child of a  parent to simulate the behavior of one of its wheels. This node also acts as a collider to detect if the wheel is touching a surface.
		Note: This class has known issues and isn't designed to provide realistic 3D vehicle physics. If you want advanced vehicle physics, you may need to write your own physics integration using another  class.

is_in_contact.description: Returns true if this wheel is in contact with a surface.

get_contact_body.description:
Returns the contacting body node if valid in the tree, as . At the moment,  is not supported so the node will be always of type .
				Returns null if the wheel is not in contact with a surface, or the contact body is not a .

get_contact_point.description: Returns the point of the suspension's collision in world space if the wheel is in contact. If the wheel isn't in contact with anything, returns the maximum point of the wheel's ray cast in world space, which is defined by wheel_rest_length + wheel_radius.

get_contact_normal.description: Returns the normal of the suspension's collision in world space if the wheel is in contact. If the wheel isn't in contact with anything, returns a vector pointing directly along the suspension axis toward the vehicle in world space.

get_skidinfo.description: Returns a value between 0.0 and 1.0 that indicates whether this wheel is skidding. 0.0 is skidding (the wheel has lost grip, e.g. icy terrain), 1.0 means not skidding (the wheel has full grip, e.g. dry asphalt road).

get_rpm.description: Returns the rotational speed of the wheel in revolutions per minute.

engine_force.description:
Accelerates the wheel by applying an engine force. The wheel is only sped up if it is in contact with a surface. The RigidBody3D.mass of the vehicle has an effect on the acceleration of the vehicle. For a vehicle with a mass set to 1000, try a value in the 25 - 50 range for acceleration.
			Note: The simulation does not take the effect of gears into account, you will need to add logic for this if you wish to simulate gears.
			A negative value will result in the wheel reversing.

brake.description: Slows down the wheel by applying a braking force. The wheel is only slowed down if it is in contact with a surface. The force you need to apply to adequately slow down your vehicle depends on the RigidBody3D.mass of the vehicle. For a vehicle with a mass set to 1000, try a value in the 25 - 30 range for hard braking.

steering.description: The steering angle for the wheel, in radians. Setting this to a non-zero value will result in the vehicle turning when it's moving.

use_as_traction.description: If true, this wheel transfers engine force to the ground to propel the vehicle forward. This value is used in conjunction with VehicleBody3D.engine_force and ignored if you are using the per-wheel engine_force value instead.

use_as_steering.description: If true, this wheel will be turned when the car steers. This value is used in conjunction with VehicleBody3D.steering and ignored if you are using the per-wheel steering value instead.

wheel_roll_influence.description: This value affects the roll of your vehicle. If set to 1.0 for all wheels, your vehicle will resist body roll, while a value of 0.0 will be prone to rolling over.

wheel_radius.description: The radius of the wheel in meters.

wheel_rest_length.description: This is the distance in meters the wheel is lowered from its origin point. Don't set this to 0.0 and move the wheel into position, instead move the origin point of your wheel (the gizmo in Godot) to the position the wheel will take when bottoming out, then use the rest length to move the wheel down to the position it should be in when the car is in rest.

wheel_friction_slip.description:
This determines how much grip this wheel has. It is combined with the friction setting of the surface the wheel is in contact with. 0.0 means no grip, 1.0 is normal grip. For a drift car setup, try setting the grip of the rear wheels slightly lower than the front wheels, or use a lower value to simulate tire wear.
			It's best to set this to 1.0 when starting out.

suspension_travel.description: This is the distance the suspension can travel. As Godot units are equivalent to meters, keep this setting relatively low. Try a value between 0.1 and 0.3 depending on the type of car.

suspension_stiffness.description: The stiffness of the suspension, measured in Newtons per millimeter (N/mm), or megagrams per second squared (Mg/s²). Use a value lower than 50 for an off-road car, a value between 50 and 100 for a race car and try something around 200 for something like a Formula 1 car.

suspension_max_force.description: The maximum force the spring can resist. This value should be higher than a quarter of the RigidBody3D.mass of the  or the spring will not carry the weight of the vehicle. Good results are often obtained by a value that is about 3× to 4× this number.

damping_compression.description: The damping applied to the suspension spring when being compressed, meaning when the wheel is moving up relative to the vehicle. It is measured in Newton-seconds per millimeter (N⋅s/mm), or megagrams per second (Mg/s). This value should be between 0.0 (no damping) and 1.0, but may be more. A value of 0.0 means the car will keep bouncing as the spring keeps its energy. A good value for this is around 0.3 for a normal car, 0.5 for a race car.

damping_relaxation.description: The damping applied to the suspension spring when rebounding or extending, meaning when the wheel is moving down relative to the vehicle. It is measured in Newton-seconds per millimeter (N⋅s/mm), or megagrams per second (Mg/s). This value should be between 0.0 (no damping) and 1.0, but may be more. This value should always be slightly higher than the damping_compression property. For a damping_compression value of 0.3, try a relaxation value of 0.5.

VideoStream.description: Base resource type for all video streams. Classes that derive from  can all be used as resource types to play back videos in .

_instantiate_playback.description: Called when the video starts playing, to initialize and return a subclass of .

file.description:
The video file path or URI that this  resource handles.
			For , this filename should be an Ogg Theora video file with the .ogv extension.

VideoStreamPlayback.brief_description: Internal class used by  to manage playback state when played from a .
VideoStreamPlayback.description: This class is intended to be overridden by video decoder extensions with custom implementations of .

_stop.description: Stops playback. May be called multiple times before _play, or in response to VideoStreamPlayer.stop. _is_playing should return false once stopped.

_play.description: Called in response to VideoStreamPlayer.autoplay or VideoStreamPlayer.play. Note that manual playback may also invoke _stop multiple times before this method is called. _is_playing should return true once playing.

_is_playing.description: Returns the playback state, as determined by calls to _play and _stop.

_set_paused.description: Set the paused status of video playback. _is_paused must return paused. Called in response to the VideoStreamPlayer.paused setter.

_is_paused.description: Returns the paused status, as set by _set_paused.

_get_length.description: Returns the video duration in seconds, if known, or 0 if unknown.

_get_playback_position.description: Return the current playback timestamp. Called in response to the VideoStreamPlayer.stream_position getter.

_seek.description: Seeks to time seconds. Called in response to the VideoStreamPlayer.stream_position setter.

_set_audio_track.description: Select the audio track idx. Called when playback starts, and in response to the VideoStreamPlayer.audio_track setter.

_get_texture.description: Allocates a  in which decoded video frames will be drawn.

_update.description: Ticks video playback for delta seconds. Called every frame as long as both _is_paused and _is_playing return true.

_get_channels.description: Returns the number of audio channels.

_get_mix_rate.description: Returns the audio sample rate used for mixing.

mix_audio.description: Render num_frames audio frames (of _get_channels floats each) from buffer, starting from index offset in the array. Returns the number of audio frames rendered, or -1 on error.

VideoStreamPlayer.brief_description: A control used for video playback.
VideoStreamPlayer.description:
A control used for playback of  resources.
		Supported video formats are Ogg Theora (.ogv, ) and any format exposed via a GDExtension plugin.
		Warning: On Web, video playback will perform poorly due to missing architecture-specific assembly optimizations.

play.description: Starts the video playback from the beginning. If the video is paused, this will not unpause the video.

stop.description:
Stops the video playback and sets the stream position to 0.
				Note: Although the stream position will be set to 0, the first frame of the video stream won't become the current frame.

is_playing.description:
Returns true if the video is playing.
				Note: The video is still considered playing if paused during playback.

get_stream_name.description: Returns the video stream's name, or "<No Stream>" if no video stream is assigned.

get_stream_length.description: The length of the current stream, in seconds.

get_video_texture.description: Returns the current frame as a .

audio_track.description: The embedded audio track to play.

stream.description: The assigned video stream. See description for supported formats.

volume.description: Audio volume as a linear value.

speed_scale.description: The stream's current speed scale. 1.0 is the normal speed, while 2.0 is double speed and 0.5 is half speed. A speed scale of 0.0 pauses the video, similar to setting paused to true.

autoplay.description: If true, playback starts when the scene loads.

paused.description: If true, the video is paused.

expand.description: If true, the video scales to the control size. Otherwise, the control minimum size will be automatically adjusted to match the video stream's dimensions.

loop.description: If true, the video restarts when it reaches its end.

buffering_msec.description: Amount of time in milliseconds to store in buffer while playing.

stream_position.description: The current position of the stream, in seconds.

bus.description: Audio bus to use for sound playback.

Viewport.brief_description: Abstract base class for viewports. Encapsulates drawing and interaction with a game world.
Viewport.description:
A  creates a different view into the screen, or a sub-view inside another viewport. Child 2D nodes will display on it, and child Camera3D 3D nodes will render on it too.
		Optionally, a viewport can have its own 2D or 3D world, so it doesn't share what it draws with other viewports.
		Viewports can also choose to be audio listeners, so they generate positional audio depending on a 2D or 3D camera child of it.
		Also, viewports can be assigned to different screens in case the devices have multiple screens.
		Finally, viewports can also behave as render targets, in which case they will not be visible unless the associated texture is used to draw.

find_world_2d.description: Returns the first valid  for this viewport, searching the world_2d property of itself and any Viewport ancestor.

get_stretch_transform.description:
Returns the automatically computed 2D stretch transform, taking the 's stretch settings into account. The final value is multiplied by Window.content_scale_factor, but only for the root viewport. If this method is called on a  (e.g., in a scene tree with  and ), the scale factor of the root window will not be applied. Using Transform2D.get_scale on the returned value, this can be used to compensate for scaling when zooming a  node, or to scale down a  to be pixel-perfect regardless of the automatically computed scale factor.
				Note: Due to how pixel scaling works, the returned transform's X and Y scale may differ slightly, even when Window.content_scale_aspect is set to a mode that preserves the pixels' aspect ratio. If Window.content_scale_aspect is , the X and Y scale may differ significantly.

get_final_transform.description: Returns the transform from the viewport's coordinate system to the embedder's coordinate system.

get_screen_transform.description: Returns the transform from the Viewport's coordinates to the screen coordinates of the containing window manager window.

get_visible_rect.description: Returns the visible rectangle in global screen coordinates.

get_render_info.description: Returns rendering statistics of the given type.

get_viewport_rid.description: Returns the viewport's RID from the .

push_text_input.description: Helper method which calls the set_text() method on the currently focused , provided that it is defined (e.g. if the focused Control is  or ).

push_input.description:
Triggers the given event in this . This can be used to pass an  between viewports, or to locally apply inputs that were sent over the network or saved to a file.
				If in_local_coords is false, the event's position is in the embedder's coordinates and will be converted to viewport coordinates. If in_local_coords is true, the event's position is in viewport coordinates.
				While this method serves a similar purpose as Input.parse_input_event, it does not remap the specified event based on project settings like ProjectSettings.input_devices/pointing/emulate_touch_from_mouse.
				Calling this method will propagate calls to child nodes for following methods in the given order:
				- Node._input
				- Control._gui_input for  nodes
				- Node._shortcut_input
				- Node._unhandled_key_input
				- Node._unhandled_input
				If an earlier method marks the input as handled via set_input_as_handled, any later method in this list will not be called.
				If none of the methods handle the event and physics_object_picking is true, the event is used for physics object picking.

push_unhandled_input.description:
Triggers the given event in this . This can be used to pass an  between viewports, or to locally apply inputs that were sent over the network or saved to a file.
				If in_local_coords is false, the event's position is in the embedder's coordinates and will be converted to viewport coordinates. If in_local_coords is true, the event's position is in viewport coordinates.
				Calling this method will propagate calls to child nodes for following methods in the given order:
				- Node._shortcut_input
				- Node._unhandled_key_input
				- Node._unhandled_input
				If an earlier method marks the input as handled via set_input_as_handled, any later method in this list will not be called.
				If none of the methods handle the event and physics_object_picking is true, the event is used for physics object picking.
				Note: This method doesn't propagate input events to embedded s or s.

notify_mouse_entered.description:
Inform the Viewport that the mouse has entered its area. Use this function before sending an  or  to the  with Viewport.push_input. See also notify_mouse_exited.
				Note: In most cases, it is not necessary to call this function because  nodes that are children of  are notified automatically. This is only necessary when interacting with viewports in non-default ways, for example as textures in  or with an  that forwards input events.

notify_mouse_exited.description:
Inform the Viewport that the mouse has left its area. Use this function when the node that displays the viewport notices the mouse has left the area of the displayed viewport. See also notify_mouse_entered.
				Note: In most cases, it is not necessary to call this function because  nodes that are children of  are notified automatically. This is only necessary when interacting with viewports in non-default ways, for example as textures in  or with an  that forwards input events.

get_mouse_position.description: Returns the mouse's position in this  using the coordinate system of this .

warp_mouse.description:
Moves the mouse pointer to the specified position in this  using the coordinate system of this .
				Note: warp_mouse is only supported on Windows, macOS and Linux. It has no effect on Android, iOS and Web.

update_mouse_cursor_state.description: Force instantly updating the display based on the current mouse cursor position. This includes updating the mouse cursor shape and sending necessary , ,  and  signals and their respective mouse_exited counterparts.

gui_cancel_drag.description: Cancels the drag operation that was previously started through Control._get_drag_data or forced with Control.force_drag.

gui_get_drag_data.description: Returns the drag data from the GUI, that was previously returned by Control._get_drag_data.

gui_get_drag_description.description: Returns the human-readable description of the drag data, used for assistive apps.

gui_set_drag_description.description: Sets the human-readable description of the drag data to description, used for assistive apps.

gui_is_dragging.description:
Returns true if a drag operation is currently ongoing and where the drop action could happen in this viewport.
				Alternative to  and  when you prefer polling the value.

gui_is_drag_successful.description: Returns true if the drag operation is successful.

gui_release_focus.description: Removes the focus from the currently focused  within this viewport. If no  has the focus, does nothing.

gui_get_focus_owner.description: Returns the currently focused  within this viewport. If no  is focused, returns null.

gui_get_hovered_control.description:
Returns the  that the mouse is currently hovering over in this viewport. If no  has the cursor, returns null.
				Typically the leaf  node or deepest level of the subtree which claims hover. This is very useful when used together with Node.is_ancestor_of to find if the mouse is within a control tree.

set_positional_shadow_atlas_quadrant_sub.description: Sets the number of subdivisions to use in the specified quadrant. A higher number of subdivisions allows you to have more shadows in the scene at once, but reduces the quality of the shadows. A good practice is to have quadrants with a varying number of subdivisions and to have as few subdivisions as possible.

get_positional_shadow_atlas_quadrant_sub.description: Returns the positional shadow atlas quadrant subdivision of the specified quadrant.

set_input_as_handled.description:
Stops the input from propagating further up the .
				Note: This does not affect the methods in , only the way events are propagated.

is_input_handled.description:
Returns whether the current  has been handled. Input events are not handled until set_input_as_handled has been called during the lifetime of an .
				This is usually done as part of input handling methods like Node._input, Control._gui_input or others, as well as in corresponding signal handlers.
				If handle_input_locally is set to false, this method will try finding the first parent viewport that is set to handle input locally, and return its value for is_input_handled instead.

get_embedded_subwindows.description:
Returns a list of the visible embedded s inside the viewport.
				Note: s inside other viewports will not be listed.

set_canvas_cull_mask_bit.description: Set/clear individual bits on the rendering layer mask. This simplifies editing this 's layers.

get_canvas_cull_mask_bit.description: Returns an individual bit on the rendering layer mask.

get_audio_listener_2d.description: Returns the currently active 2D audio listener. Returns null if there are no active 2D audio listeners, in which case the active 2D camera will be treated as listener.

get_camera_2d.description:
Returns the currently active 2D camera. Returns null if there are no active cameras.
				Note: If called while the Camera Override system is active in editor, this will return the internally managed override camera. It is therefore advised to avoid caching the return value, or to check that the cached value is still a valid instance and is the current camera before use. See @GlobalScope.is_instance_valid and Camera2D.is_current.

find_world_3d.description: Returns the first valid  for this viewport, searching the world_3d property of itself and any Viewport ancestor.

get_audio_listener_3d.description: Returns the currently active 3D audio listener. Returns null if there are no active 3D audio listeners, in which case the active 3D camera will be treated as listener.

get_camera_3d.description:
