Returns true if there is a matching  in the tree that has an icon item with the specified name and theme_type.
				See Control.get_theme_color for details.

has_theme_stylebox.description:
Returns true if there is a matching  in the tree that has a stylebox item with the specified name and theme_type.
				See Control.get_theme_color for details.

has_theme_font.description:
Returns true if there is a matching  in the tree that has a font item with the specified name and theme_type.
				See Control.get_theme_color for details.

has_theme_font_size.description:
Returns true if there is a matching  in the tree that has a font size item with the specified name and theme_type.
				See Control.get_theme_color for details.

has_theme_color.description:
Returns true if there is a matching  in the tree that has a color item with the specified name and theme_type.
				See Control.get_theme_color for details.

has_theme_constant.description:
Returns true if there is a matching  in the tree that has a constant item with the specified name and theme_type.
				See Control.get_theme_color for details.

get_theme_default_base_scale.description:
Returns the default base scale value from the first matching  in the tree if that  has a valid Theme.default_base_scale value.
				See Control.get_theme_color for details.

get_theme_default_font.description:
Returns the default font from the first matching  in the tree if that  has a valid Theme.default_font value.
				See Control.get_theme_color for details.

get_theme_default_font_size.description:
Returns the default font size value from the first matching  in the tree if that  has a valid Theme.default_font_size value.
				See Control.get_theme_color for details.

get_window_id.description: Returns the ID of the window.

set_layout_direction.description: Sets layout direction and text writing direction. Right-to-left layouts are necessary for certain languages (e.g. Arabic and Hebrew).

get_layout_direction.description: Returns layout direction and text writing direction.

is_layout_rtl.description: Returns true if the layout is right-to-left.

set_use_font_oversampling.description: Enables font oversampling. This makes fonts look better when they are scaled up.

is_using_font_oversampling.description: Returns true if font oversampling is enabled. See set_use_font_oversampling.

popup.description:
Shows the  and makes it transient (see transient). If rect is provided, it will be set as the 's size. Fails if called on the main window.
				If ProjectSettings.display/window/subwindows/embed_subwindows is true (single-window mode), rect's coordinates are global and relative to the main window's top-left corner (excluding window decorations). If rect's position coordinates are negative, the window will be located outside the main window and may not be visible as a result.
				If ProjectSettings.display/window/subwindows/embed_subwindows is false (multi-window mode), rect's coordinates are global and relative to the top-left corner of the leftmost screen. If rect's position coordinates are negative, the window will be placed at the top-left corner of the screen.
				Note: rect must be in global coordinates if specified.

popup_on_parent.description: Popups the  with a position shifted by parent 's position. If the  is embedded, has the same effect as popup.

popup_centered.description:
Popups the  at the center of the current screen, with optionally given minimum size. If the  is embedded, it will be centered in the parent  instead.
				Note: Calling it with the default value of minsize is equivalent to calling it with size.

popup_centered_ratio.description:
If  is embedded, popups the  centered inside its embedder and sets its size as a ratio of embedder's size.
				If  is a native window, popups the  centered inside the screen of its parent  and sets its size as a ratio of the screen size.

popup_centered_clamped.description:
Popups the  centered inside its parent . fallback_ratio determines the maximum size of the , in relation to its parent.
				Note: Calling it with the default value of minsize is equivalent to calling it with size.

popup_exclusive.description:
Attempts to parent this dialog to the last exclusive window relative to from_node, and then calls Window.popup on it. The dialog must have no current parent, otherwise the method fails.
				See also set_unparent_when_invisible and Node.get_last_exclusive_window.

popup_exclusive_on_parent.description:
Attempts to parent this dialog to the last exclusive window relative to from_node, and then calls Window.popup_on_parent on it. The dialog must have no current parent, otherwise the method fails.
				See also set_unparent_when_invisible and Node.get_last_exclusive_window.

popup_exclusive_centered.description:
Attempts to parent this dialog to the last exclusive window relative to from_node, and then calls Window.popup_centered on it. The dialog must have no current parent, otherwise the method fails.
				See also set_unparent_when_invisible and Node.get_last_exclusive_window.

popup_exclusive_centered_ratio.description:
Attempts to parent this dialog to the last exclusive window relative to from_node, and then calls Window.popup_centered_ratio on it. The dialog must have no current parent, otherwise the method fails.
				See also set_unparent_when_invisible and Node.get_last_exclusive_window.

popup_exclusive_centered_clamped.description:
Attempts to parent this dialog to the last exclusive window relative to from_node, and then calls Window.popup_centered_clamped on it. The dialog must have no current parent, otherwise the method fails.
				See also set_unparent_when_invisible and Node.get_last_exclusive_window.

mode.description:
Set's the window's current mode.
			Note: Fullscreen mode is not exclusive full screen on Windows and Linux.
			Note: This method only works with native windows, i.e. the main window and -derived nodes when Viewport.gui_embed_subwindows is disabled in the main viewport.

title.description: The window's title. If the  is native, title styles set in  will have no effect.

initial_position.description: Specifies the initial type of position for the .

position.description:
The window's position in pixels.
			If ProjectSettings.display/window/subwindows/embed_subwindows is false, the position is in absolute screen coordinates. This typically applies to editor plugins. If the setting is true, the window's position is in the coordinates of its parent .
			Note: This property only works if initial_position is set to .

size.description: The window's size in pixels. See also content_scale_size, which doesn't set the window's physical size but affects how scaling works relative to the current content_scale_mode.

current_screen.description: The screen the window is currently on.

nonclient_area.description: If set, defines the window's custom decoration area which will receive mouse input, even if normal input to the window is blocked (such as when it has an exclusive child opened). See also .

visible.description: If true, the window is visible.

wrap_controls.description:
If true, the window's size will automatically update when a child node is added or removed, ignoring min_size if the new size is bigger.
			If false, you need to call child_controls_changed manually.

transient.description:
If true, the  is transient, i.e. it's considered a child of another . The transient window will be destroyed with its transient parent and will return focus to their parent when closed. The transient window is displayed on top of a non-exclusive full-screen parent window. Transient windows can't enter full-screen mode.
			Note that behavior might be different depending on the platform.

transient_to_focused.description: If true, and the  is transient, this window will (at the time of becoming visible) become transient to the currently focused window instead of the immediate parent window in the hierarchy. Note that the transient parent is assigned at the time this window becomes visible, so changing it afterwards has no effect until re-shown.

exclusive.description:
If true, the  will be in exclusive mode. Exclusive windows are always on top of their parent and will block all input going to the parent .
			Needs transient enabled to work.

unresizable.description: If true, the window can't be resized.

borderless.description: If true, the window will have no borders.

always_on_top.description: If true, the window will be on top of all other windows. Does not work if transient is enabled.

transparent.description:
If true, the 's background can be transparent. This is best used with embedded windows.
			Note: Transparency support is implemented on Linux, macOS and Windows, but availability might vary depending on GPU driver, display manager, and compositor capabilities.
			Note: This property has no effect if ProjectSettings.display/window/per_pixel_transparency/allowed is set to false.

unfocusable.description: If true, the  can't be focused nor interacted with. It can still be visible.

popup_window.description: If true, the  will be considered a popup. Popups are sub-windows that don't show as separate windows in system's window manager's window list and will send close request when anything is clicked outside of them (unless exclusive is enabled).

extend_to_title.description:
If true, the  contents is expanded to the full size of the window, window title bar is transparent.
			Note: This property is implemented only on macOS.
			Note: This property only works with native windows.

mouse_passthrough.description:
If true, all mouse events will be passed to the underlying window of the same application. See also mouse_passthrough_polygon.
			Note: This property is implemented on Linux (X11), macOS and Windows.
			Note: This property only works with native windows.

sharp_corners.description:
If true, the  will override the OS window style to display sharp corners.
			Note: This property is implemented only on Windows (11).
			Note: This property only works with native windows.

exclude_from_capture.description:
If true, the  is excluded from screenshots taken by DisplayServer.screen_get_image, DisplayServer.screen_get_image_rect, and DisplayServer.screen_get_pixel.
			Note: This property is implemented on macOS and Windows.
			Note: Enabling this setting will prevent standard screenshot methods from capturing a window image, but does NOT guarantee that other apps won't be able to capture an image. It should not be used as a DRM or security measure.

popup_wm_hint.description: If true, the  will signal to the window manager that it is supposed to be an implementation-defined "popup" (usually a floating, borderless, untileable and immovable child window).

minimize_disabled.description:
If true, the 's minimize button is disabled.
			Note: If both minimize and maximize buttons are disabled, buttons are fully hidden, and only close button is visible.
			Note: This property is implemented only on macOS and Windows.

maximize_disabled.description:
If true, the 's maximize button is disabled.
			Note: If both minimize and maximize buttons are disabled, buttons are fully hidden, and only close button is visible.
			Note: This property is implemented only on macOS and Windows.

force_native.description: If true, native window will be used regardless of parent viewport and project settings.

min_size.description:
If non-zero, the  can't be resized to be smaller than this size.
			Note: This property will be ignored in favor of get_contents_minimum_size if wrap_controls is enabled and if its size is bigger.

max_size.description:
If non-zero, the  can't be resized to be bigger than this size.
			Note: This property will be ignored if the value is lower than min_size.

keep_title_visible.description: If true, the  width is expanded to keep the title bar text fully visible.

content_scale_size.description:
The content's base size in "virtual" pixels. Not to be confused with size, which sets the actual window's physical size in pixels. If set to a value greater than 0 and content_scale_mode is set to a value other than , the 's content will be scaled when the window is resized to a different size. Higher values will make the content appear smaller, as it will be able to fit more of the project in view. On the root , this is set to match ProjectSettings.display/window/size/viewport_width and ProjectSettings.display/window/size/viewport_height by default.
			For example, when using  and content_scale_size set to Vector2i(1280, 720), using a window size of 2560×1440 will make 2D elements appear at double their original size, as the content is scaled by a factor of 2.0 (2560.0 / 1280.0 = 2.0, 1440.0 / 720.0 = 2.0).
			See the Base size section of the Multiple resolutions documentation for details.

content_scale_mode.description: Specifies how the content is scaled when the  is resized.

content_scale_aspect.description: Specifies how the content's aspect behaves when the  is resized. The base aspect is determined by content_scale_size.

content_scale_stretch.description: The policy to use to determine the final scale factor for 2D elements. This affects how content_scale_factor is applied, in addition to the automatic scale factor determined by content_scale_size.

content_scale_factor.description: Specifies the base scale of 's content when its size is equal to content_scale_size. See also Viewport.get_stretch_transform.

auto_translate.description: Toggles if any text should automatically change to its translated version depending on the current locale.

accessibility_name.description: The human-readable node name that is reported to assistive apps.

accessibility_description.description: The human-readable node description that is reported to assistive apps.

theme.description:
The  resource this node and all its  and  children use. If a child node has its own  resource set, theme items are merged with child's definitions having higher priority.
			Note:  styles will have no effect unless the window is embedded.

theme_type_variation.description: The name of a theme type variation used by this  to look up its own theme items. See Control.theme_type_variation for more details.

WorkerThreadPool.brief_description: A singleton that allocates some s on startup, used to offload tasks to these threads.

add_task.description:
Adds action as a task to be executed by a worker thread. high_priority determines if the task has a high priority or a low priority (default). You can optionally provide a description to help with debugging.
				Returns a task ID that can be used by other methods.
				Warning: Every task must be waited for completion using wait_for_task_completion or wait_for_group_task_completion at some point so that any allocated resources inside the task can be cleaned up.

is_task_completed.description:
Returns true if the task with the given ID is completed.
				Note: You should only call this method between adding the task and awaiting its completion.

wait_for_task_completion.description:
Pauses the thread that calls this method until the task with the given ID is completed.
				Returns  if the task could be successfully awaited.
				Returns  if a task with the passed ID does not exist (maybe because it was already awaited and disposed of).
				Returns  if the call is made from another running task and, due to task scheduling, there's potential for deadlocking (e.g., the task to await may be at a lower level in the call stack and therefore can't progress). This is an advanced situation that should only matter when some tasks depend on others (in the current implementation, the tricky case is a task trying to wait on an older one).

get_caller_task_id.description:
Returns the task ID of the current thread calling this method, or -1 if the task is a group task, invalid or the current thread is not part of the thread pool (e.g. the main thread).
				Can be used by a task to get its own task ID, or to determine whether the current code is running inside the worker thread pool.
				Note: Group tasks have their own IDs, so this method will return -1 for group tasks.

add_group_task.description:
Adds action as a group task to be executed by the worker threads. The  will be called a number of times based on elements, with the first thread calling it with the value 0 as a parameter, and each consecutive execution incrementing this value by 1 until it reaches element - 1.
				The number of threads the task is distributed to is defined by tasks_needed, where the default value -1 means it is distributed to all worker threads. high_priority determines if the task has a high priority or a low priority (default). You can optionally provide a description to help with debugging.
				Returns a group task ID that can be used by other methods.
				Warning: Every task must be waited for completion using wait_for_task_completion or wait_for_group_task_completion at some point so that any allocated resources inside the task can be cleaned up.

is_group_task_completed.description:
Returns true if the group task with the given ID is completed.
				Note: You should only call this method between adding the group task and awaiting its completion.

get_group_processed_element_count.description:
Returns how many times the  of the group task with the given ID has already been executed by the worker threads.
				Note: If a thread has started executing the  but is yet to finish, it won't be counted.

wait_for_group_task_completion.description: Pauses the thread that calls this method until the group task with the given ID is completed.

get_caller_group_id.description: Returns the task group ID of the current thread calling this method, or -1 if invalid or the current thread is not part of a task group.

World2D.brief_description: A resource that holds all components of a 2D world, such as a canvas and a physics space.
World2D.description: Class that has everything pertaining to a 2D world: A physics space, a canvas, and a sound space. 2D nodes register their resources into the current 2D world.

canvas.description: The  of this world's canvas resource. Used by the  for 2D drawing.

navigation_map.description: The  of this world's navigation map. Used by the .

space.description: The  of this world's physics space resource. Used by the  for 2D physics, treating it as both a space and an area.

direct_space_state.description: Direct access to the world's physics 2D space state. Used for querying current and potential collisions. When using multi-threaded physics, access is limited to Node._physics_process in the main thread.

World3D.brief_description: A resource that holds all components of a 3D world, such as a visual scenario and a physics space.
World3D.description: Class that has everything pertaining to a world: A physics space, a visual scenario, and a sound space. 3D nodes register their resources into the current 3D world.

fallback_environment.description: The World3D's fallback environment will be used if environment fails or is missing.

camera_attributes.description: The default  resource to use if none set on the .

navigation_map.description: The  of this world's navigation map. Used by the .

direct_space_state.description: Direct access to the world's physics 3D space state. Used for querying current and potential collisions. When using multi-threaded physics, access is limited to Node._physics_process in the main thread.

WorldBoundaryShape2D.brief_description: A 2D world boundary (half-plane) shape used for physics collision.
WorldBoundaryShape2D.description: A 2D world boundary shape, intended for use in physics.  works like an infinite straight line that forces all physics bodies to stay above it. The line's normal determines which direction is considered as "above" and in the editor, the smaller line over it represents this direction. It can for example be used for endless flat floors.

normal.description: The line's normal, typically a unit vector. Its direction indicates the non-colliding half-plane. Can be of any length but zero. Defaults to .

distance.description:
The distance from the origin to the line, expressed in terms of normal (according to its direction and magnitude). Actual absolute distance from the origin to the line can be calculated as abs(distance) / normal.length().
			In the scalar equation of the line ax + by = d, this is d, while the (a, b) coordinates are represented by the normal property.

WorldBoundaryShape3D.brief_description: A 3D world boundary (half-space) shape used for physics collision.
WorldBoundaryShape3D.description:
A 3D world boundary shape, intended for use in physics.  works like an infinite plane that forces all physics bodies to stay above it. The plane's normal determines which direction is considered as "above" and in the editor, the line over the plane represents this direction. It can for example be used for endless flat floors.
		Note: When the physics engine is set to Jolt Physics in the project settings (ProjectSettings.physics/3d/physics_engine),  has a finite size (centered at the shape's origin). It can be adjusted by changing ProjectSettings.physics/jolt_physics_3d/limits/world_boundary_shape_size.

plane.description: The  used by the  for collision.

WorldEnvironment.brief_description: Default environment properties for the entire scene (post-processing effects, lighting and background settings).
WorldEnvironment.description:
The  node is used to configure the default  for the scene.
		The parameters defined in the  can be overridden by an  node set on the current . Additionally, only one  may be instantiated in a given scene at a time.
		The  allows the user to specify default lighting parameters (e.g. ambient lighting), various post-processing effects (e.g. SSAO, DOF, Tonemapping), and how to draw the background (e.g. solid color, skybox). Usually, these are added in order to improve the realism/color balance of the scene.

environment.description: The  resource used by this , defining the default properties.

camera_attributes.description: The default  resource to use if none set on the .

compositor.description: The default  resource to use if none set on the .

X509Certificate.description:
The X509Certificate class represents an X509 certificate. Certificates can be loaded and saved like any other .
		They can be used as the server certificate in StreamPeerTLS.accept_stream (along with the proper ), and to specify the only certificate that should be accepted when connecting to a TLS server via StreamPeerTLS.connect_to_stream.

save.description: Saves a certificate to the given path (should be a "*.crt" file).

load.description: Loads a certificate from path ("*.crt" file).

save_to_string.description: Returns a string representation of the certificate, or an empty string if the certificate is invalid.

load_from_string.description: Loads a certificate from the given string.

XMLParser.brief_description: Provides a low-level interface for creating parsers for XML files.

read.description: Parses the next node in the file. This method returns an error code.

get_node_type.description: Returns the type of the current node. Compare with  constants.

get_node_name.description:
Returns the name of a node. This method will raise an error if the currently parsed node is a text node.
				Note: The content of a  node and the comment string of a  node are also considered names.

get_node_data.description: Returns the contents of a text node. This method will raise an error if the current parsed node is of any other type.

get_node_offset.description: Returns the byte offset of the currently parsed node since the beginning of the file or buffer. This is usually equivalent to the number of characters before the read position.

get_attribute_count.description:
Returns the number of attributes in the currently parsed element.
				Note: If this method is used while the currently parsed node is not  or , this count will not be updated and will still reflect the last element.

get_attribute_name.description: Returns the name of an attribute of the currently parsed element, specified by the idx index.

get_attribute_value.description: Returns the value of an attribute of the currently parsed element, specified by the idx index.

has_attribute.description: Returns true if the currently parsed element has an attribute with the name.

get_named_attribute_value.description: Returns the value of an attribute of the currently parsed element, specified by its name. This method will raise an error if the element has no such attribute.

get_named_attribute_value_safe.description: Returns the value of an attribute of the currently parsed element, specified by its name. This method will return an empty string if the element has no such attribute.

is_empty.description: Returns true if the currently parsed element is empty, e.g. <element />.

get_current_line.description: Returns the current line in the parsed file, counting from 0.

skip_section.description: Skips the current section. If the currently parsed node contains more inner nodes, they will be ignored and the cursor will go to the closing of the current element.

seek.description: Moves the buffer cursor to a certain offset (since the beginning) and reads the next node there. This method returns an error code.

open.description: Opens an XML file for parsing. This method returns an error code.

open_buffer.description: Opens an XML raw buffer for parsing. This method returns an error code.

XRAnchor3D.brief_description: An anchor point in AR space.
XRAnchor3D.description:
The  point is an  that maps a real world location identified by the AR platform to a position within the game world. For example, as long as plane detection in ARKit is on, ARKit will identify and update the position of planes (tables, floors, etc.) and create anchors for them.
		This node is mapped to one of the anchors through its unique ID. When you receive a signal that a new anchor is available, you should add this node to your scene for that anchor. You can predefine nodes and set the ID; the nodes will simply remain on (0, 0, 0) until a plane is recognized.
		Keep in mind that, as long as plane detection is enabled, the size, placing and orientation of an anchor will be updated as the detection logic learns more about the real world out there especially if only part of the surface is in view.

get_size.description: Returns the estimated size of the plane that was detected. Say when the anchor relates to a table in the real world, this is the estimated size of the surface of that table.

get_plane.description: Returns a plane aligned with our anchor; handy for intersection testing.

XRBodyModifier3D.brief_description: A node for driving body meshes from  data.
XRBodyModifier3D.description:
This node uses body tracking data from an  to pose the skeleton of a body mesh.
		Positioning of the body is performed by creating an  ancestor of the body mesh driven by the same .
		The body tracking position-data is scaled by Skeleton3D.motion_scale when applied to the skeleton, which can be used to adjust the tracked body to match the scale of the body model.

body_tracker.description: The name of the  registered with  to obtain the body tracking data from.

body_update.description: Specifies the body parts to update.

bone_update.description: Specifies the type of updates to perform on the bones.

XRBodyTracker.description:
A body tracking system will create an instance of this object and add it to the . This tracking system will then obtain skeleton data, convert it to the Godot Humanoid skeleton and store this data on the  object.
		Use  to animate a body mesh using body tracking data.

set_joint_flags.description: Sets flags about the validity of the tracking data for the given body joint.

get_joint_flags.description: Returns flags about the validity of the tracking data for the given body joint.

set_joint_transform.description: Sets the transform for the given body joint.

get_joint_transform.description: Returns the transform for the given body joint.

has_tracking_data.description: If true, the body tracking data is valid.

body_flags.description: The type of body tracking data captured.

XRCamera3D.brief_description: A camera node with a few overrules for AR/VR applied, such as location tracking.
XRCamera3D.description:
This is a helper 3D node for our camera. Note that, if stereoscopic rendering is applicable (VR-HMD), most of the camera properties are ignored, as the HMD information overrides them. The only properties that can be trusted are the near and far planes.
		The position and orientation of this node is automatically updated by the XR Server to represent the location of the HMD if such tracking is available and can thus be used by game logic. Note that, in contrast to the XR Controller, the render thread has access to the most up-to-date tracking data of the HMD and the location of the XRCamera3D can lag a few milliseconds behind what is used for rendering as a result.

XRController3D.brief_description: A 3D node representing a spatially-tracked controller.
XRController3D.description:
This is a helper 3D node that is linked to the tracking of controllers. It also offers several handy passthroughs to the state of buttons and such on the controllers.
		Controllers are linked by their ID. You can create controller nodes before the controllers are available. If your game always uses two controllers (one for each hand), you can predefine the controllers with ID 1 and 2; they will become active as soon as the controllers are identified. If you expect additional controllers to be used, you should react to the signals and add XRController3D nodes to your scene.
		The position of the controller node is automatically updated by the . This makes this node ideal to add child nodes to visualize the controller.
		The current  defines the names of inputs. In the case of OpenXR, these are the names of actions in the current action set from the OpenXR action map.

is_button_pressed.description:
Returns true if the button with the given name is pressed.
				Note: The current  defines the name for each input. In the case of OpenXR, these are the names of actions in the current action set.

get_input.description:
Returns a  for the input with the given name. This works for any input type, the variant will be typed according to the actions configuration.
				Note: The current  defines the name for each input. In the case of OpenXR, these are the names of actions in the current action set.

get_float.description:
Returns a numeric value for the input with the given name. This is used for triggers and grip sensors.
				Note: The current  defines the name for each input. In the case of OpenXR, these are the names of actions in the current action set.

get_vector2.description:
Returns a  for the input with the given name. This is used for thumbsticks and thumbpads found on many controllers.
				Note: The current  defines the name for each input. In the case of OpenXR, these are the names of actions in the current action set.

get_tracker_hand.description: Returns the hand holding this controller, if known.

XRControllerTracker.description:
An instance of this object represents a controller that is tracked.
		As controllers are turned on and the  detects them, instances of this object are automatically added to this list of active tracking objects accessible through the .
		The  consumes objects of this type and should be used in your project.

XRFaceModifier3D.brief_description: A node for driving standard face meshes from  weights.
XRFaceModifier3D.description:
This node applies weights from an  to a mesh with supporting face blend shapes.
		The Unified Expressions blend shapes are supported, as well as ARKit and SRanipal blend shapes.
		The node attempts to identify blend shapes based on name matching. Blend shapes should match the names listed in the Unified Expressions Compatibility chart.

XRFaceTracker.description:
An instance of this object represents a tracked face and its corresponding blend shapes. The blend shapes come from the Unified Expressions standard, and contain extended details and visuals for each blend shape. Additionally the Tracking Standard Comparison page documents the relationship between Unified Expressions and other standards.
		As face trackers are turned on they are registered with the .

get_blend_shape.description: Returns the requested face blend shape weight.

set_blend_shape.description: Sets a face blend shape weight.

blend_shapes.description: The array of face blend shape weights with indices corresponding to the  enum.

XRHandModifier3D.brief_description: A node for driving hand meshes from  data.
XRHandModifier3D.description:
This node uses hand tracking data from an  to pose the skeleton of a hand mesh.
		Positioning of hands is performed by creating an  ancestor of the hand mesh driven by the same .
		The hand tracking position-data is scaled by Skeleton3D.motion_scale when applied to the skeleton, which can be used to adjust the tracked hand to match the scale of the hand model.

hand_tracker.description: The name of the  registered with  to obtain the hand tracking data from.

bone_update.description: Specifies the type of updates to perform on the bones.

XRHandTracker.description:
A hand tracking system will create an instance of this object and add it to the . This tracking system will then obtain skeleton data, convert it to the Godot Humanoid hand skeleton and store this data on the  object.
		Use  to animate a hand mesh using hand tracking data.

set_hand_joint_flags.description: Sets flags about the validity of the tracking data for the given hand joint.

get_hand_joint_flags.description: Returns flags about the validity of the tracking data for the given hand joint.

set_hand_joint_transform.description: Sets the transform for the given hand joint.

get_hand_joint_transform.description: Returns the transform for the given hand joint.

set_hand_joint_radius.description: Sets the radius of the given hand joint.

get_hand_joint_radius.description: Returns the radius of the given hand joint.

set_hand_joint_angular_velocity.description: Sets the angular velocity for the given hand joint.
